# Palantir Foundry OSDK for TypeScript

> Build applications on Palantir Foundry with type-safe TypeScript and React SDKs for the Ontology, Platform APIs, and AIP.

This file contains every page of the documentation as Markdown. An index of the pages is at [llms.txt](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/llms.txt).

# Authentication

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/authentication

> Sign users in with @osdk/oauth, handle the OAuth redirect, authenticate servers with client credentials, and pass the token provider to createClient.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Developer Console permissions](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/developer-console/permissions)
- [API authentication](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/api/v2/general/overview/authentication)

Every OSDK request needs a Foundry bearer token. `@osdk/oauth` creates token providers that sign users in, store and refresh tokens, and plug straight into `createClient`.

## Choose a token provider

| Provider | Use it for | Grant |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createPublicOauthClient` | Browser apps where each user signs in with their own Foundry account. | Authorization code with PKCE |
| `createConfidentialOauthClient` | Servers, scheduled jobs, and backends that act as a service user. | Client credentials |
| `createAuthlessClient` | Public apps that read Foundry data without a signed-in user, such as those from the **React (Public)** template of `@osdk/create-app`. | None |
| Your own function | Scripts and tests that already have a token. | None |

A token provider is any function that returns `Promise<string>`. The OAuth clients are callable, so you pass them to `createClient` directly:

```ts title="src/client.ts"
import { $ontologyRid } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { createClient } from "@osdk/client";
import { createPublicOauthClient } from "@osdk/oauth";

const foundryUrl = "https://example.palantirfoundry.com";

export const auth = createPublicOauthClient(
  "<your-client-id>",
  foundryUrl,
  "http://localhost:8080/auth/callback",
);

export const client = createClient(foundryUrl, $ontologyRid, auth);
```

The client calls `auth()` before each request. You can call it yourself: `await auth()` resolves to the current access token and starts sign-in when there is none.

## Sign users in from a browser

`createPublicOauthClient` runs the OAuth authorization code flow with PKCE against Foundry. Create it once, at module scope, next to your client.

```ts
createPublicOauthClient(clientId, url, redirectUrl, options?)
```

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clientId` | `string` | The client ID from **OAuth & scopes** in Developer Console. |
| `url` | `string` | The base URL of your Foundry stack, such as `https://example.palantirfoundry.com`. |
| `redirectUrl` | `string` | The URL Foundry sends the user back to after sign-in. It must exactly match a redirect URL on **OAuth & scopes**. |
| `options` | `PublicOauthClientOptions` | Optional settings, listed below. |

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scopes` | `string[]` | `["api:read-data", "api:write-data", "api:use-ontologies-read", "api:use-ontologies-write"]` | OAuth scopes to request. See [Scopes](#scopes). |
| `tokenStorage` | `"localStorage" \| "sessionStorage" \| "none"` | `"localStorage"` | Where to keep the refresh token. See [Token storage](#token-storage). |
| `postLoginPage` | `string` | The page URL when the client is created | Used with `loginPage`: the page to return to after sign-in. Without `loginPage`, the client returns to the page the user was on. |
| `loginPage` | `string` | | A page in your app to show before redirecting to Foundry, such as `/login`. When set, the client navigates there instead of redirecting straight to Foundry. |
| `useHistory` | `boolean` | `true` | Navigate within your app, to `loginPage` or back to the original page after sign-in, with `history.replaceState()` instead of `window.location.assign()`, so the page does not reload. |
| `refreshTokenMarker` | `string` | | An extra value stored with the refresh token. Change it to invalidate stored refresh tokens and make every user sign in again. |
| `fetchFn` | `typeof fetch` | `globalThis.fetch` | The `fetch` used for token requests. |
| `ctxPath` | `string` | `"multipass"` | The path of Foundry's authorization server under `url`. |
| `logger` | `OauthLogger` | | Receives warnings, such as a failed refresh. Without it, warnings are dropped. Compatible with the `Logger` from `@osdk/api`. |

```ts title="src/client.ts"
export const auth = createPublicOauthClient(clientId, foundryUrl, redirectUrl, {
  scopes: ["api:read-data", "api:use-ontologies-read"],
  tokenStorage: "sessionStorage",
});
```

> [!NOTE]
> The fourth argument can also be the older positional form, `useHistory, loginPage, postLoginPage, scopes, fetchFn, ctxPath`. Pass either an options object or positional arguments, not both. `tokenStorage`, `refreshTokenMarker`, and `logger` are only available in the options object.

### How the flow works

1. The first time your app needs a token, the client looks for a stored refresh token and uses it if it is valid.
2. Without one, it saves a PKCE verifier and the current URL in `sessionStorage`, then redirects to Foundry's sign-in page.
3. Foundry redirects to `redirectUrl` with an authorization code.
4. On that page, your app asks for a token again. The client exchanges the code, stores the refresh token, and navigates back to the page the user started on.
5. The client refreshes the access token one minute before it expires. You do not schedule refreshes yourself.

Concurrent token requests share one sign-in, so several components asking for data at once trigger a single redirect.

### Handle the redirect callback

Render a route at your redirect URL's path that calls `auth.signIn()`. This completes step 4. The React template from `@osdk/create-app` uses this component, which then navigates to `/`; navigate elsewhere if your app needs to:

```tsx title="src/AuthCallback.tsx"
import { auth } from "@/client";
import React, { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { useNavigate } from "react-router-dom";

function AuthCallback(): React.ReactElement {
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | undefined>(undefined);
  const navigate = useNavigate();

  useEffect(() => {
    auth
      .signIn()
      .then(() => navigate("/", { replace: true }))
      .catch((e: unknown) => {
        setError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e));
      });
  }, [navigate]);

  return <div>{error != null ? error : "Authenticating…"}</div>;
}

export default AuthCallback;
```

Register it at the same path as `redirectUrl`:

```tsx title="src/router.tsx"
import AuthCallback from "@/AuthCallback";
import Home from "@/Home";
import { createBrowserRouter } from "react-router-dom";

export const router = createBrowserRouter(
  [
    { path: "/", element: <Home /> },
    { path: "/auth/callback", element: <AuthCallback /> },
  ],
  { basename: import.meta.env.BASE_URL },
);
```

If the redirect URL in your code, in `.env` files, and on **OAuth & scopes** differ in any character, including the port and a trailing slash, Foundry rejects the sign-in.

### Require sign-in before rendering

The client starts sign-in on the first request, so pages that load OSDK data trigger it automatically. To keep a route from rendering until the user is signed in, check for a token first. `getTokenOrUndefined()` returns the current access token synchronously, or `undefined` if there is none or it has expired:

```tsx title="src/AuthenticatedRoute.tsx"
import { auth } from "@/client";
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { Outlet } from "react-router-dom";

export function AuthenticatedRoute() {
  const [token, setToken] = useState(auth.getTokenOrUndefined());

  useEffect(() => {
    auth()
      .then(setToken)
      .catch((e: unknown) => {
        console.error("Sign-in failed", e);
        setToken(undefined);
      });
  }, []);

  return token == null ? null : <Outlet />;
}
```

### Scopes

Scopes limit what the token can do. Both OAuth clients default to `api:read-data`, `api:write-data`, `api:use-ontologies-read`, and `api:use-ontologies-write`. Request only what your app needs, and make sure each scope is allowed for your application on **OAuth & scopes** in Developer Console. A read-only app can drop the two `write` scopes.

The defaults only cover the Ontology. Add the scopes for anything else your app calls: each Platform SDK endpoint lists its required scopes (see [Platform SDK setup](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/setup.md)), and the AI packages need `api:use-language-models-execute` (see [AI](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai.md)).

The public client also requests `offline_access` so Foundry issues a refresh token, unless `tokenStorage` is `"none"`. A stored refresh token is only reused when it was issued for the same set of scopes, so changing `scopes` signs users in again.

### Token storage

| `tokenStorage` | Refresh token kept | Trade-off |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"localStorage"` | Across browser sessions | Fewest sign-ins. Anyone with access to the browser profile stays signed in. |
| `"sessionStorage"` | Until the tab or browser closes | Recommended for shared devices. |
| `"none"` | Never | Users sign in on every page load. No `offline_access` scope is requested. |

The refresh token is stored under the key `@osdk/oauth : refresh : <clientId>`. Access tokens stay in memory.

### Sign out

`signOut()` revokes the access token with Foundry, deletes the stored refresh token, and emits a `signOut` event. It does not navigate, so redirect the user yourself:

```tsx title="src/SignOutButton.tsx"
import { auth } from "@/client";

export function SignOutButton() {
  async function handleClick() {
    try {
      await auth.signOut();
    } finally {
      window.location.assign("/");
    }
  }

  return (
    <button type="button" onClick={handleClick}>
      Sign out
    </button>
  );
}
```

`signOut()` throws if nobody is signed in. The next token request after sign-out starts a new sign-in.

### Listen for auth events

The public client emits `signIn`, `refresh`, and `signOut` events. `signIn` and `refresh` carry the new token in `event.detail`:

```ts
import { auth } from "./client";

function handleSignOut() {
  console.info("Signed out");
}

auth.addEventListener("signIn", (event) => {
  console.info("Signed in; token expires at", new Date(event.detail.expires_at));
});
auth.addEventListener("signOut", handleSignOut);

auth.removeEventListener("signOut", handleSignOut);
```

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `auth()` | Resolves to a valid access token, refreshing or signing in when needed. |
| `auth.signIn()` | Runs sign-in: refreshes from a stored token, completes a redirect callback, or redirects to Foundry. Resolves to the token object. |
| `auth.refresh()` | Refreshes the access token with the stored refresh token. |
| `auth.signOut()` | Revokes the token and clears stored state. |
| `auth.getTokenOrUndefined()` | Returns the current access token, or `undefined` if there is none or it has expired. |
| `auth.addEventListener(type, listener)` | Listens for `signIn`, `refresh`, or `signOut`. |
| `auth.removeEventListener(type, listener)` | Removes a listener. |

## Authenticate a server or service

`createConfidentialOauthClient` uses the client credentials grant with a client ID and secret from a confidential application in Developer Console. Requests run as that application's service user, not as a person.

```ts
createConfidentialOauthClient(clientId, clientSecret, url, scopes?, fetchFn?, ctxPath?)
```

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clientId` | `string` | | The confidential application's client ID. |
| `clientSecret` | `string` | | The client secret. |
| `url` | `string` | | The base URL of your Foundry stack. |
| `scopes` | `string[]` | `["api:read-data", "api:write-data", "api:use-ontologies-read", "api:use-ontologies-write"]` | Scopes to request. |
| `fetchFn` | `typeof fetch` | `globalThis.fetch` | The `fetch` used for token requests. |
| `ctxPath` | `string` | `"multipass"` | The path of Foundry's authorization server under `url`. |

```ts title="server/client.ts"
import { $ontologyRid } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { createClient } from "@osdk/client";
import { createConfidentialOauthClient } from "@osdk/oauth";

const foundryUrl = "https://example.palantirfoundry.com";
const clientId = process.env.FOUNDRY_CLIENT_ID;
const clientSecret = process.env.FOUNDRY_CLIENT_SECRET;

if (clientId == null || clientSecret == null) {
  throw new Error("Set FOUNDRY_CLIENT_ID and FOUNDRY_CLIENT_SECRET");
}

const auth = createConfidentialOauthClient(clientId, clientSecret, foundryUrl, [
  "api:read-data",
  "api:use-ontologies-read",
]);

export const client = createClient(foundryUrl, $ontologyRid, auth);
```

The client requests a new token when the current one expires. There is no refresh token or browser storage. It supports `signIn()`, `signOut()`, `getTokenOrUndefined()`, and `signIn` and `signOut` events, but not `refresh()`.

> [!CAUTION]
> Never use `createConfidentialOauthClient` in browser code. Anything you ship to a browser, including environment variables inlined by your bundler, is readable by users, and the client secret lets anyone act as your application.

## Public apps without sign-in

`createAuthlessClient()` returns a token provider that sends a fixed public token, for apps that let anyone view data without a Foundry account:

```ts title="src/client.ts"
import { createClient } from "@osdk/client";
import { createAuthlessClient } from "@osdk/oauth";

const foundryUrl = import.meta.env.VITE_FOUNDRY_API_URL;
const ontologyRid = import.meta.env.VITE_FOUNDRY_ONTOLOGY_RID;

export const client = createClient(foundryUrl, ontologyRid, createAuthlessClient());
```

The **React (Public)** template of `@osdk/create-app` sets this up, including the request proxy it relies on. It reads the Foundry URL and Ontology RID from the `osdk-foundryUrl` and `osdk-ontologyRid` `<meta>` tags instead of environment variables, so a Marketplace installation uses its destination's Foundry URL and Ontology.

## Use an existing token

For scripts, tests, and one-off tools, pass a function that returns a token you already have, such as one from an environment variable:

```ts title="scripts/countEngineers.ts"
import { $ontologyRid, Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { createClient } from "@osdk/client";

const token = process.env.FOUNDRY_TOKEN;
if (token == null) {
  throw new Error("Set FOUNDRY_TOKEN");
}

const client = createClient(
  "https://example.palantirfoundry.com",
  $ontologyRid,
  () => Promise.resolve(token),
);

const result = await client(Employee)
  .where({ department: "Engineering" })
  .aggregate({ $select: { $count: "unordered" } });

console.log(result.$count);
```

The client does not refresh a static token. When it expires, requests fail with `401` until you supply a new one.

# Create a client

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/client

> Configure createClient with your Foundry URL, Ontology RID, and token provider, share it through OsdkProvider, and query without React.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [TypeScript OSDK](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/ontology-sdk/typescript-osdk)

The client from `@osdk/client` sends every OSDK request: it fetches objects, applies actions, and executes functions. Create it once per app, then hand it to `OsdkProvider` for React or call it directly.

## `createClient`

```ts
createClient(baseUrl, ontologyRid, tokenProvider, options?, fetchFn?)
```

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `baseUrl` | `string` | The base URL of your Foundry stack, such as `https://example.palantirfoundry.com`. In local development behind a CORS proxy, your dev server's origin. |
| `ontologyRid` | `string \| Promise<string>` | The Ontology to query, such as `ri.ontology.main.ontology.<id>`. Usually `$ontologyRid` from your generated SDK. |
| `tokenProvider` | `() => Promise<string>` | Returns a bearer token for each request. Usually an OAuth client from `@osdk/oauth`. See [Authentication](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/authentication.md). |
| `options` | `object` | Optional settings, listed below. |
| `fetchFn` | `typeof fetch` | The `fetch` used for every request. Defaults to the global `fetch`. |

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `headers` | `Record<string, string>` | | Extra headers added to every request. |
| `logger` | `Logger` | A minimal built-in logger | A `Logger`, as defined in `@osdk/api`, that receives the client's log output. |
| `UNSTABLE_DO_NOT_USE_BRANCH` | `string \| null` | Read from the page | Beta. The Foundry branch to read and write on. When omitted in a browser, the client uses the `foundryBranchRid` query parameter, then the branch meta tag injected by OSDK build tooling. `null` pins the default branch. |

`createClient` throws `Invalid ontology RID` when `ontologyRid` is a string that does not start with `ri.`.

```ts title="src/client.ts"
import { $ontologyRid } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { createClient, type Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { createPublicOauthClient } from "@osdk/oauth";

const foundryUrl = "https://example.palantirfoundry.com";

export const auth = createPublicOauthClient(
  "<your-client-id>",
  foundryUrl,
  "http://localhost:8080/auth/callback",
);

export const client: Client = createClient(foundryUrl, $ontologyRid, auth);
```

Some generated SDKs omit `$ontologyRid`, because they are built to run on more than one Foundry stack and an embedded RID would only be correct on one. Pass the RID from configuration instead.

## Keep one client per app

Create the client at module scope in a single file, such as `src/client.ts`, and import it everywhere. `OsdkProvider` builds its cache from the client instance, so a new instance starts over with an empty cache.

Read configuration from your environment instead of hard-coding it. With Vite, use `import.meta.env`:

```ts title="src/client.ts"
import { createClient } from "@osdk/client";
import { createPublicOauthClient } from "@osdk/oauth";

const foundryUrl = import.meta.env.VITE_FOUNDRY_API_URL;
const clientId = import.meta.env.VITE_FOUNDRY_CLIENT_ID;
const redirectUrl = import.meta.env.VITE_FOUNDRY_REDIRECT_URL;
const ontologyRid = import.meta.env.VITE_FOUNDRY_ONTOLOGY_RID;

export const auth = createPublicOauthClient(clientId, foundryUrl, redirectUrl);
export const client = createClient(foundryUrl, ontologyRid, auth);
```

The React template from `@osdk/create-app` goes one step further: `index.html` renders the env values into `<meta>` tags, such as `<meta name="osdk-foundryUrl" content="%VITE_FOUNDRY_API_URL%" />`, and `src/client.ts` reads them at startup. Hosting can then change configuration by rewriting the HTML, without a new JavaScript build:

```ts title="src/client.ts"
function getMetaTagContent(tagName: string): string {
  const elements = document.querySelectorAll(`meta[name="${tagName}"]`);
  const value = elements.item(elements.length - 1)?.getAttribute("content");
  if (value == null || value === "") {
    throw new Error(`Meta tag ${tagName} not found or empty`);
  }
  return value;
}

const foundryUrl = getMetaTagContent("osdk-foundryUrl");
const ontologyRid = getMetaTagContent("osdk-ontologyRid");
```

### Platform API only clients

`createPlatformClient(baseUrl, tokenProvider, options?, fetchFn?)` creates a client for Foundry Platform APIs, such as `@osdk/foundry.admin`, without an Ontology. Use it in apps that have no generated SDK. A client from `createClient` also works with the `@osdk/foundry.*` Platform SDK functions, so most apps need only one client. The exception is the AI helpers in `@osdk/aip-core`, such as `foundryModel`, which require a client from `createPlatformClient` (see [Chat and streaming](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/chat.md)):

```ts title="src/currentUser.ts"
import { Users } from "@osdk/foundry.admin";
import { client } from "./client";

const me = await Users.getCurrent(client);
console.log(me.username);
```

## Provide the client to React

Wrap your app's root in `OsdkProvider` from `@osdk/react`. Every `@osdk/react` hook reads the client and its cache from the provider.

```tsx title="src/main.tsx"
import { OsdkProvider } from "@osdk/react";
import ReactDOM from "react-dom/client";
import { App } from "./App";
import { client } from "./client";

const rootElement = document.getElementById("root");
if (rootElement == null) {
  throw new Error("Root element not found");
}

ReactDOM.createRoot(rootElement).render(
  <OsdkProvider client={client}>
    <App />
  </OsdkProvider>,
);
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `client` | `Client` | | The client from `createClient`. The provider creates its cache from this instance. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | | Your app. |
| `enableDevTools` | `boolean` | `true` when `@osdk/react-devtools` is registered | Turns the [OSDK Devtools](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/devtools.md) panel on or off. Has no effect in production builds. |
| `devMode` | `object` | | Development-only cache behavior, ignored in production builds. See below. |

| `devMode` field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `actionDelayMs` | `number` | `1000` | Delays the result of an action that has an optimistic update, so you can see the optimistic state. Set `0` to turn it off. |
| `logLevel` | `"trace" \| "debug" \| "info" \| "warn" \| "error" \| "fatal"` | `"error"` | Log level of the cache layer. `"debug"` shows its tracing. |
| `debug.refCounts` | `boolean` | `false` | Logs cache entry reference counts and cleanup, and shortens retention so cleanup happens sooner. |
| `debug.cacheKeys` | `boolean` | `false` | Logs cache key lookups. |

```tsx
<OsdkProvider client={client} devMode={{ actionDelayMs: 0, logLevel: "debug" }}>
  <App />
</OsdkProvider>
```

Put the provider above everything that uses OSDK data, including headers and navigation, and pass it a client created at module scope. `<OsdkProvider client={createClient(...)}>` inside a component creates a new client, and an empty cache, on every render.

A hook rendered outside the provider throws:

```txt
No OsdkProvider found. Did you forget to wrap your component tree with <OsdkProvider>?
```

To call the client inside a component, for example in an event handler, read it from the provider with `useOsdkClient`:

```tsx title="src/ExportButton.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkClient } from "@osdk/react";

export function ExportButton() {
  const client = useOsdkClient();

  async function handleClick() {
    const names: string[] = [];
    for await (const employee of client(Employee).asyncIter({ $select: ["fullName"] })) {
      names.push(employee.fullName ?? "");
    }
    await navigator.clipboard.writeText(names.join("\n"));
  }

  return (
    <button type="button" onClick={() => void handleClick()}>
      Copy all names
    </button>
  );
}
```

For data you render, prefer the hooks, such as `useOsdkObjects` and `useOsdkAction`: they cache results and update when objects change. Direct client calls bypass the cache.

## Use the client without React

Call `client` with a definition from your SDK. What it returns depends on the definition:

| You pass | You get | Main methods |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Object type, such as `Employee` | An object set of all objects of that type | `where`, `fetchPage`, `fetchOne`, `asyncIter`, `aggregate`, `pivotTo` |
| Interface | An object set over every type that implements it | Object set methods except `fetchOne`; see [Interfaces](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/interfaces.md) |
| Action, such as `modifyEmployee` | An action invoker | `applyAction`, `batchApplyAction` |
| Function (query) | A function invoker | `executeFunction` |

### Fetch objects

`fetchPage` returns one page with `data`, `nextPageToken`, and `totalCount`. `where` narrows the set and returns a new object set, so you can chain it:

```ts title="src/employees.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const page = await client(Employee)
  .where({ department: "Engineering" })
  .fetchPage({
    $select: ["fullName", "jobTitle"],
    $orderBy: { fullName: "asc" },
    $pageSize: 50,
  });

for (const employee of page.data) {
  console.log(employee.$primaryKey, employee.fullName, employee.jobTitle);
}

if (page.nextPageToken != null) {
  const next = await client(Employee)
    .where({ department: "Engineering" })
    .fetchPage({ $pageSize: 50, $nextPageToken: page.nextPageToken });
  console.log(next.data.length);
}
```

Without `$select`, the response includes the type's default properties. Select only what you read. `$pageSize` sizes each page; it does not cap the total.

Fetch one object by primary key with `fetchOne`, and follow links from it through `$link`:

```ts
const employee = await client(Employee).fetchOne(12345);
const office = await employee.$link.office.fetchOne();
```

To process every matching object, iterate with `asyncIter`. It fetches page after page from a consistent snapshot, so each object arrives once even if the data changes during the loop:

```ts
for await (const employee of client(Employee).asyncIter({ $select: ["fullName"] })) {
  console.log(employee.fullName);
}
```

For counts, sums, and group-bys, use `aggregate` instead of loading every object.

### Apply an action

`applyAction` takes the action's parameters and an optional options object. Object parameters accept an object instance or its primary key:

```ts title="src/promote.ts"
import { modifyEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { ActionValidationError } from "@osdk/client";
import { client } from "./client";

try {
  const edits = await client(modifyEmployee).applyAction(
    { employee: 12345, jobTitle: "Senior Engineer" },
    { $returnEdits: true },
  );
  console.log(edits);
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof ActionValidationError) {
    console.error("Invalid parameters", e.validation);
  } else {
    throw e;
  }
}
```

| Option | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| none | `undefined` |
| `{ $returnEdits: true }` | The edits the action made: objects added, modified, and deleted. |
| `{ $validateOnly: true }` | The validation result, without applying the action. |

`applyAction` throws `ActionValidationError` when the parameters fail validation, with the details in `error.validation`. `batchApplyAction` takes an array of parameter objects and applies them in one request.

### Execute a function

```ts
const result = await client(getEmployeeCount).executeFunction({ department: "Engineering" });
```

Replace `getEmployeeCount` with a function from your SDK. Its parameters and return type come from the function's definition.

### Read metadata

`client.fetchMetadata(definition)` returns runtime metadata, such as display names and descriptions, for an object type, interface, action, or function:

```ts
const metadata = await client.fetchMetadata(Employee);
console.log(metadata.displayName, metadata.description);
```

# Caching and reactivity

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/concepts/caching

> How @osdk/react stores objects once, shares them across hooks, deduplicates requests, and updates every view after an action.

{/* cspell:ignore refetched refetches */}

`@osdk/react` keeps one normalized cache per `OsdkProvider`. This page explains what the cache stores, when hooks hit the network, and how data updates after actions, so you can predict what a component renders.

## One cache per provider

`OsdkProvider` wraps your `Client` in an `ObservableClient` from `@osdk/client/observable`. Every hook below that provider reads from and writes to the same cache:

```tsx title="src/main.tsx"
import { OsdkProvider } from "@osdk/react";
import ReactDOM from "react-dom/client";
import App from "./App";
import { client } from "./client";

ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById("root")!).render(
  <OsdkProvider client={client}>
    <App />
  </OsdkProvider>,
);
```

Create the client once, outside any component. A new client creates a new, empty cache.

## Objects are stored once

The cache stores each object under its object type and primary key, such as `Employee:12345`. Lists, links, and object sets do not copy objects. They store references to those entries.

| Hook | What the cache stores |
| --- | --- |
| `useOsdkObject` | One entry per object type and primary key. |
| `useOsdkObjects`, `useObjectSet` | The ordered list of references, plus `totalCount` and paging state. |
| `useLinks` | References to the linked objects, keyed by source object, link name, and filters. |
| `useOsdkAggregation` | The aggregation result, keyed by object type, filter, and aggregate definition. |
| `useOsdkFunction` | The function result, keyed by function and parameters. |

Because objects are shared, a change to `Employee:12345` reaches every list, link, and detail view that contains it in the same render:

```tsx title="src/EmployeeViews.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useLinks, useOsdkObject, useOsdkObjects } from "@osdk/react";

function Directory() {
  const { data } = useOsdkObjects(Employee);
  return <ul>{data?.map(e => <li key={e.$primaryKey}>{e.fullName}</li>)}</ul>;
}

function Profile({ id }: { id: number }) {
  const { object } = useOsdkObject(Employee, id);
  return <h1>{object?.fullName}</h1>;
}

function Team({ manager }: { manager: Employee.OsdkInstance }) {
  const { links } = useLinks(manager, "reports");
  return <ul>{links?.map(e => <li key={e.$primaryKey}>{e.fullName}</li>)}</ul>;
}
```

All three render the same `Employee` instance for `12345`.

### Read an instance you already have

`useOsdkObject(instance)` reads the object from the cache and does not send a request. Use it in a row component to get `isOptimistic` for an object a list already loaded:

```tsx title="src/EmployeeRow.tsx"
import type { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkObject } from "@osdk/react";

function EmployeeRow({ employee }: { employee: Employee.OsdkInstance }) {
  const { object, isOptimistic } = useOsdkObject(employee);
  return (
    <li style={{ opacity: isOptimistic ? 0.5 : 1 }}>
      {object?.fullName ?? employee.fullName}
    </li>
  );
}
```

`useOsdkObject(Employee, id)` with a type and primary key does fetch. Calls for the same object type made within 25 ms are batched into one request of up to 100 objects.

## When two hooks share an entry

Two hooks share a cache entry when they ask for the same data. The client canonicalizes options before building the key, so structurally equal options match even if you write them inline or list keys in a different order.

| Part of the key | Not part of the key |
| --- | --- |
| Object type or interface | `pageSize` |
| `where` | `enabled` |
| `orderBy` | `dedupeIntervalMs` |
| `withProperties` | `autoFetchMore` |
| `$select`, `intersectWith`, `pivotTo`, `rids` | |

For example, these share one entry, and each component sees its own page size:

```tsx
useOsdkObjects(Employee, { where: { department: "Sales" }, pageSize: 10 });
useOsdkObjects(Employee, { where: { department: "Sales" }, pageSize: 50 });
```

These are separate entries, because the filters differ:

```tsx
useOsdkObjects(Employee, { where: { department: "Sales" } });
useOsdkObjects(Employee, { where: { department: "Support" } });
```

Adding `withProperties` creates a separate variant of each object, so derived properties never leak into views that did not request them.

## When hooks fetch

The cache serves data immediately and refreshes it in the background. When a hook subscribes, it does three things:

1. Returns any data already in the cache for its key.
2. Starts a request to revalidate the entry, unless a request for that entry is already in flight or one started within `dedupeIntervalMs`.
3. Updates when the response arrives.

So a component that mounts onto cached data renders it at once, with `isLoading: true` while the refresh runs. See [Loading and errors](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/concepts/loading-and-errors.md) for how to render that state.

### Deduplication

`dedupeIntervalMs` defaults to `2000` on `useOsdkObjects`, `useObjectSet`, `useLinks`, `useOsdkAggregation`, and `useOsdkFunction`. If two components mount the same query within that window, the second one reuses the first request.

```tsx
const { data } = useOsdkObjects(Employee, {
  where: { department: "Sales" },
  dedupeIntervalMs: 30_000,
});
```

When several mounted hooks share an entry, the smallest `dedupeIntervalMs` among them applies. In-flight requests are always shared, whatever the interval.

### Retention

An entry stays in the cache for about 60 seconds after its last hook unmounts. Navigating away and back within that window renders the cached data while it revalidates. After that, the entry is removed and the next mount starts empty.

## Updates after actions

When you apply an action with `useOsdkAction`, the client requests the action's edits from the server and updates the cache from them. You do not need to invalidate anything.

| Edit | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Object modified | The object is refetched. Every list, link, and detail view that references it re-renders. |
| Object added | The object is fetched. Lists of that type whose `where` clause it matches add it. |
| Object deleted | The object is removed from the cache and from every list that contained it. |
| Any edit to a type | Aggregations over that type refetch. Links to that type re-evaluate. Functions with `dependsOn` that include the type refetch. |

The action's promise resolves after the edited objects are refetched. Aggregation and other type-wide refreshes continue in the background.

### How lists stay correct

For a modified or added object, each list of that type checks the object against its `where` clause in the browser:

- If the object matches, the list keeps it or inserts it.
- If the object no longer matches, the list removes it.
- If the clause uses a filter the browser cannot evaluate, such as full-text search, the list refetches from the server with `isLoading: true` and keeps its current data until the response arrives.

Lists that follow a link (`pivotTo`) or return a different object type than they start from always refetch from the server when objects of their result type change.

### Functions

Function results are not tied to objects, so the cache cannot know which edits affect them. Declare the dependency with `dependsOn` or `dependsOnObjects`:

```tsx
import { type Employee, getEmployeeReport } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkFunction } from "@osdk/react";

function EmployeeReport({ employee }: { employee: Employee.OsdkInstance }) {
  const { data } = useOsdkFunction(getEmployeeReport, {
    params: { employeeId: employee.$primaryKey },
    dependsOnObjects: [employee],
  });
  return <pre>{data}</pre>;
}
```

| Option | Refetches when |
| --- | --- |
| `dependsOn: [Employee]` | An action edits any `Employee`. |
| `dependsOnObjects: [employee]` | An action edits that specific object. |
| `dependsOnObjects: [objectSet]` | An action edits any object of the object set's type. |

## Optimistic updates

`useOsdkAction` accepts `$optimisticUpdate`, which writes your predicted change to a temporary layer above the server data. Every view shows the predicted change at once and reports `isOptimistic: true`. When the action finishes, the layer is removed and the server's data replaces it. If the action fails, the layer is removed and the views return to the previous data.

In development, an action with an optimistic update is delayed by 1000 ms so you can see the optimistic state. Set `devMode={{ actionDelayMs: 0 }}` on `OsdkProvider` to turn the delay off. The delay never applies in production builds.

See [Optimistic updates](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/optimistic-updates.md) for the API.

## Real-time updates

Pass `streamUpdates: true` to `useOsdkObjects` to keep a list current over a WebSocket. Changes made outside your app, by other users or pipelines, arrive without polling. `streamUpdates` cannot be combined with `pivotTo`, because the server does not support subscriptions for link traversal.

## When you need to invalidate

Automatic updates cover changes that go through `useOsdkAction` in this app. Invalidate manually when data changes another way:

- Another system or pipeline edits the data.
- Your code edits data with `@osdk/client` directly, a REST call, or a background job.
- A function reads data the cache cannot track.

See [Cache invalidation](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/cache-invalidation.md) for `invalidateObjects`, `invalidateObjectType`, `invalidateFunction`, and the other methods.

## Practices

- **Let actions drive updates.** Do not call `invalidate*` after `applyAction`. The cache already handles the edits.
- **Keep one source of truth.** Do not copy OSDK data into Redux, TanStack Query, or component state. Copies miss optimistic updates and action edits.
- **Declare function dependencies.** Prefer `dependsOn` and `dependsOnObjects` over invalidating functions by hand.
- **Use the devtools.** The [Cache panel](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/devtools/cache.md) shows entries, hits, and misses in a running app.

# Loading and errors

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/concepts/loading-and-errors

> Render @osdk/react hooks correctly while data loads, refreshes, or fails, and narrow errors to PalantirApiError and ActionValidationError.

{/* cspell:ignore refetched refetches */}

`@osdk/react` hooks can return data and report loading at the same time. This page shows the loading pattern that avoids flashing UI, the error shape of each hook, and how to turn an error into a message the user can act on.

## Loading is not the same as empty

`isLoading` means a request for the hook's data is in flight. It does not mean `data` is missing. The cache serves what it has and refreshes in the background, so `isLoading` is `true` with data present when:

- The component mounts onto data that another component already cached.
- An action edits an object and a list must refetch to decide whether the object still belongs in it.
- You call `refetch`, or something invalidates the entry.
- An optimistic update is applied to a list.

The states you can see are:

| `data` | `isLoading` | Meaning | Render |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `undefined` | `true` | First load, nothing cached. | A placeholder or skeleton. |
| Present | `true` | Refreshing cached data. | The data, with a small refreshing indicator. |
| Present | `false` | Up to date. | The data. |
| `undefined` | `false` | The hook is disabled with `enabled: false`, or the load failed. | An empty state, or the error. |

See [Caching and reactivity](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/concepts/caching.md) for when hooks refetch.

## Keep rendering while loading

Do not return early on `isLoading`. An early return replaces the content with a spinner every time the cache refreshes, which makes the page flash and resets scroll position and focus. The only early return that is safe is the initial state, when there is no data yet:

```tsx title="src/EmployeeList.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkObjects } from "@osdk/react";

export function EmployeeList() {
  const { data, isLoading, error, refetch, fetchMore } = useOsdkObjects(
    Employee,
    { where: { department: "Engineering" }, orderBy: { fullName: "asc" } },
  );

  if (data == null && isLoading) {
    return <p>Loading employees…</p>;
  }

  return (
    <section aria-busy={isLoading}>
      <header>
        <h2>Engineering</h2>
        {isLoading && <span>Refreshing…</span>}
      </header>

      {error != null && (
        <div role="alert">
          <p>Could not load employees: {error.message}</p>
          <button onClick={() => void refetch()}>Retry</button>
        </div>
      )}

      <ul>
        {data?.map(employee => (
          <li key={employee.$primaryKey}>{employee.fullName}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>

      {fetchMore != null && (
        <button onClick={() => void fetchMore()} disabled={isLoading}>
          Load more
        </button>
      )}
    </section>
  );
}
```

The component checks `error` separately from `data`. A refresh can fail after earlier data loaded, so both can be set at once.

> [!WARNING]
> Do not write `if (isLoading) return <Spinner />`. Use `if (data == null && isLoading)` for the initial load, and render an inline indicator for refreshes.

## Loading and error fields by hook

The hooks do not all use the same field names. Check this table before you destructure:

| Hook | Data | Loading | Error | Retry |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `useOsdkObjects` | `data` | `isLoading` | `error: Error \| undefined` | `refetch()` |
| `useObjectSet` | `data` | `isLoading` | `error: Error \| undefined` | `refetch()` |
| `useOsdkObject` | `object` | `isLoading` | `error: Error \| undefined` | None |
| `useLinks` | `links` | `isLoading` | `error: Error \| undefined` | None |
| `useOsdkAggregation` | `data` | `isLoading` | `error: Error \| undefined` | `refetch()` |
| `useOsdkFunction` | `data` | `isLoading` | `error: Error \| undefined` | `refetch()` |
| `useOsdkAction` | `data` | `isPending`, `isValidating` | `error: { actionValidation?, unknown? } \| undefined` | Call `applyAction` again |
| `useOsdkMetadata` | `metadata` | `loading` | `error: string \| undefined` | None |

Details that differ between hooks:

- **`refetch` scope.** On `useOsdkObjects`, `useObjectSet`, and `useOsdkAggregation`, `refetch` invalidates the whole object type, so every list and aggregation of that type refetches. On `useOsdkFunction`, it refetches only that function call with those parameters. To refetch more narrowly, use the methods in [Cache invalidation](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/cache-invalidation.md).
- **`useOsdkObject`.** `isLoading` is `false` as soon as `error` is set.
- **`useObjectSet`.** When the object set changes, `data` keeps the last loaded result until the new set loads.
- **`useOsdkFunction`.** `isLoading` is `true` only while a request is in flight, so the first render can report `isLoading: false` with no data. Treat `data === undefined && error == null` as the initial state, or check `lastUpdated === 0`.
- **`useOsdkMetadata`.** It uses `loading`, not `isLoading`, and `error` is the error's message as a string, not an `Error`. It does not retry after a failure.
- **Disabled hooks.** With `enabled: false` (or `false` as the last argument to `useOsdkObject`), `isLoading` is `false` and no request is sent.

## Narrow API errors

Errors from Foundry are instances of `PalantirApiError`, which `@osdk/client` exports. Data hooks type `error` as `Error`, so narrow it with `instanceof`:

```tsx title="src/describeError.ts"
import { PalantirApiError } from "@osdk/client";

export function describeError(error: Error): string {
  if (!(error instanceof PalantirApiError)) {
    return error.message;
  }
  if (error.statusCode === 401) {
    return "Your session has expired. Sign in again.";
  }
  if (error.errorCode === "PERMISSION_DENIED" || error.statusCode === 403) {
    return "You do not have access to this data.";
  }
  if (error.errorCode === "NOT_FOUND") {
    return "This item no longer exists, or you cannot see it.";
  }
  return error.message;
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | `string` | The server's message, or `Failed to fetch <status> <statusText>`. |
| `errorCode` | `string \| undefined` | The error category, such as `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `NOT_FOUND`, `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `CONFLICT`, or `TIMEOUT`. |
| `errorName` | `string \| undefined` | The specific error, such as `ObjectNotFound`. |
| `errorDescription` | `string \| undefined` | A longer description of the error. |
| `statusCode` | `number \| undefined` | The HTTP status code. |
| `errorInstanceId` | `string \| undefined` | An ID for this occurrence. Include it when you report a problem to your Foundry administrator. |
| `parameters` | `unknown` | Error-specific details, such as the object type that was not found. |

Some errors carry only a message:

- When a request fails before reaching Foundry, or the response is not JSON, the error is a `PalantirApiError` subclass whose `name` is `"UnknownError"`. `statusCode` is set if a response arrived.
- `useOsdkObject(Employee, id)` for an object that does not exist, or that you cannot see, reports a `PalantirApiError` with the message `Object not found: <id>` and no `errorCode` or `statusCode`.

The client retries requests that fail with `429` or `503` up to three times, with exponential backoff, before the error reaches your hook.

## Handle action errors

`useOsdkAction` splits errors into two kinds:

| Field | Set when | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `error.actionValidation` | The server ran the action's validation and it failed: a submission criterion or a parameter constraint was not met. | `ActionValidationError` |
| `error.unknown` | Anything else, such as a network failure, a permission error, or a server error. | `unknown` |

`applyAction` also rethrows the error, so always await it in `try`/`catch` or attach `.catch`. Otherwise a failed action becomes an unhandled promise rejection:

```tsx title="src/MoveEmployeeButton.tsx"
import { type Employee, modifyEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { ActionValidationError } from "@osdk/client";
import { useOsdkAction } from "@osdk/react";
import { useState } from "react";

export function MoveEmployeeButton(
  { employee }: { employee: Employee.OsdkInstance },
) {
  const { applyAction, isPending } = useOsdkAction(modifyEmployee);
  const [message, setMessage] = useState<string>();

  async function handleClick() {
    setMessage(undefined);
    try {
      await applyAction({ employee, primary_office_id: "nyc-1" });
    } catch (e) {
      setMessage(
        e instanceof ActionValidationError
          ? validationMessage(e)
          : "Could not move the employee. Try again.",
      );
    }
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <button onClick={handleClick} disabled={isPending}>
        {isPending ? "Saving…" : "Move to New York"}
      </button>
      {message != null && <p role="alert">{message}</p>}
    </div>
  );
}

function validationMessage(error: ActionValidationError): string {
  const criteria = error.validation.submissionCriteria
    .filter(c => c.result === "INVALID")
    .flatMap(c => c.configuredFailureMessage ?? []);

  const parameters = Object.entries(error.validation.parameters)
    .filter(([, p]) => p.result === "INVALID")
    .map(([id]) => id);

  if (criteria.length > 0) {
    return criteria.join(" ");
  }
  if (parameters.length > 0) {
    return `Check these fields: ${parameters.join(", ")}.`;
  }
  return "The action is not valid.";
}
```

### `.validation`, not `.message`

`ActionValidationError.message` is `"Validation Error: "` followed by the validation response as JSON. It is useful in logs, not in UI. Read `.validation` instead:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `validation.result` | `"VALID" \| "INVALID"` | The overall result. |
| `validation.submissionCriteria` | Array of `{ result, configuredFailureMessage? }` | One entry per submission criterion. `configuredFailureMessage` is the message the action's author wrote. |
| `validation.parameters` | Record of parameter ID to `{ result, required, evaluatedConstraints }` | Per-parameter results. Use it to highlight form fields. |

### Validate before you apply

`validateAction` runs the same validation without applying the action. An invalid result does not throw: it resolves to the validation response, which the hook also stores as `validationResult`. `validateAction` throws only for other failures, and resolves to `undefined` if a newer validation or an `applyAction` call supersedes it.

```tsx
const { validateAction } = useOsdkAction(modifyEmployee);

const result = await validateAction({ employee, primary_office_id: "nyc-1" });
const invalidFields =
  result?.result === "INVALID"
    ? Object.entries(result.parameters)
      .filter(([, p]) => p.result === "INVALID")
      .map(([id]) => id)
    : [];
```

The hook clears `error` when you call `applyAction` or `validateAction` again.

## Related

- [Actions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/actions.md): apply, validate, and batch actions.
- [Troubleshooting](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/troubleshooting.md): fixes for setup, version, and auth errors.

# The Ontology and your SDK

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/concepts/ontology

> How object types, links, actions, functions, interfaces, and object sets map to the generated SDK and to Osdk.Instance values in TypeScript.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Ontology](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/ontology/overview)
- [Object types](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/object-link-types/object-types-overview)

Your generated SDK is a typed description of part of a Foundry Ontology. This page explains what each Ontology concept becomes in TypeScript, so you can read the SDK and the values it returns.

## Ontology concepts

| Concept | What it is | In the generated SDK | How you use it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Object type | A schema for real-world entities, such as employees. | A definition, `Employee`, plus the namespace types `Employee.Props` and `Employee.OsdkInstance`. | `client(Employee)` returns an object set of every `Employee`. |
| Property | A typed field on an object type. | A key in `Employee.Props`, typed from the property's base type. | Read it on an instance: `employee.fullName`. |
| Primary key | The property that uniquely identifies an object. | `primaryKeyApiName` and `primaryKeyType` on the definition. | `client(Employee).fetchOne(12345)`, or `employee.$primaryKey`. |
| Link type | A relationship between two object types. | Entries in `Employee.Links`. | `employee.$link.lead` for a single link, `employee.$link.reports` for many. |
| Action type | A transaction that edits objects. | A definition, `modifyEmployee`. | `client(modifyEmployee).applyAction({ ... })`. |
| Function (query) | Server-side logic that reads the Ontology and returns a value. | A definition, such as `getEmployeeMetrics`. | `client(getEmployeeMetrics).executeFunction({ ... })`. |
| Interface | A shared shape that several object types implement. | A definition with its own properties. | `client(MyInterface).fetchPage()`, then `instance.$as(Employee)`. |
| Object set | A lazy, composable query over objects. | `Employee.ObjectSet`. | `client(Employee).where({ ... }).pivotTo("lead")`. |

The generated package does not contain a client. It exports definitions, which are plain metadata. You pass a definition to a client created with `createClient` from `@osdk/client`, and the client does the work:

```ts title="src/example.ts"
import { Employee, getEmployeeMetrics, modifyEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const page = await client(Employee)
  .where({ department: "Engineering" })
  .fetchPage({ $pageSize: 20 });

const employee = await client(Employee).fetchOne(12345);

await client(modifyEmployee).applyAction({
  employee,
  primary_office_id: "nyc-1",
});

const metrics = await client(getEmployeeMetrics).executeFunction({
  departmentId: "engineering",
});
```

See [Create a client](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/client.md) to set up `client`.

## Why `client(Employee)`

The SDK separates the code that knows your Ontology (the generated package) from the code that talks to Foundry (`@osdk/client`). That design has practical effects:

- **Smaller bundles.** Each definition is a small named export. Bundlers drop the ones you do not import, so the SDK's cost scales with what you use, not with the size of the Ontology.
- **One runtime.** Several generated SDKs share the same `@osdk/client` code instead of each shipping its own.
- **Fixes without regenerating.** A bug fix in `@osdk/client` reaches you through a dependency update. You do not need to regenerate the SDK.

If you want autocomplete across the whole Ontology, import the namespace exports. Tree-shaking still removes what you do not reference:

```ts
import { $Objects } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const page = await client($Objects.Employee).fetchPage();
```

The generated package also exports `$Actions`, `$Queries`, and `$Interfaces`, and `$ontologyRid` when the SDK was generated for a single Foundry environment.

## Object instances

Every object you fetch, from `@osdk/client` or from `@osdk/react` hooks, is an `Osdk.Instance`. The generated alias `Employee.OsdkInstance` is the same type:

```ts
import type { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import type { Osdk } from "@osdk/client";

type A = Employee.OsdkInstance;
type B = Osdk.Instance<Employee>;
```

### Metadata fields

Fields that start with `$` describe the object rather than hold Ontology data:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$apiName` | `string` | API name of the type you queried. For an interface query, this is the interface's API name. |
| `$objectType` | `string` | API name of the concrete object type, even when you queried an interface. |
| `$primaryKey` | Primary key type | The object's primary key value. Use it as a React `key`. |
| `$title` | `string \| undefined` | Value of the object type's title property. |
| `$objectSpecifier` | `ObjectSpecifier` | A string that identifies the object by type and primary key. |
| `$link` | Links object | Accessors for the object's links. |
| `$as` | Function | Converts between an interface and an object type that implements it. |
| `$clone` | Function | Returns a copy of the instance with updated properties. |
| `$rid` | `string` | The object's RID. Present only when you request it with `$includeRid: true`. |

### Instances are immutable

Instances are frozen, and their properties are `readonly`. To get a changed copy, call `$clone`:

```ts
const renamed = employee.$clone({ fullName: "Ada Lovelace" });
```

`$clone` throws if the update changes the primary key. It does not write anything to Foundry. Use it to build optimistic state for an action, as shown in [Optimistic updates](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/optimistic-updates.md). To change data, apply an action.

### Links

A single-valued link returns an accessor with `fetchOne`. A many-valued link returns an object set:

```ts
const lead = await employee.$link.lead.fetchOne();
const reports = await employee.$link.reports.fetchPage({ $pageSize: 50 });
```

In React, use [`useLinks`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/links.md) instead so linked objects share the cache.

## Property value types

Most properties are optional on the instance (`T | undefined`). Only the primary key and properties the Ontology marks as required are always present.

| Ontology type | TypeScript value | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `string` | |
| `boolean` | `boolean` | |
| `integer`, `short`, `byte`, `float`, `double` | `number` | |
| `long` | `string` | Strings keep 64-bit precision that `number` cannot hold. |
| `decimal` | `string` | Strings keep arbitrary precision. |
| `date` | `string` | ISO 8601 date, such as `"2024-03-15"`. |
| `timestamp` | `string` | ISO 8601 date and time, such as `"2024-03-15T09:30:00Z"`. |
| `geopoint` | `GeoJSON.Point` | |
| `geoshape` | `GeoJSON.GeoJSON` | |
| `attachment` | `Attachment` | Has `rid`, `fetchMetadata()`, and `fetchContents()`, which resolves to a `Response`. |
| `mediaReference` | `Media` | Has `fetchMetadata()`, `fetchContents()`, and `getMediaReference()`. |
| `cipherText` | `CipherText` | Call `decrypt()` to get the plaintext. |
| `marking` | `string` | |
| `vector` | `number[]` | |
| Numeric, string, and sensor time series | `TimeSeriesProperty` | Has `getFirstPoint()`, `getLastPoint()`, and `getAllPoints()`. |
| `geotimeSeriesReference` | `GeotimeSeriesProperty` | |

### Dates and timestamps

The SDK returns dates and timestamps as ISO 8601 strings instead of `Date` objects or a date library's types. This keeps a large date library out of your bundle, lets you use the date library you already have, and avoids parsing values you never read.

Parse a value when you need date math:

```ts
const startDate =
  employee.startDate != null ? new Date(employee.startDate) : undefined;
```

To send a date-only value, `@osdk/client` exports helpers that format a `Date` as `YYYY-MM-DD`:

```ts
import { extractDateInLocalTime, extractDateInUTC } from "@osdk/client";

extractDateInLocalTime(new Date()); // "2024-03-15" in the user's time zone
extractDateInUTC(new Date()); // "2024-03-15" in UTC
```

`extractDate` returns the date part of an ISO 8601 timestamp string.

## Object sets

An object set describes which objects you want. Building one does not send a request; only fetching does:

```ts
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const engineers = client(Employee).where({ department: "Engineering" });
const theirLeads = engineers.pivotTo("lead");

const page = await theirLeads.fetchPage({ $pageSize: 20 });
```

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `where(clause)` | Object set | Filters the set. |
| `union(...sets)`, `intersect(...sets)`, `subtract(...sets)` | Object set | Combines sets of the same type. |
| `pivotTo(link)` | Object set | Follows a link to the linked type. |
| `withProperties(...)` | Object set | Adds derived properties computed on the server. |
| `fetchPage(options)` | `Promise` of a page | Fetches one page: `data`, `nextPageToken`, and `totalCount`. |
| `fetchOne(primaryKey)` | `Promise` of an instance | Fetches one object. Object types only. |
| `asyncIter()` | Async iterator | Iterates over every object across pages. |
| `aggregate(options)` | `Promise` of results | Runs an aggregation on the server. |
| `subscribe(listener)` | Subscription | Receives changes to the set over a WebSocket. |

In React, pass the same filters to [`useOsdkObjects`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/objects.md) or build a set with [`useObjectSet`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/object-sets.md).

## Interfaces

An interface lets you query several object types through one shape. Instances from an interface query expose the interface's properties. `$objectType` tells you the concrete type, and `$as` converts to it:

```ts
import { Employee, Worker } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const { data } = await client(Worker).fetchPage();

for (const worker of data) {
  if (worker.$objectType === "Employee") {
    const employee = worker.$as(Employee);
    console.log(employee.fullName);
  }
}
```

## Related

- [Caching and reactivity](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/concepts/caching.md): how `@osdk/react` stores these instances.
- [Objects](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/objects.md): query objects in React.
- [Actions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/actions.md): edit objects.

# Develop on Foundry branches

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/deploy/branches

> Point your OSDK app at a Foundry global branch with osdk branch sync, @osdk/vite-plugin-branch, and the beta UNSTABLE_DO_NOT_USE_BRANCH client option.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Global Branching](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/global-branching/overview)
- [Branching applications](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/developer-console/branching-integration)

{/* cspell:ignore postinstall */}

Develop against Ontology changes on a Foundry global branch before they merge, using the SDK versions generated for that branch and sending every request to it. Three pieces work together: `osdk branch sync` installs the branch's SDK, `@osdk/vite-plugin-branch` tells the client which branch you are on, and the client sends that branch with its requests.

> [!WARNING]
> Branch support is beta. The client option is named `UNSTABLE_DO_NOT_USE_BRANCH`, and `@osdk/create-app` only sets it up behind `--unstableFeatures`. Names and behavior can change in any release.

## How it works

| Piece | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Branched SDK versions | An SDK generated on a branch is published as a prerelease under the npm dist tag `<branch>-latest`. Its `package.json` records the branch RID in `osdk.branch`, and the SDK exports it as `$branch`. |
| `osdk branch sync` | Reads your git branch and installs the matching SDK version: the branch's prerelease on a branch, the stable `latest` on `main`. |
| `@osdk/vite-plugin-branch` | Injects the current branch into your app's HTML, and reloads the page when you switch git branches. |
| `@osdk/client` | Reads the injected branch when you create the client, then reads and writes objects, actions, and queries on that branch. |

Both the CLI and the plugin take the branch from `git branch --show-current`, so use the same name for your git branch and the Foundry branch you develop against.

## Set up a new app

Pass `--unstableFeatures` to `@osdk/create-app`:

```npm
npx @osdk/create-app@latest my-osdk-app --unstableFeatures
```

For an app with an SDK, this adds three things to the generated project:

- `@osdk/cli` as a dev dependency.
- A `postinstall` script that runs `osdk branch sync`, so every install picks the SDK for your branch.
- `@osdk/vite-plugin-branch`, registered in `vite.config.ts`, for the Vite templates.

## Add to an existing app

### Install the packages

Install `@osdk/vite-plugin-branch` at the same version as `@osdk/client`. It supports Vite 6, 7, and 8.

```npm
npm install @osdk/vite-plugin-branch
npm install --save-dev @osdk/cli
```
### Sync the SDK on install

```json title="package.json"
{
  "scripts": {
    "postinstall": "osdk branch sync"
  }
}
```
### Register the Vite plugin

```ts title="vite.config.ts"
import { branchPlugin } from "@osdk/vite-plugin-branch";
import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react";
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig(({ mode }) => ({
  plugins: [react(), branchPlugin()],
  define: {
    "process.env.NODE_ENV": JSON.stringify(mode),
  },
}));
```

`branchPlugin()` takes no options.

## Install the branch's SDK

```sh
npx osdk branch sync
```

For each dependency in your root `package.json` whose installed `package.json` has an `osdk` block, the command reads the package's npm dist tags and picks a target:

| You are on | Installed SDK | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A branch | Any | The `<branch>-latest` dist tag, if one is published. Otherwise the SDK is left alone. |
| `main`, `master`, or a detached `HEAD` | Generated on a branch | The `latest` dist tag. |
| `main`, `master`, or a detached `HEAD` | Generated on main | Left alone. |

It installs every SDK whose declared version differs from its target in one `npm install <pkg>@<version> --save-exact`, so your `package.json` pins exact versions. It always runs `npm`, and only looks at `dependencies`, not `devDependencies`.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--branchName <name>` | Sync to this branch instead of the current git branch. |
| `--packageName <name>` | Sync only this SDK. |
| `--dryRun` | Print `Would install <pkg>@<version>` lines without installing. |

The command reads dist tags from your registry, so it needs the same `.npmrc` and `FOUNDRY_TOKEN` as a normal install. A `401` from the registry fails with `Not authorized to read <pkg>`. See [Installation](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/installation.md).

## Inject the branch with Vite

`branchPlugin()` adds a meta tag to the `<head>` of your HTML:

```html
<meta name="osdk-foundry-branch-rid" content="my-feature" />
```

It decides the value in this order:

| Condition | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `FOUNDRY_BRANCH_RID` is set in the environment or a `.env` file | That value. |
| The git branch is `main` or `master` | Empty, which means the default branch. |
| Any other git branch | The branch name. |
| No branch: detached `HEAD`, or not a git repository, during `vite dev` | `ri.branch..branch.unknown`. Requests fail instead of silently reading the default branch. |
| No branch during `vite build` | Empty, which means the default branch. |

`FOUNDRY_BRANCH_RID` has no `VITE_` prefix, so Vite does not expose it to your client code. Use it to pin a branch RID, or to build for a branch in CI where HEAD is detached:

```sh
FOUNDRY_BRANCH_RID=ri.branch..branch.<id> npm run build
```

The dev server logs the branch it uses, such as `Using Foundry branch "my-feature".` While it runs, it checks the git branch every second and reloads open pages when it changes, so you do not restart the server. Reloading needs HMR, which is on by default.

A production build fixes the branch at build time. Rebuild to deploy for another branch.

## Choose the branch in the client

`createClient` resolves the branch once, when you create the client:

1. The `UNSTABLE_DO_NOT_USE_BRANCH` option, when you pass it. `null` forces the default branch.
2. The `foundryBranchRid` query parameter in the page URL, such as `?foundryBranchRid=ri.branch..branch.<id>`. This lets a page that embeds your app in an iframe choose the branch.
3. The `osdk-foundry-branch-rid` meta tag from the Vite plugin.

Blank values count as unset. Outside a browser, only the option applies.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `UNSTABLE_DO_NOT_USE_BRANCH` | `string \| null` | `undefined` | Beta. The branch for every request. `undefined` reads the query parameter, then the meta tag. `null` ignores both and uses the default branch. |

To pin a client to the branch your SDK was generated on, pass the SDK's `$branch` export. It is `undefined` for SDKs generated on main, which keeps the default lookup:

```ts title="src/client.ts"
import { $branch, $ontologyRid } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { createClient } from "@osdk/client";
import { createPublicOauthClient } from "@osdk/oauth";

const foundryUrl = "https://example.palantirfoundry.com";

const auth = createPublicOauthClient(
  "<your-client-id>",
  foundryUrl,
  "http://localhost:8080/auth/callback",
);

export const client = createClient(foundryUrl, $ontologyRid, auth, {
  UNSTABLE_DO_NOT_USE_BRANCH: $branch,
});
```

In Node.js scripts there is no meta tag, so pass the branch explicitly:

```ts title="scripts/client.ts"
import { $ontologyRid } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { createClient } from "@osdk/client";

const token = process.env.FOUNDRY_TOKEN;
if (token == null) {
  throw new Error("Set FOUNDRY_TOKEN");
}

export const client = createClient(
  "https://example.palantirfoundry.com",
  $ontologyRid,
  () => Promise.resolve(token),
  { UNSTABLE_DO_NOT_USE_BRANCH: process.env.FOUNDRY_BRANCH_RID ?? null },
);
```

## Generate an SDK on a branch

To generate SDK files locally from a branch's Ontology, pass the branch RID to `osdk unstable typescript generate --branch`. See [Generate an SDK](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/deploy/generate-sdk.md#generate-locally).

# CLI reference

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/deploy/cli

> Every @osdk/cli command and flag for deploying sites and widget sets, managing versions, syncing branched SDKs, and generating SDKs locally.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Application hosting](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/developer-console/deploy-custom-application-on-foundry)

{/* cspell:ignore widgetset */}

`@osdk/cli` deploys your app to Foundry website hosting, manages its versions, publishes widget sets, keeps branched SDKs in sync, and generates SDKs from an Ontology. This page lists every command and flag.

## Run the CLI

Run it with `npx`, or install it as a dev dependency to get the `osdk` binary:

```sh
npx @osdk/cli@latest site deploy
```

```npm
npm install --save-dev @osdk/cli
```

```sh
npx osdk site deploy
```

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`osdk site deploy`](#osdk-site-deploy) | Upload a new version of your site and, by default, make it live. |
| [`osdk site version`](#osdk-site-version) | List, get, set, unset, and delete site versions. |
| [`osdk widgetset deploy`](#osdk-widgetset-deploy) | Publish a new widget set version. |
| [`osdk widgetset version`](#osdk-widgetset-version) | List, inspect, and delete widget set versions. |
| [`osdk branch sync`](#osdk-branch-sync) | Install the SDK versions published for your current branch. |
| [`osdk unstable typescript generate`](#osdk-unstable-typescript-generate) | Generate SDK source files from an Ontology. Unstable. |
| [`osdk unstable auth login`](#osdk-unstable-auth-login) | Test an OAuth sign-in from the terminal. Unstable. |

`osdk experimental` is an alias for `osdk unstable`. Commands under it can change or be removed in any release.

## Global options

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--verbose`, `-v` | count | Debug logging. Pass `-vv` for trace logging, which includes every HTTP request. |
| `--help` | boolean | Print the commands and options available at that level, such as `osdk site version --help`. |

Each option also accepts its kebab-case form: `--foundryUrl` and `--foundry-url` are the same option.

## Configuration

Options come from three places. The first one set wins:

1. The command-line flag.
2. An environment variable named `OSDK_` plus the option in upper snake case, such as `OSDK_FOUNDRY_URL`, `OSDK_APPLICATION`, or `OSDK_DIRECTORY`.
3. `foundry.config.json`, for the options it covers.

The CLI looks for `foundry.config.json` in the current directory and then each parent, and uses the first one it finds. A file holds either a `site` block or a `widgetSet` block, not both. The full schema is in [Host on Foundry](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/deploy/hosting.md#foundryconfigjson).

### Tokens

Every `site` and `widgetset` command needs a Foundry token. The CLI uses the first of:

1. `--token <token>`
2. `--tokenFile <path>`, a file whose contents are the token
3. The `FOUNDRY_TOKEN` environment variable
4. The `FOUNDRY_SDK_AUTH_TOKEN` environment variable, which is deprecated and logs a warning

`--token` and `--tokenFile` cannot be used together. The token must be a JWT. Without one, the command exits with `No token found.`

```sh
export FOUNDRY_TOKEN=<token>
npx @osdk/cli@latest site version list
```

## `osdk site`

Manages the website hosted for a Developer Console application. Run it with a subcommand: `deploy` or `version`.

These options apply to every `site` subcommand:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--application` | `string` | `site.application` | The application RID, such as `ri.third-party-applications.main.application.<id>`. Required. |
| `--foundryUrl` | `string` | `foundryUrl` | The Foundry stack URL. Must start with `https://`. Required. |
| `--token` | `string` | | A Foundry token. Conflicts with `--tokenFile`. |
| `--tokenFile` | `string` | | A path to a file containing a Foundry token. Conflicts with `--token`. |

### `osdk site deploy`

Zips the contents of a directory, uploads it as a new site version, and makes that version live.

```sh
npx @osdk/cli@latest site deploy --directory ./dist --version 1.2.0
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--directory` | `string` | `site.directory` | The directory to upload, usually your build output. Required. Everything in it is zipped, with the directory itself as the root. |
| `--version` | `string` | | The version to create. Must be valid SemVer. Conflicts with `--autoVersion`; when `site.autoVersion` is set in the config file, `--version` overrides it. |
| `--autoVersion` | `"git-describe" \| "package-json"` | `site.autoVersion.type` | Compute the version instead of passing `--version`. See [Automatic versions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/deploy/hosting.md#automatic-versions). |
| `--gitTagPrefix` | `string` | `site.autoVersion.tagPrefix` | With `git-describe`, match only tags that start with this prefix, and strip it from the version. Without it, every tag matches and a leading `v` is stripped. Only valid with `git-describe`. |
| `--uploadOnly` | `boolean` | `site.uploadOnly`, else `false` | Upload the version without making it live. The CLI prints a preview link instead. |
| `--snapshot` | `boolean` | `false` | Upload a snapshot version with automatic retention. The CLI never makes a snapshot live. Cannot be combined with `--uploadOnly`. |
| `--snapshotId` | `string` | | An alias to attach to the snapshot version. Requires `--snapshot`. |

You must pass `--version` or `--autoVersion`, or set `site.autoVersion` in `foundry.config.json`. When the deploy succeeds, the CLI prints the live URL, `https://<subdomain>`. With `--uploadOnly`, it prints `https://<subdomain>/.system/preview?previewVersion=<version>` instead.

### `osdk site version`

Manages existing versions. Run it with a subcommand.

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `osdk site version list` | Lists every version that is valid SemVer, newest first, and marks the live one `(deployed)`. |
| `osdk site version get` | Prints the live version, or `No live site version set`. |
| `osdk site version set <version>` | Makes `<version>` live. Use it to roll back or to publish a version uploaded with `--uploadOnly`. |
| `osdk site version unset` | Clears the live version after a confirmation prompt. The site is unreachable until you set a version again. |
| `osdk site version delete <version>` | Deletes a version after a confirmation prompt. You cannot delete the live version, and deletion cannot be undone. |

| Option | Applies to | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--yes`, `-y` | `unset`, `delete` | `boolean` | Skip the confirmation prompt. |

```sh
npx @osdk/cli@latest site version set 1.1.0
npx @osdk/cli@latest site version delete 1.0.0 --yes
```

### Site errors

The CLI turns Foundry errors into these messages:

| Message | Cause | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `The site version already exists` | A version with that number was uploaded before. | Use a new version. Versions are immutable. |
| `The site version is invalid and must be a valid SemVer string` | The version is not SemVer. | Fix `--version`, or the tag or `package.json` version that `--autoVersion` reads. |
| `The site contains too many versions` | The application reached its version limit, shown in the message. | Delete old versions with `osdk site version delete`. |
| `The .zip file contains too many files` | The build output has more files than the limit. | Reduce the number of files in the build. |
| `The .zip file contains a file ... that is too large` | One file exceeds the size limit. | Shrink or split that file. |
| `The website version is being scanned for vulnerabilities and cannot be deployed yet` | Foundry is still scanning the upload. | Deploy with `--uploadOnly`, then make the version live after the scan, with `osdk site version set` or from **Website hosting** in Developer Console. |
| `The site version to delete is live and cannot be deleted` | You tried to delete the live version. | Set another version live first. |
| `The site version could not be found` | The version does not exist. | Check `osdk site version list`. |

A `401` means the token is invalid or expired; a `403` means it lacks the permission or scopes for the request.

## `osdk widgetset`

Publishes and manages widget sets for Workshop custom widgets. Run it with a subcommand: `deploy` or `version`. [Publish a widget set](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/widgets/publish.md) covers the build and the manifest.

These options apply to every `widgetset` subcommand:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--widgetSet` | `string` | `widgetSet.rid` | The widget set RID. Required. |
| `--foundryUrl` | `string` | `foundryUrl` | The Foundry stack URL. Must start with `https://`. Required. |
| `--token` | `string` | | A Foundry token. Conflicts with `--tokenFile`. |
| `--tokenFile` | `string` | | A path to a file containing a Foundry token. Conflicts with `--token`. |

### `osdk widgetset deploy`

Zips a directory and publishes it as a new widget set version. The version comes from the manifest at `.palantir/widgets.config.json` inside the directory; there is no version flag.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--directory` | `string` | `widgetSet.directory` | The directory to upload. Required. |
| `--repository` | `string` | `widgetSet.repository` | A code repository RID to publish through. The repository must be authorized to publish the widget set. |
| `--branchName` | `string` | The current git branch | The git branch to publish from. |

### `osdk widgetset version`

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `osdk widgetset version list` | Lists published versions for the current git branch. Accepts `--branchName`. |
| `osdk widgetset version info <version>` | Prints the details of one version. |
| `osdk widgetset version delete <version>` | Deletes a version after a confirmation prompt. `--yes` or `-y` skips the prompt. |

## `osdk branch sync`

Installs the version of each generated SDK that matches your current branch: the newest prerelease published for that branch, or the stable `latest` release when you are on `main`. [Develop on Foundry branches](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/deploy/branches.md) explains the workflow.

```sh
npx @osdk/cli@latest branch sync
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--branchName` | `string` | The current git branch | The branch to sync to. `main`, `master`, and a detached `HEAD` mean the default branch. |
| `--packageName` | `string` | | Sync only this SDK instead of every SDK found. |
| `--dryRun` | `boolean` | `false` | Print what would be installed without changing anything. |

`osdk unstable branch sync` is the same command under its earlier name.

## `osdk unstable typescript generate`

Generates SDK source files from an Ontology, either by signing in to Foundry or from a saved Ontology metadata file. [Generate an SDK](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/deploy/generate-sdk.md#generate-locally) shows when to use it.

```sh
npx @osdk/cli@latest unstable typescript generate \
  --foundryUrl https://example.palantirfoundry.com \
  --clientId <your-client-id> \
  --outDir src/generatedNoCheck \
  --version dev
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--outDir` | `string` | | Where to write the generated files. Required. |
| `--version` | `string` | | The SDK version: `dev` or a SemVer string. Sent in the request user agent, and used as the package version with `--asPackage`. Required. |
| `--foundryUrl` | `string` | | Load the Ontology from this stack. Requires `--clientId`. Alias: `--stack`. |
| `--clientId` | `string` | | The OAuth client ID to sign in with. Requires `--foundryUrl`. |
| `--ontologyRid` | `string` | | With `--foundryUrl`, use this Ontology. Needed when the client can see more than one. |
| `--branch` | `string` | | With `--foundryUrl`, the Foundry branch RID to load the Ontology from. |
| `--ontologyWritePath` | `string` | | With `--foundryUrl`, also save the loaded Ontology metadata as JSON at this path. |
| `--ontologyPath` | `string` | | Generate from an Ontology metadata JSON file instead of Foundry. Conflicts with `--foundryUrl` and `--clientId`. |
| `--packageType` | `"commonjs" \| "module"` | `"commonjs"` | The module format of the project you generate into. |
| `--clean` | `boolean` | | Delete `--outDir` before generating. |
| `--skipPackageJsonUpdate` | `boolean` | `false` | Do not add `@osdk/api` and `@osdk/client` to the nearest `package.json`. |
