| `--externalObjects` | `string` | | Import these object types from another generated SDK instead of generating them, as `ApiName:@scope/package` pairs separated by commas. |
| `--externalInterfaces` | `string` | | The same, for interfaces. |
| `--experimentalOntologyMetadata` | `boolean` | `false` | Also emit the raw Ontology metadata as an `./experimental/ontology-metadata` export. May change or be removed. |
| `--asPackage` | `boolean` | | Generate a standalone package with its own `package.json`. Requires `--packageName` and `--beta`. |
| `--packageName` | `string` | | The package name when using `--asPackage`. |
| `--beta` | `boolean` | | Required with `--asPackage`. |
| `--internal` | `boolean` | `false` | For the `osdk-ts` repository only. Writes `workspace:` dependency versions. |

Pass either `--ontologyPath`, or `--foundryUrl` and `--clientId`.

## `osdk unstable auth login`

Runs the OAuth authorization code flow in your browser, to check that a client ID and redirect URL work. It does not save or print the token.

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--foundryUrl` | `string` | The Foundry stack URL. Required. Alias: `--baseUrl`. |
| `--clientId` | `string` | The OAuth client ID. Required. Alias: `--applicationId`. |

The CLI listens on port 8080 and uses `http://localhost:8080/auth/callback` as the redirect URL, so that URL must be allowed on **OAuth & scopes** in Developer Console and port 8080 must be free. It requests the `offline_access`, `api:read-data`, and `api:use-ontologies-read` scopes. `osdk unstable typescript generate --foundryUrl` uses the same sign-in.

# Generate an SDK

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/deploy/generate-sdk

> Generate your Ontology SDK in Developer Console or locally with osdk unstable typescript generate or @osdk/foundry-sdk-generator, and update it when the Ontology changes.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Developer Console](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/developer-console/overview)

{/* cspell:ignore postinstall */}

Your generated SDK holds typed definitions for the object types, links, actions, functions, and interfaces your app uses. Generate it in Developer Console and install it from your Foundry npm registry, or generate it yourself from the command line.

## Choose a method

| Method | Output | Use it when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Developer Console | A versioned npm package in your Foundry registry. | Almost always. Apps from `@osdk/create-app` expect it. |
| `osdk unstable typescript generate` | TypeScript source files in a folder of your project. | You want the SDK in your repository, or you work offline from a saved Ontology file. |
| `@osdk/foundry-sdk-generator` | A built npm package directory you can pack or publish. | You publish SDK packages from your own pipeline. |

## Generate in Developer Console

### Choose the resources

In your application in Developer Console, add the object types, link types, actions, functions, and interfaces your app uses to the application's SDK. Only those resources are generated.
### Generate a version

On **SDK versions**, generate a new version with the **npm** package type and the latest generator. The install instructions show the package name, such as `@my-app/sdk`, and your registry URL.
### Install it

Point your SDK's npm scope at the Foundry registry in `.npmrc`, then install:

```npm
npm install @my-app/sdk@latest
```

[Installation](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/installation.md) covers the `.npmrc` lines, the token, and the other packages you need.

### What the package exports

| Export | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Object types, such as `Employee` | Pass to `client(Employee)` to query. |
| Actions, such as `modifyEmployee` | Pass to `client(modifyEmployee).applyAction(...)`. |
| Functions and interfaces | Pass to `client(...)` the same way. |
| `$ontologyRid` | The Ontology RID, for `createClient`. |
| `$branch` | The Foundry branch RID the SDK was generated on, or `undefined` for main. See [Develop on Foundry branches](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/deploy/branches.md). |

## Update the SDK when the Ontology changes

The SDK is a snapshot of the Ontology when you generated it. When you add a resource to the SDK, or a property, parameter, or link you use changes:

1. Generate a new version in Developer Console.
2. Install it:

   ```npm
   npm install @my-app/sdk@latest
   ```

3. Run your type checker. Renamed or removed properties and parameters show up as type errors where your code uses them.

The SDK has a peer dependency on the `@osdk/client` version that generated it. If npm reports a peer conflict, align `@osdk/client`, `@osdk/api`, and `@osdk/react` as described in [Version compatibility](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/installation.md#version-compatibility). On a Foundry branch, `osdk branch sync` picks the branch's SDK version instead of `latest`.

## Generate locally

`osdk unstable typescript generate` from `@osdk/cli` writes the SDK as TypeScript source files into your project. It is unstable: flags and output can change in any release.

**From Foundry**

```sh
npx @osdk/cli@latest unstable typescript generate \
  --foundryUrl https://example.palantirfoundry.com \
  --clientId <your-client-id> \
  --outDir src/generatedNoCheck \
  --version dev \
  --packageType module \
  --ontologyWritePath ontology.json
```

The CLI opens your browser to sign in, with `http://localhost:8080/auth/callback` as the redirect URL, so allow that URL on **OAuth & scopes** and keep port 8080 free. It generates every object type, action, function, and interface the client can see in the Ontology, except functions that return Ontology edits. If the client can see more than one Ontology, pass `--ontologyRid`. Pass `--branch <branch RID>` to read a branch's Ontology.

`--ontologyWritePath` saves the loaded metadata so you can regenerate later without signing in.
**From a saved file**

```sh
npx @osdk/cli@latest unstable typescript generate \
  --ontologyPath ontology.json \
  --outDir src/generatedNoCheck \
  --version dev \
  --packageType module \
  --clean
```

`--ontologyPath` takes an Ontology metadata file written by `--ontologyWritePath`.

Import from the generated folder instead of a package:

```ts title="src/client.ts"
import { createClient } from "@osdk/client";
import { createPublicOauthClient } from "@osdk/oauth";
import { $ontologyRid } from "./generatedNoCheck/index.js";

const foundryUrl = "https://example.palantirfoundry.com";

const auth = createPublicOauthClient(
  "<your-client-id>",
  foundryUrl,
  "http://localhost:8080/auth/callback",
);

export const client = createClient(foundryUrl, $ontologyRid, auth);
```

Unless you pass `--skipPackageJsonUpdate`, the command also edits the nearest `package.json` above `--outDir`: it adds `@osdk/api` and `@osdk/client` as peer dependencies and `@osdk/api` as a dev dependency, and sets any existing `@osdk/api` and `@osdk/client` entries to the versions the CLI was built with. Install `@osdk/client` as a regular dependency of your app yourself.

All flags are in the [CLI reference](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/deploy/cli.md#osdk-unstable-typescript-generate).

## Build a package with `@osdk/foundry-sdk-generator`

`@osdk/foundry-sdk-generator` loads the resources you name from Foundry and writes a compiled npm package with ESM, CommonJS, and bundled type definitions.

```sh
npx @osdk/foundry-sdk-generator generatePackage \
  --authToken "$FOUNDRY_TOKEN" \
  --foundryHostname example.palantirfoundry.com \
  --ontology ri.ontology.main.ontology.<id> \
  --objectTypes Employee Office \
  --linkTypes Employee.lead Employee.reports Employee.office Office.occupants \
  --actionTypes modifyEmployee \
  --interfaceTypes Worker \
  --packageName @my-app/sdk \
  --packageVersion 0.1.0 \
  --outputDir ./out
```

The package is written to `<outputDir>/<packageName>`, here `./out/@my-app/sdk`, with a `peerDependencies` entry for `@osdk/client`. Pack or publish it from there with npm.

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--authToken` | `string` | A Foundry token. Required. |
| `--foundryHostname` | `string` | Your stack, such as `example.palantirfoundry.com`. A full `https://` URL also works. Required. |
| `--ontology` | `string` | The Ontology RID or API name. |
| `--packageName` | `string` | The npm package name. Required. |
| `--packageVersion` | `string` | The package version. Must be SemVer. Required. |
| `--outputDir` | `string` | The directory to write the package under. Required. |
| `--objectTypes` | `string[]` | Object type API names. |
| `--linkTypes` | `string[]` | Links to include, as `ObjectTypeApiName.linkApiName`. |
| `--actionTypes` | `string[]` | Action type API names. |
| `--queryTypes` | `string[]` | Function API names. Add `:<version>` to pin a version, such as `countEmployees:1.2.0`. |
| `--interfaceTypes` | `string[]` | Interface API names. |
| `--agents` | `string[]` | AIP Agents, as `apiName:version`. |
| `--experimentalOntologyMetadata` | `boolean` | Also export the raw metadata at `./experimental/ontology-metadata`. Experimental. |

Each list flag takes space-separated values. The generator includes only what you list: an object type's links are left out unless you pass them in `--linkTypes`, and generation fails if a requested resource is missing.

# Host on Foundry

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/deploy/hosting

> Build your OSDK app with Vite and deploy it to Foundry website hosting with osdk site deploy, foundry.config.json, versions, previews, and rollbacks.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Application hosting](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/developer-console/deploy-custom-application-on-foundry)

Foundry website hosting serves your app's static build from a subdomain of your Foundry stack. You upload each build as a version with `@osdk/cli`, and one version at a time is live. This page covers configuring production, deploying, and managing versions; the [CLI reference](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/deploy/cli.md#osdk-site) lists every flag.

## Before you start

| You need | Where to get it |
| --- | --- |
| An application in Developer Console with website hosting set up | Developer Console. Note the subdomain, such as `https://myapp.example.palantirfoundry.com`. |
| The application RID | The application's Developer Console URL, `/workspace/developer-console/app/<rid>`. |
| A Foundry token | Set it as `FOUNDRY_TOKEN`. The CLI accepts only JWTs. |
| A static build | Any framework works. Apps from `@osdk/create-app` build to `./dist` with Vite. |

## Deploy your app

### Add `foundry.config.json`

Apps from `@osdk/create-app` already have this file. Otherwise, create it in your project root:

```json title="foundry.config.json"
{
  "foundryUrl": "https://example.palantirfoundry.com",
  "site": {
    "application": "ri.third-party-applications.main.application.1c66b352-4e00-40d2-995d-061c9d533ace",
    "directory": "./dist",
    "autoVersion": {
      "type": "git-describe",
      "tagPrefix": ""
    }
  }
}
```

The CLI reads it from the current directory or the nearest parent, so you do not repeat these values on every command. All fields are described in [`foundry.config.json`](#foundryconfigjson).
### Set the production redirect URL

After sign-in, Foundry sends users back to your app's redirect URL, which must point at the hosted subdomain in production. In an app from `@osdk/create-app`, set it in `.env.production`:

```ini title=".env.production"
VITE_FOUNDRY_REDIRECT_URL=https://myapp.example.palantirfoundry.com/auth/callback
VITE_FOUNDRY_API_URL=https://example.palantirfoundry.com
VITE_FOUNDRY_CLIENT_ID=<your-client-id>
```

If you skipped the production URL when you created the app, the redirect line is commented out with a placeholder. Then add the same URL as a redirect URL on **OAuth & scopes** in Developer Console. The two must match exactly. See [Authentication](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/authentication.md#handle-the-redirect-callback).

The React template includes a test that fails while any of these variables is missing or still a placeholder:

```sh
VERIFY_ENV_PRODUCTION=true npm test
```
### Build

```sh
npm run build
```

In the React templates from `@osdk/create-app` this runs `tsc && vite build` (`vue-tsc && vite build` for Vue, `expo export -p web` for Expo). Vite builds in `production` mode, reads `.env.production`, and writes to `./dist`. Your Vite config must define `process.env.NODE_ENV`; see [Use OSDK with Vite](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/guides/vite.md).
### Deploy

```sh
export FOUNDRY_TOKEN=<token>
npx @osdk/cli@latest site deploy
```

The CLI computes the version, zips `./dist`, uploads it, makes it live, and prints the site URL. To set the version yourself, pass `--version 1.2.0`.

## `foundry.config.json`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `foundryUrl` | `string` | Yes | The Foundry stack URL. Must start with `https://`. |
| `site.application` | `string` | Yes | The Developer Console application RID. |
| `site.directory` | `string` | Yes | The directory to upload, relative to where you run the CLI. |
| `site.autoVersion` | `object` | No | How to compute versions. `{ "type": "git-describe", "tagPrefix"?: string }` or `{ "type": "package-json" }`. |
| `site.uploadOnly` | `boolean` | No | Upload new versions without making them live. Defaults to `false`. |

The file must not contain other top-level fields. A `widgetSet` block, used by [widget sets](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/widgets/publish.md), cannot share a file with `site`. Command-line flags and `OSDK_*` environment variables override the file; see [Configuration](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/deploy/cli.md#configuration).

## Automatic versions

Every version must be valid [SemVer](https://semver.org) and unique: Foundry rejects a version that already exists. Pass `--version`, or let the CLI compute it.

| `autoVersion.type` | Version comes from |
| --- | --- |
| `git-describe` | `git describe --tags --first-parent --dirty`, limited to tags starting with `tagPrefix` when it is set. |
| `package-json` | The `version` field of the nearest `package.json`. |

With `git-describe`, the CLI strips `tagPrefix` from the result, or a leading `v` when there is no prefix. The result depends on where you are relative to the newest tag:

| Repository state | Example tag | Version |
| --- | --- | --- |
| On the tagged commit | `v1.2.0` | `1.2.0` |
| Three commits after the tag | `v1.2.0` | `1.2.0-3-g1a2b3c4` |
| Uncommitted changes | `v1.2.0` | `1.2.0-dirty` |
| Tag prefix `my-app@` | `my-app@1.2.0` | `1.2.0` |

The deploy fails if git is missing, the directory is not a git repository, no tag matches, or the result is not SemVer. In CI, check out tags as well as commits, or `git describe` finds no tag.

To use the version in `package.json`, bump it before each deploy:

```json title="foundry.config.json"
{
  "foundryUrl": "https://example.palantirfoundry.com",
  "site": {
    "application": "ri.third-party-applications.main.application.1c66b352-4e00-40d2-995d-061c9d533ace",
    "directory": "./dist",
    "autoVersion": { "type": "package-json" }
  }
}
```

## Preview before going live

Upload a version without making it live with `--uploadOnly`, or set `site.uploadOnly` to `true` to make that the default:

```sh
npx @osdk/cli@latest site deploy --uploadOnly
```

The CLI prints a preview link, `https://<subdomain>/.system/preview?previewVersion=<version>`. When it looks right, make it live:

```sh
npx @osdk/cli@latest site version set 1.3.0
```

Use the same flow when Foundry reports that a version is still being scanned for vulnerabilities: upload with `--uploadOnly`, wait for the scan, then set the version live with the CLI or from **Website hosting** in Developer Console.

## Roll back

To roll back, set an earlier uploaded version live:

```sh
npx @osdk/cli@latest site version list
npx @osdk/cli@latest site version set 1.2.0
```

`list` shows each version, newest first, and marks the live one. `osdk site version get` prints only the live version.

## Clean up old versions

An application has a version limit. When you reach it, deploys fail with `The site contains too many versions`. Delete versions you no longer need:

```sh
npx @osdk/cli@latest site version delete 1.0.0 --yes
```

You cannot delete the live version. To take the site offline, clear the live version with `osdk site version unset`; the site is unreachable until you set one again.

## Host somewhere else

The build is static files, so any web server or CDN can host it. Foundry website hosting sets up cross-origin access to your stack for you; elsewhere you configure it yourself:

| Requirement | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Your stack allows your origin for CORS | The browser calls Foundry APIs directly from your origin. Ask your Foundry administrator to allow it. |
| The redirect URL is on **OAuth & scopes** | Foundry only redirects to listed URLs. Use your origin plus `/auth/callback`, and set the same value in `.env.production`. |
| The server returns your app for `/auth/callback` | Sign-in lands on that path. A server that returns `404` for paths without a file breaks sign-in, so serve `index.html` for unknown paths. |

# Integration testing

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/deploy/integration-testing

> Run OSDK code against a local Ontology server with @osdk/integration-testing, seed it with objects and links, and stub functions in Vitest.

`@osdk/integration-testing` starts a local Ontology server from the Foundry CLI, fills it with seed objects and links, and gives you a real `Client` connected to it. Use it to test code that queries objects, filters, and follows links end to end, without a Foundry stack. To test React components with mocks instead, see [Testing](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/testing.md).

> [!WARNING]
> `@osdk/integration-testing` is a `0.x` package and depends on the experimental `--experimentalOntologyMetadata` generator flag. Its API may change between releases.

## How it works

| Piece | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `createIntegrationServer` | Writes your Ontology metadata to a temporary `.test-run-*` directory and runs `foundry start ontology` from the Foundry CLI. |
| Seed client | Writes objects and links to the local server. Each call replaces the server's data with the seed built so far. |
| Integration client | A `Client` from `@osdk/client` pointed at the local server. Object and interface calls, such as `fetchPage`, `where`, and `pivotTo`, run against the seeded data. |
| Function stubs | The local Ontology cannot run functions, so the integration client sends function calls to an in-memory mock from `@osdk/unit-testing`. Register results with `whenQuery`. |

## Requirements

| Requirement | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Node.js | The package starts a subprocess and reads files, so tests run in Node, not a browser. |
| Foundry CLI | The `foundry` binary, version `0.224.0` or later, on your `PATH`. Pass `foundryCliPath` to use a binary elsewhere. |
| Ontology metadata | The full Ontology metadata your SDK was generated from, as JSON. See [Get the Ontology metadata](#get-the-ontology-metadata). |
| `@osdk/seed-helpers` | A peer dependency, `>=0.25.0 <1.0.0`, that builds seed data. |

## Install

```npm
npm install --save-dev @osdk/integration-testing @osdk/seed-helpers vitest
```

`@osdk/client` and `@osdk/api` are peer dependencies as well; install them as described in [Installation](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/installation.md).

### Foundry CLI

On install, a postinstall script checks for the Foundry CLI:

- If `foundry` is installed and recent enough, it does nothing.
- If it is too old, the install fails and asks you to run `foundry update self`.
- If it is missing, it downloads the installer from your Foundry stack and runs it. If that fails, the install continues with a warning, and creating a client fails until the CLI is installed.

To find your stack and authenticate the download, the script reads, in order:

| Value | Sources |
| --- | --- |
| Foundry host | `FOUNDRY_EXTERNAL_HOST` or `FOUNDRY_HOSTNAME`, then the host of the git remote `origin`. |
| Token | `FOUNDRY_TOKEN` when `FOUNDRY_HOSTNAME`, `FOUNDRY_TOKEN`, and `FOUNDRY_USERNAME` are all set, otherwise the credentials in the git remote URL. Foundry CI and Code Workspaces provide their own token automatically. |

Set the three variables before installing on a machine whose git remote does not point at Foundry:

```sh
export FOUNDRY_HOSTNAME=example.palantirfoundry.com
export FOUNDRY_USERNAME=<your-username>
export FOUNDRY_TOKEN=<token>
npm install
```

## Get the Ontology metadata

`createIntegrationServer` needs the Ontology metadata as an `OntologyFullMetadata` object. The SDK generator writes it when you generate locally with the experimental `--experimentalOntologyMetadata` flag:

```sh
npx @osdk/cli unstable typescript generate \
  --foundryUrl https://example.palantirfoundry.com \
  --clientId <your-client-id> \
  --outDir src/generatedNoCheck \
  --version dev \
  --beta true \
  --packageType module \
  --experimentalOntologyMetadata
```

The metadata lands in `experimental/ontology-metadata.json` inside `--outDir`. An SDK package generated with the flag also exports it as the `./experimental/ontology-metadata` subpath, which the examples below import. For the other generate options, see [Generate your SDK](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/deploy/generate-sdk.md).

## Write a test

This example uses Vitest. One server starts per Vitest worker, and every test resets the seed before it runs.

### Create a fixture

`test.extend` creates the server, seed client, and integration client once per worker and passes them to each test. `stop()` runs in `finally`, so a server that fails to start does not leave its process or `.test-run-*` directory behind.

```ts title="test/fixture.ts"
import metadata from "@my-app/sdk/experimental/ontology-metadata";
import {
  createIntegrationServer,
  type IntegrationClient,
  type IntegrationServer,
  type SeedClient,
} from "@osdk/integration-testing";
import { test as baseTest } from "vitest";

export { metadata };

export interface IntegrationFixtures {
  server: IntegrationServer;
  client: IntegrationClient;
  seed: SeedClient;
}

export const test = baseTest.extend<IntegrationFixtures>({
  server: [
    // eslint-disable-next-line no-empty-pattern
    async ({}, use) => {
      const server = await createIntegrationServer({ metadata });
      try {
        await server.start();
        await use(server);
      } finally {
        await server.stop();
      }
    },
    { scope: "worker" },
  ],
  seed: [async ({ server }, use) => use(await server.getSeedClient()), { scope: "worker" }],
  client: [async ({ server }, use) => use(await server.getClient()), { scope: "worker" }],
});
```
### Build the seed data

`createSeedWithMetadata` from `@osdk/seed-helpers` builds seed data without a server, and returns it with whatever your function returns. `create` returns a reference with the object's properties, `$apiName`, and `$primaryKey`; `link` connects two references by link name.

```ts title="test/seed.ts"
import { Employee, Office } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { createSeedWithMetadata } from "@osdk/seed-helpers";
import { metadata } from "./fixture.js";

export const baseSeed = createSeedWithMetadata(metadata, (seed) => {
  const london = seed.create(Office, { officeId: "lon", name: "London", city: "London" });
  const ada = seed.create(Employee, {
    employeeId: 1,
    fullName: "Ada Lovelace",
    department: "Engineering",
  });
  const grace = seed.create(Employee, {
    employeeId: 2,
    fullName: "Grace Hopper",
    department: "Engineering",
  });
  seed.link(grace, "lead", ada);
  seed.link(ada, "office", london);
  return { london, ada, grace };
});
```

`create` throws when an object of that type with the same primary key already exists, and when the properties do not match the metadata. A non-primary-key property set to `undefined` is allowed, even when the metadata marks it required, and is left empty.
### Test against the local server

Reset the seed before each test so tests do not see each other's writes, and clear function stubs after each one.

```ts title="test/employees.test.ts"
import { countEmployees, Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { afterEach, beforeEach, expect } from "vitest";
import { test, type IntegrationFixtures } from "./fixture.js";
import { baseSeed } from "./seed.js";

beforeEach<IntegrationFixtures>(async ({ seed }) => {
  await seed.set(baseSeed.output);
});

afterEach<IntegrationFixtures>(({ client }) => {
  client.clearStubs();
});

test("lists engineers", async ({ client }) => {
  const page = await client(Employee).where({ department: "Engineering" }).fetchPage();
  expect(page.data.map((employee) => employee.fullName).sort()).toEqual([
    "Ada Lovelace",
    "Grace Hopper",
  ]);
});

test("follows the lead link", async ({ client }) => {
  const leads = await client(Employee)
    .where({ employeeId: baseSeed.context.grace.employeeId })
    .pivotTo("lead")
    .fetchPage();
  expect(leads.data.map((employee) => employee.$primaryKey)).toEqual([
    baseSeed.context.ada.employeeId,
  ]);
});

test("stubs a function", async ({ client }) => {
  client.whenQuery(countEmployees).thenReturn(2);
  await expect(client(countEmployees).executeFunction()).resolves.toBe(2);
});
```

Replace `countEmployees` with a function from your SDK. Pass its parameters as the second argument of `whenQuery` to stub one call: `client.whenQuery(fn, params).thenReturn(result)`. Use `thenThrow(error)` to make the call fail.
### Run the tests

```sh
npx vitest run
```

Starting the Ontology server can take a while on the first run. If the fixture times out, raise Vitest's `hookTimeout` and `testTimeout`. Each server's `.test-run-*` directory is removed when it stops; add `.test-run-*` to `.gitignore` in case a run is killed first.

## Change data inside a test

Each seed client method updates the seed and writes it to the server before it resolves, so a test can set up extra data right before it queries:

```ts title="test/offices.test.ts"
import { Employee, Office } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { expect } from "vitest";
import { test } from "./fixture.js";

test("lists an office's occupants", async ({ client, seed }) => {
  await seed.set();
  const paris = await seed.create(Office, { officeId: "par", name: "Paris", city: "Paris" });
  const alan = await seed.create(Employee, { employeeId: 3, fullName: "Alan Turing" });
  await seed.link(paris, "occupants", [alan]);

  const occupants = await client(Office)
    .where({ officeId: paris.officeId })
    .pivotTo("occupants")
    .fetchPage();
  expect(occupants.data.map((employee) => employee.fullName)).toEqual(["Alan Turing"]);
});
```

## API reference

### `createIntegrationServer(config)`

Returns a `Promise<IntegrationServer>`. Creating the server writes the metadata to disk; `start()` launches the CLI.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `metadata` | `OntologyFullMetadata` | | The Ontology metadata to serve. Required. Interfaces that object types implement but the metadata does not include are dropped, with a warning. |
| `foundryCliPath` | `string` | `foundry` on `PATH` | Path to the Foundry CLI binary. |
| `projectPath` | `string` | The working directory | An existing directory to create the server's `.test-run-*` directory in. Servers that share a `projectPath` stay isolated. |

| `IntegrationServer` member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `start()` | Starts the Ontology service and resolves once it reports ready. |
| `stop()` | Stops the service and deletes the server's `.test-run-*` directory. |
| `getOntologyUrl()` | The local server's URL, or `undefined` before it starts. |
| `getClient()` | Resolves to the `IntegrationClient` for this server. Repeated calls return the same client. |
| `getSeedClient()` | Resolves to the `SeedClient` for this server. Repeated calls return the same seed client. |

`getClient()` and `getSeedClient()` throw `Ontology server is not ready` when called before `start()` resolves.

### `SeedClient`

Every method applies the full seed to the server before it resolves.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `seed(fn)` | Calls `fn` with a `SeedBuilder`, applies the result, and resolves to what `fn` returns. |
| `seed(output)` | Adds a `SeedOutput`, such as `baseSeed.output`, to the seed and applies it. |
| `set(output?)` | Replaces the whole seed with `output` and applies it. With no argument, clears all data. |
| `addAll(output)` | Merges a `SeedOutput` into the current seed. |
| `create(type, props)` | Creates an object and resolves to its reference. Throws if the primary key already exists. |
| `update(ref, props)` | Merges `props` into the object, leaving omitted properties unchanged. A property set to `undefined` is cleared. Creates the object if it does not exist. |
| `delete(ref)` | Removes the object. Does nothing if it does not exist. |
| `link(source, linkName, target)` | Links `source` to one reference, or an array for many-valued links. Re-adding a link does nothing. |
| `unlink(source, linkName, target)` | Removes matching links. Does nothing if none exist. |
| `ref(type, primaryKey)` | Returns the reference for an object already in the seed, or `undefined`. Does not write to the server. |

### `IntegrationClient`

A `Client` from `@osdk/client` with two extra members:

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `whenQuery(query, params?)` | Starts a function stub. Finish it with `.thenReturn(result)` or `.thenThrow(error)`. |
| `clearStubs()` | Removes every function stub. |

### Other exports

| Export | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `createIntegrationClient(config)` | Creates an `IntegrationClient` for a server that is already running, with `baseUrl` and `metadata`, and optionally `caCertPath` for the server's certificate. Without `caCertPath`, the client skips TLS certificate checks. Throws if the Foundry CLI is not installed. |
| `checkFoundryCliVersion()` | Resolves to `{ type: "installed", version }`, `{ type: "version-incompatible", version }`, `{ type: "version-error" }`, or `{ type: "not-found" }`. Use it to skip integration tests on machines without the CLI, for example with `describe.runIf`. |

```ts title="test/employees.test.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { checkFoundryCliVersion } from "@osdk/integration-testing";
import { describe, expect } from "vitest";
import { test } from "./fixture.js";

const foundryCli = await checkFoundryCliVersion();

describe.runIf(foundryCli.type === "installed")("employees", () => {
  test("loads an employee", async ({ client }) => {
    const employee = await client(Employee).fetchOne(1);
    expect(employee.fullName).toBe("Ada Lovelace");
  });
});
```

# FAQ

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/faq

> Short answers about @osdk/react versus React Query, using OSDK without React or on a server, package versions, dates, templates, and changelogs.

Short answers to common questions about the OSDK TypeScript and React SDKs. Each answer links to the page that covers the topic in full.

**How is @osdk/react different from React Query or SWR?**

React Query and SWR cache responses by a key you choose. `@osdk/react` knows the Ontology, so it caches objects themselves:

- Each object is stored once by type and primary key, and every list, link, and detail view that contains it updates together.
- Actions report which objects they added, modified, or deleted, and the cache applies those edits without manual invalidation.
- Optimistic updates roll back automatically if the action fails.
- `streamUpdates: true` keeps lists live over a WebSocket.

Use `@osdk/react` for Foundry data and keep React Query or SWR for other APIs. They work side by side, but do not copy OSDK data into another cache. See [Caching and reactivity](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/concepts/caching.md).

**Can I use OSDK without React?**

Yes. `@osdk/client` has no UI dependency and works in any browser or JavaScript runtime with `fetch`. Create a client with `createClient` and call `client(Employee).fetchPage()`, `client(modifyEmployee).applyAction()`, and so on. See [Use the client without React](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/client.md#use-the-client-without-react).

For the normalized cache outside React, `createObservableClient` from `@osdk/client/observable` is the same engine `OsdkProvider` uses.

**Which packages must share versions?**

`@osdk/api`, `@osdk/client`, and `@osdk/react` are released together with one version number. Install the same version of all three, and keep prereleases together. Your generated SDK has a peer dependency on `@osdk/client`, so generate a new SDK version when you upgrade the client across many versions.

`@osdk/react-components`, `@osdk/react-devtools`, and `@osdk/oauth` have their own version numbers. Upgrade them alongside the three core packages. See [Version compatibility](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/installation.md#version-compatibility).

**Why are dates and timestamps strings?**

Date and timestamp properties are ISO 8601 strings, such as `"2024-03-15"` and `"2024-03-15T09:30:00Z"`. Bundling a date library would add weight to every app, often duplicating a library you already use, and parsing every value costs time even when you never read it. Parse values with `Date` or your date library when you need date math. See [Dates and timestamps](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/concepts/ontology.md#dates-and-timestamps).

**Can I use OSDK on a server or in Node.js?**

Yes, with `@osdk/client` and a confidential OAuth client. `createConfidentialOauthClient` from `@osdk/oauth` uses the client credentials grant, so requests act as the application's service user, not a signed-in person:

```ts title="src/server/client.ts"
import { createClient } from "@osdk/client";
import { createConfidentialOauthClient } from "@osdk/oauth";

const auth = createConfidentialOauthClient(
  process.env.FOUNDRY_CLIENT_ID!,
  process.env.FOUNDRY_CLIENT_SECRET!,
  process.env.FOUNDRY_URL!,
);

export const client = createClient(
  process.env.FOUNDRY_URL!,
  process.env.FOUNDRY_ONTOLOGY_RID!,
  auth,
);
```

Keep the client secret on the server; never ship it to a browser. `@osdk/react` is for browser apps. See [Authenticate a server or service](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/authentication.md#authenticate-a-server-or-service).

**Is there a Vue template?**

Yes. `@osdk/create-app` has React, Vue, and Expo templates, plus a React template for public apps without sign-in. Choose one at the prompt, or pass it directly:

```bash
npx @osdk/create-app@latest my-app --template vue
```

The Vue template uses `@osdk/client` and `@osdk/oauth` directly. `@osdk/react` and its components are React-only.

**Where do I find the Ontology RID and client ID?**

Both come from your application in Developer Console:

| Value | Where to find it |
| --- | --- |
| Client ID | The **OAuth & scopes** page. |
| Ontology RID | The **Ontology SDK** page. Your generated SDK also exports it as `$ontologyRid` when it was generated for a single environment. |
| Redirect URL | Also on **OAuth & scopes**. The value in your app must match one listed there exactly. |

Apps created with `@osdk/create-app` store these in `.env.development` and `.env.production` as `VITE_FOUNDRY_CLIENT_ID`, `VITE_FOUNDRY_ONTOLOGY_RID`, and `VITE_FOUNDRY_REDIRECT_URL`.

**Why do I call client(Employee) instead of client.objects.Employee?**

The generated SDK exports definitions, and the client does the work. Importing definitions by name lets your bundler drop the parts of the Ontology you do not use, and lets several SDKs share one `@osdk/client`. See [Why `client(Employee)`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/concepts/ontology.md#why-clientemployee).

**Where is the changelog?**

Each package has a `CHANGELOG.md` on GitHub and in its npm package:

- [`@osdk/react` changelog](https://github.com/palantir/osdk-ts/blob/main/packages/react/CHANGELOG.md)
- [`@osdk/client` changelog](https://github.com/palantir/osdk-ts/blob/main/packages/client/CHANGELOG.md)
- [`@osdk/react-components` changelog](https://github.com/palantir/osdk-ts/blob/main/packages/react-components/CHANGELOG.md)

Locally, open `node_modules/@osdk/react/CHANGELOG.md` to read the notes for the version you have installed.

# Expo and React Native

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/frameworks/expo

> Build an iOS, Android, and web app on OSDK with the create-app Expo template, sign in with expo-auth-session, and query objects from React Native screens.

{/* cspell:ignore Metro metro PKCE inlines */}

The `expo` template of `@osdk/create-app` gives you an Expo Router app that signs in to Foundry and calls `@osdk/client` on iOS, Android, and the web. Sign-in works differently from the browser templates, so read [Sign in](#sign-in) before you configure redirect URLs.

## Create an Expo app

Run `@osdk/create-app` with the `expo` template:

```npm
npx @osdk/create-app@latest my-expo-app --template expo --corsProxy false
```

The CLI asks for your Foundry URL, application RID, OAuth client ID, and SDK package. [Quickstart](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/quickstart.md#run-the-cli) lists every prompt and its flag. The Expo template supports SDK version 2.x only.

> [!WARNING]
> Answer **No** to the CORS proxy prompt, or pass `--corsProxy false`. The Expo template has no proxy server, but a **Yes** still sets `EXPO_PUBLIC_FOUNDRY_API_URL` to `http://localhost:8080` in `.env.development`, so every request goes to the Expo dev server instead of Foundry.

Then install and start the app:

```sh
cd my-expo-app
export FOUNDRY_TOKEN=<token>
npm install
npm run dev
```

`FOUNDRY_TOKEN` must be able to read your SDK's npm registry; see [Installation](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/installation.md).

| Script | Runs | Use it to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dev`, `start` | `expo start --port 8080` | Start the dev server, then press `i`, `a`, or `w` to open iOS, Android, or web. |
| `ios` | `expo start --ios` | Start and open the iOS simulator. |
| `android` | `expo start --android` | Start and open the Android emulator. |
| `web` | `expo start --web --port 8080` | Start and open the web build. |
| `build` | `expo export -p web` | Export the web build to `dist/` for [hosting](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/deploy/hosting.md). |
| `test` | `vitest run --passWithNoTests` | Run tests. |
| `reset-project` | `node ./scripts/reset-project.js` | Move the starter screens to `app-example/` and start from an empty `app/`. |

## What the template generates

```text
.env.development
.env.production
.npmrc
app.json
foundry.config.json
metro.config.js
package.json
app/
  _layout.tsx
  (tabs)/
    _layout.tsx
    explore.tsx
    index.tsx
    login.tsx
foundry/
  Auth.ts
  client.ts
  osdkConst.ts
```

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.env.development`, `.env.production` | `EXPO_PUBLIC_FOUNDRY_API_URL`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_FOUNDRY_CLIENT_ID`, and `EXPO_PUBLIC_FOUNDRY_ONTOLOGY_RID`. Expo inlines `EXPO_PUBLIC_` variables into the bundle. |
| `foundry/osdkConst.ts` | Reads those variables and throws `Missing environment variable` if one is unset. |
| `foundry/Auth.ts` | Holds the access token in memory and exposes `getValidAuthToken` as the client's token provider. |
| `foundry/client.ts` | Creates `client` with `createClient`. |
| `app/(tabs)/login.tsx` | The **Login** tab, which runs the OAuth flow with `expo-auth-session`. |
| `app/(tabs)/index.tsx` | The **Home** tab. On web it also completes the sign-in popup. |
| `app/(tabs)/explore.tsx` | Lists the object types, actions, and functions in your SDK. |
| `metro.config.js` | Lets Metro resolve the OSDK packages. See [Metro configuration](#metro-configuration). |
| `app.json` | Expo config, including the URL `scheme` used for native sign-in redirects. |

The generated `.env` files also contain `EXPO_PUBLIC_FOUNDRY_REDIRECT_URL`. The Expo template does not read it: the redirect URL comes from `makeRedirectUri`, described below.

## Sign in

The browser templates use `createPublicOauthClient` from `@osdk/oauth`, which signs in by navigating the page to Foundry and back. A native app cannot do that, so the Expo template runs the same authorization code flow with PKCE through `expo-auth-session` instead, which opens Foundry's sign-in page in a system browser session and returns the code to the app.

### Store the token

`foundry/Auth.ts` keeps the token response in a module variable. `getValidAuthToken` is the token provider you pass to `createClient`; it throws until the user has signed in:

```ts title="foundry/Auth.ts"
import { TokenResponse } from "expo-auth-session";

let authToken: TokenResponse | undefined = undefined;

export const setAuthToken = (authTokenResponse: TokenResponse): void => {
  authToken = authTokenResponse;
};

export const getValidAuthToken = async (): Promise<string> => {
  if (authToken != null) {
    return Promise.resolve(authToken.accessToken);
  } else {
    throw new Error("No valid auth token");
  }
};
```

```ts title="foundry/client.ts"
import { createClient, type Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { getValidAuthToken } from "./Auth";
import { FOUNDRY_URL, ONTOLOGY_RID } from "./osdkConst";

export const client: Client = createClient(
  FOUNDRY_URL,
  ONTOLOGY_RID,
  getValidAuthToken,
);
```

The token lives only in memory. The template neither refreshes nor persists it, so the user signs in again when the app restarts or the access token expires.

### Run the authorization flow

The **Login** tab points `useAuthRequest` at Foundry's authorize and token endpoints under `/multipass/api/oauth2`, then exchanges the returned code for a token. This version adds error handling to the generated screen:

```tsx title="app/(tabs)/login.tsx"
import { setAuthToken } from "@/foundry/Auth";
import { CLIENT_ID, FOUNDRY_URL } from "@/foundry/osdkConst";
import {
  exchangeCodeAsync,
  makeRedirectUri,
  useAuthRequest,
} from "expo-auth-session";
import { useRouter } from "expo-router";
import { useCallback, useMemo, useState } from "react";
import { Button, Text, View } from "react-native";

const discovery = {
  authorizationEndpoint: `${FOUNDRY_URL}/multipass/api/oauth2/authorize`,
  tokenEndpoint: `${FOUNDRY_URL}/multipass/api/oauth2/token`,
};

export default function Login() {
  const router = useRouter();
  const [error, setError] = useState<string>();
  const redirectUri = useMemo(() => makeRedirectUri({ path: "" }), []);
  const [request, , promptAsync] = useAuthRequest(
    {
      clientId: CLIENT_ID,
      scopes: [
        "api:read-data",
        "api:write-data",
        "api:use-ontologies-read",
        "api:use-ontologies-write",
      ],
      redirectUri,
      usePKCE: true,
    },
    discovery,
  );

  const onLogin = useCallback(async () => {
    setError(undefined);
    try {
      const result = await promptAsync();
      if (result.type !== "success") {
        return;
      }
      const tokenResponse = await exchangeCodeAsync(
        {
          clientId: CLIENT_ID,
          code: result.params.code,
          redirectUri,
          extraParams: request?.codeVerifier
            ? { code_verifier: request.codeVerifier }
            : undefined,
        },
        discovery,
      );
      setAuthToken(tokenResponse);
      router.navigate("/(tabs)/explore");
    } catch (e) {
      setError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e));
    }
  }, [promptAsync, redirectUri, request?.codeVerifier, router]);

  return (
    <View>
      <Button title="Login" onPress={onLogin} disabled={request == null} />
      {error != null && <Text>{error}</Text>}
    </View>
  );
}
```

Request only the scopes your app needs, and allow each of them for your application on **OAuth & scopes** in Developer Console.

On web, `promptAsync` opens Foundry in a popup. Foundry redirects the popup to your app's root URL, where `app/(tabs)/index.tsx` calls `WebBrowser.maybeCompleteAuthSession()` from `expo-web-browser`. That call hands the result back to the original window and closes the popup. Keep it in whichever screen renders at the redirect path.

### Register redirect URLs

`makeRedirectUri({ path: "" })` returns a different URL on each platform, and each one must be registered exactly on **OAuth & scopes**:

| Where the app runs | Redirect URL |
| --- | --- |
| Web, local development | `http://localhost:8080`, with no `/auth/callback` path |
| Web, hosted on Foundry | Your site's root URL, such as `https://<subdomain>.<your-domain>.palantirfoundry.com` |
| iOS and Android | A URL with the `scheme` from `app.json`. The template's scheme is `my-app`; change it to one unique to your app. |

To see the exact value on a device, render or log `redirectUri` from the **Login** screen and copy it into Developer Console.

## Query objects

Call the client from a screen once the user has signed in. Keep the list on screen while it reloads:

```tsx title="app/(tabs)/employees.tsx"
import { client } from "@/foundry/client";
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import type { Osdk } from "@osdk/client";
import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { Button, FlatList, Text, View } from "react-native";

export default function Employees() {
  const [employees, setEmployees] = useState<Osdk.Instance<Employee>[]>();
  const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(false);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string>();

  const load = useCallback(async () => {
    setIsLoading(true);
    setError(undefined);
    try {
      const page = await client(Employee)
        .where({ department: "Engineering" })
        .fetchPage({ $orderBy: { fullName: "asc" }, $pageSize: 50 });
      setEmployees(page.data);
    } catch (e) {
      setError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e));
    } finally {
      setIsLoading(false);
    }
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    void load();
  }, [load]);

  return (
    <View>
      {error != null && (
        <View>
          <Text>Could not load employees: {error}</Text>
          <Button title="Retry" onPress={() => void load()} />
        </View>
      )}
      {isLoading && employees == null && <Text>Loading employees…</Text>}
      <FlatList
        data={employees}
        keyExtractor={(employee) => String(employee.$primaryKey)}
        renderItem={({ item }) => (
          <Text>
            {item.fullName}, {item.jobTitle}
          </Text>
        )}
      />
    </View>
  );
}
```

A request made before sign-in fails with `No valid auth token`. Send users to the **Login** tab first, as the template does by making it the initial route. The rest of the client API is the same as on the web; see [Use the client without React](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/client.md#use-the-client-without-react).

## Use `@osdk/react` hooks

`@osdk/react` does not touch the DOM, so its hooks work in React Native screens. The template lists `@osdk/react` in `package.json` but does not use it, and pins it to `^0.7.0`, a release line from before `@osdk/react` shared a version number with `@osdk/client`. Install the same version as your `@osdk/client` first, for example:

```npm
npm install @osdk/react@2.83.0
```

[Version compatibility](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/installation.md#version-compatibility) explains the rule. `react-dom`, a peer dependency of `@osdk/react`, is already in the template for the web build. Then wrap the root layout in `OsdkProvider`:

```tsx title="app/_layout.tsx"
import { client } from "@/foundry/client";
import { OsdkProvider } from "@osdk/react";
import { Stack } from "expo-router";

export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <OsdkProvider client={client}>
      <Stack>
        <Stack.Screen name="(tabs)" options={{ headerShown: false }} />
        <Stack.Screen name="+not-found" />
      </Stack>
    </OsdkProvider>
  );
}
```

The generated layout also loads fonts, controls the splash screen, and sets a theme; keep those and add `OsdkProvider` around the `Stack`. Screens can now use the hooks:

```tsx title="app/(tabs)/team.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkObjects } from "@osdk/react";
import { Button, FlatList, Text, View } from "react-native";

export default function Team() {
  const { data, isLoading, error, refetch } = useOsdkObjects(Employee, {
    where: { department: "Engineering" },
  });

  return (
    <View>
      {error && (
        <View>
          <Text>Could not load employees: {error.message}</Text>
          <Button title="Retry" onPress={() => void refetch()} />
        </View>
      )}
      {isLoading && !data && <Text>Loading employees…</Text>}
      <FlatList
        data={data}
        keyExtractor={(employee) => String(employee.$primaryKey)}
        renderItem={({ item }) => <Text>{item.fullName}</Text>}
      />
    </View>
  );
}
```

Hooks fetch as soon as a screen mounts, so mount data screens only after sign-in. Everything else about the hooks is covered under [Query objects](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/objects.md) and [Apply actions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/actions.md). `@osdk/react-components` renders HTML, so it works in the web build only.

## Metro configuration

`metro.config.js` makes three changes to Expo's default Metro config:

- **Enables package exports** (`resolver.unstable_enablePackageExports: true`), because the OSDK packages publish their entry points, such as `@osdk/client/observable`, through the `exports` field.
- **Resolves `@osdk` packages with the `browser`, `require`, and `import` conditions**, so Metro picks their browser builds on every platform.
- **Loads `.env.development` with `dotenv`** and adds `react-native-svg-transformer` for `.svg` imports.

Keep the first two if you replace the file. The template adds no polyfills.

## Deploy the web build

`npm run build` exports the web build to `dist/`, which `foundry.config.json` points at. Register your site's root URL as a redirect URL first, then follow [Hosting](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/deploy/hosting.md). Publishing to the App Store or Google Play uses Expo's own build tooling and is not covered by the template.

# Node.js

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/frameworks/node

> Use @osdk/client in Node.js scripts, servers, and serverless functions, with service-user or token auth, custom fetch, and a bulk-edit example.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Back-end TypeScript apps](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/developer-console/how-to-bootstrapping-server-side-typescript)

`@osdk/client` runs in Node.js without a browser or bundler, so you can query the Ontology and apply actions from scripts, backend services, scheduled jobs, and serverless functions. This page covers what changes outside the browser: authentication, module format, `fetch`, and configuration.

## Requirements

| Requirement | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Node.js | A version with a global `fetch`: Node 18 or later. The client and `@osdk/oauth` use `globalThis.fetch` unless you pass your own. |
| Module format | `@osdk/client`, `@osdk/api`, `@osdk/oauth`, and generated SDKs ship both ESM and CommonJS builds. The samples on this page use top-level `await`, which needs ESM: set `"type": "module"` in `package.json` or use `.mjs` and `.mts` files. |
| TypeScript | Set `"module": "NodeNext"` (or `"moduleResolution": "Bundler"` if you bundle). Older `node` resolution ignores package `exports` and cannot find subpaths such as `@osdk/client/unstable-do-not-use`. With `NodeNext`, relative imports need a `.js` extension, as in `./client.js`. |

Subscriptions work in Node without a polyfill: `@osdk/client` depends on `ws` and uses it for WebSocket connections in Node.

## Install

Install the client, the OAuth helpers, and your generated SDK. The SDK comes from your Foundry npm registry, so set up `.npmrc` first as described in [Installation](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/installation.md).

```npm
npm install @osdk/client @osdk/api @osdk/oauth @my-app/sdk@latest
```

`@osdk/react` is not needed in Node.

## Authenticate

A Node process has no browser to run the sign-in redirect, so `createPublicOauthClient` does not apply. Use one of these instead:

| Token provider | Requests run as | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createConfidentialOauthClient` from `@osdk/oauth` | The service user of a confidential application in Developer Console | Servers, scheduled jobs, CI, and serverless functions. The client fetches a new token when the current one expires. |
| A function that returns a token you already have | Whoever owns the token, such as you with a personal token | One-off scripts and local tools. The token is not refreshed; requests fail with `401` once it expires. |

Both options, and the scopes the confidential client requests, are covered on [Authentication](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/authentication.md).

## Create the client

Read the Foundry URL and credentials from environment variables and create one client at module scope. Other modules import it.

**Service user**

```ts title="src/client.ts"
import { $ontologyRid } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { createClient } from "@osdk/client";
import { createConfidentialOauthClient } from "@osdk/oauth";

const foundryUrl = process.env.FOUNDRY_URL;
const clientId = process.env.FOUNDRY_CLIENT_ID;
const clientSecret = process.env.FOUNDRY_CLIENT_SECRET;

if (foundryUrl == null || clientId == null || clientSecret == null) {
  throw new Error("Set FOUNDRY_URL, FOUNDRY_CLIENT_ID, and FOUNDRY_CLIENT_SECRET");
}

const auth = createConfidentialOauthClient(clientId, clientSecret, foundryUrl);

export const client = createClient(foundryUrl, $ontologyRid, auth);
```
**Existing token**

```ts title="src/client.ts"
import { $ontologyRid } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { createClient } from "@osdk/client";

const foundryUrl = process.env.FOUNDRY_URL;
const token = process.env.FOUNDRY_TOKEN;

if (foundryUrl == null || token == null) {
  throw new Error("Set FOUNDRY_URL and FOUNDRY_TOKEN");
}

export const client = createClient(foundryUrl, $ontologyRid, () => Promise.resolve(token));
```

`createClient` takes the same arguments in Node as in the browser; see [Create a client](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/client.md) for every option. Only an explicit `UNSTABLE_DO_NOT_USE_BRANCH` sets the branch in Node, because there is no page URL or meta tag to read it from.

### Environment variables

The OSDK packages do not read environment variables themselves. These names are a convention used on this page:

| Variable | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| `FOUNDRY_URL` | The base URL of your Foundry stack, such as `https://example.palantirfoundry.com`. |
| `FOUNDRY_CLIENT_ID` | The confidential application's client ID. |
| `FOUNDRY_CLIENT_SECRET` | The confidential application's client secret. |
| `FOUNDRY_TOKEN` | A bearer token, for the existing-token option. |

Keep secrets out of source control. Locally, put them in a `.env` file that git ignores and load it with `node --env-file=.env` (Node 20.6 and later). In production, use your platform's secret store.

## Page through every object and apply an action

This script finds every `Employee` whose department is `Eng` and renames the department to `Engineering` with the `modifyEmployee` action. Pass `--dry-run` to validate each edit without applying it.

```ts title="src/renameDepartment.ts"
import { Employee, modifyEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { ActionValidationError } from "@osdk/client";
import { client } from "./client.js";

const dryRun = process.argv.includes("--dry-run");

const employeeIds: number[] = [];
for await (const employee of client(Employee)
  .where({ department: "Eng" })
  .asyncIter({ $select: ["employeeId"] })) {
  employeeIds.push(employee.$primaryKey);
}
console.log(`Found ${employeeIds.length} employees`);

let failures = 0;
for (const employeeId of employeeIds) {
  const params = { employee: employeeId, department: "Engineering" };
  try {
    if (dryRun) {
      const validation = await client(modifyEmployee).applyAction(params, {
        $validateOnly: true,
      });
      if (validation.result === "INVALID") {
        failures++;
        console.warn(`Employee ${employeeId} would fail validation`, validation);
      }
    } else {
      await client(modifyEmployee).applyAction(params);
    }
  } catch (e) {
    failures++;
    if (e instanceof ActionValidationError) {
      console.error(`Employee ${employeeId} failed validation`, e.validation);
    } else {
      console.error(`Employee ${employeeId} failed`, e);
    }
  }
}

console.log(`${dryRun ? "Validated" : "Updated"} ${employeeIds.length - failures} employees`);
if (failures > 0) {
  process.exitCode = 1;
}
```

Run it with a TypeScript runner such as `tsx`, or compile it with `tsc` first:

```sh
npx tsx src/renameDepartment.ts --dry-run
```

How it works:

- `asyncIter` fetches page after page until every matching object has loaded. It reads from a consistent snapshot, so each object arrives once even when data changes during the loop. Page size is chosen by the client; `asyncIter` has no `$pageSize` option.
- The script collects primary keys first and applies the action afterwards. A long-running loop can outlive the snapshot, and `asyncIter` throws when the snapshot expires, so keep slow work out of the iteration.
- Object parameters such as `employee` accept a primary key or a loaded object.
- `applyAction` throws `ActionValidationError` when validation fails, with details in `error.validation`. Other request failures, such as a missing permission, throw `PalantirApiError` from `@osdk/client`. Catching per object lets the rest of the run continue.
- With `{ $validateOnly: true }`, `applyAction` returns the validation result instead of applying the action. Its `result` is `"VALID"` or `"INVALID"`.

### Apply in batches

`batchApplyAction` applies an array of parameter objects in one request, which is faster than one request per object. It does not support `$validateOnly`. Send the edits in chunks:

```ts title="src/renameDepartmentBatched.ts"
import { modifyEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client.js";

declare const employeeIds: number[];

const chunkSize = 20;
for (let i = 0; i < employeeIds.length; i += chunkSize) {
  const chunk = employeeIds.slice(i, i + chunkSize);
  await client(modifyEmployee).batchApplyAction(
    chunk.map((employeeId) => ({ employee: employeeId, department: "Engineering" })),
  );
  console.log(`Updated ${i + chunk.length} of ${employeeIds.length}`);
}
```

Pass `{ $returnEdits: true }` as the second argument to get the objects each batch added and modified.

## Use a custom `fetch`

Pass a `fetch` implementation as the fifth argument of `createClient`, and as the `fetchFn` argument of `createConfidentialOauthClient` so token requests use it too. A common reason is a stack whose TLS certificate is signed by a private certificate authority. With `undici`:

```npm
npm install undici
```

```ts title="src/client.ts"
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { $ontologyRid } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { createClient } from "@osdk/client";
import { createConfidentialOauthClient } from "@osdk/oauth";
import { Agent, fetch as undiciFetch } from "undici";

const foundryUrl = process.env.FOUNDRY_URL;
const clientId = process.env.FOUNDRY_CLIENT_ID;
const clientSecret = process.env.FOUNDRY_CLIENT_SECRET;
const caCertPath = process.env.FOUNDRY_CA_CERT;

if (foundryUrl == null || clientId == null || clientSecret == null || caCertPath == null) {
  throw new Error("Set FOUNDRY_URL, FOUNDRY_CLIENT_ID, FOUNDRY_CLIENT_SECRET, and FOUNDRY_CA_CERT");
}

const agent = new Agent({ connect: { ca: await readFile(caCertPath) } });
const fetchWithCa = ((input, init) =>
  undiciFetch(input, { ...init, dispatcher: agent })) satisfies typeof undiciFetch as unknown as typeof fetch;

const auth = createConfidentialOauthClient(
  clientId,
  clientSecret,
  foundryUrl,
  undefined,
  fetchWithCa,
);

export const client = createClient(foundryUrl, $ontologyRid, auth, undefined, fetchWithCa);
```

Passing `undefined` for the scopes keeps the default scopes.

## Logging

By default the client prints errors to the console. Pass a `logger` to route its output elsewhere. The `Logger` interface from `@osdk/api` matches [pino](https://getpino.io), so a pino logger works as-is:

```ts title="src/client.ts"
import { $ontologyRid } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { createClient } from "@osdk/client";
import { pino } from "pino";

declare const auth: () => Promise<string>;
declare const foundryUrl: string;

const logger = pino({ level: "info" });

export const client = createClient(foundryUrl, $ontologyRid, auth, { logger });
```

## Servers and serverless functions

- Create the client once at module scope, not per request. The token provider caches its access token in memory, so reusing the client avoids a token request for every call. In serverless functions, warm invocations reuse the module and its client.
- A confidential client acts as one service user for every request. To run a request as the user who called your server, create a client per request with that user's token, and do not share it across users.
- Never ship the client secret to a browser. Keep `createConfidentialOauthClient` in server code only.

# TypeScript library

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/frameworks/typescript-library

> Scaffold a standalone TypeScript package with the create-app typescript-library template, and add OSDK code that apps can share.

{/* cspell:ignore Ultracite ultracite oxlint oxfmt nvmrc */}

The `typescript-library` template of `@osdk/create-app` creates a TypeScript package that builds ESM and type declarations with `tsc`, tests with Vitest, and lints with Ultracite. Use it to start a package of shared code, such as Ontology helpers that several of your OSDK apps import.

> [!NOTE]
> This template is beta and hidden from the CLI's framework list. Select it with `--template typescript-library`. It contains no OSDK code or dependencies; you add those yourself.

## When to use it

| You want to | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Share functions, types, or object-set helpers between several apps | This template |
| Build a browser app | The `react`, `vue`, or `expo` template. See [Quickstart](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/quickstart.md). |
| Run a script, server, or serverless function | A plain Node project. See [Node.js](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/frameworks/node.md). |

## Create the library

Run `@osdk/create-app` with the template, and pass `--skipOsdk` to skip the SDK prompts. `--skipOsdk` only works with an explicit `--sdkVersion 2.x`:

```npm
npx @osdk/create-app@latest my-library --template typescript-library --sdkVersion 2.x --skipOsdk
```

The CLI still asks for a Foundry URL, application RID, and client ID, and writes `.env.development`, `.env.production`, `.npmrc`, and `foundry.config.json` from them. The library does not read the `.env` files or `foundry.config.json`; delete them if you do not need them. Keep `.npmrc` if you will install your SDK from the Foundry registry.

Then install and build:

```sh
cd my-library
npm install
npm run build
```

## Project structure

```text
.nvmrc
AGENTS.md
oxfmt.config.ts
oxlint.config.ts
package.json
tsconfig.json
.claude/
  CLAUDE.md
  settings.json
.vscode/
  extensions.json
src/
  index.ts
  __tests__/
    index.test.ts
```

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `src/index.ts` | The package entry point. Everything it exports is the library's public API. The template exports a sample `greet` function. |
| `src/__tests__/` | Vitest tests. `tsconfig.json` excludes them from the build. |
| `package.json` | An ESM package (`"type": "module"`) whose `exports`, `main`, and `types` point at `dist/`. Only `dist/` is published. |
| `tsconfig.json` | Strict settings that compile `src/` to `dist/` with declaration files, declaration maps, and source maps. Targets ES2022. |
| `oxlint.config.ts`, `oxfmt.config.ts` | The Ultracite presets for oxlint and oxfmt. Lint warns on function expressions and prefers named function declarations. |
| `.nvmrc` | Pins Node.js `v24.14.1`. |
| `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/` | Coding standards for AI agents. `.claude/settings.json` runs `npx ultracite fix` after every file edit Claude Code makes. |
| `.vscode/extensions.json` | Recommends the Oxc extension. |

## Scripts

| Script | Runs | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `build` | `tsc` | Type-checks and emits JavaScript and `.d.ts` files to `dist/`. |
| `clean` | `rm -rf dist` | Deletes the build output. |
| `test` | `vitest run` | Runs the tests once. |
| `test:watch` | `vitest` | Runs the tests in watch mode. |
| `lint` | `ultracite check` | Checks formatting and lint rules. |
| `fix` | `ultracite fix` | Fixes formatting and lint issues. |
| `format` | `oxfmt .` | Formats every file. |

The generated `README.md` mentions `npm run check`. The script is named `lint`.

## Add OSDK code

Install `@osdk/client` and your SDK. Your SDK comes from your Foundry npm registry, so set up `.npmrc` first as described in [Installation](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/installation.md):

```npm
npm install --save-dev @osdk/client @my-app/sdk
```

Also list both in `peerDependencies`, so an app that installs your library provides them. The app and your library then share one `@osdk/client` and one copy of the SDK. Your generated SDK already declares `@osdk/client` as a peer.

Take the `Client` as a parameter instead of creating one in the library. The app keeps a single client with its own authentication, and your functions use it:

```ts title="src/engineers.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import type { Client, Osdk } from "@osdk/client";

export async function listEngineers(
  client: Client,
): Promise<Osdk.Instance<Employee>[]> {
  const engineers: Osdk.Instance<Employee>[] = [];
  for await (const employee of client(Employee)
    .where({ department: "Engineering" })
    .asyncIter()) {
    engineers.push(employee);
  }
  return engineers;
}
```

Export it from the entry point:

```ts title="src/index.ts"
export { listEngineers } from "./engineers.js";
```

`tsc` does not rewrite import paths. Write relative imports with the `.js` extension, as above, so `dist/` also loads in Node.js without a bundler. [Create a client](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/client.md#use-the-client-without-react) lists the client methods you can call.

# Vue

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/frameworks/vue

> Build a Vue app on OSDK with the create-app Vue template, set up sign-in, and query objects and apply actions from components with @osdk/client.

{/* cspell:ignore composable refetches */}

Use `@osdk/client` directly from Vue components: there is no Vue-specific OSDK package. The `vue` template of `@osdk/create-app` gives you a Vite app with sign-in, routing, and a configured client.

## Create a Vue app

Run `@osdk/create-app` with the `vue` template:

```npm
npx @osdk/create-app@latest my-vue-app --template vue
```

The CLI asks for your Foundry URL, application RID, OAuth client ID, and SDK package, the same prompts as the React template. [Quickstart](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/quickstart.md#run-the-cli) lists every prompt and its flag. The template uses SDK version 2.x unless you pass `--sdkVersion 1.x`.

Then install and start the dev server:

```sh
cd my-vue-app
export FOUNDRY_TOKEN=<token>
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open `http://localhost:8080`. `FOUNDRY_TOKEN` must be able to read your SDK's npm registry; see [Installation](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/installation.md).

## What the template generates

```text
.env.development
.env.production
.npmrc
foundry.config.json
index.html
package.json
vite.config.ts
src/
  AuthCallback.vue
  client.ts
  env.test.ts
  Home.vue
  main.ts
  router.ts
  components/
    Header.vue
    NextSteps.vue
    Osdk.vue
```

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.env.development`, `.env.production` | `VITE_FOUNDRY_API_URL`, `VITE_FOUNDRY_CLIENT_ID`, `VITE_FOUNDRY_REDIRECT_URL`, and `VITE_FOUNDRY_ONTOLOGY_RID` for each mode. |
| `index.html` | Copies the env values into `<meta>` tags such as `osdk-foundryUrl` and `osdk-clientId`. |
| `src/client.ts` | Reads the meta tags, creates `auth` with `createPublicOauthClient`, and exports `client` from `createClient`. |
| `src/router.ts` | A `vue-router` router with `/` and the redirect route `/auth/callback`. |
| `src/AuthCallback.vue` | Completes sign-in when Foundry redirects back. |
| `src/env.test.ts` | Fails the test run when `.env.production` is missing a value or still has a `<placeholder>`. It runs only when `VERIFY_ENV_PRODUCTION=true`. |
| `vite.config.ts` | Serves on port `8080`, defines `process.env.NODE_ENV`, and adds the optional CORS proxy. |
| `foundry.config.json` | Settings for deploying to Foundry. See [Hosting](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/deploy/hosting.md). |

The generated `package.json` depends on `@osdk/client`, `@osdk/oauth`, `@osdk/foundry`, your SDK, `vue`, and `vue-router`, and has these scripts:

| Script | Runs |
| --- | --- |
| `dev` | `vite` |
| `build` | `vue-tsc && vite build`, which type-checks `.vue` files, then writes `dist/`. |
| `test` | `vitest run` |
| `preview` | `vite preview` |

`vite.config.ts` aliases `vue` to `vue/dist/vue.esm-bundler`, the build that includes the template compiler, because `src/main.ts` mounts the root component from a template string (`"<router-view />"`). Keep the alias, or change `main.ts` to mount a compiled `.vue` component instead.

## Set up the client and sign-in

`src/client.ts` exports one `auth` and one `client` for the whole app. It reads its configuration from the `<meta>` tags in `index.html`, so you can change values per environment without touching code:

```ts title="src/client.ts"
import { createClient, type Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { createPublicOauthClient, type PublicOauthClient } from "@osdk/oauth";

function getMetaTagContent(tagName: string): string {
  const elements = document.querySelectorAll(`meta[name="${tagName}"]`);
  const element = elements.item(elements.length - 1);
  const value = element ? element.getAttribute("content") : null;
  if (value == null || value === "") {
    throw new Error(`Meta tag ${tagName} not found or empty`);
  }
  return value;
}

const foundryUrl = getMetaTagContent("osdk-foundryUrl");
const clientId = getMetaTagContent("osdk-clientId");
const redirectUrl = getMetaTagContent("osdk-redirectUrl");
const ontologyRid = getMetaTagContent("osdk-ontologyRid");

export const auth: PublicOauthClient = createPublicOauthClient(
  clientId,
  foundryUrl,
  redirectUrl,
);

export const client: Client = createClient(foundryUrl, ontologyRid, auth);
```

The generated file also throws when a tag still holds an unreplaced `%VITE_...%` value, which means the variable is missing from your `.env` file.

The first request starts sign-in. Foundry redirects back to `/auth/callback`, where `AuthCallback.vue` exchanges the code and returns to `/`:

```vue title="src/AuthCallback.vue"
<script setup lang="ts">
import { onMounted, ref } from "vue";
import { useRouter } from "vue-router";
import { auth } from "./client";

const router = useRouter();
const error = ref<string>();

onMounted(() => {
  auth
    .signIn()
    .then(() => router.replace("/"))
    .catch((e: unknown) => {
      error.value = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e);
    });
});
</script>

<template>
  <div>{{ error != null ? error : "Authenticating…" }}</div>
</template>
```

`VITE_FOUNDRY_REDIRECT_URL` must exactly match a redirect URL on **OAuth & scopes** in Developer Console. [Authentication](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/authentication.md) covers scopes, token storage, and sign-out, all of which work the same in Vue.

## Query objects in a component

Call the client from `<script setup>` and keep the result in a `shallowRef`. This component loads the first page of engineers and keeps the list on screen while it reloads:

```vue title="src/components/EmployeeList.vue"
<script setup lang="ts">
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import type { Osdk } from "@osdk/client";
import { onMounted, ref, shallowRef } from "vue";
import { client } from "../client";

const employees = shallowRef<Osdk.Instance<Employee>[]>();
const isLoading = ref(false);
const error = ref<string>();

async function load() {
  isLoading.value = true;
  error.value = undefined;
  try {
    const page = await client(Employee)
      .where({ department: "Engineering" })
      .fetchPage({ $orderBy: { fullName: "asc" }, $pageSize: 50 });
    employees.value = page.data;
  } catch (e) {
    error.value = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e);
  } finally {
    isLoading.value = false;
  }
}

onMounted(load);
</script>

<template>
  <p v-if="error" role="alert">
    Could not load employees: {{ error }}
    <button type="button" @click="load">Retry</button>
  </p>
  <p v-if="isLoading && !employees">Loading employees…</p>
  <ul>
    <li v-for="employee in employees" :key="employee.$primaryKey">
      {{ employee.fullName }}, {{ employee.jobTitle }}
    </li>
  </ul>
</template>
```

Every method on the client, including `fetchOne`, `asyncIter`, `aggregate`, and `$link`, works the same in Vue. See [Use the client without React](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/client.md#use-the-client-without-react) for the full API.

### Refetch when inputs change

Use `watch` with `immediate: true` to load data from reactive inputs, such as a filter bound to a `<select>`. Mark each run as stale in `onCleanup`, so a slow response for an old value cannot overwrite a newer one:

```vue title="src/components/EmployeesByDepartment.vue"
<script setup lang="ts">
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import type { Osdk } from "@osdk/client";
import { ref, shallowRef, watch } from "vue";
import { client } from "../client";

const department = ref("Engineering");
const employees = shallowRef<Osdk.Instance<Employee>[]>();
const error = ref<string>();

watch(
  department,
  async (value, _previous, onCleanup) => {
    let stale = false;
    onCleanup(() => {
      stale = true;
    });
    try {
      const page = await client(Employee).where({ department: value }).fetchPage();
      if (!stale) {
        employees.value = page.data;
        error.value = undefined;
      }
    } catch (e) {
      if (!stale) {
        error.value = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e);
      }
    }
  },
  { immediate: true },
);
</script>

<template>
  <select v-model="department">
    <option>Engineering</option>
    <option>Design</option>
  </select>
  <p v-if="error" role="alert">{{ error }}</p>
  <ul>
    <li v-for="employee in employees" :key="employee.$primaryKey">
      {{ employee.fullName }}
    </li>
  </ul>
</template>
```

## Apply an action

Put the action in its own component. Await `applyAction` inside `try`/`catch`, and emit an event on success so the parent reloads; the client does not update objects you already fetched:

```vue title="src/components/PromoteButton.vue"
<script setup lang="ts">
import { Employee, modifyEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import type { Osdk } from "@osdk/client";
import { ref } from "vue";
import { client } from "../client";

const props = defineProps<{ employee: Osdk.Instance<Employee> }>();
const emit = defineEmits<{ promoted: [] }>();
const isPending = ref(false);
const error = ref<string>();

async function promote() {
  isPending.value = true;
  error.value = undefined;
  try {
    await client(modifyEmployee).applyAction({
      employee: props.employee,
      jobTitle: "Senior Engineer",
    });
    emit("promoted");
  } catch (e) {
    error.value = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e);
  } finally {
    isPending.value = false;
  }
}
</script>

<template>
  <button type="button" :disabled="isPending" @click="promote">Promote</button>
  <span v-if="error" role="alert">{{ error }}</span>
</template>
```

In `EmployeeList.vue`, render `<PromoteButton :employee="employee" @promoted="load" />` inside each `<li>`. Validation failures throw `ActionValidationError`; [Apply an action](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/client.md#apply-an-action) shows how to read them.

## Reactivity tips

- **Store results in `shallowRef`.** OSDK objects are frozen. Vue does not wrap frozen objects in reactive proxies, so changes are never detected inside them anyway. Replace the whole value when new data arrives.
- **Never mutate an object to update the UI.** Assigning to `employee.jobTitle` throws in strict mode. Apply an action, then fetch again.
- **Key lists by `$primaryKey`.** It is unique within an object type and stable across fetches.
- **Create the client once.** Import `client` from `src/client.ts` in every component. Do not call `createClient` inside `setup`.
- **Do not reach for `@osdk/react`.** Its hooks need React. For a shared cache in Vue, use the observable client below.

### Keep lists live with the observable client

`createObservableClient` from `@osdk/client/observable` is the cache that powers `@osdk/react`. It deduplicates requests, shares objects between subscribers, and refetches affected lists after an action you apply through it. Wrap it in a composable:

```ts title="src/useEmployees.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import {
  createObservableClient,
  type ObserveObjectsCallbackArgs,
} from "@osdk/client/observable";
import { ref, shallowRef, watchEffect } from "vue";
import { client } from "./client";

export const observableClient = createObservableClient(client);

type EmployeeList = ObserveObjectsCallbackArgs<Employee>;

export function useEmployees(department: () => string) {
  const employees = shallowRef<EmployeeList["resolvedList"]>();
  const status = ref<EmployeeList["status"]>("init");
  const error = shallowRef<unknown>();
  const hasMore = ref(false);
  let fetchMore: EmployeeList["fetchMore"] = () => Promise.resolve();

  watchEffect((onCleanup) => {
    const subscription = observableClient.observeList<Employee>(
      { type: Employee, where: { department: department() }, pageSize: 50 },
      {
        next: (payload) => {
          employees.value = payload.resolvedList;
          status.value = payload.status;
          hasMore.value = payload.hasMore;
          fetchMore = payload.fetchMore;
        },
        error: (e: unknown) => {
          error.value = e;
          status.value = "error";
        },
        complete: () => {},
      },
    );
    onCleanup(() => subscription.unsubscribe());
  });

  return { employees, status, error, hasMore, loadMore: () => fetchMore() };
}
```

`watchEffect` resubscribes when `department()` changes and unsubscribes when the component unmounts. Call `useEmployees(() => props.department)` from `<script setup>`.

Apply actions through `observableClient.applyAction(modifyEmployee, { ... })` instead of `client(modifyEmployee).applyAction(...)`. When it resolves, every subscribed list and object of the edited types refetches, so the component updates without a manual reload. It throws like `applyAction`, so await it in `try`/`catch`.

## Deploy

`npm run build` writes the app to `dist/`, which `foundry.config.json` already points at. Before you build for production, set `VITE_FOUNDRY_REDIRECT_URL` in `.env.production` to your hosted app's `/auth/callback` and add that URL on **OAuth & scopes**. [Hosting](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/deploy/hosting.md) covers uploading the build to Foundry.

# Use OSDK with Vite

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/guides/vite

> Configure Vite for OSDK apps, including the process.env fix, a local CORS proxy to Foundry, and the OSDK Devtools plugin.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
