- [Links and actions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ontology-as-code/links-and-actions.md): Relate object types and define the actions that edit them.
- [Interfaces and shared properties](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ontology-as-code/interfaces.md): Share properties and contracts across object types.
- [Local development](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ontology-as-code/local-development.md): Generate an SDK and run a mock Foundry API with Vite.

# Interfaces and shared properties

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ontology-as-code/interfaces

> Define shared property types and interfaces with @osdk/maker, implement them on object types, and add interface links, actions, and schema migrations.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Interfaces](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/interfaces/interface-overview)

A shared property type is a property definition that several object types reuse. An interface is a contract of properties and links that object types implement, so code can work with any object that is a `Worker` without knowing its concrete type. Define both with `@osdk/maker` in your `.ontology/ontology.mts` file.

## Shared property types

```ts title=".ontology/ontology.mts"
import { defineSharedPropertyType } from "@osdk/maker";

export const name = defineSharedPropertyType({
  apiName: "name",
  type: "string",
  displayName: "Name",
  description: "A person's display name.",
});

export const skills = defineSharedPropertyType({
  apiName: "skills",
  type: "string",
  array: true,
  displayName: "Skills",
});
```

`type`, `array`, `reducers`, `description`, `visibility`, `nullability`, `typeClasses`, and `baseFormatter` work as they do on [object type properties](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ontology-as-code/object-types.md#properties). The other options:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `apiName` | `string` | | Required. The API name, without the namespace. |
| `displayName` | `string` | `apiName` | The name shown in Foundry. |
| `aliases` | `Array<string>` | | Other names to find the property by in search. |
| `valueType` | `OntologyIrValueTypeReferenceWithMetadata` | | A reference to an installed value type. |
| `gothamMapping` | `SharedPropertyTypeGothamMapping` | | A mapping to a Gotham property. |
| `permission` | `"roles" \| "publicProject" \| { type: "ontologyPackage"; ontologyPackageRid: string }` | | The permission model. |

To back an object type's property with a shared property type, set `sharedPropertyType` on the property and keep `type` and `array` the same as the shared property type's:

```ts title=".ontology/ontology.mts"
import { defineObject, defineSharedPropertyType } from "@osdk/maker";

export const skills = defineSharedPropertyType({
  apiName: "skills",
  type: "string",
  array: true,
});

export const contractor = defineObject({
  apiName: "Contractor",
  displayName: "Contractor",
  pluralDisplayName: "Contractors",
  primaryKeyPropertyApiName: "contractorId",
  titlePropertyApiName: "contractorId",
  properties: {
    contractorId: { type: "string" },
    skills: { type: "string", array: true, sharedPropertyType: skills },
  },
});
```

### Refer to a shared property type defined elsewhere

`importSharedPropertyType` refers to a shared property type that another ontology defines. Maker records it as an imported type, and `typeHint` tells the SDK generator its type:

```ts title=".ontology/ontology.mts"
import { importSharedPropertyType } from "@osdk/maker";

export const costCenter = importSharedPropertyType({
  apiName: "costCenter",
  packageName: "com.example.finance",
  typeHint: "string",
});
```

The full API name is `<packageName>.<apiName>`, here `com.example.finance.costCenter`. `packageName` must be lowercase and cannot end with `.`. To import many types from an existing ontology at once, use [`@osdk/maker-import`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ontology-as-code/import.md).

## Define an interface

```ts title=".ontology/ontology.mts"
import { defineInterface, defineSharedPropertyType } from "@osdk/maker";

export const name = defineSharedPropertyType({ apiName: "name", type: "string" });
export const email = defineSharedPropertyType({ apiName: "email", type: "string" });

export const party = defineInterface({
  apiName: "Party",
  displayName: "Party",
  properties: { name },
});

export const worker = defineInterface({
  apiName: "Worker",
  displayName: "Worker",
  description: "Anyone who does work for the company.",
  icon: { locator: "person", color: "#2D72D2" },
  extends: [party],
  properties: {
    email: { sharedPropertyType: email, required: false },
    jobTitle: { type: "string", displayName: "Job title" },
    hourlyRate: { type: "double", required: false },
  },
});
```

`Worker` inherits `name` from `Party`, so an object type that implements `Worker` must provide `name` and `jobTitle`, and may provide `email` and `hourlyRate`.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `apiName` | `string` | | Required. The API name, without the namespace. |
| `displayName` | `string` | `apiName` | The name shown in Foundry. |
| `description` | `string` | `displayName` | A description shown in Foundry. |
| `icon` | `{ locator: BlueprintIcon; color: string }` | | A Blueprint icon name and a hex color. |
| `properties` | `Record<string, InterfaceProperty>` | | The properties, keyed by API name. See below. |
| `extends` | `InterfaceType \| Array<InterfaceType>` | | Interfaces whose properties this interface inherits. Pass the values `defineInterface` returned. |
| `status` | `{ type: "active" } \| { type: "experimental" } \| { type: "example" } \| { type: "deprecated"; message: string; deadline: string }` | `{ type: "active" }` | The interface's status. |
| `searchable` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the interface appears in search. |
| `permission` | `"roles" \| "publicProject" \| { type: "ontologyPackage"; ontologyPackageRid: string }` | | The permission model. |
| `schemaMigrations` | `{ transitions: Array<Transition> }` | | Opts into schema migrations. See [Schema migrations](#schema-migrations). |

Each entry in `properties` takes one of three forms:

| Form | Example | Required to implement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A shared property type | `name` | Yes |
| A shared property type with a flag | `{ sharedPropertyType: email, required: false }` | As set |
| An interface-defined property | `{ type: "string", required?: boolean, displayName?, description?, array?, primaryKeyConstraint? }` | `required`, default `true` |

When you use a shared property type, its key must be the shared property type's API name: `properties: { name }` works, and `properties: { fullName: name }` throws. `primaryKeyConstraint` is `"MUST_BE_PK"`, `"CANNOT_BE_PK"`, or `"NO_RESTRICTION"`.

> [!NOTE]
> Locally generated SDKs include only the shared-property-type properties of an interface. Interface-defined properties are in the IR but not in the SDK that `@osdk/vite-plugin-oac` generates. See [Local development](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ontology-as-code/local-development.md#limitations).

## Implement an interface

List the interface in the object type's `implementsInterfaces`, and map each interface property to one of the object's properties:

```ts title=".ontology/ontology.mts"
import { defineInterface, defineObject, defineSharedPropertyType } from "@osdk/maker";

export const name = defineSharedPropertyType({ apiName: "name", type: "string" });

export const worker = defineInterface({
  apiName: "Worker",
  displayName: "Worker",
  properties: {
    name,
    jobTitle: { type: "string" },
  },
});

export const employee = defineObject({
  apiName: "Employee",
  displayName: "Employee",
  pluralDisplayName: "Employees",
  primaryKeyPropertyApiName: "employeeId",
  titlePropertyApiName: "fullName",
  properties: {
    employeeId: { type: "integer" },
    fullName: { type: "string" },
    jobTitle: { type: "string" },
  },
  implementsInterfaces: [
    {
      implements: worker,
      propertyMapping: [
        { interfaceProperty: "name", mapsTo: "fullName" },
        { interfaceProperty: "jobTitle", mapsTo: "jobTitle" },
      ],
    },
  ],
});
```

`defineObject` throws if a required interface property, including one inherited through `extends`, is not mapped, if a mapping names an interface property that does not exist, or if the object property's type differs from the interface property's type.

## Interface links

`defineInterfaceLinkConstraint` adds a link to an interface. Every object type that implements the interface must provide the link when `required` is `true`.

```ts title=".ontology/ontology.mts"
import { defineInterface, defineInterfaceLinkConstraint } from "@osdk/maker";

export const worker = defineInterface({
  apiName: "Worker",
  displayName: "Worker",
  properties: { jobTitle: { type: "string" } },
});

export const workerManager = defineInterfaceLinkConstraint({
  apiName: "manager",
  from: worker,
  toOne: worker,
  displayName: "Manager",
  required: false,
});
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `apiName` | `string` | | Required. The link's API name on the `from` interface. |
| `from` | `InterfaceType` | | Required. The interface the link belongs to. It must be defined in this ontology, not imported. |
| `toOne` or `toMany` | `InterfaceType \| string` | | Required, exactly one. The target interface, or its API name. |
| `displayName` | `string` | `apiName` | The name shown in Foundry. |
| `description` | `string` | `displayName` | A description shown in Foundry. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether implementing object types must provide the link. |

## Interface actions

These helpers generate action types that work on any object that implements an interface. Their options match the [object action helpers](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ontology-as-code/links-and-actions.md#helper-options), with `interfaceType` in place of `objectType`.

| Helper | Default API name | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `defineCreateInterfaceObjectAction` | `create-<interface>`, or `create-<interface>-<object>` with `objectType` | Creates an object that implements the interface. Without `objectType`, the user picks the object type in an `objectTypeParameter` parameter. |
| `defineModifyInterfaceObjectAction` | `modify-<interface>`, or `modify-<interface>-<object>` with `objectType` | Modifies an object through the interface's properties. |
| `defineDeleteInterfaceObjectAction` | `delete-interface-object-<interface>` | Deletes an object that implements the interface. |
| `defineCreateInterfaceLinkAction` | Derived from the interface and link names | Adds an interface link between two objects. |
| `defineDeleteInterfaceLinkAction` | Derived from the interface and link names | Removes an interface link. |

```ts title=".ontology/ontology.mts"
import {
  defineCreateInterfaceLinkAction,
  defineCreateInterfaceObjectAction,
  defineDeleteInterfaceObjectAction,
  defineInterface,
  defineInterfaceLinkConstraint,
  defineModifyInterfaceObjectAction,
} from "@osdk/maker";

export const worker = defineInterface({
  apiName: "Worker",
  displayName: "Worker",
  properties: {
    jobTitle: { type: "string" },
    hourlyRate: { type: "double", required: false },
  },
});

export const workerManager = defineInterfaceLinkConstraint({
  apiName: "manager",
  from: worker,
  toOne: worker,
});

export const createWorker = defineCreateInterfaceObjectAction({ interfaceType: worker });

export const modifyWorker = defineModifyInterfaceObjectAction({
  interfaceType: worker,
  excludedProperties: ["hourlyRate"],
});

export const deleteWorker = defineDeleteInterfaceObjectAction({ interfaceType: worker });

export const setManager = defineCreateInterfaceLinkAction({ interfaceLink: workerManager });
```

The link actions take the value `defineInterfaceLinkConstraint` returned as `interfaceLink`, or the link's API name together with `from`. Use `sourceParameter` and `targetParameter` to rename their two parameters.

### Action type constraints

`defineInterfaceActionTypeConstraint` declares an action that implementing object types provide, with the parameters it must accept:

```ts title=".ontology/ontology.mts"
import { defineInterface, defineInterfaceActionTypeConstraint } from "@osdk/maker";

export const worker = defineInterface({
  apiName: "Worker",
  displayName: "Worker",
  properties: { jobTitle: { type: "string" } },
});

defineInterfaceActionTypeConstraint({
  interfaceType: worker,
  apiName: "reassign",
  displayName: "Reassign",
  description: "Moves a worker to a new team.",
  requireImplementation: false,
  parameters: [
    {
      apiName: "team",
      displayName: "Team",
      type: { type: "string", string: {} },
      requireImplementation: true,
    },
  ],
});
```

The interface must be defined in this ontology, and the constraint's API name must be unique on it.

## Schema migrations

> [!WARNING]
> Interface schema migrations are in beta in Foundry and may not be available on your enrollment.

Changing a published interface can break the object types that implement it. A schema migration announces a change and gives implementers a grace period before it is enforced. Adding `schemaMigrations` to an interface also turns on compatibility checks, so maker rejects breaking changes that are not staged as a migration.

The only migration is `addRequiredProperty`, which makes an optional property required. While the migration is active, the property stays `required: false`:

```ts title=".ontology/ontology.mts"
import { defineInterface } from "@osdk/maker";

export const order = defineInterface({
  apiName: "Order",
  displayName: "Order",
  properties: {
    orderId: { type: "string" },
    shippedAt: { type: "timestamp", required: false },
  },
  schemaMigrations: {
    transitions: [
      {
        id: "requireShippedAt",
        title: "Require shipped at",
        description: "Every order must record when it shipped.",
        gracePeriod: { type: "afterInstall", days: 45 },
        instructions: [{ type: "addRequiredProperty", property: "shippedAt" }],
      },
    ],
  },
});
```

A transition groups migrations that are finalized or deleted together:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | A stable ID, unique on the interface. 1 to 150 characters: a letter or digit, then letters, digits, `_`, or `-`. |
| `title` | `string` | A summary of the change. |
| `description` | `string` | Optional details. |
| `gracePeriod` | `{ type: "afterInstall"; days: number } \| { type: "deadline"; deadline: string }` | How long implementers have to comply. `afterInstall` allows 7 to 180 days and suits Marketplace-distributed ontologies. `deadline` is an ISO 8601 UTC date-time, and installing after it fails. |
| `instructions` | `Array<{ type: "addRequiredProperty"; property: string }>` | The migrations in the transition. |

Use `schemaMigrations: { transitions: [] }` to turn on compatibility checks without a migration.

### The lockfile

Maker tracks opted-in interfaces in `ontology-schema-lock.json`, next to the ontology file. Commit it.

### Create the lockfile

```sh
npx maker -i .ontology/ontology.mts --write-locks
```

Without `--write-locks`, maker fails when an interface has opted in and no lockfile exists, or when the lockfile is out of date.
### End a transition

After the grace period, remove the transition and update the schema in the same change: set the property to `required: true` to **finalize**, or leave it optional to **delete** the transition. Then run `maker --write-locks` again. Maker compares the schema with the lockfile, asks you to confirm `FINALIZE` or `DELETE`, and rejects a schema that matches neither. Pass `--yes` to confirm without a prompt.

# Links and actions

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ontology-as-code/links-and-actions

> Relate object types with defineLink and define action types with the create, modify, and delete helpers from @osdk/maker.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Link types](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/object-link-types/link-types-overview)
- [Action types](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/action-types/overview)

Link types connect object types, so that an `Employee` can reach its `Office`. Action types describe the edits users can make, such as changing an employee's job title. Define both with `@osdk/maker` in your `.ontology/ontology.mts` file.

## Link types

`defineLink` supports three kinds of link, chosen by the keys you pass:

| Kind | Keys | Joined on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One-to-many | `one`, `toMany`, `manyForeignKeyProperty` | A foreign key property on the "many" object type. |
| Many-to-many | `many`, `toMany` | A link dataset of primary key pairs. |
| Intermediary | `many`, `toMany`, `intermediaryObjectType` | An object type that sits between the two, joined by two one-to-many links. |

`defineLink` records the link without looking up its object types, so a link can refer to an object type that is defined later in the file. Maker checks the link when it compiles the ontology.

### One-to-many

Each side's `metadata.apiName` is the name of the link as seen from that side's object type. The `one` side's name leads to many objects, and the `toMany` side's name leads to one:

```ts title=".ontology/ontology.mts"
import { defineLink, defineObject } from "@osdk/maker";

export const office = defineObject({
  apiName: "Office",
  displayName: "Office",
  pluralDisplayName: "Offices",
  primaryKeyPropertyApiName: "officeId",
  titlePropertyApiName: "name",
  properties: {
    officeId: { type: "string" },
    name: { type: "string" },
    city: { type: "string" },
  },
});

export const employee = defineObject({
  apiName: "Employee",
  displayName: "Employee",
  pluralDisplayName: "Employees",
  primaryKeyPropertyApiName: "employeeId",
  titlePropertyApiName: "fullName",
  properties: {
    employeeId: { type: "integer" },
    fullName: { type: "string" },
    leadId: { type: "integer" },
    officeId: { type: "string" },
  },
});

export const officeOccupants = defineLink({
  apiName: "office-occupants",
  one: {
    object: office,
    metadata: { apiName: "occupants", displayName: "Occupant", pluralDisplayName: "Occupants" },
  },
  toMany: { object: employee, metadata: { apiName: "office" } },
  manyForeignKeyProperty: "officeId",
});

export const employeeReports = defineLink({
  apiName: "employee-reports",
  one: { object: employee, metadata: { apiName: "reports" } },
  toMany: { object: employee, metadata: { apiName: "lead" } },
  manyForeignKeyProperty: "leadId",
});
```

These two links give the generated SDK the following link names:

| Object type | Link | Leads to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Office` | `occupants` | Many `Employee` objects whose `officeId` is the office's primary key. |
| `Employee` | `office` | The one `Office` named by `officeId`. |
| `Employee` | `reports` | Many `Employee` objects whose `leadId` is this employee's primary key. |
| `Employee` | `lead` | The one `Employee` named by `leadId`. |

`manyForeignKeyProperty` must be a property of the `toMany` object type, with the same type as the `one` object type's primary key. Set `cardinality: "OneToOne"` when each object on the `one` side links to at most one object on the `toMany` side; the default is `"OneToMany"`.

### Many-to-many

```ts title=".ontology/ontology.mts"
import { defineLink, defineObject } from "@osdk/maker";

export const project = defineObject({
  apiName: "Project",
  displayName: "Project",
  pluralDisplayName: "Projects",
  primaryKeyPropertyApiName: "projectId",
  titlePropertyApiName: "projectId",
  properties: { projectId: { type: "string" } },
});

export const employee = defineObject({
  apiName: "Employee",
  displayName: "Employee",
  pluralDisplayName: "Employees",
  primaryKeyPropertyApiName: "employeeId",
  titlePropertyApiName: "employeeId",
  properties: { employeeId: { type: "integer" } },
});

export const projectMembers = defineLink({
  apiName: "project-members",
  many: {
    object: project,
    metadata: { apiName: "members", displayName: "Member", pluralDisplayName: "Members" },
  },
  toMany: { object: employee, metadata: { apiName: "projects" } },
});
```

Maker backs a many-to-many link with a dataset named `link-<apiName>` that has one column per primary key. When both object types use the same primary key name, the columns get `_from` and `_to` suffixes.

### Intermediary

An intermediary link connects two object types through a third. Define the intermediary object type and a one-to-many link from each side to it, then pass those links as `linkToIntermediary`:

```ts title=".ontology/ontology.mts"
import { defineLink, defineObject } from "@osdk/maker";

export const project = defineObject({
  apiName: "Project",
  displayName: "Project",
  pluralDisplayName: "Projects",
  primaryKeyPropertyApiName: "projectId",
  titlePropertyApiName: "projectId",
  properties: { projectId: { type: "string" } },
});

export const employee = defineObject({
  apiName: "Employee",
  displayName: "Employee",
  pluralDisplayName: "Employees",
  primaryKeyPropertyApiName: "employeeId",
  titlePropertyApiName: "employeeId",
  properties: { employeeId: { type: "integer" } },
});

export const assignment = defineObject({
  apiName: "Assignment",
  displayName: "Assignment",
  pluralDisplayName: "Assignments",
  primaryKeyPropertyApiName: "assignmentId",
  titlePropertyApiName: "assignmentId",
  properties: {
    assignmentId: { type: "string" },
    projectId: { type: "string" },
    employeeId: { type: "integer" },
  },
});

export const projectAssignments = defineLink({
  apiName: "project-assignments",
  one: { object: project, metadata: { apiName: "assignments" } },
  toMany: { object: assignment, metadata: { apiName: "project" } },
  manyForeignKeyProperty: "projectId",
});

export const employeeAssignments = defineLink({
  apiName: "employee-assignments",
  one: { object: employee, metadata: { apiName: "assignments" } },
  toMany: { object: assignment, metadata: { apiName: "employee" } },
  manyForeignKeyProperty: "employeeId",
});

export const projectStaff = defineLink({
  apiName: "project-staff",
  many: {
    object: project,
    metadata: { apiName: "staff" },
    linkToIntermediary: projectAssignments,
  },
  toMany: {
    object: employee,
    metadata: { apiName: "staffedProjects" },
    linkToIntermediary: employeeAssignments,
  },
  intermediaryObjectType: assignment,
});
```

### Link options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `apiName` | `string` | | Required. Converted to a lowercase, hyphenated link type ID. Not prefixed by `--apiNamespace`. |
| `one`, `many`, `toMany` | `{ object, metadata }` | | The two sides. `object` is a definition from `defineObject`, an imported object type, or an object type API name. |
| `manyForeignKeyProperty` | `string` | | One-to-many only. The foreign key property on the `toMany` object type. |
| `cardinality` | `"OneToMany" \| "OneToOne"` | `"OneToMany"` | One-to-many only. |
| `intermediaryObjectType` | `ObjectTypeDefinition \| string` | | Intermediary only. |
| `description` | `string` | | A description shown in Foundry. |
| `status` | `LinkStatus` | `"active"` | See [Status](#status). |
| `editsEnabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether users can edit the link. |
| `permission` | `"roles" \| "publicProject" \| { type: "ontologyPackage"; ontologyPackageRid: string }` | | The permission model for the link. |

Each side's `metadata`:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `apiName` | `string` | | Required. The link name on this side's object type. Starts with a letter, then letters, digits, and `_`. |
| `displayName` | `string` | `apiName` with its first letter capitalized | The singular name shown in Foundry. |
| `pluralDisplayName` | `string` | `apiName` capitalized, with an `s` added unless it ends in `s` | The plural name shown in Foundry. |
| `visibility` | `"PROMINENT" \| "NORMAL" \| "HIDDEN"` | `"NORMAL"` | How prominently Foundry shows the link. |
| `groupDisplayName` | `string` | `""` | A group to show the link under. |
| `typeClasses` | `Array<{ kind: string; name: string }>` | `[]` | Type classes. |

### Status

A link's `status` is `"active"`, `"experimental"`, `"example"`, or `{ type: "deprecated", message, deadline, replacedBy? }`. It must agree with the object types it connects: if either side is deprecated, the link must be deprecated, and if either side is experimental or example, the link must be experimental or example.

## Action types

Most actions create, change, or delete one object. The helpers below generate an action type from an object type: one parameter per property, the logic rule, and a default parameter order.

| Helper | Default API name | Parameters | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defineCreateObjectAction` | `create-object-<object>` | Every property, including the primary key | Adds an object. |
| `defineModifyObjectAction` | `modify-object-<object>` | `objectToModifyParameter`, then every property except the primary key | Modifies the chosen object. Each parameter defaults to the object's current value. |
| `defineCreateOrModifyObjectAction` | `create-or-modify-<object>` | `objectToCreateOrModifyParameter`, then every property except the primary key | Modifies the chosen object, or creates one. Each parameter defaults to the object's current value. |
| `defineDeleteObjectAction` | `delete-object-<object>` | `objectToDeleteParameter` | Deletes the chosen object. |

`<object>` is the object type's API name in lowercase with hyphens, so `Employee` gives `modify-object-employee`. Parameters skip vector properties, properties in `excludedProperties`, and properties set by `nonParameterMappings`; create and create-or-modify also skip derived properties. For interfaces, see [Interface actions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ontology-as-code/interfaces.md#interface-actions).

```ts title=".ontology/ontology.mts"
import {
  defineCreateObjectAction,
  defineDeleteObjectAction,
  defineModifyObjectAction,
  defineObject,
} from "@osdk/maker";

export const employee = defineObject({
  apiName: "Employee",
  displayName: "Employee",
  pluralDisplayName: "Employees",
  primaryKeyPropertyApiName: "employeeId",
  titlePropertyApiName: "fullName",
  properties: {
    employeeId: { type: "integer" },
    fullName: { type: "string" },
    jobTitle: { type: "string" },
    department: { type: "string" },
    salary: { type: "double" },
  },
});

export const createEmployee = defineCreateObjectAction({
  apiName: "create-employee",
  objectType: employee,
});

export const modifyEmployee = defineModifyObjectAction({
  apiName: "modify-employee",
  objectType: employee,
});

export const deleteEmployee = defineDeleteObjectAction({
  apiName: "delete-employee",
  objectType: employee,
});
```

Action API names must contain lowercase letters and digits in segments separated by `-` or `.`. The SDK generator converts them to camelCase, so `modify-employee` is `modifyEmployee` in your generated SDK.

The parameter IDs of the chosen object are exported as constants:

| Constant | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `MODIFY_OBJECT_PARAMETER` | `"objectToModifyParameter"` |
| `CREATE_OR_MODIFY_OBJECT_PARAMETER` | `"objectToCreateOrModifyParameter"` |
| `DELETE_OBJECT_PARAMETER` | `"objectToDeleteParameter"` |
| `CREATE_INTERFACE_OBJECT_PARAMETER` | `"objectTypeParameter"` |
| `MODIFY_INTERFACE_OBJECT_PARAMETER` | `"interfaceObjectToModifyParameter"` |

### Helper options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `objectType` | `ObjectTypeDefinition` | | Required. The object type to act on. |
| `apiName` | `string` | See the table above | The action's API name. |
| `displayName` | `string` | `Create`, `Modify`, `Create or Modify`, or `Delete`, then the object's display name | The name shown in Foundry. |
| `description` | `string` | | A description shown in Foundry. |
| `status` | `"active" \| "experimental" \| "example" \| deprecated` | `"active"` | The action's status. |
| `excludedProperties` | `Array<string>` | | Properties that do not get a parameter. |
| `parameterConfiguration` | `Record<string, ParameterConfiguration>` | | Per-parameter settings. See [Configure parameters](#configure-parameters). |
| `nonParameterMappings` | `Record<string, MappingValue>` | | Properties set without a parameter. See [Set properties without a parameter](#set-properties-without-a-parameter). |
| `actionLevelValidation` | `Array<{ condition; displayMetadata? }>` | | Conditions that must all pass to submit the action. See [Who can submit](#who-can-submit). |
| `parameterOrdering` | `Array<string>` | Configured parameters first, then properties in definition order | The form's parameter order. Must list every parameter; the chosen-object parameter is added first if you leave it out. |
| `sections` | `Array<ActionSection>` | | Group parameters into form sections. See [Form sections](#form-sections). |
| `defaultFormat` | `"FORM" \| "TABLE"` | | The form's default layout. |
| `enableLayoutSwitch` | `boolean` | | Let users switch between form and table layouts. |
| `tableConfiguration` | `{ columnWidthByParameterRid; enableFileImport; ... }` | | Settings for the table layout. |
| `submissionMetadata` | `{ successMessage: string; submitButtonDisplayMetadata?; undoButtonConfiguration?: boolean }` | | The submit button and the message shown after it succeeds. |
| `icon` | `{ locator: BlueprintIcon; color: string }` | | The action's icon. |
| `permission` | `"roles" \| "publicProject" \| { type: "ontologyPackage"; ontologyPackageRid: string }` | | The permission model for the action. |

`defineDeleteObjectAction` reads only `objectType`, `apiName`, `displayName`, `description`, `status`, `actionLevelValidation`, `icon`, and `permission`.

### Configure parameters

`parameterConfiguration` is keyed by parameter ID, which for property parameters is the property's API name. A key that is not a property adds a new parameter, and needs `customParameterType`.

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `displayName` | `string` | The parameter's label. Defaults to the property's display name. |
| `description` | `string` | Help text under the parameter. |
| `required` | `boolean \| { listLength: { min?: number; max?: number } }` | Whether a value is required. Defaults to `true` when the property sets `nullability.noNulls`, and for arrays to a minimum length of 1 when it sets `noEmptyCollections`. |
| `allowedValues` | `AllowedValues` | The values the parameter accepts, such as `{ type: "oneOf", oneOf }`, `{ type: "range", min?, max? }`, or `{ type: "text", minLength?, maxLength?, regex? }`. Defaults to what the property type allows. |
| `defaultValue` | `OntologyIrParameterPrefill` | A prefilled value. |
| `defaultVisibility` | `"editable" \| "disabled" \| "hidden"` | How the parameter starts. |
| `conditionalOverrides` | `Array<ConditionalOverride>` | Change the visibility, whether a value is required, the default, or the allowed values when a condition passes. |
| `renderHint` | `ParameterRenderHint` | Which input control to use. |
| `structFieldValidations` | `Record<string, StructFieldConfiguration>` | For struct parameters, per-field settings, including `defaultValue`. Set a field's `defaultValue` to `null` to turn off the default that modify helpers infer. |
| `customParameterType` | `ActionParameterType` | The type of a parameter that is not a property, such as `"string"` or `"booleanList"`. |

A conditional override is one of:

| Override | Effect when `condition` passes |
| --- | --- |
| `{ type: "visibility", condition, then? }` | Sets visibility to `then`: `"editable"`, `"disabled"`, or `"hidden"`. |
| `{ type: "disabled", condition, then? }` | Disables the parameter. |
| `{ type: "required", condition }` | Makes the parameter required. |
| `{ type: "defaultValue", condition, defaultValue }` | Uses a different default. |
| `{ type: "constraint", condition, constraint }` | Uses different allowed values. |

### Conditions

Validation rules and overrides take a `ConditionDefinition`:

| Condition | Passes when |
| --- | --- |
| `{ type: "group", name }` | The user is in the group chosen for the input `name` when the ontology is installed. |
| `{ type: "parameter", parameterId, matches }` | The parameter's value equals `matches`, such as `{ type: "staticValue", staticValue: { type: "string", string: "Engineering" } }`. |
| `{ type: "and" \| "or", conditions }` | All or any of `conditions` pass. |

### Who can submit

`actionLevelValidation` is a list of rules that must all pass before a user can submit. `displayMetadata.failureMessage` is shown when a rule fails.

This action can only be submitted by members of the HR group, shows `skills` only when the department is Engineering, limits `department` to two values, and records who made the edit:

```ts title=".ontology/ontology.mts"
import {
  type ConditionDefinition,
  defineModifyObjectAction,
  defineObject,
} from "@osdk/maker";

export const employee = defineObject({
  apiName: "Employee",
  displayName: "Employee",
  pluralDisplayName: "Employees",
  primaryKeyPropertyApiName: "employeeId",
  titlePropertyApiName: "fullName",
  properties: {
    employeeId: { type: "integer" },
    fullName: { type: "string" },
    jobTitle: { type: "string" },
    department: { type: "string" },
    salary: { type: "double" },
    skills: { type: "string", array: true },
    leadId: { type: "integer" },
    lastModifiedBy: { type: "string" },
  },
});

const isHr: ConditionDefinition = { type: "group", name: "hrGroup" };

const isEngineering: ConditionDefinition = {
  type: "parameter",
  parameterId: "department",
  matches: {
    type: "staticValue",
    staticValue: { type: "string", string: "Engineering" },
  },
};

export const modifyEmployee = defineModifyObjectAction({
  apiName: "modify-employee",
  objectType: employee,
  excludedProperties: ["leadId"],
  nonParameterMappings: {
    lastModifiedBy: { type: "currentUser" },
  },
  actionLevelValidation: [
    {
      condition: isHr,
      displayMetadata: { failureMessage: "Only HR can edit employees.", typeClasses: [] },
    },
  ],
  parameterConfiguration: {
    department: {
      required: true,
      allowedValues: {
        type: "oneOf",
        oneOf: [
          { label: "Engineering", value: { type: "string", string: "Engineering" } },
          { label: "Research", value: { type: "string", string: "Research" } },
        ],
      },
    },
    skills: {
      defaultVisibility: "hidden",
      conditionalOverrides: [{ type: "visibility", condition: isEngineering, then: "editable" }],
    },
    salary: { displayName: "Annual salary", description: "Gross salary in USD." },
  },
});
```

### Set properties without a parameter

`nonParameterMappings` sets a property from something other than user input. The property gets no parameter.

| Value | Sets the property to |
| --- | --- |
| `{ type: "currentUser" }` | The ID of the user who submits the action. |
| `{ type: "currentTime" }` | The time the action is submitted. |
| `{ type: "uuid", linkId? }` | A new UUID. Properties that share a `linkId` get the same UUID. |
| `{ type: "staticValue", staticValue }` | A fixed value. |
| `{ type: "parameterId", parameterId }` | The value of another parameter, such as a custom parameter. |

### Form sections

Each entry in `sections` has an `id`, a `displayName`, and the `parameters` it holds, plus optional `description`, `defaultVisibility` (`"visible"` or `"hidden"`), `columnCount` (`1` or `2`), `showTitleBar`, `collapsedByDefault`, `style` (`"box"` or `"minimal"`), and `conditionalOverrides`.

### Define an action from rules

`defineAction` takes the parameters and logic rules directly, for actions the helpers do not cover. The rules use the Ontology IR rule types, such as `addObjectRule`, `modifyObjectRule`, `deleteObjectRule`, `addOrModifyObjectRuleV2`, and `addInterfaceRule`.

```ts title=".ontology/ontology.mts"
import { defineAction, defineObject } from "@osdk/maker";

export const employee = defineObject({
  apiName: "Employee",
  displayName: "Employee",
  pluralDisplayName: "Employees",
  primaryKeyPropertyApiName: "employeeId",
  titlePropertyApiName: "fullName",
  properties: {
    employeeId: { type: "integer" },
    fullName: { type: "string" },
    jobTitle: { type: "string" },
  },
});

export const promoteEmployee = defineAction({
  apiName: "promote-employee",
  displayName: "Promote employee",
  status: "active",
  parameters: [
    {
      id: "employee",
      displayName: "Employee",
      type: { type: "objectReference", objectReference: { objectTypeId: employee.apiName } },
      validation: { required: true, allowedValues: { type: "objectQuery" } },
    },
    {
      id: "newTitle",
      displayName: "New title",
      type: "string",
      validation: { required: true, allowedValues: { type: "text" } },
    },
  ],
  rules: [
    {
      type: "modifyObjectRule",
      modifyObjectRule: {
        objectToModify: "employee",
        propertyValues: {
          jobTitle: { type: "parameterId", parameterId: "newTitle" },
        },
        structFieldValues: {},
      },
    },
  ],
});
```

`defineAction` throws when there are no rules, when parameter IDs repeat, or when a rule or section references a parameter that is not defined.

# Local development

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ontology-as-code/local-development

> Use @osdk/vite-plugin-oac to compile your ontology, generate an SDK, and serve a seeded mock Foundry API from the Vite dev server.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [SuperRepo](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/superrepo/overview)

`@osdk/vite-plugin-oac` lets you build an app against your ontology-as-code definitions before they exist in Foundry. On every change to `.ontology/`, it compiles the ontology again, regenerates an SDK into `.osdk/src`, and answers OSDK requests from the Vite dev server with data from a seed file.

> [!WARNING]
> In `@osdk/vite-plugin-oac` 0.85.0, the step that converts the IR to Ontology metadata reads a `blockData` key, but `@osdk/maker` 0.82.0 writes the IR under `ontology`. The conversion fails with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'interfaceTypes')`, so no SDK is generated and the mock serves no types. Check the changelog for a fix before you adopt the plugin.

## How it works

| Step | Tool | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Compile the ontology | `pnpm exec maker -i <ontologyDir>/ontology.mts` | `node_modules/.osdk/.oac/.ontology.ir.json` |
| 2. Convert the IR to Ontology metadata | `@osdk/generator-converters.ontologyir` | `node_modules/.osdk/.oac/.ontology.json` |
| 3. Generate an SDK | `pnpm exec osdk unstable typescript generate` | `.osdk/src`, then `pnpm exec tsc` in `.osdk` |
| 4. Start the mock (dev server only) | `@osdk/faux` | Ontology metadata and `seed.ts` data, served from the dev server |

The plugin writes the SDK to a temporary directory first, then copies only the files whose contents changed into `.osdk/src` and deletes files that are no longer generated.

| Command | What runs |
| --- | --- |
| `vite` (dev server) | All four steps before the server starts, then all four again on every add, change, or delete under the ontology directory. After each successful run, the browser does a full reload. Failures are logged, and the server keeps running. |
| `vite build` | Steps 1 to 3 in the `buildStart` hook. The build fails if any step fails. No mock server. |

## Requirements

- **pnpm.** The plugin runs `maker`, `osdk`, and `tsc` with `pnpm exec`, so pnpm must be on your `PATH` and each binary must be installed in your project.
- **Vite** and a Node.js version that can import `.mts` files natively: 22.18 or later, or 23.6 or later.
- **A `tsconfig.json` in `.osdk`.** After generating, the plugin runs `tsc` with `.osdk` as the working directory and fails if it exits with an error.

## Install

```npm
npm install --save-dev @osdk/vite-plugin-oac @osdk/maker @osdk/cli @osdk/faux typescript
```

The app itself needs `@osdk/client` and `@osdk/api`, which the generated SDK imports, plus `@osdk/react` if you use React. `@osdk/faux` is only needed for the seed file's types.

## Configure Vite

Add `ontologyAsCode` to your Vite config:

```ts title="vite.config.ts"
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

import { ontologyAsCode } from "@osdk/vite-plugin-oac";
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    ontologyAsCode({
      ontologyDir: fileURLToPath(new URL("./.ontology", import.meta.url)),
    }),
  ],
  resolve: {
    alias: {
      "@my-app/sdk": fileURLToPath(new URL("./.osdk/src/index.ts", import.meta.url)),
    },
  },
});
```

Pass `ontologyDir` as an absolute path: the plugin ignores a changed file unless its path starts with `ontologyDir`, and Vite's watcher reports absolute paths. The `resolve.alias` entry is one way to import the generated SDK as `@my-app/sdk`; add a matching `paths` entry to your app's `tsconfig.json` so TypeScript resolves it too.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ontologyDir` | `string` | | Required. The directory that holds `ontology.mts` and `seed.ts`. Created if it does not exist. |
| `loggerLevel` | `"debug" \| "info" \| "warn" \| "error"` | `"info"` | The lowest level the plugin logs. Messages are prefixed with `[osdk]`. |
| `hooks.preSeed` | `(ontology: FauxOntology) => Promise<void>` | | Runs after the plugin registers the generated metadata with the mock and before it applies the seed. Errors are logged and ignored. |

Create `.osdk/tsconfig.json` for the `tsc` step. The generated code uses ES module imports with `.js` extensions:

```json title=".osdk/tsconfig.json"
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "NodeNext",
    "moduleResolution": "NodeNext",
    "strict": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "noEmit": true
  },
  "include": ["src"]
}
```

Add `.osdk/src` to `.gitignore`, or commit it so the app builds without running the plugin. Do not edit it by hand.

## Seed data

The mock starts empty. The plugin loads `seed.ts` from the ontology directory after every regeneration and calls its default export with the mock's `FauxFoundry`. The file is required: without it, each regeneration logs an error and the browser does not reload.

```ts title=".ontology/seed.ts"
import type { FauxFoundry } from "@osdk/faux";

export default function seed(fauxFoundry: FauxFoundry): void {
  const store = fauxFoundry.getDefaultDataStore();

  const london = store.registerObject({
    __apiName: "Office",
    __primaryKey: "lon",
    officeId: "lon",
    name: "London",
    city: "London",
  });

  const ada = store.registerObject({
    __apiName: "Employee",
    __primaryKey: 1,
    employeeId: 1,
    fullName: "Ada Lovelace",
    jobTitle: "Engineer",
    department: "Research",
    startDate: "2024-01-15",
    salary: 120000,
    skills: ["math", "analysis"],
  });

  const grace = store.registerObject({
    __apiName: "Employee",
    __primaryKey: 2,
    employeeId: 2,
    fullName: "Grace Hopper",
    jobTitle: "Engineering Manager",
    department: "Research",
    startDate: "2023-06-01",
    salary: 150000,
    skills: ["compilers"],
  });

  store.registerLink(london, "occupants", ada, "office");
  store.registerLink(grace, "reports", ada, "lead");
}
```

`registerObject` takes the object's API name in `__apiName`, its primary key in `__primaryKey`, and property values in their wire format, such as ISO 8601 strings for dates. `registerLink(source, linkName, target, reverseLinkName)` takes both sides' link names and sets the foreign key for you, so this seed sets Ada's `officeId` to `"lon"` and her `leadId` to `2`.

Every regeneration rebuilds the mock from the seed, so edits made through actions last only until the next change to `.ontology/`.

## Connect your app

The mock answers on the dev server's own origin, and passes any request it does not handle on to Vite. Create the client with the dev server's origin, the mock's Ontology RID, and the token the mock accepts:

```ts title="src/client.ts"
import { createClient } from "@osdk/client";

const LOCAL_ONTOLOGY_RID = "ri.ontology.main.ontology.00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000";

export const client = createClient(
  window.location.origin,
  LOCAL_ONTOLOGY_RID,
  async () => "myAccessToken",
);
```

| Value | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `window.location.origin` | The mock runs inside the Vite dev server. |
| `ri.ontology.main.ontology.00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` | The RID of the mock's only ontology. Do not use the generated SDK's `$ontologyRid`; a locally generated SDK sets it to a placeholder. |
| `"myAccessToken"` | The mock rejects any other bearer token with `401`. |

From there, use the client as you would against Foundry. With `@osdk/react`, pass it to `OsdkProvider` and query the generated types:

```tsx title="src/EmployeeList.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkObjects } from "@osdk/react";

export function EmployeeList() {
  const { data, isLoading, error } = useOsdkObjects(Employee);

  return (
    <div>
      {isLoading && <p>Loading…</p>}
      {error != null && <p>Could not load employees.</p>}
      <ul>
        {data?.map((employee) => (
          <li key={employee.$primaryKey}>
            {employee.fullName}, {employee.jobTitle}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </div>
  );
}
```

See [Create a client](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/client.md) for `OsdkProvider`, and [Load objects](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/objects.md) for the hooks.

## Limitations

The mock is an approximation of Foundry built from the generated metadata.

| Area | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Actions | Create, modify, and delete object rules work. Add and delete link rules are only partly supported. Interface create, modify, and delete rules throw `not implemented`. |
| Numeric primary keys | The mock accepts an object parameter only as a string, while the client sends the primary key as it is. Modify and delete actions on object types with numeric primary keys, such as `employeeId`, fail validation with `INVALID`. Use string primary keys for types you edit locally. |
| Interfaces | Only shared-property-type properties reach the generated SDK and the mock, every interface property is optional, and object types do not record which interfaces they implement. Interface-defined properties are missing. |
| Functions | The generated metadata has no queries, so there are no functions to call. |
| Schema migrations | The plugin runs `maker` without `--write-locks`. If an interface uses [schema migrations](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ontology-as-code/interfaces.md#schema-migrations), commit an up-to-date `ontology-schema-lock.json` or compilation fails. |

## Seed data for the local Ontology server

`@osdk/seed-helpers` and `@osdk/seed-compiler` build seed data for a different local server: the Ontology server that `@osdk/integration-testing` starts, which loads seed JSON into SQLite. They do not seed the Vite plugin's mock. To use them in tests, see [Integration testing](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/deploy/integration-testing.md).

`seed-compiler` merges a directory of seed files into one JSON file:

```sh
npx seed-compiler --metadata ontology-metadata.json --seed-dir seed --output seed-data.json
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--metadata` | Required. The `ontology-metadata.json` that the SDK generator writes with `--experimentalOntologyMetadata`. |
| `--seed-dir` | Required. A directory of seed files. Every top-level `.mts` file whose name does not start with `$` is loaded, in file name order. |
| `-o`, `--output` | Required. Where to write the merged JSON. |

Each seed file default-exports the result of `createSeedWithMetadata` from `@osdk/seed-helpers`, or its `output`. All files are merged through one builder, so primary keys must be unique across the whole directory, and a link can reference objects created in any file:

```ts title="seed/employees.mts"
import { Employee, Office } from "@my-app/sdk";
import metadata from "@my-app/sdk/experimental/ontology-metadata";
import { createSeedWithMetadata } from "@osdk/seed-helpers";

export default createSeedWithMetadata(metadata, (seed) => {
  const london = seed.create(Office, { officeId: "lon", name: "London", city: "London" });
  const ada = seed.create(Employee, { employeeId: 1, fullName: "Ada Lovelace" });
  seed.link(ada, "office", london);
});
```

# Object types

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ontology-as-code/object-types

> Define object types with defineObject from @osdk/maker, including property types, primary keys, titles, value types, and datasources.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Object types](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/object-link-types/object-types-overview)

{/* cspell:ignore geospatial */}

An object type describes one kind of thing in your ontology, such as an employee or an office: its properties, which property identifies each object, and where its data comes from. Define one with `defineObject` from `@osdk/maker` in your `.ontology/ontology.mts` file.

## Define an object type

```ts title=".ontology/ontology.mts"
import { defineObject } from "@osdk/maker";

export const employee = defineObject({
  apiName: "Employee",
  displayName: "Employee",
  pluralDisplayName: "Employees",
  description: "A person employed by the company.",
  icon: { locator: "person", color: "#2D72D2" },
  primaryKeyPropertyApiName: "employeeId",
  titlePropertyApiName: "fullName",
  properties: {
    employeeId: { type: "integer", displayName: "Employee ID" },
    fullName: { type: "string", displayName: "Full name" },
    jobTitle: { type: "string" },
    department: { type: "string" },
    startDate: { type: "date" },
    salary: { type: "double" },
    skills: { type: "string", array: true },
  },
});
```

`defineObject` registers the type and returns its definition with the namespaced API name, so `employee.apiName` is `com.example.Employee` when you compile with `--apiNamespace com.example`. Pass the returned value wherever another definition needs the object type, such as a link or an action.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `apiName` | `string` | | Required. The API name, without the namespace. |
| `displayName` | `string` | | Required. The singular name shown in Foundry. |
| `pluralDisplayName` | `string` | | Required. The plural name shown in Foundry. |
| `primaryKeyPropertyApiName` | `string` | | Required. The property whose value identifies each object. |
| `titlePropertyApiName` | `string` | | Required. The property shown as each object's title. |
| `properties` | `Record<string, PropertyDefinition>` | | The properties, keyed by API name. See [Properties](#properties). |
| `description` | `string` | | A description shown in Foundry. |
| `icon` | `{ locator: BlueprintIcon; color: string }` | | A [Blueprint](https://blueprintjs.com/docs/#icons) icon name and a hex color. |
| `visibility` | `"PROMINENT" \| "NORMAL" \| "HIDDEN"` | | How prominently Foundry shows the type. |
| `status` | `ObjectTypeStatus` | `"active"` | See [Status](#status). |
| `implementsInterfaces` | `Array<InterfaceImplementation>` | | Interfaces the type implements. See [Interfaces](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ontology-as-code/interfaces.md#implement-an-interface). |
| `datasources` | `Array<DatasourceDefinition>` | A dataset | Where property values come from. See [Datasources](#datasources). |
| `editsEnabled` | `boolean` | | Whether users can edit objects of this type. |
| `editsHistoryConfig` | `{ enabled: boolean; storeAllPreviousProperties?: boolean }` | | Whether to keep a history of edits. |
| `aliases` | `Array<string>` | | Other names to find the type by in search. |
| `includeEmptyBackingDatasource` | `boolean` | | Ask `@osdk/maker-experimental` to package an empty backing dataset. Only valid when every datasource is `dataset` or `derived`. The `maker` CLI ignores it. |
| `permission` | `"roles" \| "publicProject" \| { type: "ontologyPackage"; ontologyPackageRid: string }` | | The permission model for the type. |

## Primary key and title

The primary key and title must both name properties of the object type, and `defineObject` throws if either is missing.

- **Primary key.** Must be a primitive type, such as `string` or `integer`, and cannot be `editOnly`. Every object needs a unique value.
- **Title.** Must be a primitive type, or a struct whose `mainValue` is primitive.

## Properties

Each entry in `properties` maps an API name to a property definition. Only `type` is required. Property API names start with a letter and contain letters, digits, and `_`.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `PropertyTypeType` | | Required. See [Property types](#property-types). |
| `displayName` | `string` | The API name with its first letter capitalized | The name shown in Foundry. |
| `description` | `string` | | A description shown in Foundry. |
| `array` | `boolean` | `false` | Store a list of values of `type`. |
| `reducers` | `Array<{ direction: "ascending" \| "descending"; structField?: string }>` | | For arrays, how to reduce the list to one value for display. |
| `valueType` | `ValueTypeDefinitionVersion` | | A value type from `defineValueType`. Its constraints apply to the property. See [Value types](#value-types). |
| `sharedPropertyType` | `SharedPropertyType` | | Back the property with a shared property type. A shared property type can back only one property per object type. See [Shared property types](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ontology-as-code/interfaces.md#shared-property-types). |
| `nullability` | `{ noNulls: boolean; noEmptyCollections: boolean }` | | Disallow nulls or empty lists. Generated actions make the parameter required when `noNulls` is set. |
| `visibility` | `"PROMINENT" \| "NORMAL" \| "HIDDEN"` | `"NORMAL"` | How prominently Foundry shows the property. |
| `status` | `ObjectTypeStatus` | | The property's status. Must match the object's status unless the object is active. |
| `editOnly` | `boolean` | | The property has no datasource column and only holds values written by edits. |
| `indexedForSearch` | `boolean` | `true`, except `attachment` | Whether the property is searchable. |
| `typeClasses` | `Array<{ kind: string; name: string }>` | `SELECTABLE` and `SORTABLE` render hints | Type classes. `struct`, `geoshape`, `mediaReference`, `geotimeSeries`, `attachment`, and `vector` properties cannot have render hints. |
| `baseFormatter` | `OntologyIrBaseFormatter` | | How Foundry formats values for display. |
| `includeEmptyBackingMediaSet` | `boolean` | | For `mediaReference` properties, ask `@osdk/maker-experimental` to package an empty media set. The `maker` CLI ignores it. |

### Property types

`type` takes a string for most types and an object for types with options.

| Type | Value | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Boolean | `"boolean"` | |
| Integers | `"byte"`, `"short"`, `"integer"`, `"long"` | |
| Decimals | `"float"`, `"double"`, `"decimal"` | `{ type: "decimal", precision?: number, scale?: number }` sets precision and scale, which default to 5 and 2. |
| String | `"string"` | `{ type: "string", ... }` sets search options; see below. |
| Date and time | `"date"`, `"timestamp"` | |
| Attachment | `"attachment"` | |
| Geospatial | `"geopoint"`, `"geoshape"` | |
| Media | `"mediaReference"` | Each `mediaReference` property gets its own media set datasource. |
| Time series | `"geotimeSeries"` | |
| Marking | `{ type: "marking", markingType: "MANDATORY" \| "CBAC", markingInputGroupName: string }` | `markingInputGroupName` names the marking input chosen when the ontology is installed. |
| Struct | `{ type: "struct", structDefinition, mainValue? }` | See [Struct properties](#struct-properties). |
| Vector | `{ type: "vector", dimension: number, supportsSearchWith, embeddingModel?, quantization? }` | `supportsSearchWith` is `"COSINE_SIMILARITY"`, `"DOT_PRODUCT"`, or `"EUCLIDEAN_DISTANCE"`. `dimension` must be an integer of at least 1, and a vector property cannot be an array. |

The object form of `string` accepts `isLongText`, `supportsEfficientLeadingWildcard`, `supportsExactMatching`, `supportsFullTextRegex`, `supportsPhonetic`, `enableAsciiFolding`, and `analyzerOverride`:

```ts title=".ontology/ontology.mts"
import { defineObject } from "@osdk/maker";

export const article = defineObject({
  apiName: "Article",
  displayName: "Article",
  pluralDisplayName: "Articles",
  primaryKeyPropertyApiName: "articleId",
  titlePropertyApiName: "headline",
  properties: {
    articleId: { type: "string" },
    headline: { type: "string" },
    body: { type: { type: "string", isLongText: true, supportsPhonetic: true } },
  },
});
```

### Struct properties

A struct property groups named fields into one value. Each field is a type name, or an object with `fieldType` and `displayMetadata`. Fields cannot be structs, markings, or vectors. `mainValue` names the field or fields that represent the struct when it is shown as a single value, such as a title.

```ts title=".ontology/ontology.mts"
import { defineObject } from "@osdk/maker";

export const customer = defineObject({
  apiName: "Customer",
  displayName: "Customer",
  pluralDisplayName: "Customers",
  primaryKeyPropertyApiName: "customerId",
  titlePropertyApiName: "customerId",
  properties: {
    customerId: { type: "string" },
    address: {
      type: {
        type: "struct",
        structDefinition: {
          street: "string",
          city: "string",
          postcode: {
            fieldType: "string",
            displayMetadata: { displayName: "Postcode", description: "Postal code" },
          },
        },
        mainValue: { fields: "street", type: "string" },
      },
    },
  },
});
```

## Value types

A value type is a reusable, versioned type with constraints, such as "a string that looks like an email address". Define it with `defineValueType`, then reference it from a property with `valueType`. Value types are written to `value-types.json` as well as the IR.

```ts title=".ontology/ontology.mts"
import { defineObject, defineValueType } from "@osdk/maker";

export const emailAddress = defineValueType({
  apiName: "emailAddress",
  displayName: "Email address",
  version: "1.0.0",
  type: {
    type: "string",
    constraints: [
      {
        constraint: {
          type: "regex",
          regex: { regexPattern: "^[^@]+@[^@]+$", usePartialMatch: false },
        },
        failureMessage: { message: "Enter a valid email address." },
      },
    ],
  },
});

export const contact = defineObject({
  apiName: "Contact",
  displayName: "Contact",
  pluralDisplayName: "Contacts",
  primaryKeyPropertyApiName: "contactId",
  titlePropertyApiName: "email",
  properties: {
    contactId: { type: "string" },
    email: { type: "string", valueType: emailAddress },
  },
});
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `apiName` | `string` | | Required. The value type's API name. |
| `displayName` | `string` | | Required. The name shown in Foundry. |
| `version` | `string` | | Required. A semantic version. You can define several versions of the same API name; each version must be unique. |
| `type` | `{ type, constraints? }` | | Required. The base type and its constraints. |
| `description` | `string` | | A description shown in Foundry. |
| `status` | `"active" \| { type: "deprecated"; message: string; deadline: string; replacedBy?: string }` | `"active"` | Deprecate a version. |
| `namespacePrefix` | `boolean` | `false` | Prefix the API name with `--apiNamespace`. |

`type.type` is one of `boolean`, `binary`, `byte`, `short`, `integer`, `long`, `float`, `double`, `decimal`, `string`, `date`, `timestamp`, `array`, `map`, `optional`, or `structV2`. Each entry in `constraints` has a `constraint` for that base type and an optional `failureMessage`. String constraints are `regex`, `oneOf`, `length`, `isUuid`, and `isRid`:

```ts title=".ontology/ontology.mts"
import { defineValueType } from "@osdk/maker";

export const seniority = defineValueType({
  apiName: "seniority",
  displayName: "Seniority",
  version: "1.0.0",
  type: {
    type: "string",
    constraints: [
      {
        constraint: {
          type: "oneOf",
          oneOf: { values: ["junior", "senior", "principal"], useIgnoreCase: false },
        },
      },
    ],
  },
});
```

## Status

`status` is `"active"`, `"experimental"`, `"example"`, or `{ type: "deprecated", message, deadline }`, where `deadline` is an ISO 8601 date or date-time. An experimental, example, or deprecated object type can only contain properties with the same status, and a link to it must have a matching status. See [Link status](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ontology-as-code/links-and-actions.md#status).

```ts title=".ontology/ontology.mts"
import { defineObject } from "@osdk/maker";

export const legacyBadge = defineObject({
  apiName: "LegacyBadge",
  displayName: "Legacy badge",
  pluralDisplayName: "Legacy badges",
  primaryKeyPropertyApiName: "badgeId",
  titlePropertyApiName: "badgeId",
  properties: { badgeId: { type: "string" } },
  status: {
    type: "deprecated",
    message: "Use BadgeScan instead.",
    deadline: "2027-01-01",
  },
});
```

## Datasources

`datasources` says where property values come from. Without it, a dataset backs every property. Give an object type one base datasource (`dataset`, `stream`, `restrictedView`, or `direct`) plus any number of `derived` datasources; `defineObject` throws if you list more than one `dataset`, `stream`, or `restrictedView`. Properties not mapped by a `derived` datasource come from the base datasource.

| `type` | Options | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"dataset"` | `objectSecurityPolicy?`, `propertySecurityGroups?` | A dataset backs the properties. |
| `"stream"` | `retentionPeriod?` | A stream backs the properties. `retentionPeriod` is an ISO 8601 duration, such as `"P90D"`. |
| `"restrictedView"` | | A restricted view backs the properties. |
| `"direct"` | `objectSecurityPolicy?`, `propertySecurityGroups?` | A direct source backs the properties. |
| `"derived"` | `linkDefinition`, `propertyMapping` | Properties computed from linked objects. See [Derived properties](#derived-properties). |

```ts title=".ontology/ontology.mts"
import { defineObject } from "@osdk/maker";

export const badgeScan = defineObject({
  apiName: "BadgeScan",
  displayName: "Badge scan",
  pluralDisplayName: "Badge scans",
  primaryKeyPropertyApiName: "scanId",
  titlePropertyApiName: "scanId",
  properties: {
    scanId: { type: "string" },
    scannedAt: { type: "timestamp" },
  },
  datasources: [{ type: "stream", retentionPeriod: "P90D" }],
});
```

### Property security

On `dataset` and `direct` datasources, `propertySecurityGroups` restricts who can read a set of properties, and `objectSecurityPolicy` restricts who can read the objects. Each takes a `name`, an optional `granularPolicy` condition, and optional `appliedMarkings` and `assumedMarkings` maps from a marking input name to `"CBAC"` or `"MANDATORY"`.

A `granularPolicy` condition is one of:

| Condition | Passes when |
| --- | --- |
| `{ type: "group", name }` | The user is in the group chosen for the input `name` when the ontology is installed. |
| `{ type: "groupProperty", property }` | The user is in a group listed in `property`. |
| `{ type: "markingProperty", property }` | The user satisfies the markings in the marking property `property`. |
| `{ type: "and" \| "or", conditions }` | All or any of `conditions` pass. |

```ts title=".ontology/ontology.mts"
import { defineObject } from "@osdk/maker";

export const caseFile = defineObject({
  apiName: "CaseFile",
  displayName: "Case file",
  pluralDisplayName: "Case files",
  primaryKeyPropertyApiName: "caseId",
  titlePropertyApiName: "caseId",
  properties: {
    caseId: { type: "string" },
    summary: { type: "string" },
    classification: {
      type: { type: "marking", markingType: "MANDATORY", markingInputGroupName: "caseMarkings" },
    },
  },
  datasources: [
    {
      type: "dataset",
      propertySecurityGroups: [
        {
          name: "restrictedSummary",
          properties: ["summary"],
          granularPolicy: {
            type: "and",
            conditions: [
              { type: "markingProperty", property: "classification" },
              { type: "group", name: "investigators" },
            ],
          },
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
});
```

### Derived properties

A `derived` datasource computes properties from objects reached through one or more links. `linkDefinition` lists the links to follow in order, and `propertyMapping` maps each derived property to either a property on the linked object or an aggregation.

| Aggregation | Derived property must be | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{ type: "count" }` | Any | The number of linked objects. |
| `{ type: "sum" \| "avg", property }` | Numeric | The sum or average of `property`. |
| `{ type: "min" \| "max", property }` | Primitive | The smallest or largest value of `property`. |
| `{ type: "approximateCardinality" \| "exactCardinality", property }` | Primitive | The number of distinct values of `property`. |
| `{ type: "collectList" \| "collectSet", property, limit }` | An array | Up to `limit` values of `property`, at most 100. |

Aggregations skip linked objects where the property is null. Generated create and create-or-modify actions leave derived properties out of their parameters.

The link must be defined before the object that uses it. When the object is not defined yet, refer to it from the link by its API name:

```ts title=".ontology/ontology.mts"
import { defineLink, defineObject } from "@osdk/maker";

export const employee = defineObject({
  apiName: "Employee",
  displayName: "Employee",
  pluralDisplayName: "Employees",
  primaryKeyPropertyApiName: "employeeId",
  titlePropertyApiName: "fullName",
  properties: {
    employeeId: { type: "integer" },
    fullName: { type: "string" },
    officeId: { type: "string" },
  },
});

export const officeOccupants = defineLink({
  apiName: "office-occupants",
  one: { object: "Office", metadata: { apiName: "occupants" } },
  toMany: { object: employee, metadata: { apiName: "office" } },
  manyForeignKeyProperty: "officeId",
});

export const office = defineObject({
  apiName: "Office",
  displayName: "Office",
  pluralDisplayName: "Offices",
  primaryKeyPropertyApiName: "officeId",
  titlePropertyApiName: "name",
  properties: {
    officeId: { type: "string" },
    name: { type: "string" },
    headcount: { type: "integer" },
    occupantNames: { type: "string", array: true },
  },
  datasources: [
    { type: "dataset" },
    {
      type: "derived",
      linkDefinition: [{ linkType: officeOccupants }],
      propertyMapping: {
        headcount: { type: "count" },
        occupantNames: { type: "collectList", property: "fullName", limit: 100 },
      },
    },
  ],
});
```

When you compile with `--apiNamespace`, the string reference must include the namespace, such as `"com.example.Office"`.

# What is OSDK

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/overview

> The Ontology SDK gives TypeScript apps a typed client for your Foundry Ontology's objects, links, actions, functions, and interfaces.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Ontology SDK](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/ontology-sdk/overview)
- [Developer Console](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/developer-console/overview)

The Ontology SDK (OSDK) lets you read and write your Foundry Ontology from TypeScript with types generated from your own object types, actions, and functions. Use it in browser apps, Node.js services, and scripts, and add `@osdk/react` to get cached, reactive hooks in React.

## How it works

You pick the Ontology resources your app needs in Developer Console, and Foundry generates an npm package for them, such as `@my-app/sdk`. The generated package contains typed definitions only. The runtime that sends requests, pages results, and applies actions lives in `@osdk/client`, and you pass definitions to it:

```ts
const employees = await client(Employee).fetchPage();
```

| Ontology concept | Generated export | How you use it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Object type | `Employee`, `Office` | `client(Employee).where(...).fetchPage()`, or `useOsdkObjects(Employee)` in React |
| Link type | `$link` on each object | `employee.$link.office.fetchOne()`, or `useLinks` in React |
| Action type | `modifyEmployee` | `client(modifyEmployee).applyAction(...)`, or `useOsdkAction(modifyEmployee)` in React |
| Function (query) | A function definition per query | `client(fn).executeFunction(...)`, or `useOsdkFunction(fn)` in React |
| Interface | One definition per interface | `client(MyInterface).fetchPage()` returns objects of every type that implements it |

Because the SDK holds metadata rather than generated implementation code, its size grows with the number of types you include, unused definitions tree-shake away, and fixes to the client ship as a dependency bump without regenerating your SDK. The generated package also exports namespaces such as `$Objects`, `$Actions`, and `$Queries`, so `import * as Sdk from "@my-app/sdk"` gives you autocomplete over everything in it.

Dates and timestamps arrive as ISO 8601 strings. OSDK does not bundle a date library, so parse them with the one your app already uses.

## Packages

| Package | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `@osdk/client` | The runtime. `createClient` returns the `client` you call with definitions to fetch objects, follow links, apply actions, and execute functions. |
| `@osdk/api` | Shared type definitions that `@osdk/client` and generated SDKs both depend on. Install it alongside `@osdk/client`. |
| Generated SDK (`@my-app/sdk`) | Your Ontology's object types, interfaces, actions, and functions, generated in Developer Console and installed from your Foundry npm registry. |
| `@osdk/oauth` | Token providers: `createPublicOauthClient` for browser apps, `createConfidentialOauthClient` for servers, `createAuthlessClient` for public apps. |
| `@osdk/react` | `OsdkProvider` and hooks such as `useOsdkObjects`, `useOsdkObject`, `useLinks`, `useOsdkAction`, and `useOsdkFunction`, backed by a normalized cache. |
| `@osdk/react-components` | Ontology-aware React components, such as `ObjectTable`, `FilterList`, and `ActionForm`, built on `@osdk/react`. |
| `@osdk/create-app` | A CLI that scaffolds a React, Vue, or Expo app with authentication, client setup, and your SDK already wired in. |
| `@osdk/react-devtools` | A development panel and Vite plugin for inspecting the queries, cache entries, and actions of a running `@osdk/react` app. |

## A first query

Create a client once, then pass it a definition from your SDK. `createClient` takes the Foundry URL, your Ontology RID, and a token provider, here the OAuth client from `@osdk/oauth`:

```ts title="src/client.ts"
import { $ontologyRid } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { createClient } from "@osdk/client";
import { createPublicOauthClient } from "@osdk/oauth";

const foundryUrl = "https://example.palantirfoundry.com";

const auth = createPublicOauthClient(
  "<your-client-id>",
  foundryUrl,
  "http://localhost:8080/auth/callback",
);

export const client = createClient(foundryUrl, $ontologyRid, auth);
```

```ts title="src/listEngineers.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const page = await client(Employee)
  .where({ department: "Engineering" })
  .fetchPage({ $pageSize: 25, $orderBy: { fullName: "asc" } });

for (const employee of page.data) {
  console.log(employee.$primaryKey, employee.fullName);
}
```

In React, wrap your app in `OsdkProvider` with the same client, and read the data with a hook. The hook loads the page, caches it, and re-renders the component when the objects change:

```tsx title="src/EmployeeList.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkObjects } from "@osdk/react";

export function EmployeeList() {
  const { data, isLoading, error } = useOsdkObjects(Employee, {
    where: { department: "Engineering" },
    orderBy: { fullName: "asc" },
    pageSize: 25,
  });

  return (
    <div>
      {isLoading && <p>Loading…</p>}
      {error && <p role="alert">{error.message}</p>}
      <ul>
        {data?.map((employee) => (
          <li key={employee.$primaryKey}>{employee.fullName}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </div>
  );
}
```

See [Create a client](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/client.md) for `OsdkProvider` setup and the full `createClient` reference.

## Why use `@osdk/react`

You can call `@osdk/client` from any data layer, including TanStack Query. `@osdk/react` adds behavior that a generic request cache cannot reproduce because it understands Ontology objects:

- **Normalized object cache.** Each object, such as `Employee:42`, is stored once. When it changes, every list, link, and detail view that contains it re-renders with the new values.
- **Deduplicated requests.** Components that ask for the same objects with the same options share one cache entry and one request.
- **Updates after actions.** An action's response lists the objects it added, modified, and deleted. The cache reloads those objects and re-evaluates affected lists against their `where` clauses, with no manual invalidation.
- **Optimistic updates with rollback.** Pass `$optimisticUpdate` to `applyAction` to show the expected result immediately. If the action fails, the cache restores the previous state.
- **Live data.** `streamUpdates: true` keeps a list current over a WebSocket subscription instead of polling.
- **Function dependencies.** `useOsdkFunction` reruns a function when objects it depends on change, using `dependsOn` for object types or `dependsOnObjects` for specific instances.

Use `@osdk/react` for Ontology data and keep a general-purpose library such as TanStack Query for non-Foundry APIs. The two work side by side. [Caching](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/concepts/caching.md) explains how the cache stores and shares entries.

## Next steps

- [Quickstart](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/quickstart.md): Scaffold a React app with `@osdk/create-app` and run your first query and action.
- [Installation](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/installation.md): Add OSDK packages and your generated SDK to an existing app.
- [Load objects](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/objects.md): Fetch lists and single objects with `useOsdkObjects` and `useOsdkObject`.
- [Components](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/components.md): Build with Ontology-aware tables, filters, and action forms.

# Quickstart

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/quickstart

> Scaffold a React app with @osdk/create-app, sign in to Foundry, and run your first OSDK query and action.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Bootstrap a TypeScript app](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/developer-console/how-to-bootstrapping-typescript)

Use `@osdk/create-app` to generate a React and Vite app that already signs users in, creates an OSDK client, and installs your generated SDK. By the end of this page you have a local app that lists `Employee` objects and applies the `modifyEmployee` action.

To add OSDK to an app you already have, see [Installation](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/installation.md) instead.

## Before you start

You need Node.js and an application in Foundry Developer Console. The CLI asks for these values, so collect them first:

| Value | Example | Where to find it in Developer Console |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Foundry URL | `https://example.palantirfoundry.com` | The URL of your Foundry stack. |
| Application RID | `ri.third-party-applications.main.application.1c66b352-…` | The application's Developer Console URL, `/workspace/developer-console/app/<rid>`. |
| OAuth client ID | `2650385ab6c5e0df3b44aff776b00a42` | **OAuth & scopes**. |
| Ontology RID | `ri.ontology.main.ontology.1df1ce4c-…` | **Ontology SDK**. |
| SDK package name | `@my-app/sdk` | The npm install instructions of a generated SDK version. Must match `@<scope>/sdk`. |
| npm registry URL | `https://example.palantirfoundry.com/artifacts/api/repositories/<repository-rid>/contents/release/npm` | The SDK's npm install instructions. |

In Developer Console, also:

1. Add the object types, link types, actions, and functions your app uses to the application's SDK, then generate a new version on **SDK versions** with the **npm** package type and the latest generator. Generate a new version whenever you change the resources.
2. On **OAuth & scopes**, add `http://localhost:8080/auth/callback` as a redirect URL. The generated app runs on port 8080 and handles the sign-in redirect at that path.
3. Get a Foundry token with access to the SDK's npm registry. The generated `.npmrc` reads it from the `FOUNDRY_TOKEN` environment variable when you install packages.

## Create the app

### Run the CLI

Run `@osdk/create-app` and pass the project directory name:

```npm
npx @osdk/create-app@latest my-osdk-app
```

`npm create @osdk/app@latest` runs the same CLI. The prompts, in order:

| Prompt | Default | Flag |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Project name (letters, digits, `-`, `_`) | `my-osdk-app` | positional `[project]` |
| Framework: React, React (Public), Expo, or Vue | | `--template` |
| Foundry URL (must start with `https://`) | | `--foundryUrl` |
| Do you know your production URL? | | `--applicationUrl` or `--skipApplicationUrl` |
| Application RID | | `--application` |
| OAuth client ID | | `--clientId` |
| Will you use an OSDK? (No means Platform APIs only) | | `--skipOsdk` |
| Ontology RID | | `--ontology` |
| SDK package name | | `--osdkPackage` |
| npm registry URL | | `--osdkRegistryUrl` |
| Include a CORS proxy for local development? | No | `--corsProxy` |
| OAuth scopes | `api:read-data api:write-data api:use-ontologies-read api:use-ontologies-write` | `--scopes` |

Choose **React** for this guide. Answer **Yes** to the CORS proxy unless your Foundry administrator has allowed `http://localhost:8080` as a CORS origin.

To skip every prompt, pass all values as flags:

```npm
npx @osdk/create-app@latest my-osdk-app \
  --template react \
  --foundryUrl https://example.palantirfoundry.com \
  --skipApplicationUrl \
  --application ri.third-party-applications.main.application.<id> \
  --clientId <client-id> \
  --ontology ri.ontology.main.ontology.<id> \
  --osdkPackage @my-app/sdk \
  --osdkRegistryUrl https://example.palantirfoundry.com/artifacts/api/repositories/ri.artifacts.main.repository.<id>/contents/release/npm \
  --corsProxy true
```
### Install dependencies

Export your token so npm can reach your SDK's registry, then install:

```sh
cd my-osdk-app
export FOUNDRY_TOKEN=<token>
npm install
```

A `401` or `404` for `@my-app/sdk` means `FOUNDRY_TOKEN` is missing, expired, or lacks access to the registry.
### Start the dev server

```sh
npm run dev
```

Open `http://localhost:8080`. The app sends you to Foundry to sign in, Foundry redirects back to `/auth/callback`, and the app returns you to the home page. If Foundry reports an invalid redirect URL, add `http://localhost:8080/auth/callback` on **OAuth & scopes** in Developer Console.

index.html
package.json

public/
  resources.json
