```text
  Home.tsx
  main.tsx
  router.tsx
  components/
    ErrorBoundary.tsx
    Header.tsx
    Loading.tsx
    NextSteps.tsx
    Osdk.tsx
```

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.env.development`, `.env.production` | `VITE_FOUNDRY_API_URL`, `VITE_FOUNDRY_CLIENT_ID`, `VITE_FOUNDRY_REDIRECT_URL`, and `VITE_FOUNDRY_ONTOLOGY_RID` for each mode. With the CORS proxy, the development API URL is `http://localhost:8080`. |
| `index.html` | Copies the env values into `<meta>` tags such as `osdk-foundryUrl` and `osdk-clientId`, so you can change configuration without rebuilding JavaScript. |
| `src/client.ts` | Reads the meta tags, creates `auth` with `createPublicOauthClient`, and exports `client` from `createClient`. |
| `src/main.tsx` | Renders the router inside `<OsdkProvider client={client}>`. |
| `src/router.tsx` | Maps `/` to `Home` and `/auth/callback` to `AuthCallback`. |
| `src/AuthCallback.tsx` | Calls `auth.signIn()` to finish the OAuth redirect, then navigates to `/`. |
| `vite.config.ts` | Serves on port 8080, proxies `/api` and `/multipass/api` to Foundry when you chose the CORS proxy, and defines `process.env.NODE_ENV`. See [Use OSDK with Vite](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/guides/vite.md). |
| `.npmrc` | Points your SDK's npm scope at the Foundry registry and authenticates with `${FOUNDRY_TOKEN}`. |
| `foundry.config.json` | Deployment settings for Foundry website hosting with `@osdk/cli`. Delete it if you host elsewhere. |
| `src/env.test.ts` | A test that checks `.env.production` is filled in before you deploy. |

The generated `src/client.ts` looks like this:

```ts title="src/client.ts"
import { createClient, type Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { createPublicOauthClient, type PublicOauthClient } from "@osdk/oauth";

function getMetaTagContent(tagName: string): string {
  const elements = document.querySelectorAll(`meta[name="${tagName}"]`);
  const element = elements.item(elements.length - 1);
  const value = element ? element.getAttribute("content") : null;
  if (value == null || value === "") {
    throw new Error(`Meta tag ${tagName} not found or empty`);
  }
  if (value.match(/%.+%/)) {
    throw new Error(
      `Meta tag ${tagName} contains placeholder value. Please add ${value.replace(
        /%/g,
        "",
      )} to your .env files`,
    );
  }
  return value;
}

const foundryUrl = getMetaTagContent("osdk-foundryUrl");
const clientId = getMetaTagContent("osdk-clientId");
const redirectUrl = getMetaTagContent("osdk-redirectUrl");
const ontologyRid = getMetaTagContent("osdk-ontologyRid");

export const auth: PublicOauthClient = createPublicOauthClient(
  clientId,
  foundryUrl,
  redirectUrl,
);

export const client: Client = createClient(foundryUrl, ontologyRid, auth);

export default client;
```

[Authentication](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/authentication.md) explains the sign-in flow and the callback route. [Create a client](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/client.md) covers `createClient` and `OsdkProvider`.

## Run your first query

Create a component that lists employees with `useOsdkObjects`. Replace `Employee`, `department`, and `fullName` with an object type and properties from your SDK:

```tsx title="src/EmployeeList.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkObjects } from "@osdk/react";
import { PromoteButton } from "./PromoteButton";

export function EmployeeList() {
  const { data, isLoading, error } = useOsdkObjects(Employee, {
    where: { department: "Engineering" },
    orderBy: { fullName: "asc" },
    pageSize: 25,
  });

  return (
    <section>
      {isLoading && <p>Loading…</p>}
      {error && <p role="alert">Could not load employees: {error.message}</p>}
      <ul>
        {data?.map((employee) => (
          <li key={employee.$primaryKey}>
            {employee.fullName} ({employee.jobTitle}){" "}
            <PromoteButton employee={employee} />
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </section>
  );
}
```

Render it from `src/Home.tsx`:

```tsx title="src/Home.tsx"
import React from "react";
import css from "./Home.module.css";
import { EmployeeList } from "./EmployeeList";
import Header from "@/components/Header";

function Home(): React.ReactElement {
  return (
    <div className={css.home}>
      <Header />
      <EmployeeList />
    </div>
  );
}

export default Home;
```

The list keeps rendering while it loads and reloads, so show the loading indicator next to the data instead of in place of it. See [Load objects](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/objects.md) for filters, pagination, and live updates.

## Apply your first action

Add a button that applies `modifyEmployee`. `useOsdkAction` tracks the pending state and the last error, and `applyAction` rethrows, so attach a `catch`:

```tsx title="src/PromoteButton.tsx"
import { type Employee, modifyEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import type { Osdk } from "@osdk/client";
import { useOsdkAction } from "@osdk/react";

export function PromoteButton({ employee }: { employee: Osdk.Instance<Employee> }) {
  const { applyAction, isPending, error } = useOsdkAction(modifyEmployee);

  function handleClick() {
    applyAction({ employee, jobTitle: "Senior Engineer" }).catch((e: unknown) => {
      console.error("modifyEmployee failed", e);
    });
  }

  return (
    <>
      <button type="button" onClick={handleClick} disabled={isPending}>
        {isPending ? "Saving…" : "Promote"}
      </button>
      {error?.actionValidation && <span role="alert">The action is not valid for this employee.</span>}
      {error?.unknown != null && <span role="alert">Something went wrong. Try again.</span>}
    </>
  );
}
```

When the action succeeds, the list updates without a refetch call: the action response tells the cache which objects changed. See [Apply actions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/actions.md) for validation, batches, and optimistic updates.

## Next steps

- [Load objects](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/objects.md): Filter, sort, paginate, and stream updates with `useOsdkObjects`.
- [Apply actions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/actions.md): Validate parameters and show optimistic results.
- [Components](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/components.md): Drop in `ObjectTable`, `FilterList`, and `ActionForm`.
- [Devtools](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/devtools.md): Inspect your app's queries and cache while you develop.

# Troubleshooting

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/troubleshooting

> Fixes for common OSDK errors, including a missing OsdkProvider, mismatched package versions, CORS, auth failures, and Vite build issues.

Find the error message or symptom you see, then apply the fix. Each section names the cause first.

## `No OsdkProvider found. Did you forget to wrap your component tree with <OsdkProvider>?`

A component called an `@osdk/react` hook, or used the client from `useOsdkClient`, outside an `OsdkProvider`. Outside a provider, every hook gets a placeholder client that throws this error.

Render `OsdkProvider` once at the root, above every component that uses OSDK hooks:

```tsx title="src/main.tsx"
import { OsdkProvider } from "@osdk/react";
import ReactDOM from "react-dom/client";
import App from "./App";
import { client } from "./client";

ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById("root")!).render(
  <OsdkProvider client={client}>
    <App />
  </OsdkProvider>,
);
```

If only some components fail, they render outside the provider, for example in a header or a portal mounted next to `<App />`. Move `OsdkProvider` up so it wraps them.

In tests, wrap the component under test in a provider. See [Testing](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/testing.md).

## `"<name>" is not exported by @osdk/client/…/observable.js`

You might also see the same error for `unstable-do-not-use.js` or a path in `@osdk/api`. `@osdk/react` imports its runtime from `@osdk/client/observable`, and your installed `@osdk/client` or `@osdk/api` comes from a different release than your `@osdk/react`.

`@osdk/api`, `@osdk/client`, and `@osdk/react` share one version number. Install the same version of all three, and keep prereleases together:

```npm
npm install @osdk/api@<version> @osdk/client@<version> @osdk/react@<version>
```

Check what is installed with `npm ls @osdk/api @osdk/client @osdk/react`. Do not delete the failing import or downgrade one package on its own. See [Version compatibility](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/installation.md#version-compatibility).

## Peer dependency warnings for `@osdk/client` or `@osdk/api`

The peer ranges that `@osdk/react` declares, such as `^2.15.0`, are broader than what works. Pin `@osdk/api`, `@osdk/client`, and `@osdk/react` to the same version instead of ignoring the warning.

If the warning comes from your generated SDK, the SDK was built against a newer `@osdk/client` than you have. Upgrade the three OSDK packages, or generate a new SDK version. If npm still cannot resolve peers, use `overrides` as shown in [Installation](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/installation.md#version-compatibility).

## `Rollup failed to resolve import "@osdk/foundry.admin"`

The same error can name `@osdk/foundry.core`. You import from `@osdk/react/platform-apis`, which depends on two optional peer packages that are not installed.

Install them:

```npm
npm install @osdk/foundry.admin @osdk/foundry.core
```

If you do not use the platform API hooks, remove the imports from `@osdk/react/platform-apis` instead. See [Platform APIs](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/platform-apis.md).

## `ReferenceError: process is not defined`

OSDK packages read `process.env.NODE_ENV`, and Vite does not replace it by default. Add `"process.env.NODE_ENV": JSON.stringify(mode)` to `define` in your Vite config. See [Use OSDK with Vite](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/guides/vite.md#define-processenvnode_env) for the full config.

## CORS errors in local development

The browser console shows an error like `Access to fetch at 'https://<your-stack>/api/...' from origin 'http://localhost:8080' has been blocked by CORS policy`. Your Foundry environment does not allow requests from your dev server's origin.

Fix it in one of two ways:

- **Allow the origin.** Ask your Foundry administrator to allow `http://localhost:8080` for CORS on your environment.
- **Proxy through Vite.** Forward `/api` and `/multipass/api` to Foundry from the dev server, and set `VITE_FOUNDRY_API_URL=http://localhost:8080`. Requests then go to your own origin, so CORS does not apply. See [Proxy Foundry requests in development](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/guides/vite.md#proxy-foundry-requests-in-development).

Apps created with `@osdk/create-app` include the proxy when you answer yes to the CORS proxy prompt or pass `--corsProxy`. The proxy runs only under `vite dev`, so keep the real Foundry URL in `.env.production`.

## `401 Unauthorized`

The request had no valid token. Check, in order:

1. **Client ID.** The client ID passed to `createPublicOauthClient` matches the one on your application's **OAuth & scopes** page in Developer Console.
2. **Redirect URL.** The redirect URL matches one listed on the same page exactly, including protocol, port, and path, such as `http://localhost:8080/auth/callback`.
3. **Callback route.** Your app renders a route at the redirect path, so the OAuth client can complete sign-in.
4. **Token provider.** The client receives the OAuth client as its token provider: `createClient(foundryUrl, ontologyRid, auth)`.

To detect an expired session in UI code, check `error.statusCode === 401` on a `PalantirApiError`. See [Loading and errors](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/concepts/loading-and-errors.md#narrow-api-errors).

## `403 Forbidden` or `PERMISSION_DENIED`

The token is valid but cannot do what you asked. Common causes:

- **Missing scopes.** The OAuth client requests `api:read-data`, `api:write-data`, `api:use-ontologies-read`, and `api:use-ontologies-write` by default. Other APIs need more. For example, the user and marking hooks in `@osdk/react/platform-apis` need `api:admin-read`. Add the scope to the application in Developer Console, then request it:

  ```ts title="src/client.ts"
  import { createPublicOauthClient } from "@osdk/oauth";

  const clientId = import.meta.env.VITE_FOUNDRY_CLIENT_ID;
  const foundryUrl = import.meta.env.VITE_FOUNDRY_API_URL;
  const redirectUrl = import.meta.env.VITE_FOUNDRY_REDIRECT_URL;

  export const auth = createPublicOauthClient(clientId, foundryUrl, redirectUrl, {
    scopes: [
      "api:use-ontologies-read",
      "api:use-ontologies-write",
      "api:read-data",
      "api:write-data",
      "api:admin-read",
    ],
  });
  ```

  Changing `scopes` signs users in again so the new token carries them. See [Scopes](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/authentication.md#scopes).
- **Resources outside the application's scope.** The object type, action, or function is not included in the application's Ontology SDK resources in Developer Console.
- **User permissions.** The signed-in user cannot see the data or apply the action. Requests made with a public OAuth client act as the signed-in user and never exceed that user's access.

A `NOT_FOUND` error, such as `ObjectNotFound`, can also mean the user lacks access to an object that exists.

## `Invalid ontology RID`

`createClient` throws this when its second argument does not start with `ri.`. The value is often empty, an API name, or a placeholder from an env file. Pass the full Ontology RID, such as `ri.ontology.main.ontology.<uuid>`. Find it on the **Ontology SDK** page of your application in Developer Console, or import `$ontologyRid` from your generated SDK.

## `Meta tag osdk-clientId contains placeholder value`

Apps created with `@osdk/create-app` read their configuration from `<meta>` tags that Vite fills in from `.env` files. This error means a variable, such as `VITE_FOUNDRY_CLIENT_ID`, is not set for the current mode. Add it to `.env.development` or `.env.production` and restart the dev server.

## `Rendered more hooks than during the previous render`

A component called an `@osdk/react` hook conditionally. Call every hook on every render, and use `enabled` to skip the request:

```tsx
const { data } = useOsdkObjects(Employee, { enabled: showEmployees });
const { object } = useOsdkObject(Employee, employeeId, false);
```

## Actions take about a second in development

In development, actions that have an `$optimisticUpdate` wait 1000 ms after the server responds so you can see the optimistic state. The console logs `[@osdk/client] Applied a 1000ms dev-mode delay…` the first time it happens. Production builds never delay. To turn it off in development:

```tsx
<OsdkProvider client={client} devMode={{ actionDelayMs: 0 }}>
  <App />
</OsdkProvider>
```

## Data does not update after a change made elsewhere

The cache updates itself after actions you apply through `useOsdkAction`. It cannot see changes made by other systems, by `@osdk/client` calls outside the hooks, or by REST calls. Invalidate the affected data, or use `streamUpdates: true` on lists that must stay live. See [Caching and reactivity](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/concepts/caching.md) and [Cache invalidation](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/cache-invalidation.md).

## Deprecation warnings for `@osdk/react/experimental`

The hooks from `@osdk/react/experimental` are now exported from `@osdk/react`, and `OsdkProvider2` is now `OsdkProvider`. Change the imports:

```tsx
import { OsdkProvider, useOsdkObjects } from "@osdk/react";
```

The `experimental` entry point will be removed in a future major version.

## The devtools panel does not appear

| Symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| No panel. | Confirm `osdkDevTools()` from `@osdk/react-devtools/vite` is in your Vite `plugins` and you run `vite dev`. Pass `osdkDevTools({ verbose: true })` and look for `Injected devtools into HTML` in the terminal. |
| Panel shows no data. | The screen must read data through `@osdk/react` hooks under `OsdkProvider`. The panel does not see raw `fetch` calls. |
| Component inspection is unavailable. | Something loaded React before the devtools script. Remove scripts in `index.html` that load React first. |

See the [devtools troubleshooting table](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/devtools.md#troubleshooting) for more.

# Custom widgets

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/widgets

> Build React or plain TypeScript widgets that run inside Foundry UIs such as Workshop, exchange parameters and events with the host, and call the OSDK.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Custom widgets](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/custom-widgets/overview)
- [Create a widget set](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/custom-widgets/create)

{/* cspell:ignore widgetregistry */}

A custom widget is a web page you build with Vite that Foundry embeds inside a host UI such as Workshop. The host passes values into the widget as parameters, the widget sends events back to update them, and the widget can read and write your Ontology through the OSDK.

## How it works

Widgets ship in a **widget set**, a Foundry resource with a RID such as `ri.widgetregistry..widget-set.<id>`. One project builds one widget set, and each HTML entrypoint in its Vite config becomes one widget in the set. You deploy the set as numbered versions, and the host loads the scripts and stylesheets that the version's manifest lists.

Each widget declares its contract in a config file built with `defineConfig`: an ID and name, the parameters the host can set, and the events the widget can emit. At build time, `@osdk/widget.vite-plugin` turns those configs into the manifest at `.palantir/widgets.config.json`, which tells Foundry what to show in the widget's setup panel. See [Parameters and events](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/widgets/parameters-and-events.md).

At runtime the host injects `window.__PALANTIR_WIDGET_API__` into the widget's page, and the two sides exchange typed messages through it:

| Message | Direction | Payload | When |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `widget.ready` | Widget to host | `{ apiVersion: "1.0.0" }` | The widget is listening and wants its first parameter values. |
| `host.update-parameters` | Host to widget | `{ parameters }`, one async value per parameter ID | Parameter values or their loading states change. |
| `widget.emit-event` | Widget to host | `{ eventId, parameterUpdates }` | The widget fires one of its declared events. |
| `widget.resize` | Widget to host | `{ width, height }` of the document body's border box | The widget's content changes size. |
| `widget.reload` | Widget to host | `{}` | The widget needs a full reload, such as a Vite full-page reload in development. |

`FoundryWidget` from `@osdk/widget.client-react` sends `widget.ready`, `widget.resize`, and `widget.reload` for you and exposes the rest through a hook. See [React widgets](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/widgets/react.md).

## Packages

| Package | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `@osdk/widget.api` | The contract itself: message, manifest, and parameter value types, `BrowserPermission`, and `MANIFEST_FILE_LOCATION`. `@osdk/widget.client` re-exports the parts you need, so you rarely import it directly. |
| `@osdk/widget.client` | `defineConfig` for widget configs, `createFoundryWidgetClient` for widgets without React, and `createFoundryWidgetTokenProvider` for OSDK clients inside a widget. |
| `@osdk/widget.client-react` | The `FoundryWidget` provider and the `useFoundryWidgetContext` hook. Supports React 18 and 19. |
| `@osdk/widget.vite-plugin` | Generates the manifest during `vite build` and runs developer mode during `vite`. Supports Vite 6 and 7. |
| `@osdk/create-widget` | A CLI that scaffolds a React widget set project with all of the above wired in. |
| `@osdk/cli` | `osdk widgetset deploy` and `osdk widgetset version` for publishing and managing versions. See [Build and publish](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/widgets/publish.md). |

## Create a widget set project

Before you start, you need:

1. A widget set in Foundry and its RID, `ri.widgetregistry..widget-set.<id>`.
2. A Foundry token in the `FOUNDRY_TOKEN` environment variable. Developer mode, `osdk widgetset deploy`, and installing your SDK package from Foundry's npm registry all read it.
3. To call the Ontology, the name of your widget set's SDK package, such as `@my-app/sdk`, and the URL of the npm registry that hosts it. The registry URL has the form `https://<stack>/artifacts/api/repositories/ri.artifacts.main.repository.<id>/contents/release/npm`.

### Run the CLI

```npm
npx @osdk/create-widget@latest my-osdk-widget
```

`npm create @osdk/widget@latest` runs the same CLI. It prompts for each value you do not pass as a flag:

| Prompt | Flag | Accepted values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Project name | positional `[project]` | Letters, digits, `-`, and `_`. Defaults to `my-osdk-widget`. |
| Overwrite the existing directory? | `--overwrite` | Asked only if the directory exists. `--overwrite` removes its files; `--no-overwrite` keeps them and writes over matching paths. |
| Framework | `--template` | `widget-react`, listed as **OSDK React**: React, Vite, and Blueprint. |
| OSDK version | `--sdkVersion` | `2.x`, the only version the React template supports. Not prompted unless the value is invalid. |
| Foundry URL | `--foundryUrl` | Must start with `https://`, such as `https://example.palantirfoundry.com`. |
| Will you be using an OSDK? | `--skipOsdk` | Passing `--osdkPackage` or `--osdkRegistryUrl` answers yes. `--skipOsdk` answers no and conflicts with both. |
| OSDK package name | `--osdkPackage` | Must match `@<scope>/sdk`, such as `@my-app/sdk`. |
| npm registry URL | `--osdkRegistryUrl` | The Foundry Artifacts URL ending in `/contents/release/npm`. |
| Widget set RID | `--widgetSet` | `ri.widgetregistry..widget-set.<id>`. |
| None | `--repository` | Optional code repository RID, written to `foundry.config.json` for `osdk widgetset deploy`. |

To skip every prompt:

```npm
npx @osdk/create-widget@latest my-osdk-widget \
  --template widget-react \
  --foundryUrl https://example.palantirfoundry.com \
  --widgetSet ri.widgetregistry..widget-set.<id> \
  --osdkPackage @my-app/sdk \
  --osdkRegistryUrl https://example.palantirfoundry.com/artifacts/api/repositories/ri.artifacts.main.repository.<id>/contents/release/npm
```
### Install dependencies

```sh
cd my-osdk-widget
export FOUNDRY_TOKEN=<token>
npm install
```

The generated `.npmrc` sends `FOUNDRY_TOKEN` to your Foundry npm registry, so a `401` or `404` for your SDK package means the token is missing, expired, or lacks access.
### Start developer mode

```sh
npm run dev
```

The terminal prints a setup URL. Open it to load your local widgets in Foundry, as described in [Run locally](#run-locally).

## Project layout

```text
.gitignore
.npmrc
README.md
eslint.config.mjs
foundry.config.json
index.html
package.json
tsconfig.json
tsconfig.node.json
vite.config.ts
src/
  client.ts
  main.config.ts
  main.css
  main.tsx
  useDarkTheme.ts
  vite-env.d.ts
  Widget.module.css
  Widget.tsx
```

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `foundry.config.json` | The Foundry URL and widget set settings that the Vite plugin and `osdk widgetset deploy` read. See [Build and publish](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/widgets/publish.md#foundryconfigjson). |
| `.npmrc` | Points your SDK package's scope at your Foundry registry and authenticates with `${FOUNDRY_TOKEN}`. Only generated with an OSDK. |
| `vite.config.ts` | Adds `@vitejs/plugin-react` and `@osdk/widget.vite-plugin`, serves on port 8080 with CORS enabled, and lists `./index.html` as the build input. |
| `index.html` | The widget's entrypoint. It loads `/src/main.tsx`. |
| `src/main.config.ts` | The widget config: ID `widgetId`, a `greetingName` string parameter, a `counterValue` number parameter, and a `setCounterValue` event. |
| `src/main.tsx` | Renders `Widget` inside `FoundryWidget`, and inside `OsdkProvider` when you use an OSDK. Importing `main.config.ts` here is what lets the Vite plugin find it. |
| `src/client.ts` | Creates the OSDK client. Only generated with an OSDK. |
| `src/Widget.tsx` | Reads both parameters, increments the counter every second by emitting `setCounterValue`, and renders a reset button. |
| `src/useDarkTheme.ts` | Tracks `prefers-color-scheme: dark` so the widget can apply Blueprint's dark theme. |

Without an OSDK, the CLI omits `.npmrc` and `src/client.ts`, and `package.json` drops `@osdk/client`, `@osdk/react`, and the SDK package.

The `package.json` scripts:

| Script | Command | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dev` | `vite` | Starts the dev server and developer mode. |
| `build` | `tsc && vite build` | Typechecks, builds to `dist/`, and writes `dist/.palantir/widgets.config.json`. |
| `lint` | `eslint . --report-unused-disable-directives --max-warnings 0` | Lints the project. |
| `test` | `vitest run --passWithNoTests` | Runs tests. |
| `preview` | `vite preview` | Serves the production build locally. |

## Run locally

Developer mode loads widget code from your dev server into Foundry, so you can preview changes against real host data without deploying a version.

### Start the dev server

Export `FOUNDRY_TOKEN` and run `npm run dev`. The plugin stops with `FOUNDRY_TOKEN environment variable not found` if the variable is missing. Instead of the usual local URL, Vite prints:

```txt
➜  Click to enter developer mode for your widget set: http://localhost:8080/.palantir/setup/
```
### Open the setup URL

The setup page loads each HTML entrypoint so Vite parses its widget config, then builds a development manifest whose scripts point at your dev server. It sends that manifest for the widget set in `foundry.config.json` to Foundry, enables developer mode, and redirects you to the widget set's preview page at `<foundryUrl>/workspace/custom-widgets/preview/<widgetSetRid>`.

If a widget's config is never found, the page gives up after 10 attempts with `Timed out waiting for widget config files to be parsed. Are you sure a widget config is imported?`.
### Edit your code

Component changes reach the embedded widget through Vite hot module replacement. A change to a widget config file does not: the terminal warns that the config changed, and you open the setup URL again to send the new parameters and events to Foundry.

You do not need to publish a widget set before developing on it. To place the widget in a Workshop module, publish a version once so the widget appears in Workshop's **Widget setup** panel. See [Build and publish](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/widgets/publish.md).

### Code Workspaces

In Foundry Code Workspaces, run Vite in the `code-workspaces` mode instead:

```json title="package.json"
{
  "scripts": {
    "dev:remote": "vite --mode code-workspaces"
  }
}
```

In this mode the plugin reads the Foundry URL from `FOUNDRY_PROXY_URL`, the token from the file named by `FOUNDRY_PROXY_TOKEN`, and the dev server address from `DEV_SERVER_DOMAIN` and `DEV_SERVER_BASE_PATH`, all set by the workspace. Open the preview panel to enter developer mode, and refresh it after you change a widget config. The plugin warns when you run `npm run dev` inside a workspace, or the `code-workspaces` mode outside one.

## Use the OSDK in a widget

Inside Foundry, a widget authenticates through the host instead of OAuth. Create the client against the page origin with the widget token provider:

```ts title="src/client.ts"
import { $ontologyRid } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { createClient } from "@osdk/client";
import { createFoundryWidgetTokenProvider } from "@osdk/widget.client";

export const client = createClient(
  window.location.origin,
  $ontologyRid,
  createFoundryWidgetTokenProvider(),
);
```

`createFoundryWidgetTokenProvider` resolves to a placeholder that Foundry replaces with real credentials on each request. Pass the client to `FoundryWidget`, which needs it to resolve object set parameters, and to `OsdkProvider` so `@osdk/react` hooks work inside the widget:

```tsx title="src/main.tsx"
import { OsdkProvider } from "@osdk/react";
import { FoundryWidget } from "@osdk/widget.client-react";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
import { client } from "./client.js";
import MainConfig from "./main.config.js";
import { Widget } from "./Widget.js";

createRoot(document.getElementById("root")!).render(
  <FoundryWidget config={MainConfig} client={client}>
    <OsdkProvider client={client}>
      <Widget />
    </OsdkProvider>
  </FoundryWidget>,
);
```

From there, query with the hooks in [Query objects](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/objects.md) or read object sets the host passes in, as shown in [React widgets](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/widgets/react.md#object-set-parameters). At build time, the Vite plugin also lists every installed package whose `package.json` has an `osdk.packageRid` field, with its version, in the manifest's `inputSpec`.

## Build a widget without React

`createFoundryWidgetClient` from `@osdk/widget.client` speaks the same protocol without a framework. Outside a Foundry host or developer mode, it throws `Invariant failed: [FoundryWidgetClient] Missing __PALANTIR_WIDGET_API__ in window`.

```ts title="src/main.ts"
import { createFoundryWidgetClient } from "@osdk/widget.client";
import MainConfig from "./main.config.js";

const widget = createFoundryWidgetClient<typeof MainConfig>();

widget.hostEventTarget.addEventListener("host.update-parameters", (event) => {
  const greeting = event.detail.parameters.greetingName?.value;
  if (greeting?.type === "loaded" || greeting?.type === "reloading") {
    document.body.textContent = `Hello, ${greeting.value ?? "World"}!`;
  }
});

document.body.addEventListener("click", () => {
  widget.emitEvent("setCounterValue", {
    parameterUpdates: { counterValue: 0 },
  });
});

new ResizeObserver(() => {
  const { width, height } = document.body.getBoundingClientRect();
  widget.resize({ width, height });
}).observe(document.body);

widget.subscribe();
widget.ready();
```

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `subscribe()` | Starts forwarding host messages to `hostEventTarget`. Call it before `ready()`. |
| `unsubscribe()` | Stops forwarding host messages. |
| `ready()` | Sends `widget.ready` so the host sends the first parameter values. |
| `emitEvent(eventId, { parameterUpdates })` | Sends `widget.emit-event`. Typed against the events in your config. |
| `resize({ width, height })` | Sends `widget.resize`. |
| `reload()` | Sends `widget.reload`. |
| `sendMessage(message)` | Sends any widget message. Prefer the methods above. |
| `hostEventTarget` | An `EventTarget` that dispatches `host.update-parameters` with the message payload in `event.detail`. |

- [Parameters and events](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/widgets/parameters-and-events.md): Every parameter type, event, permission, and how they map to the manifest.
- [React widgets](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/widgets/react.md): Read parameters, emit events, and handle loading states with `FoundryWidget`.
