# Parameters and events

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/widgets/parameters-and-events

> Declare a widget's parameters, events, and browser permissions with defineConfig, and see how each field maps to the widgets.config.json manifest.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Parameters and events](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/custom-widgets/parameters-and-events)

{/* cspell:ignore widgetregistry */}

A widget config declares what the host can pass into your widget and what the widget can send back. Write one per widget with `defineConfig` from `@osdk/widget.client`. The config also types your React hooks, and the Vite plugin turns it into the manifest Foundry reads.

## Define a config

```ts title="src/main.config.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { defineConfig } from "@osdk/widget.client";

export default defineConfig({
  id: "employeeDirectory",
  name: "Employee directory",
  description: "Lists employees and reports the selected one",
  type: "workshop",
  parameters: {
    title: {
      displayName: "Title",
      type: "string",
    },
    employees: {
      displayName: "Employees",
      type: "objectSet",
      allowedType: Employee,
    },
    selectedEmployeeId: {
      displayName: "Selected employee ID",
      type: "number",
    },
    departments: {
      displayName: "Departments",
      type: "array",
      subType: "string",
    },
  },
  events: {
    selectEmployee: {
      displayName: "Select employee",
      parameterUpdateIds: ["selectedEmployeeId"],
    },
  },
});
```

Export the config as the file's default export, name the file `*.config.ts` (or `.js`, `.tsx`, `.jsx`), and import it from the widget's entrypoint script. The Vite plugin finds configs through that import; see [Build and publish](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/widgets/publish.md#how-the-plugin-finds-configs).

`defineConfig` returns its argument unchanged. Its `const` type parameter keeps parameter IDs, types, and `parameterUpdateIds` as literal types, which is what lets `useFoundryWidgetContext` and `emitEvent` type-check against your config.

## Config fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | Required | Unique within the widget set. camelCase: letters and digits only, starting with a lowercase letter. At most 100 characters. |
| `name` | `string` | Required | The name shown in the host. At most 100 characters. |
| `description` | `string` | | Shown in the host. At most 250 characters. |
| `type` | `"workshop"` | Required | The host the widget targets. `"workshop"` is the only value. |
| `parameters` | `Record<string, ParameterDefinition>` | Required | Values the host passes in, keyed by parameter ID. Use `{}` for none. |
| `events` | `Record<string, EventDefinition>` | Required | Events the widget can emit, keyed by event ID. Use `{}` for none. |
| `permissions` | `BrowserPermission[]` | | Extra browser capabilities the widget requests. See [Permissions](#permissions). |
| `refreshHostDataOnAction` | `boolean` | Plugin default, else unset | Asks the host to refresh the Ontology data it passes in, currently object set parameters, when the widget is thought to have applied an action through the Ontology APIs. |

TypeScript cannot check ID formats and lengths, so the Vite plugin validates them when it loads the config and fails the build or developer mode with messages such as `Widget id "my-widget" does not match allowed pattern (must be camelCase)`.

## Parameter types

Every parameter needs a `type` and a `displayName`, the label shown in the host's setup panel. Parameter IDs follow the same camelCase rule and 100-character limit as widget IDs.

| `type` | Extra fields | Value in the widget | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `"string"` | | `string` | |
| `"number"` | | `number` | |
| `"boolean"` | | `boolean` | |
| `"date"` | | `string` | An ISO date, `YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| `"timestamp"` | | `string` | An ISO datetime. |
| `"scenario"` | | `string` | A Scenario RID. |
| `"array"` | `subType` | An array of the `subType` value | `subType` is any of the six types above. |
| `"objectSet"` | `allowedType` | `{ objectSetRid: string }` | `allowedType` is an object type or interface from your generated SDK, such as `Employee` or `Worker`. In React, the value also carries a hydrated `objectSet`; see [React widgets](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/widgets/react.md#object-set-parameters). |
| `"mapTileLayer"` | | `{ tileSourceId: string }` | Read-only: a tile source ID for the Foundry Tiles APIs. Events cannot update it. |

An `objectSet` parameter needs the RID that generated SDKs embed in each type definition. If it is missing, the plugin fails with `ObjectSet parameter "employees" must have a valid rid in its metadata, make sure your OSDK was generated with a generator version >=2.6.2`. The older `objectType` field is deprecated; use `allowedType`.

Dates and timestamps stay strings. Parse them with the date library your widget already uses.

### Loading states

The host sends each parameter as an async value, so your widget can show what is still loading. The `type` field moves through these states:

| `type` | `value` | `error` | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `"not-started"` | | | The host has not started loading the value. |
| `"loading"` | | | The first load is in progress. |
| `"loaded"` | The value, or `undefined` | | The value is ready. `undefined` means the host variable has no value. |
| `"reloading"` | The previous value | | A new value is loading. |
| `"failed"` | The last value, if any | `Error` | Loading failed. |

The types are exported from `@osdk/widget.client` as `AsyncValue`, `AsyncLoadedValue`, `AsyncFailedValue`, and so on. [React widgets](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/widgets/react.md#loading-states) covers how `FoundryWidget` combines them.

## Events

An event tells the host to update one or more of the widget's parameters. Declare each event with a label and the parameters it updates:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `displayName` | `string` | The event name shown in the host, where builders attach behavior to it. |
| `parameterUpdateIds` | `string[]` | The parameter IDs the event sets. Each must be a parameter in the same config, and none can be a `mapTileLayer` parameter. |

When you emit the event, `parameterUpdates` must contain a value for every ID in `parameterUpdateIds`, typed like the parameter's value:

```ts
emitEvent("selectEmployee", {
  parameterUpdates: { selectedEmployeeId: 42 },
});
```

To fire an event without updating anything, set `parameterUpdateIds: []` and emit `parameterUpdates: {}`. Listing a `mapTileLayer` parameter is a type error, and the plugin rejects it with `Event "selectTile" cannot update read-only map tile layer parameter "tiles"`.

## Permissions

A widget runs in a sandboxed frame. Request extra capabilities with `permissions`:

```ts title="src/main.config.ts"
import { defineConfig } from "@osdk/widget.client";

export default defineConfig({
  id: "badgeScanner",
  name: "Badge scanner",
  type: "workshop",
  parameters: {},
  events: {},
  permissions: ["camera", "allow-downloads"],
});
```

| Value | Requests |
| --- | --- |
| `"camera"` | The `camera` permissions policy. |
| `"microphone"` | The `microphone` permissions policy. |
| `"autoplay"` | The `autoplay` permissions policy. |
| `"allow-downloads"` | The `allow-downloads` sandbox flag. |
| `"allow-forms"` | The `allow-forms` sandbox flag. |
| `"allow-modals"` | The `allow-modals` sandbox flag. |
| `"allow-popups"` | The `allow-popups` sandbox flag. |

The same values are available as constants on `BrowserPermission` from `@osdk/widget.api`, such as `BrowserPermission.CAMERA`. A request does not guarantee access: the user may still need to accept a browser prompt, depending on the permission and browser settings.

## How the config maps to the manifest

`vite build` writes one manifest per widget set to `.palantir/widgets.config.json` in the build output. Each widget's config becomes an entry under `widgetSet.widgets`, keyed by widget ID. For the config at the top of this page, the manifest looks like this:

```json title="dist/.palantir/widgets.config.json"
{
  "manifestVersion": "1.0.0",
  "widgetSet": {
    "rid": "ri.widgetregistry..widget-set.<id>",
    "version": "1.2.0",
    "widgets": {
      "employeeDirectory": {
        "id": "employeeDirectory",
        "name": "Employee directory",
        "description": "Lists employees and reports the selected one",
        "type": "workshopWidgetV1",
        "entrypointJs": [{ "path": "assets/index-Bx1a2b3c.js", "type": "module" }],
        "entrypointCss": [{ "path": "assets/index-Dq4e5f6g.css" }],
        "parameters": {
          "title": { "displayName": "Title", "type": "string" },
          "employees": {
            "type": "objectSet",
            "displayName": "Employees",
            "objectTypeRids": ["ri.ontology.main.object-type.<id>"],
            "allowedType": "ri.ontology.main.object-type.<id>"
          },
          "selectedEmployeeId": { "displayName": "Selected employee ID", "type": "number" },
          "departments": { "displayName": "Departments", "type": "array", "subType": "string" }
        },
        "events": {
          "selectEmployee": {
            "displayName": "Select employee",
            "parameterUpdateIds": ["selectedEmployeeId"]
          }
        }
      }
    },
    "inputSpec": {
      "discovered": {
        "sdks": [{ "rid": "ri.third-party-applications.main.sdk-package.<id>", "version": "1.0.0" }]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

| Manifest field | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `widgetSet.rid` | `widgetSet.rid` in `foundry.config.json`. |
| `widgetSet.version` | `widgetSet.autoVersion` in `foundry.config.json`; by default the `version` in `package.json`. See [Versioning](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/widgets/publish.md#versioning). |
| `widgets.<id>` | One entry per HTML entrypoint, keyed by the config's `id`. Two widgets with the same ID fail the build with `Duplicate widget ID`. |
| `id`, `name`, `description`, `events`, `permissions` | Copied from the config. |
| `type` | `"workshop"` becomes `"workshopWidgetV1"`. |
| `entrypointJs`, `entrypointCss` | The script and stylesheet tags in the built HTML file, in order, with the leading `/` removed. |
| `parameters` | Copied from the config, except `objectSet`: `allowedType` becomes the type's RID, and `objectTypeRids` holds the object type RID, or is empty for an interface. |
| `refreshHostDataOnAction` | The config's value, else the plugin's `defaults.refreshHostDataOnAction`. |
| `inputSpec.discovered.sdks` | The `rid` and `version` of every installed package whose `package.json` has an `osdk.packageRid`. |
| `inputSpec.discovered.authorizations` | `authorizations.read` and `authorizations.requiredRead` from `resources.json` in the project root, when that file exists. |

Fields without a value, such as an unset `permissions`, are left out of the JSON. In developer mode the plugin sends Foundry the same widget entries, but with `entrypointJs` pointing at your dev server.

# Build and publish

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/widgets/publish

> Configure @osdk/widget.vite-plugin, build a widget set and its manifest, deploy versions with osdk widgetset deploy, and manage them.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Publish a widget set](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/custom-widgets/publish)

{/* cspell:ignore widgetregistry widgetset */}

Publishing a widget set takes two commands: `vite build` produces your widget files and a manifest, and `osdk widgetset deploy` uploads them to Foundry as a new version. This page covers the Vite plugin, `foundry.config.json`, versioning, and the CLI.

## Add the Vite plugin

`@osdk/widget.vite-plugin` writes the manifest during `vite build` and runs [developer mode](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/widgets.md#run-locally) during `vite`. Projects from `@osdk/create-widget` already include it.

```npm
npm install -D @osdk/widget.vite-plugin
```

```ts title="vite.config.ts"
import foundryWidgetPlugin from "@osdk/widget.vite-plugin";
import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react";
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), foundryWidgetPlugin()],
  server: {
    port: 8080,
    cors: true,
  },
  build: {
    rollupOptions: {
      input: ["./index.html"],
    },
  },
});
```

The plugin supports Vite 6 and 7. It takes one optional argument:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaults.refreshHostDataOnAction` | `boolean` | | The `refreshHostDataOnAction` value for every widget whose config does not set it. See [Config fields](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/widgets/parameters-and-events.md#config-fields). |

```ts title="vite.config.ts"
foundryWidgetPlugin({ defaults: { refreshHostDataOnAction: true } });
```

## How the plugin finds configs

Each HTML file in `build.rollupOptions.input` is one widget. For each one, the plugin looks for a widget config among the modules its entry script imports:

- The file name, minus its extension, ends in `.config`, such as `main.config.ts`.
- The file lives under `src/` and the entrypoint script imports it directly. Developer mode only tracks direct imports.
- The default export is the config from `defineConfig`.

If you do not need the config object at runtime, a side-effect import such as `import "./main.config.js";` is enough. Each entrypoint must import exactly one config.

## Build multiple widgets

Add an HTML file per widget, each loading its own script that imports its own config:

```text
index.html
second.html
vite.config.ts
src/
  main.tsx
  main.config.ts
  second.tsx
  second.config.ts
```

Then list every HTML file as a build input. Both the array and object forms of `input` work:

```ts title="vite.config.ts"
import foundryWidgetPlugin from "@osdk/widget.vite-plugin";
import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react";
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), foundryWidgetPlugin()],
  build: {
    rollupOptions: {
      input: ["./index.html", "./second.html"],
    },
  },
});
```

The build writes one manifest with an entry per widget, keyed by each config's `id`, so every widget in the set needs a different ID.

## Build

```sh
npm run build
```

The template's `build` script runs `tsc && vite build`. Vite writes your HTML, scripts, and styles to its output directory, `dist/` by default, and the plugin then adds the manifest:

```text
dist/
  index.html
  assets/
    index-[hash].js
    index-[hash].css
  .palantir/
    widgets.config.json
```

To write the manifest, the plugin reads each built HTML file for its script and stylesheet tags, evaluates each widget config in a separate Vite server, computes the version, and scans `package.json` dependencies for SDK packages. [Parameters and events](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/widgets/parameters-and-events.md#how-the-config-maps-to-the-manifest) shows the result field by field.

Build errors from the plugin:

| Error | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `foundry.config.json file not found.` | No `foundry.config.json` in the working directory or any parent. |
| `No widget config files found for entrypoint ...` | The entrypoint does not import a `*.config` module. |
| `Multiple widget config files found for entrypoint ...` | The entrypoint's bundle includes more than one `*.config` module. |
| `No default export found in ...` | The config file has no default export. |
| `Duplicate widget ID: ...` | Two configs share an `id`. |
| `Entrypoint chunk not found for input file: ...` | The built HTML's script paths do not match a bundle entry. Keep Vite's `base` at its default, `/`. |
| `Unexpected inline content found in Vite HTML output` | The built HTML has an inline `<script>` or `<link>` with content. Load scripts with `src`. |
| `Unexpected ... attribute found in Vite HTML output` | A `<script>` has attributes other than `src`, `type`, and `crossorigin`, or a stylesheet `<link>` has attributes other than `rel`, `href`, and `crossorigin`. |
| `Invalid script type attribute found in Vite HTML output: ...` | A `<script>` `type` other than `module` or `text/javascript`. |
| `The version string ... is not SemVer compliant.` | The computed version is not valid SemVer. See [Versioning](#versioning). |

Config validation errors, such as a widget ID that is not camelCase, are listed in [Parameters and events](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/widgets/parameters-and-events.md#config-fields).

## `foundry.config.json`

The plugin and `osdk widgetset` commands read `foundry.config.json` from the working directory or the nearest parent. `@osdk/create-widget` writes it for you:

```json title="foundry.config.json"
{
  "foundryUrl": "https://example.palantirfoundry.com",
  "widgetSet": {
    "rid": "ri.widgetregistry..widget-set.<id>",
    "directory": "./dist",
    "autoVersion": {
      "type": "package-json"
    }
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `foundryUrl` | `string` | Required | Your Foundry stack. Developer mode and the CLI send requests here. |
| `widgetSet.rid` | `string` | Required | The widget set RID, written to the manifest and used as the deploy target. |
| `widgetSet.directory` | `string` | Required | The build output to deploy. Match Vite's `build.outDir`. |
| `widgetSet.repository` | `string` | | A code repository RID to publish through instead of the widget set. See [Deploy](#deploy). |
| `widgetSet.autoVersion` | `{ type: "package-json" }` or `{ type: "git-describe", tagPrefix?: string }` | `package-json` | How the build computes the version. |

The file is validated on load. Unknown top-level fields fail with `does not match the expected schema`.

## Versioning

Every deployed version needs a [SemVer](https://semver.org) version string. The build computes it once and writes it to the manifest's `widgetSet.version`; `osdk widgetset deploy` reads it from there and has no version flag.

**package-json**

The default. The version is the `version` field of the nearest `package.json`. Bump it, then rebuild before you deploy:

```sh
npm version minor
npm run build
```
**git-describe**

The version comes from `git describe --tags --first-parent --dirty`:

```json title="foundry.config.json"
{
  "foundryUrl": "https://example.palantirfoundry.com",
  "widgetSet": {
    "rid": "ri.widgetregistry..widget-set.<id>",
    "directory": "./dist",
    "autoVersion": {
      "type": "git-describe",
      "tagPrefix": ""
    }
  }
}
```

With an empty `tagPrefix`, the build uses the most recent tag reachable from `HEAD` and strips a leading `v`, so `v1.4.0` becomes `1.4.0`. With a prefix such as `widgets/`, it only matches tags that start with the prefix and strips it, so `widgets/1.4.0` becomes `1.4.0`. Commits after the tag and uncommitted changes add a suffix such as `1.4.0-3-g1a2b3c4-dirty`. The build fails if git is missing, the directory is not a repository, or no tag matches.

## Deploy

`osdk widgetset deploy` from `@osdk/cli` zips the build output and publishes it as a new version.

### Build

```sh
npm run build
```
### Deploy

```sh
export FOUNDRY_TOKEN=<token>
npx @osdk/cli@latest widgetset deploy
```

The CLI reads the version from `.palantir/widgets.config.json` in the directory, zips everything in the directory, and uploads it. When `repository` is set, it uploads to that code repository on behalf of the widget set, which works only if the repository is authorized to publish the widget set. It passes the current git branch along, unless HEAD is detached or the project is not a git repository.

Every option defaults to the matching `foundry.config.json` field where one exists:

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--widgetSet` | `widgetSet.rid` | The widget set RID. |
| `--foundryUrl` | `foundryUrl` | The Foundry URL. Must start with `https://`. |
| `--directory` | `widgetSet.directory` | The directory to upload. It must contain `.palantir/widgets.config.json`. |
| `--repository` | `widgetSet.repository` | A code repository RID to publish through. |
| `--branchName` | The current git branch | The branch to publish from. |
| `--token` | | A Foundry token. Conflicts with `--tokenFile`. |
| `--tokenFile` | | A file containing a Foundry token. |
| `--verbose`, `-v` | | Verbose logging. Repeat for more. |

Without `--token` or `--tokenFile`, the CLI reads `FOUNDRY_TOKEN`. The deprecated `FOUNDRY_SDK_AUTH_TOKEN` still works with a warning. The token must be a JWT.

After the first version is published, the widget appears in Workshop's **Widget setup** panel. Until then you can still preview it with [developer mode](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/widgets.md#run-locally).

## Manage versions

The same options select the widget set and credentials:

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `osdk widgetset version list` | Lists published versions, newest first, for the current git branch or `--branchName`. |
| `osdk widgetset version info <version>` | Prints the details of one version as JSON. |
| `osdk widgetset version delete <version>` | Deletes a version after a confirmation prompt. `--yes` or `-y` skips the prompt. Deletion cannot be undone. |

```sh
npx @osdk/cli@latest widgetset version list
npx @osdk/cli@latest widgetset version delete 1.3.0 --yes
```

# React widgets

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/widgets/react

> Render a widget with FoundryWidget, read typed parameters and loading states with useFoundryWidgetContext, and emit events back to the host.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Develop a widget set](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/custom-widgets/development)
- [Use OSDK in a widget set](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/custom-widgets/use-osdk)

`@osdk/widget.client-react` connects a React tree to the Foundry host. `FoundryWidget` handles the message protocol, and `useFoundryWidgetContext` gives every component typed parameter values and an `emitEvent` function derived from your [widget config](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/widgets/parameters-and-events.md).

## Install

Projects from `@osdk/create-widget` already include these packages. To add them to an existing Vite and React project:

```npm
npm install @osdk/widget.client @osdk/widget.client-react
```

```npm
npm install -D @osdk/widget.vite-plugin
```

`@osdk/widget.client-react` supports React 18 and 19 and lists `@osdk/client` as a peer dependency. Add `@osdk/client`, `@osdk/react`, and your SDK package to call the Ontology.

## Render `FoundryWidget`

Wrap the widget's root in `FoundryWidget` and pass its config. Importing the config in the entrypoint is also what lets the Vite plugin find it.

```ts title="src/main.config.ts"
import { defineConfig } from "@osdk/widget.client";

export default defineConfig({
  id: "todoList",
  name: "Todo list",
  description: "A checklist backed by Workshop variables",
  type: "workshop",
  parameters: {
    headerText: {
      displayName: "Widget title",
      type: "string",
    },
    showWarning: {
      displayName: "Show warning callout",
      type: "boolean",
    },
    todoItems: {
      displayName: "Todo items",
      type: "array",
      subType: "string",
    },
  },
  events: {
    updateTodoItems: {
      displayName: "Update todo items",
      parameterUpdateIds: ["todoItems"],
    },
  },
});
```

```tsx title="src/main.tsx"
import { FoundryWidget } from "@osdk/widget.client-react";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
import MainConfig from "./main.config.js";
import { TodoWidget } from "./TodoWidget.js";

createRoot(document.getElementById("root")!).render(
  <FoundryWidget config={MainConfig}>
    <TodoWidget />
  </FoundryWidget>,
);
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `config` | The return type of `defineConfig` | Required | The widget config. Every parameter and event type in the context comes from it. |
| `children` | `React.ReactNode` | Required | The widget. |
| `client` | `Client` from `@osdk/client` | | An OSDK client, used to hydrate object set parameters and to serialize object sets you emit. Required by the types when the config has an `objectSet` parameter. |
| `initialValues` | Async value per parameter ID | Every parameter `not-started` | Starting values for `asyncParameterValues` before the host's first update. |

On mount, `FoundryWidget`:

1. Subscribes to host messages and sends `widget.ready`, so the host sends the first parameter values.
2. Observes the size of `document.body` and sends `widget.resize` with its border-box width and height on every change.
3. Sends `widget.reload` before a Vite full-page reload in development.
4. Wraps `children` in an error boundary. An uncaught render error shows its stack trace, plus troubleshooting tips when `NODE_ENV` is not `production`. Add your own error boundary inside `FoundryWidget` to show a custom message instead.

Render one `FoundryWidget` per widget, at the root. It creates the widget client once, when it mounts.

## Read parameters

`useFoundryWidgetContext` returns the context for the nearest `FoundryWidget`. The context is not generic at runtime, so bind your config's type once with `withTypes` and import that hook everywhere:

```ts title="src/context.ts"
import type { FoundryWidgetClientContext } from "@osdk/widget.client-react";
import { useFoundryWidgetContext } from "@osdk/widget.client-react";
import type MainConfig from "./main.config.js";

export const useWidgetContext: () => FoundryWidgetClientContext<
  typeof MainConfig
> = useFoundryWidgetContext.withTypes<typeof MainConfig>();
```

`useFoundryWidgetContext<typeof MainConfig>()` is equivalent. Outside a `FoundryWidget`, the hook returns a default context; see [Render outside Foundry](#render-outside-foundry).

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `parameters.values` | Each parameter's value, all optional | The latest values, typed from the config: `headerText` is `string \| undefined`, `todoItems` is `string[] \| undefined`. |
| `parameters.state` | `"not-started" \| "loading" \| "loaded" \| "reloading" \| "failed"` | One loading state for the widget's parameters. See [Loading states](#loading-states). |
| `asyncParameterValues` | Per parameter ID: `{ type, value }`, where `value` is an `AsyncValue` | The individual state of each parameter, for widgets that load parameters independently. |
| `emitEvent` | `(eventId, { parameterUpdates }) => void` | Sends one of the config's events. See [Emit events](#emit-events). |
| `hostEventTarget` | `FoundryHostEventTarget` | The raw stream of host messages. See [Listen to host messages](#listen-to-host-messages). |

## Loading states

`parameters.state` summarizes the parameters in the host's most recent update, in this order of precedence:

| State | When |
| --- | --- |
| `"failed"` | Any parameter failed. `parameters.values` keeps the values that did arrive. |
| `"loading"` | Any parameter is loading for the first time. |
| `"reloading"` | Any parameter is reloading. Values keep their previous contents. |
| `"not-started"` | Any parameter has not started loading. |
| `"loaded"` | Every parameter loaded. |

While the state is `not-started` or `loading`, `parameters.values` is `{}`, so give every read a fallback and keep rendering. Show progress next to the content instead of replacing it:

```tsx title="src/TodoWidget.tsx"
import { useCallback, useState } from "react";
import { useWidgetContext } from "./context.js";

export function TodoWidget() {
  const { parameters, emitEvent } = useWidgetContext();
  const headerText = parameters.values.headerText ?? "Todo list";
  const todoItems = parameters.values.todoItems ?? [];
  const isPending =
    parameters.state === "not-started" ||
    parameters.state === "loading" ||
    parameters.state === "reloading";
  const [newItem, setNewItem] = useState("");

  const handleAdd = useCallback(() => {
    emitEvent("updateTodoItems", {
      parameterUpdates: { todoItems: [...todoItems, newItem] },
    });
    setNewItem("");
  }, [emitEvent, todoItems, newItem]);

  const handleChange = useCallback(
    (event: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) =>
      setNewItem(event.target.value),
    [],
  );

  return (
    <section aria-busy={isPending}>
      <h2>{headerText}</h2>
      {parameters.state === "failed" && (
        <p role="alert">Some values failed to load.</p>
      )}
      {parameters.values.showWarning === true && (
        <p role="status">This is a data warning</p>
      )}
      <ul>
        {todoItems.map((item, index) => (
          <li key={index}>{item}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      <input value={newItem} onChange={handleChange} placeholder="Add item" />
      <button onClick={handleAdd} disabled={newItem === ""}>
        Add item
      </button>
    </section>
  );
}
```

To react to one parameter without waiting on the others, read `asyncParameterValues`:

```tsx title="src/Header.tsx"
import { useWidgetContext } from "./context.js";

export function Header() {
  const { asyncParameterValues } = useWidgetContext();
  const header = asyncParameterValues.headerText.value;

  return (
    <h2 aria-busy={header.type === "loading" || header.type === "reloading"}>
      {header.value ?? "Todo list"}
      {header.type === "failed" && ` (failed: ${header.error.message})`}
    </h2>
  );
}
```

## Emit events

`emitEvent(eventId, { parameterUpdates })` sends a `widget.emit-event` message. TypeScript limits `eventId` to the config's events and requires a value for every ID in the event's `parameterUpdateIds`. The call returns nothing and does not report whether the host acted on the event.

In the example above, `handleAdd` emits `updateTodoItems` with the new list. The widget does not keep its own copy: when the host writes the update to the variable bound to `todoItems`, the new list arrives through `parameters.values` and the widget re-renders. The template's counter works the same way, reading `counterValue` and emitting `setCounterValue` with the next number.

## Object set parameters

For an `objectSet` parameter, the host sends an object set RID. Pass an OSDK `client` to `FoundryWidget`, and the value in `parameters.values` gains an `objectSet` you can query, typed by the parameter's `allowedType`.

```ts title="src/directory.config.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { defineConfig } from "@osdk/widget.client";

export default defineConfig({
  id: "employeeDirectory",
  name: "Employee directory",
  type: "workshop",
  parameters: {
    employees: {
      displayName: "Employees",
      type: "objectSet",
      allowedType: Employee,
    },
    selectedEmployees: {
      displayName: "Selected employees",
      type: "objectSet",
      allowedType: Employee,
    },
  },
  events: {
    selectEmployee: {
      displayName: "Select employee",
      parameterUpdateIds: ["selectedEmployees"],
    },
  },
});
```

```tsx title="src/directory.tsx"
import { OsdkProvider } from "@osdk/react";
import { FoundryWidget } from "@osdk/widget.client-react";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
import { client } from "./client.js";
import DirectoryConfig from "./directory.config.js";
import { EmployeeDirectory } from "./EmployeeDirectory.js";

createRoot(document.getElementById("root")!).render(
  <FoundryWidget config={DirectoryConfig} client={client}>
    <OsdkProvider client={client}>
      <EmployeeDirectory />
    </OsdkProvider>
  </FoundryWidget>,
);
```

Query the set with `useObjectSet` from `@osdk/react`. Hydrated object sets are cached per parameter, so the `objectSet` reference only changes when the host sends a new RID, and it is safe to pass straight to hooks. To emit an object set, pass an `ObjectSet` from `@osdk/client`:

```tsx title="src/EmployeeDirectory.tsx"
import { useObjectSet } from "@osdk/react";
import { useFoundryWidgetContext } from "@osdk/widget.client-react";
import { useCallback } from "react";
import type DirectoryConfig from "./directory.config.js";

const useDirectoryContext =
  useFoundryWidgetContext.withTypes<typeof DirectoryConfig>();

export function EmployeeDirectory() {
  const { parameters, emitEvent } = useDirectoryContext();
  const employees = parameters.values.employees?.objectSet;
  const { data, isLoading, error } = useObjectSet(employees, {
    orderBy: { fullName: "asc" },
  });

  const handleSelect = useCallback(
    (employeeId: number) => {
      if (employees == null) {
        return;
      }
      emitEvent("selectEmployee", {
        parameterUpdates: {
          selectedEmployees: employees.where({ employeeId }),
        },
      });
    },
    [employees, emitEvent],
  );

  return (
    <div aria-busy={isLoading}>
      {error != null && <p role="alert">{error.message}</p>}
      <ul>
        {data?.map((employee) => (
          <li key={employee.$primaryKey}>
            <button onClick={() => handleSelect(employee.employeeId)}>
              {employee.fullName}
            </button>
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`emitEvent` turns each `ObjectSet` into a temporary object set RID with an extra request before it sends the event. Because of that step:

- If you emit the same event again before the request finishes, only the last call is sent.
- Errors, such as a failed request, are not reported to the caller.
- Emitting an object set without a `client` on `FoundryWidget` fails, and so does receiving one.

See [Work with object sets](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/object-sets.md) for filtering, pivoting, and combining the sets you receive.

## Listen to host messages

`hostEventTarget` dispatches every `host.update-parameters` message, with the raw payload in `event.detail`. Use it to log or react to updates beyond what `parameters` exposes:

```tsx title="src/useLogParameterUpdates.ts"
import { useEffect } from "react";
import { useWidgetContext } from "./context.js";

export function useLogParameterUpdates() {
  const { hostEventTarget } = useWidgetContext();

  useEffect(() => {
    const listener = (event: CustomEvent) => {
      console.log("Parameters updated", event.detail);
    };
    hostEventTarget.addEventListener("host.update-parameters", listener);
    return () =>
      hostEventTarget.removeEventListener("host.update-parameters", listener);
  }, [hostEventTarget]);
}
```

## Render outside Foundry

`FoundryWidget` needs the host API that Foundry injects. Outside Foundry and developer mode, it throws `Invariant failed: [FoundryWidgetClient] Missing __PALANTIR_WIDGET_API__ in window` when it renders.

Components below it still render on their own: without a `FoundryWidget` ancestor, `useFoundryWidgetContext` returns a default context whose `parameters.state` is `not-started`, whose `parameters.values` is `{}`, and whose `emitEvent` does nothing. Because widget components already handle empty values, you can render them directly in unit tests and Storybook.

To start `asyncParameterValues` in a known state before the host's first update, pass `initialValues` to `FoundryWidget`. It does not affect `parameters.values` or `parameters.state`, which stay `{}` and `not-started` until the first `host.update-parameters` message.

```tsx title="src/main.tsx"
import { FoundryWidget } from "@osdk/widget.client-react";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
import { Header } from "./Header.js";
import MainConfig from "./main.config.js";

createRoot(document.getElementById("root")!).render(
  <FoundryWidget
    config={MainConfig}
    initialValues={{
      headerText: { type: "string", value: { type: "loading" } },
      showWarning: { type: "boolean", value: { type: "loading" } },
      todoItems: { type: "array", subType: "string", value: { type: "loading" } },
    }}
  >
    <Header />
  </FoundryWidget>,
);
```

# Agents

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/agents

> Converse with AIP Agents through the Platform SDK, start sessions for agents in your generated SDK, and read injected clients with @osdk/agents.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [AIP Chatbot Studio](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/agent-studio/overview)
- [Agent API](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/api/v2/aip-agents-v2-resources/agents/agent-basics)

An agent is configured in Foundry and runs its own model calls, tools, and retrieval; your app sends it input and reads its answers. Use this page to call an AIP Agent built in AIP Agent Studio, to start a session for an agent included in your generated SDK, or to reach the OSDK clients from code inside an agent.

> [!WARNING]
> Every API on this page is pre-release. The AIP Agents platform endpoints are marked beta, the generated-SDK session method is `experimental_createSession`, the Agents session endpoints are marked alpha, and `@osdk/agents` is at version 0.x with its client helpers under `/experimental`.

| You want to | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Chat with an agent built in AIP Agent Studio | `Sessions` from `@osdk/foundry.aipagents` |
| Start a session for an agent your generated SDK exports | `client(agent).experimental_createSession()` from `@osdk/client` |
| Call the Ontology from code that runs inside an agent | `getClient()` from `@osdk/agents/experimental` |
| Chat with a language model directly, without an agent | [`generateText`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/chat.md) or [`useChat`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/react.md) |

The `AipAgentChat` component chats with a language model, not with an AIP Agent.

## Chat with an AIP Agent

`@osdk/foundry.aipagents` is the Platform SDK package for AIP Agents. It works with the `Client` from `createClient` or a `PlatformClient`; see [Platform SDK setup](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/setup.md).

```npm
npm install @osdk/foundry.aipagents
```

| Function | Required scope | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Sessions.create(client, agentRid, { agentVersion? })` | `api:aip-agents-write` | Starts a session. Omit `agentVersion` for the latest published version. |
| `Sessions.blockingContinue(client, agentRid, sessionRid, body)` | `api:aip-agents-write` | Sends a message and resolves with the full answer. |
| `Sessions.streamingContinue(client, agentRid, sessionRid, body)` | `api:aip-agents-write` | Sends a message and resolves with a `Response` whose body streams the answer as Markdown text. |
| `Sessions.cancel(client, agentRid, sessionRid, { messageId, response? })` | `api:aip-agents-write` | Cancels a streamed exchange, optionally replacing the answer. |
| `Sessions.list(client, agentRid)`, `Sessions.get(client, agentRid, sessionRid)` | `api:aip-agents-read` | Reads sessions this client created. |

Each function takes query parameters as its last argument. Pass `{ preview: true }` while the endpoints are in beta. Find the agent RID in AIP Agent Studio.

### Send a message

```ts title="src/askAgent.ts"
import { Sessions } from "@osdk/foundry.aipagents";
import { client } from "./client";

const agentRid = "ri.aip-agents..agent.<id>";

const session = await Sessions.create(client, agentRid, {}, { preview: true });

const result = await Sessions.blockingContinue(
  client,
  agentRid,
  session.rid,
  {
    userInput: { text: "Which offices have open desks this week?" },
    parameterInputs: {},
  },
  { preview: true },
);

console.log(result.agentMarkdownResponse);
console.log(result.totalTokensUsed);
```

| Request field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `userInput` | `{ text: string }` | The user's message. |
| `parameterInputs` | `Record<string, ParameterValue>` | Values for the agent's application variables. Pass `{}` if it has none. |
| `contextsOverride` | `Array<InputContext>` | Replaces the context the agent would retrieve for this message. |
| `messageId` | `string` | Streaming only. An id you choose, so you can cancel the exchange. |
| `sessionTraceId` | `string` | An id for tracing this exchange. |

`blockingContinue` resolves with `agentMarkdownResponse`, `parameterUpdates`, `totalTokensUsed`, `interruptedOutput`, and `sessionTraceId`.

### Stream the answer

`streamingContinue` resolves with a `Response`. Read its body as text:

```ts title="src/streamAgent.ts"
import { Sessions } from "@osdk/foundry.aipagents";
import { client } from "./client";

export async function streamAgentAnswer(
  agentRid: string,
  sessionRid: string,
  text: string,
  onText: (markdown: string) => void,
): Promise<void> {
  const messageId = crypto.randomUUID();
  const response = await Sessions.streamingContinue(
    client,
    agentRid,
    sessionRid,
    { userInput: { text }, parameterInputs: {}, messageId },
    { preview: true },
  );
  if (response.body == null) {
    return;
  }

  const reader = response.body.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream()).getReader();
  let markdown = "";
  while (true) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read();
    if (done) {
      break;
    }
    markdown += value;
    onText(markdown);
  }
}
```

A session handles one exchange at a time: wait for the answer, or cancel it with `Sessions.cancel` and the same `messageId`, before sending the next message. Cancelling does not close the stream, so also stop reading it.

## Start a session for a generated agent

When your generated SDK includes agents, it exports each one alongside your object types, and all of them as `$Agents`. Pass one to the client and call `experimental_createSession` with the agent's arguments:

```ts title="src/startSession.ts"
import { Employee, employeeAssistant } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const employee = await client(Employee).fetchOne(50030);

const session = await client(employeeAssistant).experimental_createSession({
  employee,
  team: client(Employee).where({ department: "Engineering" }),
});

console.log(session.id);
```

| Behavior | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Arguments | A record keyed by argument name. OSDK objects and object sets are converted to the agent's argument types, including nested values. Omit the argument for agents that take none. |
| Return value | `AgentSession`, with the session's `id`. |
| Version | The version pinned in your generated SDK. Override it with `client({ ...employeeAssistant, version: "2.0.0" })`. |
| Unsupported clients | Throws before sending a request on branch, scenario, and transaction clients. |
| Scopes | Loads the agent definition (`api:agents-read`) and creates the session (`api:agents-write`). |

Creating a session runs agent logic and can modify platform data.

### Send events to a session

After creation, interact with the session through `AgentSessions` in `@osdk/foundry.agents`. These endpoints are alpha and take `{ preview: true }`.

```npm
npm install @osdk/foundry.agents
```

```ts title="src/sendEvent.ts"
import { AgentSessions } from "@osdk/foundry.agents";
import { client } from "./client";

export async function sendToAgent(sessionId: string, payload: unknown) {
  const { result } = await AgentSessions.sendEvent(
    client,
    sessionId,
    {
      event: { id: crypto.randomUUID(), eventType: "<event-type>", payload },
    },
    { preview: true },
  );

  if (result.type === "sessionNotReady") {
    return undefined;
  }
  return AgentSessions.getSessionState(client, sessionId, {
    consistencyKey: result.consistencyKey,
    preview: true,
  });
}
```

| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `sendEvent(client, sessionId, { event })` | Sends an event of a type the agent declared when it was published. `result.type` is `"accepted"`, with a `consistencyKey`, or `"sessionNotReady"`; retry the latter after a short delay. |
| `getSessionState(client, sessionId, { consistencyKey? })` | Reads the session. `type` is `"available"`, with `status`, `agentState`, `arguments`, and context items; `"behind"` when it has not yet caught up to `consistencyKey`; or `"notReady"`. |
| `get(client, sessionId)` | Reads the session's agent RID and version. |

The event types and payload shapes are defined by the agent, so check its published definition.

## Reach the clients from agent code

`@osdk/agents` is for code that runs inside a Foundry agent, not for apps that call one. Foundry injects an Ontology `Client` and a `PlatformClient` into each invocation; `@osdk/agents/experimental` reads them.

```npm
npm install @osdk/agents @osdk/client @osdk/functions
```

| Export | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `getClient()` | The Ontology SDK `Client` for the current invocation. Throws if no Ontology is imported into the repository. |
| `getPlatformClient()` | The `PlatformClient` for the current invocation. |
| `withClients(clients, run)` | Runs `run` with `clients` as the current clients. Use it in tests. |
| `ScopeResources`, `ScopeAuthorization`, `Scope` | Resource and authorization scope declarations, re-exported from `@osdk/functions/experimental`. |

The `AgentConfig` type from `@osdk/agents` describes the `export const config` an agent declares alongside its code: `locator: string`, plus optional `apiName`, `sources: Array<string>`, and an experimental `scope`.

```ts title="src/lookUpEmployee.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { getClient } from "@osdk/agents/experimental";

export async function lookUpEmployee(employeeId: number) {
  const employee = await getClient()(Employee).fetchOne(employeeId);
  return { fullName: employee.fullName, jobTitle: employee.jobTitle };
}
```

The clients exist only while an invocation runs. Call `getClient()` and `getPlatformClient()` inside your handlers, not at module load and not from work that outlives the invocation.

To call a language model from agent code, pass `getPlatformClient()` to [`foundryModel`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/chat.md#create-a-model).

# Generate and stream text

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/chat

> Call Foundry-hosted language models with generateText and streamText from @osdk/aip-core, in Node.js or the browser.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Supported LLMs](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/aip/supported-llms)

`@osdk/aip-core` sends chat completions to the Foundry Language Model Service (LMS) with the same auth, governance, and usage tracking as the rest of your OSDK app. Use `generateText` for a complete answer and `streamText` to render tokens as they arrive.

> [!WARNING]
> `@osdk/aip-core` is at version 0.x, and its API can change in any minor release. The current release runs one model call per request: there is no built-in multi-step tool loop, no structured (JSON) output, and only text content parts are sent. Image and file parts are dropped with a warning.

## Install

```npm
npm install @osdk/aip-core @osdk/client @osdk/oauth
```

`@osdk/client` is a peer dependency. `@osdk/aip-core` brings in `@osdk/language-models` itself.

## Create a model

Every call takes a model handle from `foundryModel`. It needs a `PlatformClient` from `createPlatformClient` and the model's LMS API name.

```ts title="src/model.ts"
import { foundryModel } from "@osdk/aip-core";
import { createPlatformClient } from "@osdk/client";
import { createPublicOauthClient } from "@osdk/oauth";

const foundryUrl = "https://example.palantirfoundry.com";

export const auth = createPublicOauthClient(
  "<your-client-id>",
  foundryUrl,
  "http://localhost:8080/auth/callback",
  {
    scopes: [
      "api:read-data",
      "api:write-data",
      "api:use-ontologies-read",
      "api:use-ontologies-write",
      "api:use-language-models-execute",
    ],
  },
);

export const platformClient = createPlatformClient(foundryUrl, auth);

export const model = foundryModel({ client: platformClient, model: "gpt-4o" });
```

> [!NOTE]
> Pass a client from `createPlatformClient`, not the `Client` from `createClient`: `foundryModel` reads `baseUrl`, `fetch`, and `tokenProvider` from the client, and an Ontology `Client` does not expose them. Reuse the same token provider for both clients so the user signs in once.

OAuth applications must request the `api:use-language-models-execute` scope. The default scopes of `createPublicOauthClient` do not include it, so list every scope your app needs. See [Authentication](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/authentication.md) for the other token providers.

### Model identifiers

`model` accepts an API name string or a `ModelIdentifier`:

| Value | Example | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `"gpt-4o"` | A built-in LMS model, by API name. Shorthand for `{ type: "lmsModel", apiName }`. |
| `{ type: "lmsModel", apiName }` | `{ type: "lmsModel", apiName: "gpt-4o" }` | The same, spelled out. |
| `{ type: "registeredModel", registeredModelRid }` | `{ type: "registeredModel", registeredModelRid: "ri.language-model-service..." }` | A model your organization registered in Foundry. |

Which models you can call depends on your enrollment. Look up API names in Model Catalog in Foundry. The handle's `modelId` is `foundry/<apiName or rid>`, useful for logging.

## Generate text

`generateText` sends one request and resolves with the full response.

```ts title="src/summarize.ts"
import { generateText } from "@osdk/aip-core";
import { model } from "./model";

const result = await generateText({
  model,
  system: "Answer in one sentence.",
  prompt: "What does an Ontology action type do?",
  temperature: 0,
  maxOutputTokens: 200,
});

console.log(result.text);
console.log(result.finishReason, result.usage.totalTokens);
```

### Prompts, messages, and system instructions

Give the conversation as either `prompt` or `messages`. Passing both throws. At least one of `system`, `prompt`, or `messages` is required.

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prompt` | `string \| Array<ModelMessage>` | A string becomes one user message. |
| `messages` | `Array<ModelMessage>` | The full conversation history. |
| `system` | `string \| SystemModelMessage \| Array<SystemModelMessage>` | Instructions prepended before the conversation. An empty string is ignored. |

A `ModelMessage` is one of:

| `role` | `content` |
| --- | --- |
| `"system"` | `string` |
| `"user"` | `string`, or an array of `{ type: "text", text }` parts. Image and file parts are accepted by the type but dropped. |
| `"assistant"` | `string`, or an array of text and `tool-call` parts. |
| `"tool"` | An array of `tool-result` parts. See [Tool calling](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/tools.md). |

To hold a multi-turn conversation, keep the history and append each answer before the next question:

```ts title="src/conversation.ts"
import { generateText, type ModelMessage } from "@osdk/aip-core";
import { model } from "./model";

const messages: Array<ModelMessage> = [];

export async function ask(question: string): Promise<string> {
  messages.push({ role: "user", content: question });
  const result = await generateText({
    model,
    system: "You help employees find internal information.",
    messages,
  });
  messages.push({ role: "assistant", content: result.text });
  return result.text;
}
```

## Stream text

`streamText` returns immediately and starts the request. Read tokens from `textStream`, or every event from `fullStream`. The other fields are promises that resolve when the stream ends.

**Node.js**

```ts title="src/stream.ts"
import { streamText } from "@osdk/aip-core";
import { model } from "./model";

const result = streamText({
  model,
  prompt: "Write a short welcome note for a new engineer.",
});

for await (const delta of result.textStream) {
  process.stdout.write(delta);
}

console.log("\n", await result.usage);
```
**Browser**

```ts title="src/stream.ts"
import { streamText } from "@osdk/aip-core";
import { model } from "./model";

export async function streamInto(element: HTMLElement, prompt: string) {
  const result = streamText({ model, prompt });
  const reader = result.textStream.getReader();
  element.textContent = "";
  while (true) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read();
    if (done) {
      break;
    }
    element.textContent += value;
  }
  return result.finishReason;
}
```

Use `getReader()` in browsers: not every browser supports `for await` over a `ReadableStream`.

### Stream result

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `textStream` | `ReadableStream<string>` | Text deltas only. |
| `fullStream` | `ReadableStream<TextStreamChunk>` | Every event, listed below. |
| `text` | `Promise<string>` | The full answer. |
| `reasoningText` | `Promise<string \| undefined>` | Reasoning text, for models that return it. |
| `toolCalls` | `Promise<Array<ToolCall>>` | Tool calls requested by the model. |
| `finishReason` | `Promise<FinishReason>` | Why generation stopped. |
| `usage`, `totalUsage` | `Promise<LanguageModelUsage>` | Token counts. Identical while each call is a single step. |
| `warnings` | `Promise<Array<Warning> \| undefined>` | Ignored inputs. Resolves even when the stream fails. |
| `request`, `response` | `Promise<RequestMetadata \| undefined>`, `Promise<ResponseMetadata \| undefined>` | The request body sent, and the response id, model, timestamp, and assistant message. |

`fullStream` emits these `TextStreamChunk` events:

| `type` | Fields | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"text-delta"` | `id`, `delta` | Each piece of answer text. |
| `"reasoning-delta"` | `id`, `delta` | Each piece of reasoning text. |
| `"tool-call"` | `toolCallId`, `toolName`, `input` | Once per tool call, after the model finishes, with `input` parsed from JSON. |
| `"finish"` | `finishReason`, `rawFinishReason`, `usage` | Once, at the end. |
| `"error"` | `error` | The request or stream failed. The stream then errors with the same `Error`. |

`streamText` also takes `onChunk`, `onError`, and `onFinish` callbacks. `onFinish` receives `finishReason`, `text`, `reasoningText`, `toolCalls`, `usage`, `totalUsage`, `warnings`, `request`, and `response`.

## Sampling options

`generateText` and `streamText` share these options:

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `maxOutputTokens` | `number` | Maximum tokens to generate. |
| `temperature` | `number` | Randomness. `0` is the most deterministic. |
| `topP` | `number` | Nucleus sampling threshold. |
| `presencePenalty` | `number` | Penalizes tokens that have appeared at all. |
| `frequencyPenalty` | `number` | Penalizes tokens by how often they have appeared. |
| `stopSequences` | `Array<string>` | Stops generation at any of these strings. |
| `seed` | `number` | Seed for repeatable sampling, where the model supports it. |
| `headers` | `Record<string, string \| undefined>` | Extra HTTP headers on the request. |
| `abortSignal` | `AbortSignal` | Cancels the request. |

Models differ in which options they honor. The LMS proxy does not accept `topK`, so there is no such option.

## Cancel a request

Pass an `AbortSignal`. `generateText` rejects, and `streamText` errors its streams and rejects its promises. Calling `cancel()` on `textStream` or `fullStream` also aborts the request.

```ts title="src/cancel.ts"
import { streamText } from "@osdk/aip-core";
import { model } from "./model";

const controller = new AbortController();
const result = streamText({
  model,
  prompt: "Write a long report on office utilization.",
  abortSignal: controller.signal,
});

setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 5_000);

try {
  console.log(await result.text);
} catch (error) {
  if (controller.signal.aborted) {
    console.log("Stopped by the user");
  } else {
    throw error;
  }
}
```

Check `signal.aborted` rather than `error.name`: the client's `fetch` wraps the abort in its own error type.

## Usage and finish reason

`generateText` resolves with a `GenerateTextResult`:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `string` | The answer text. |
| `reasoningText` | `string \| undefined` | Reasoning text, for models that return it. |
| `content` | `Array<ContentPart>` | Text, reasoning, and tool-call parts in order. |
| `toolCalls` | `Array<ToolCall>` | Tool calls requested by the model. |
| `toolResults` | `Array<ToolResult>` | Always empty: tools are not executed for you. |
| `finishReason` | `FinishReason` | Normalized stop reason. |
| `rawFinishReason` | `string \| undefined` | The provider's own value, such as `"tool_calls"`. |
| `usage` | `LanguageModelUsage` | Token counts for this call. |
| `totalUsage` | `LanguageModelUsage` | Same as `usage`. |
| `steps` | `Array<StepResult>` | One entry per model call. Always one. |
| `warnings` | `Array<Warning> \| undefined` | Inputs that were ignored. |
| `request`, `response` | `RequestMetadata`, `ResponseMetadata` | The request body, plus response `id`, `modelId`, `timestamp`, `body`, and `messages`. |

`FinishReason` is one of `"stop"`, `"length"` (hit `maxOutputTokens`), `"tool-calls"`, `"content-filter"`, `"error"`, or `"other"`.

`LanguageModelUsage` has `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, and `totalTokens`, each `number | undefined`, plus optional `reasoningTokens` and `cachedInputTokens`. Fields are `undefined` when the model does not report usage.

`generateText` also accepts `onStepFinish(step)` and `onFinish(event)`, where `event` adds `steps` and `totalUsage` to the step result.

## Errors and warnings

Failed requests reject with `PalantirApiError` from `@osdk/client`, which carries `statusCode`, `errorName`, and `message`. A `403` usually means the token lacks `api:use-language-models-execute` or your user cannot use the model.

Unsupported input does not throw. It is skipped and reported in `warnings`:

| Input | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Image or file parts in a user message | Dropped. |
| Reasoning or file parts in an assistant message | Dropped. |
| Media in a tool result | Dropped. |
| A tool whose `inputSchema` is not a JSON Schema object | Sent with empty parameters. |
| Tool-call arguments that are not valid JSON | Passed through as the raw string. |

## Use the AI SDK

If your app already uses the [AI SDK](https://ai-sdk.dev), `@osdk/aip-core/ai-sdk` provides a Foundry provider for it. You get the AI SDK's own `generateText`, `streamText`, and `tool()` helpers, including its multi-step tool loop. The provider implements the v3 provider specification, so use `ai` version 6.

```npm
npm install @osdk/aip-core ai @ai-sdk/provider
```

```ts title="src/aiSdk.ts"
import { createFoundryAI } from "@osdk/aip-core/ai-sdk";
import { streamText } from "ai";
import { platformClient } from "./model";

const foundry = createFoundryAI({ client: platformClient });

const result = streamText({
  model: foundry("gpt-4o"),
  prompt: "Suggest three names for an onboarding checklist app.",
});

for await (const delta of result.textStream) {
  process.stdout.write(delta);
}
```

`foundry(model)` and `foundry.languageModel(model)` accept the same API name or `ModelIdentifier` as `foundryModel`. The provider also ignores `topK` and JSON response formats, and reports them as warnings.

## Call a provider SDK directly

`@osdk/language-models` is the lower-level package `@osdk/aip-core` is built on. It returns Foundry's provider-compatible proxy URLs, so you can point an OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google SDK at Foundry instead of the provider. Use it when you need a provider feature `@osdk/aip-core` does not cover yet, such as the OpenAI Responses API or embeddings.

| Function | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `getOpenAiBaseUrl(client)` | `<foundryUrl>/api/v2/llm/proxy/openai/v1` |
| `getAnthropicBaseUrl(client)` | `<foundryUrl>/api/v2/llm/proxy/anthropic` |
| `getGoogleBaseUrl(client)` | `<foundryUrl>/api/v2/llm/proxy/google` |
| `createFetch(client)` | The client's `fetch`, which sets a fresh `Authorization` header on every request. |
| `getFoundryToken(client)` | `Promise<string>` with the current token. |

Each function accepts an Ontology `Client` or a `PlatformClient`.

```ts title="src/openai.ts"
import { createFetch, getFoundryToken, getOpenAiBaseUrl } from "@osdk/language-models";
import OpenAI from "openai";
import { platformClient } from "./model";

const openai = new OpenAI({
  apiKey: await getFoundryToken(platformClient),
  baseURL: getOpenAiBaseUrl(platformClient),
  fetch: createFetch(platformClient),
});

const completion = await openai.chat.completions.create({
  model: "gpt-4o",
  messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Hello" }],
});
console.log(completion.choices[0]?.message.content);
```

`createFetch` replaces the `Authorization` header on each request, so the client keeps working after the token from `getFoundryToken` expires. The proxy accepts each provider's native request format; Foundry's [LLM-provider compatible APIs](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/aip/llm-provider-compatible-apis) documentation lists the supported endpoints.
