- [React chat UIs](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/react.md): stream into React with `useChat`.

# AI overview

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai

> Packages for adding LLM features to OSDK apps with Foundry's Language Model Service, what each one does, and what you need before you start.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [AIP](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/aip/overview)

{/* cspell:ignore llms */}

Add text generation, tool calling, chat UIs, and agents to an OSDK app using models hosted by Foundry's Language Model Service (LMS). Requests run with the signed-in user's permissions and Foundry's governance and usage tracking, so you never ship a provider API key.

> [!WARNING]
> These packages are pre-release. `@osdk/aip-core`, `@osdk/language-models`, and `@osdk/agents` are at version 0.x, and the React APIs ship from `/experimental` entry points. Expect breaking changes in minor releases.

## Packages

| Package | Import | What it does | Maturity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@osdk/aip-core` | `@osdk/aip-core` | `foundryModel`, `generateText`, `streamText`, tool definitions, and the `LmsChatTransport` chat transport. | 0.x |
| `@osdk/aip-core` | `@osdk/aip-core/ai-sdk` | `createFoundryAI`, a Foundry provider for the [AI SDK](https://ai-sdk.dev) version 6. | 0.x |
| `@osdk/language-models` | `@osdk/language-models` | Proxy base URLs and an authenticated `fetch` for the OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google SDKs. `@osdk/aip-core` is built on it. | 0.x |
| `@osdk/react` | `@osdk/react/experimental/aip` | `useChat`, a hook that streams a conversation into React state. | Experimental |
| `@osdk/react-components` | `@osdk/react-components/experimental/aip-agent-chat` | [`AipAgentChat`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/components/aip-agent-chat.md), a prebuilt chat panel built on `useChat`. | Experimental |
| `@osdk/foundry.aipagents` | `@osdk/foundry.aipagents` | Platform SDK for agents built in AIP Agent Studio: sessions, blocking and streaming replies. | Beta endpoints |
| `@osdk/agents` | `@osdk/agents`, `@osdk/agents/experimental` | `AgentConfig` and the injected `getClient` and `getPlatformClient` for code that runs inside an agent. | 0.x |

## Which to use

| Goal | Start with |
| --- | --- |
| Summarize, classify, or draft text from a script or server | [`generateText`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/chat.md) in Node.js |
| Show an answer token by token | [`streamText`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/chat.md#stream-text) |
| Let the model look up Ontology data or propose actions | [Tool calling](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/tools.md) |
| Add a chat panel to a React app with no custom UI | [`AipAgentChat`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/components/aip-agent-chat.md) |
| Build your own chat UI | [`useChat`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/react.md) |
| Use the AI SDK's helpers, Zod tools, and multi-step loop | [`@osdk/aip-core/ai-sdk`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/chat.md#use-the-ai-sdk) |
| Call an OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google SDK feature that `@osdk/aip-core` lacks | [`@osdk/language-models`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/chat.md#call-a-provider-sdk-directly) |
| Talk to an agent configured in AIP Agent Studio | [Agents](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/agents.md) |

`@osdk/language-models` is not superseded: `@osdk/aip-core` depends on it for the proxy URL. Use `@osdk/aip-core` for a provider-neutral API, and `@osdk/language-models` when you want a provider's own SDK.

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details |
| --- | --- |
| AIP on your enrollment | AIP must be enabled, and your users need permission to use AIP builder capabilities. |
| OAuth scope | Third-party applications must request `api:use-language-models-execute`. The default scopes of `createPublicOauthClient` do not include it. Agents need `api:aip-agents-read` and `api:aip-agents-write`, or `api:agents-read` and `api:agents-write` for generated agents. |
| A `PlatformClient` | `foundryModel`, `createFoundryAI`, and `AipAgentChat` take a client from `createPlatformClient`, not the Ontology `Client`. Create it with the same token provider. |
| A model | Use a model API name, such as `"gpt-4o"`, or a registered model RID. Available models vary by enrollment; look them up in Model Catalog. |

```ts title="src/model.ts"
import { foundryModel } from "@osdk/aip-core";
import { createPlatformClient } from "@osdk/client";
import { createPublicOauthClient } from "@osdk/oauth";

const foundryUrl = "https://example.palantirfoundry.com";

const auth = createPublicOauthClient(
  "<your-client-id>",
  foundryUrl,
  "http://localhost:8080/auth/callback",
  {
    scopes: [
      "api:read-data",
      "api:write-data",
      "api:use-ontologies-read",
      "api:use-ontologies-write",
      "api:use-language-models-execute",
    ],
  },
);

export const platformClient = createPlatformClient(foundryUrl, auth);
export const model = foundryModel({ client: platformClient, model: "gpt-4o" });
```

## Current limits

| Limit | Applies to |
| --- | --- |
| One model call per request; you run the tool loop yourself. | `generateText`, `streamText` |
| Tool `inputSchema` must be JSON Schema; Zod schemas are not converted. | `generateText`, `streamText` |
| Text only: image and file parts are dropped with a warning. | `@osdk/aip-core`, `useChat` |
| No structured JSON output, no `topK`. | `@osdk/aip-core`, `@osdk/aip-core/ai-sdk` |
| No tools, multi-step loops, or stream resume. | `useChat`, `AipAgentChat` |

The AI SDK provider lifts the first two: the AI SDK runs the loop and converts Zod schemas.

- [Generate and stream text](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/chat.md): `generateText`, `streamText`, models, messages, and usage.
- [Tool calling](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/tools.md): Query the Ontology and propose actions from model tool calls.
- [React chat UIs](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/react.md): `useChat`, custom transports, and streaming rendering.
- [Agents](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/agents.md): AIP Agents, generated agent sessions, and `@osdk/agents`.
- [AipAgentChat](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/components/aip-agent-chat.md): A prebuilt chat panel for React.
- [Use these docs with AI](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/llms.md): `llms.txt`, per-page Markdown, and AGENTS.md for coding assistants.

# Use these docs with AI

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/llms

> Give coding assistants accurate OSDK context with llms.txt, per-page Markdown, and the package AGENTS.md files.

Every page on this site is also published as plain Markdown, so you can hand OSDK documentation to ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, or your own agent without scraping HTML.

## From any page

Each page header has two controls:

| Control | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Copy Markdown** | Copies the page as Markdown, ready to paste into a chat or prompt. |
| **Open** menu | Opens the page in ChatGPT, Claude, or Cursor with a prompt that points at the Markdown version, or opens the source on GitHub. |

## Markdown for every URL

Append `.md` to any docs URL to get the Markdown version:

```txt
https://palantir.github.io/osdk-ts/react/actions
https://palantir.github.io/osdk-ts/react/actions.md
```

## llms.txt

The site follows the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) convention:

| File | Contents | Use it when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`/llms.txt`](https://palantir.github.io/osdk-ts/llms.txt) | An index of every page, grouped by section, with a one-line summary and a link to its Markdown. | Your tool fetches pages on demand. |
| [`/llms-full.txt`](https://palantir.github.io/osdk-ts/llms-full.txt) | Every page, concatenated. | You want the whole SDK in a single context window. |

**Cursor**

In chat, type `@Docs`, choose **Add new doc**, and enter `https://palantir.github.io/osdk-ts/llms-full.txt`. Mention it with `@Docs` in later prompts.
**Claude Code**

Add the index to your project's `CLAUDE.md` so Claude fetches the pages it needs:

```md title="CLAUDE.md"
OSDK documentation: https://palantir.github.io/osdk-ts/llms.txt
Fetch the linked .md pages before writing OSDK code.
```
**Any agent**

Fetch `https://palantir.github.io/osdk-ts/llms.txt`, pick the relevant pages, then fetch their `.md` links. Use `llms-full.txt` when the agent can't make follow-up requests.

## Docs inside your node_modules

The React packages ship agent instructions and documentation in their npm tarballs, so assistants working in your repository can read docs that match your installed version:

| Package | Files |
| --- | --- |
| `@osdk/react` | `AGENTS.md` (install rules, version matching, correct and incorrect patterns) and `docs/` (the React guides on this site) |
| `@osdk/react-components` | `AGENTS.md` and `docs/` (one page per component, including generated prop tables) |

Point your assistant at them directly:

```md title="AGENTS.md"
Before using @osdk/react, read node_modules/@osdk/react/AGENTS.md.
Before using @osdk/react-components, read node_modules/@osdk/react-components/AGENTS.md.
```

> [!NOTE]
> The files in `node_modules` match the version you have installed. This site always documents the latest release.

# React chat UIs

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/react

> Build streaming chat interfaces with useChat from @osdk/react/experimental/aip, custom chat transports, or the prebuilt AipAgentChat component.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [AIP Chatbot Studio](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/agent-studio/overview)

`useChat` streams a conversation with a Foundry-hosted model into React state: you render `messages` and call `sendMessage`. For a finished UI, drop in the `AipAgentChat` component instead.

> [!WARNING]
> `useChat` is exported from the experimental entry point `@osdk/react/experimental/aip`, and `AipAgentChat` from `@osdk/react-components/experimental/aip-agent-chat`. Both can change in any minor release. The current version is text-only: it does not send tools, run multi-step loops, or resume a dropped stream, and it does not render reasoning text.

## Choose an approach

| Approach | You write | Use it when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`AipAgentChat`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/components/aip-agent-chat.md) | One element | You want a complete chat panel with a composer, message list, and optional model picker. |
| `useChat` | The UI | You need your own layout, message rendering, or controls. |
| `useChat` with a custom `transport` | The UI and the transport | You need to observe or change the stream, such as recording token usage. |

## Install

```npm
npm install @osdk/react @osdk/aip-core @osdk/client @osdk/oauth
```

`@osdk/react` already depends on `@osdk/aip-core`; install it directly because your code imports `foundryModel` from it. `useChat` does not read from `OsdkProvider`, so it works inside or outside one.

## Create the model once

`useChat` needs a model from `foundryModel`, which takes a `PlatformClient` and the model's LMS API name. Create it at module scope so it stays the same object across renders. A new model object rebuilds the hook's transport.

```ts title="src/model.ts"
import { foundryModel } from "@osdk/aip-core";
import { createPlatformClient } from "@osdk/client";
import { createPublicOauthClient } from "@osdk/oauth";

const foundryUrl = "https://example.palantirfoundry.com";

export const auth = createPublicOauthClient(
  "<your-client-id>",
  foundryUrl,
  "http://localhost:8080/auth/callback",
  {
    scopes: [
      "api:read-data",
      "api:write-data",
      "api:use-ontologies-read",
      "api:use-ontologies-write",
      "api:use-language-models-execute",
    ],
  },
);

export const platformClient = createPlatformClient(foundryUrl, auth);

export const model = foundryModel({ client: platformClient, model: "gpt-4o" });
```

If your app already has an Ontology client, pass the same `auth` to `createClient` so the user signs in once. Model selection and scopes are covered in [Generate and stream text](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/chat.md#create-a-model).

## Build a chat with `useChat`

```tsx title="src/ChatMessage.tsx"
import { getUIMessageText } from "@osdk/aip-core";
import type { UIMessage } from "@osdk/react/experimental/aip";

export function ChatMessage({ message }: { message: UIMessage }) {
  return (
    <div className={`message message-${message.role}`}>
      <strong>{message.role === "user" ? "You" : "Assistant"}</strong>
      <p style={{ whiteSpace: "pre-wrap" }}>{getUIMessageText(message)}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

```tsx title="src/Chat.tsx"
import { useChat } from "@osdk/react/experimental/aip";
import { type FormEvent, useState } from "react";
import { ChatMessage } from "./ChatMessage";
import { model } from "./model";

export function Chat() {
  const { messages, status, error, sendMessage, stop, clearError } = useChat({
    model,
    system: "You are a concise assistant for employees.",
  });
  const [input, setInput] = useState("");
  const busy = status === "submitted" || status === "streaming";

  function handleSubmit(event: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    event.preventDefault();
    const text = input.trim();
    if (text === "" || busy) {
      return;
    }
    setInput("");
    void sendMessage({ text });
  }

  return (
    <div className="chat">
      {messages.map((message) => (
        <ChatMessage key={message.id} message={message} />
      ))}
      {status === "submitted" && <p className="thinking">Thinking…</p>}
      {error != null && (
        <p role="alert">
          {error.message} <button onClick={clearError}>Dismiss</button>
        </p>
      )}
      <form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
        <input
          value={input}
          onChange={(event) => setInput(event.target.value)}
          placeholder="Ask a question"
        />
        {busy ? (
          <button type="button" onClick={stop}>
            Stop
          </button>
        ) : (
          <button type="submit">Send</button>
        )}
      </form>
    </div>
  );
}
```

The list keeps rendering while a reply streams and after an error, so earlier messages never disappear.

### How streaming renders

1. `sendMessage` appends the user message and sets `status` to `"submitted"`.
2. On the first text token, an assistant message is added and `status` becomes `"streaming"`. Its single text part grows as tokens arrive.
3. Updates are batched every 50 ms by default, so a fast stream does not render once per token. Change it with `experimentalThrottle`.
4. When the stream ends, `status` returns to `"ready"` and `onFinish` fires with the final message.

`stop()` aborts the request and keeps the partial reply; `status` returns to `"ready"` with no error. A failed request sets `status` to `"error"`, fills `error`, and calls `onError`. `sendMessage` resolves in every case; it does not reject.

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | `LanguageModel` | | The model from `foundryModel`. Required unless you pass `transport`. |
| `system` | `string` | | System prompt sent with every request. Replaces any system messages in `messages`. |
| `temperature`, `maxOutputTokens`, `topP`, `presencePenalty`, `frequencyPenalty`, `stopSequences`, `seed` | | | Sampling options, as in [`generateText`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/chat.md#sampling-options). |
| `headers` | `Record<string, string \| undefined>` | | Extra HTTP headers on each request. |
| `id` | `string` | Generated | Chat id. Changing it starts a new, empty store seeded from `messages`. |
| `messages` | `ReadonlyArray<UIMessage>` | `[]` | Initial messages. Read once per `id`. |
| `transport` | `ChatTransport<UIMessage>` | `new LmsChatTransport(...)` | Replaces the default transport. When set, `model`, `system`, sampling options, and `headers` are ignored. |
| `experimentalThrottle` | `number` | `50` | Minimum milliseconds between re-renders while streaming. |
| `onError` | `(error: Error) => void` | | Called when a request or stream fails. Not called for `stop()`. |
| `onFinish` | `(event: { message, messages }) => void` | | Called once after a reply completes. |

Changing `model` or a sampling option takes effect on the next message and keeps the conversation, which is how a model picker works.

## Return value

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | The chat id. |
| `messages` | `ReadonlyArray<UIMessage>` | The conversation, including the reply in progress. |
| `status` | `ChatStatus` | `"ready"`, `"submitted"`, `"streaming"`, or `"error"`. |
| `error` | `Error \| undefined` | The last failure, while `status` is `"error"`. |
| `sendMessage` | `(input: SendMessageInput) => Promise<void>` | Sends `{ text }`, or `{ role: "user", parts }`. |
| `regenerate` | `(options?: { messageId?: string }) => Promise<void>` | Removes the last assistant message, or the one with `messageId` and everything after it, and generates again. |
| `stop` | `() => void` | Aborts the reply in progress. |
| `setMessages` | `(messages \| (prev) => messages) => void` | Replaces the conversation. Ignored while `status` is `"submitted"` or `"streaming"`; call `stop()` first. |
| `clearError` | `() => void` | Resets `status` from `"error"` to `"ready"`. |
| `resumeStream` | `() => Promise<void>` | Reconnects to a dropped stream. The LMS transport cannot reconnect, so this does nothing. |

Clear the conversation with `setMessages([])`, or render a new chat by changing `id`.

## Messages

A `UIMessage` is what the UI renders:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | Stable id. Use it as the React `key`. |
| `role` | `"system" \| "user" \| "assistant"` | Who wrote it. |
| `parts` | `Array<UIMessagePart>` | `{ type: "text", text }`, `{ type: "reasoning", text }`, or `{ type: "file", url, mediaType }`. |
| `metadata` | `Record<string, unknown>` | Optional app data. |

Only text parts reach the model. `getUIMessageText(message)` from `@osdk/aip-core` joins a message's text parts. To restore a saved conversation, pass it as `messages` with a stable `id`, and persist the final list from `onFinish`.

## Custom transports

A transport turns the conversation into a stream of `UIMessageChunk` events. The default, `LmsChatTransport` from `@osdk/aip-core`, calls `streamText` and takes the same model, `system`, sampling, and `headers` options as `useChat`. Write your own to observe or change the stream.

A `ChatTransport` has two methods:

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `sendMessages({ trigger, chatId, messageId, messages, abortSignal, headers })` | Returns `Promise<ReadableStream<UIMessageChunk>>`. `trigger` is `"submit-message"` or `"regenerate-message"`; `messageId` is the id for the assistant reply. Honor `abortSignal` so `stop()` works. |
| `reconnectToStream({ chatId })` | Returns a stream to resume, or `null`. |

This transport wraps `LmsChatTransport` and reports token usage from the `"finish"` chunk:

```ts title="src/UsageTrackingTransport.ts"
import {
  type ChatTransport,
  type ChatTransportReconnectArgs,
  type ChatTransportSendMessagesArgs,
  type LanguageModel,
  type LanguageModelUsage,
  LmsChatTransport,
  type UIMessage,
  type UIMessageChunk,
} from "@osdk/aip-core";

export class UsageTrackingTransport implements ChatTransport<UIMessage> {
  private readonly inner: LmsChatTransport;
  private readonly onUsage: (usage: LanguageModelUsage) => void;

  constructor(
    model: LanguageModel,
    system: string,
    onUsage: (usage: LanguageModelUsage) => void,
  ) {
    this.inner = new LmsChatTransport({ model, system });
    this.onUsage = onUsage;
  }

  async sendMessages(
    args: ChatTransportSendMessagesArgs<UIMessage>,
  ): Promise<ReadableStream<UIMessageChunk>> {
    const stream = await this.inner.sendMessages(args);
    const onUsage = this.onUsage;
    return stream.pipeThrough(
      new TransformStream<UIMessageChunk, UIMessageChunk>({
        transform(chunk, controller) {
          if (chunk.type === "finish" && chunk.messageMetadata?.usage != null) {
            onUsage(chunk.messageMetadata.usage);
          }
          controller.enqueue(chunk);
        },
      }),
    );
  }

  reconnectToStream(
    args: ChatTransportReconnectArgs,
  ): Promise<ReadableStream<UIMessageChunk> | null> {
    return this.inner.reconnectToStream(args);
  }
}
```

```tsx title="src/ChatWithUsage.tsx"
import { useChat } from "@osdk/react/experimental/aip";
import { useMemo, useState } from "react";
import { ChatMessage } from "./ChatMessage";
import { model } from "./model";
import { UsageTrackingTransport } from "./UsageTrackingTransport";

export function ChatWithUsage() {
  const [totalTokens, setTotalTokens] = useState(0);
  const transport = useMemo(
    () =>
      new UsageTrackingTransport(model, "You are a concise assistant.", (usage) =>
        setTotalTokens((total) => total + (usage.totalTokens ?? 0)),
      ),
    [],
  );
  const { messages, sendMessage } = useChat({ transport });

  return (
    <div>
      <p>Tokens used: {totalTokens}</p>
      {messages.map((message) => (
        <ChatMessage key={message.id} message={message} />
      ))}
      <button onClick={() => void sendMessage({ text: "Summarize my week" })}>
        Summarize
      </button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Keep the transport stable with `useMemo` or module scope, for the same reason as the model.

### Stream chunks

`LmsChatTransport` emits these chunks in order. `useChat` reads `"text-delta"` and `"error"`; the others are there for custom transports and consumers.

| `type` | Fields | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"start"` | `messageId` | The reply started. |
| `"start-step"`, `"finish-step"` | | Bracket the model call. |
| `"text-start"`, `"text-delta"`, `"text-end"` | `id`, plus `delta` on deltas | Answer text. |
| `"reasoning-start"`, `"reasoning-delta"`, `"reasoning-end"` | `id`, plus `delta` on deltas | Reasoning text, for models that return it. |
| `"tool-input-available"` | `toolCallId`, `toolName`, `input` | A tool call. `useChat` sends no tools, so this appears only from custom transports. |
| `"finish"` | `messageMetadata?: { finishReason?, usage? }` | The reply finished. |
| `"error"` | `errorText` | The stream failed. |

## Use the prebuilt component

`AipAgentChat` wraps `useChat` in a styled chat panel. It takes the `PlatformClient` and model API names and builds the model itself:

```tsx title="src/AssistantPanel.tsx"
import { AipAgentChat } from "@osdk/react-components/experimental/aip-agent-chat";
import { platformClient } from "./model";

export function AssistantPanel() {
  return (
    <AipAgentChat
      client={platformClient}
      defaultModel="gpt-4o"
      availableModels={["gpt-4o", "gpt-4o-mini"]}
      system="You are a concise assistant for employees."
    />
  );
}
```

Despite the name, it chats with a language model through the Language Model Service, not with an agent built in AIP Agent Studio. For props, render slots, `BaseAipAgentChat`, and theming, see [AipAgentChat](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/components/aip-agent-chat.md); for the stylesheet setup, see [Prerequisites](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/components/prerequisites.md). To call AIP Agents, see [Agents](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/agents.md).

# Tool calling

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/tools

> Let a Foundry-hosted model call your code to query the Ontology and propose actions, with JSON Schema tools and a confirm-before-apply loop.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Supported LLMs](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/aip/supported-llms)

Tools let the model ask your app to run code, such as an Ontology query, and then answer from the result. With `@osdk/aip-core`, the model returns tool calls and your code runs them, so you decide what executes and when.

> [!WARNING]
> `@osdk/aip-core` is at version 0.x and its API can change in any minor release. Two limits shape this page:
>
> - Each `generateText` or `streamText` call is one model step. Tools are never executed for you; you run them and loop.
> - `inputSchema` must be a plain JSON Schema object. A Zod schema is not converted: the tool is sent with empty parameters and a warning. For Zod schemas and an automatic loop, use the [AI SDK provider](#use-the-ai-sdk).

## Set up the clients

Tool code needs two clients: the Ontology `Client` to run queries and actions, and a model built on a `PlatformClient`. Create both from one token provider. This Node.js setup uses a service user; the scopes must include `api:use-language-models-execute`.

```ts title="src/client.ts"
import { $ontologyRid } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { foundryModel } from "@osdk/aip-core";
import { createClient, createPlatformClient } from "@osdk/client";
import { createConfidentialOauthClient } from "@osdk/oauth";

const foundryUrl = process.env.FOUNDRY_URL;
const clientId = process.env.FOUNDRY_CLIENT_ID;
const clientSecret = process.env.FOUNDRY_CLIENT_SECRET;

if (foundryUrl == null || clientId == null || clientSecret == null) {
  throw new Error("Set FOUNDRY_URL, FOUNDRY_CLIENT_ID, and FOUNDRY_CLIENT_SECRET");
}

const auth = createConfidentialOauthClient(clientId, clientSecret, foundryUrl, [
  "api:read-data",
  "api:write-data",
  "api:use-ontologies-read",
  "api:use-ontologies-write",
  "api:use-language-models-execute",
]);

export const client = createClient(foundryUrl, $ontologyRid, auth);
export const platformClient = createPlatformClient(foundryUrl, auth);
export const model = foundryModel({ client: platformClient, model: "gpt-4o" });
```

In a browser, use `createPublicOauthClient` with the same scopes, as shown in [Generate and stream text](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ai/chat.md#create-a-model).

## Define tools

A `ToolSet` maps tool names to definitions. The name is what the model calls, so make it descriptive.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | `string` | When and why to use the tool. The model reads this to decide. |
| `inputSchema` | JSON Schema object | The arguments, as `{ type: "object", properties, required }`. |
| `providerOptions` | `Record<string, Record<string, unknown>>` | Provider-specific options. |

```ts title="src/tools.ts"
import type { ToolSet } from "@osdk/aip-core";

export const tools = {
  searchEmployees: {
    description:
      "List employees in a department. Returns at most 20, with id, name, and job title.",
    inputSchema: {
      type: "object",
      properties: {
        department: {
          type: "string",
          description: "Exact department name, such as Engineering",
        },
      },
      required: ["department"],
      additionalProperties: false,
    },
  },
} satisfies ToolSet;
```

`satisfies ToolSet` keeps the literal tool names, so `toolName` on each returned call is typed as `"searchEmployees"`.

### Control tool choice

| `toolChoice` | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `"auto"` | The model decides whether to call a tool. The default when tools are present. |
| `"required"` | The model must call at least one tool. |
| `"none"` | The model must answer in text. |
| `{ type: "tool", toolName: "searchEmployees" }` | The model must call that tool. |

## Read tool calls

When the model wants a tool, `finishReason` is `"tool-calls"` and `toolCalls` lists each call:

```ts title="src/firstStep.ts"
import { generateText } from "@osdk/aip-core";
import { model } from "./client";
import { tools } from "./tools";

const result = await generateText({
  model,
  prompt: "Who works in Engineering?",
  tools,
});

for (const call of result.toolCalls) {
  console.log(call.toolCallId, call.toolName, call.input);
}
```

| `ToolCall` field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `toolCallId` | `string` | Pass it back with the result. |
| `toolName` | `string` | The tool to run. |
| `input` | `unknown` | Arguments parsed from the model's JSON. If the JSON is invalid, the raw string, with a warning. |

`input` is whatever the model produced. It is not validated against `inputSchema`, so check it before use.

## Run the loop

To finish the answer, append the model's message and a `tool` message with your results, then call the model again. Stop when it answers without tool calls, or after a step limit.

```ts title="src/answer.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import {
  generateText,
  type ModelMessage,
  type ToolCall,
  type ToolResultOutput,
  type ToolResultPart,
} from "@osdk/aip-core";
import { client, model } from "./client";
import { tools } from "./tools";

function readString(input: unknown, key: string): string | undefined {
  if (typeof input !== "object" || input == null) {
    return undefined;
  }
  const value = (input as Record<string, unknown>)[key];
  return typeof value === "string" ? value : undefined;
}

async function runTool(call: ToolCall): Promise<ToolResultOutput> {
  switch (call.toolName) {
    case "searchEmployees": {
      const department = readString(call.input, "department");
      if (department == null) {
        return { type: "error-text", value: "department must be a string" };
      }
      const page = await client(Employee)
        .where({ department })
        .fetchPage({ $pageSize: 20, $select: ["employeeId", "fullName", "jobTitle"] });
      return {
        type: "json",
        value: page.data.map((e) => ({
          employeeId: e.employeeId,
          fullName: e.fullName,
          jobTitle: e.jobTitle,
        })),
      };
    }
    default:
      return { type: "error-text", value: `Unknown tool: ${call.toolName}` };
  }
}

export async function answer(question: string, maxSteps = 5): Promise<string> {
  const messages: Array<ModelMessage> = [{ role: "user", content: question }];

  for (let step = 0; step < maxSteps; step++) {
    const result = await generateText({
      model,
      system: "Answer questions about employees. Use tools to look up data.",
      messages,
      tools,
    });

    messages.push(...(result.response?.messages ?? []));
    if (result.toolCalls.length === 0) {
      return result.text;
    }

    const content: Array<ToolResultPart> = [];
    for (const call of result.toolCalls) {
      let output: ToolResultOutput;
      try {
        output = await runTool(call);
      } catch (error) {
        output = { type: "error-text", value: String(error) };
      }
      content.push({
        type: "tool-result",
        toolCallId: call.toolCallId,
        toolName: call.toolName,
        output,
      });
    }
    messages.push({ role: "tool", content });
  }

  throw new Error(`No answer after ${maxSteps} steps`);
}
```

`result.response.messages` holds the assistant message, including its tool-call parts. Each `tool-result` part must use the `toolCallId` of the call it answers.

A tool result `output` is one of:

| `type` | `value` | Sent to the model as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"text"` | `string` | The string. |
| `"json"` | `unknown` | `JSON.stringify(value)`. |
| `"error-text"` | `string` | The string. Use it so the model can recover from bad input. |
| `"error-json"` | `unknown` | `JSON.stringify(value)`. |
| `"content"` | Array of `{ type: "text", text }` and media parts | The text parts joined by newlines. Media is dropped. |

### Keep tool results small

Every tool result is sent back as input tokens on the next step.

- Pass `$select` so the query loads only the properties the model needs. See [Load objects](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/objects.md).
- Set a small `$pageSize` and say the limit in the tool description.
- Map OSDK objects to plain fields, as above, instead of returning whole instances.
- Filter on the server with `where` instead of asking the model to filter a long list. See [Filter objects](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/filtering.md).

## Propose actions, then confirm

A model can misread a request or be steered by text in the data it reads. Do not apply an action from inside a tool. Have the tool record a proposal, show it to the user, and apply it only after they confirm.

```ts title="src/proposals.ts"
import { modifyEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import type { ToolCall, ToolResultOutput, ToolSet } from "@osdk/aip-core";
import { client } from "./client";

export interface JobTitleProposal {
  employeeId: number;
  jobTitle: string;
}

export const actionTools = {
  proposeJobTitleChange: {
    description:
      "Propose a new job title for an employee. This does not change anything; the user reviews and confirms it.",
    inputSchema: {
      type: "object",
      properties: {
        employeeId: { type: "integer" },
        jobTitle: { type: "string" },
      },
      required: ["employeeId", "jobTitle"],
      additionalProperties: false,
    },
  },
} satisfies ToolSet;

export const proposals: Array<JobTitleProposal> = [];

export async function runProposalTool(call: ToolCall): Promise<ToolResultOutput> {
  const input = call.input as Partial<Record<string, unknown>>;
  const { employeeId, jobTitle } = input;
  if (typeof employeeId !== "number" || typeof jobTitle !== "string") {
    return { type: "error-text", value: "employeeId must be a number and jobTitle a string" };
  }

  const validation = await client(modifyEmployee).applyAction(
    { employee: employeeId, jobTitle },
    { $validateOnly: true },
  );
  if (validation.result !== "VALID") {
    return { type: "error-json", value: validation.parameters };
  }

  proposals.push({ employeeId, jobTitle });
  return { type: "text", value: "Proposal recorded. The user must confirm it." };
}

export async function applyProposal(proposal: JobTitleProposal): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await client(modifyEmployee).applyAction({
      employee: proposal.employeeId,
      jobTitle: proposal.jobTitle,
    });
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("Could not apply the change", error);
    throw error;
  }
}
```

Call `runProposalTool` from your loop's `runTool` for `proposeJobTitleChange`, and pass `{ ...tools, ...actionTools }` to `generateText`. `$validateOnly: true` checks the parameters against the action's rules without applying it, so the model learns about invalid input while it can still correct it. Show `proposals` in your UI and call `applyProposal` from the user's confirm button. See [Apply actions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/actions.md) for the validation result and errors.

## Stream with tools

`streamText` takes the same `tools` and `toolChoice`. Tool calls arrive on `fullStream` as `"tool-call"` chunks after the text, once the model finishes, and `toolCalls` resolves to the same list. Run them and call `streamText` again with the extended `messages`. `(await result.response)?.messages` holds the assistant message to append.

## Use the AI SDK

The AI SDK provider in `@osdk/aip-core/ai-sdk` accepts Zod schemas, runs each tool's `execute` for you, and loops until a stop condition. It needs `ai` version 6.

```npm
npm install @osdk/aip-core ai @ai-sdk/provider zod
```

```ts title="src/aiSdkTools.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { createFoundryAI } from "@osdk/aip-core/ai-sdk";
import { generateText, stepCountIs, tool } from "ai";
import { z } from "zod";
import { client, platformClient } from "./client";

const foundry = createFoundryAI({ client: platformClient });

const result = await generateText({
  model: foundry("gpt-4o"),
  system: "Answer questions about employees. Use tools to look up data.",
  prompt: "Who works in Engineering?",
  stopWhen: stepCountIs(5),
  tools: {
    searchEmployees: tool({
      description: "List employees in a department. Returns at most 20.",
      inputSchema: z.object({ department: z.string() }),
      execute: async ({ department }) => {
        const page = await client(Employee)
          .where({ department })
          .fetchPage({ $pageSize: 20, $select: ["employeeId", "fullName", "jobTitle"] });
        return page.data.map((e) => ({
          employeeId: e.employeeId,
          fullName: e.fullName,
          jobTitle: e.jobTitle,
        }));
      },
    }),
  },
});

console.log(result.text);
```

`execute` runs without asking anyone, so keep action tools on the propose-then-confirm pattern above: `execute` records the proposal and your UI applies it.

## Safety checklist

- Treat tool `input` as untrusted. Check types and ranges before you query or write.
- Tool calls run with the signed-in user's permissions, or the service user's in Node. Give a service user only the scopes and data access the feature needs.
- Never apply an action, send a message, or delete data without an explicit user confirmation.
- Limit the number of steps so a confused model cannot loop forever.
- Text in Ontology data can contain instructions. Do not let tool results grant the model new permissions.

# Call platform APIs

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/calling-apis

> The calling convention for @osdk/foundry functions, including argument order, pagination, errors, binary responses, and preview endpoints.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [API getting started](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/api/v2/general/overview/getting-started)

{/* cspell:ignore mediasets */}

Every Platform SDK function takes the client first, then the endpoint's path, body, query, and header arguments, in that order. This page covers that convention and how to handle pagination, errors, binary content, and preview endpoints.

## Import a namespace

Each package exports one namespace per resource, named in the plural: `Users`, `Groups`, `Datasets`, `Files`, `MediaSets`. Each function in a namespace maps to one REST endpoint.

```ts title="src/currentUser.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { Users, type User } from "@osdk/foundry.admin";

export async function currentUser(client: Client): Promise<User> {
  return Users.getCurrent(client);
}
```

Request and response types, such as `User`, `Group`, and `ListUsersResponse`, are exported by name from the same package. Identifier types such as `UserId` and `PageToken` are strings, so plain string values work wherever they are expected.

## Argument order

After the client, a function takes up to four groups of arguments, always in this order:

| Position | Argument | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | The client | `client` |
| 2 | Path parameters, one positional argument each, in URL order | `datasetRid`, `filePath` |
| 3 | The request body, for `POST` and `PUT` endpoints | `{ where: { type: "queryString", value: "jane" } }` |
| 4 | Query parameters, as one object | `{ pageSize: 100, preview: true }` |
| 5 | Header parameters, as one object | `{ ReadToken: token }` |

A function only takes the groups its endpoint has:

```ts title="src/examples.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { GroupMembers, Groups, Users } from "@osdk/foundry.admin";
import { Files } from "@osdk/foundry.datasets";

export async function examples(client: Client, groupId: string, userId: string) {
  // Path parameter only
  const group = await Groups.get(client, groupId);

  // Path parameter, then query parameters
  const members = await GroupMembers.list(client, groupId, { transitive: true });

  // Body only
  const matches = await Users.search(client, {
    where: { type: "queryString", value: "jane" },
  });

  // Path parameter, then body
  await GroupMembers.add(client, groupId, { principalIds: [userId] });

  // Two path parameters, a binary body, then query parameters
  const file = await Files.upload(
    client,
    "ri.foundry.main.dataset.<id>",
    "reports/summary.csv",
    new Blob(["name,count\nalpha,1\n"], { type: "text/csv" }),
    { transactionType: "UPDATE" },
  );

  return { group, members, matches, file };
}
```

When a function has optional query parameters and you need to pass headers, pass `undefined` or an object for the query parameters first. Your editor shows the parameter names, such as `$queryParams` and `$headerParams`, on hover.

## Responses

| Endpoint returns | The function resolves to |
| --- | --- |
| JSON | The parsed body, typed, such as `User` or `ListGroupsResponse`. |
| No content (`204`) | `undefined`. The return type is `Promise<void>`. |
| Binary content | The `Response`. Read it with `.blob()`, `.arrayBuffer()`, `.text()`, or `.body`. |

Binary endpoints include `Files.content`, `Datasets.readTable`, `MediaSets.read`, and `Users.profilePicture`. Their return type is `Promise<Response>`:

```ts title="src/avatar.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { Users } from "@osdk/foundry.admin";

export async function avatarUrl(client: Client, userId: string): Promise<string> {
  const response = await Users.profilePicture(client, userId);
  const blob = await response.blob();
  return URL.createObjectURL(blob);
}
```

Call `URL.revokeObjectURL` when you no longer show the image.

Upload endpoints such as `Files.upload` and `MediaSets.upload` take the bytes as a `Blob`. A `File` from an `<input type="file">` is a `Blob`, so you can pass it directly.

## Paginate

List and search endpoints return one page at a time as `{ data, nextPageToken }`. Pass `nextPageToken` back as `pageToken` to get the next page. The last page has no `nextPageToken`.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pageSize` | `number` | Preferred page size. The server can return more or fewer items, and some endpoints cap it. |
| `pageToken` | `string` | Token from the previous page. Omit it for the first page. |

For `GET` endpoints, such as `Users.list`, these are query parameters. For `POST` endpoints, such as `Users.search`, they go in the body.

A small async generator turns any paged endpoint into a stream of items:

```ts title="src/paginate.ts"
export async function* paginate<T>(
  fetchPage: (
    pageToken: string | undefined,
  ) => Promise<{ data: T[]; nextPageToken?: string }>,
): AsyncGenerator<T> {
  let pageToken: string | undefined;
  do {
    const page = await fetchPage(pageToken);
    for (const item of page.data) {
      yield item;
    }
    pageToken = page.nextPageToken;
  } while (pageToken != null);
}
```

Use it with query-parameter and body pagination alike:

```ts title="src/listAllUsers.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { Users, type User } from "@osdk/foundry.admin";
import { paginate } from "./paginate";

export async function listAllUsers(client: Client): Promise<User[]> {
  const users: User[] = [];
  for await (const user of paginate((pageToken) =>
    Users.list(client, { pageSize: 1000, pageToken }),
  )) {
    users.push(user);
  }
  return users;
}

export async function findUsers(client: Client, prefix: string, limit: number) {
  const found: User[] = [];
  for await (const user of paginate((pageToken) =>
    Users.search(client, {
      where: { type: "queryString", value: prefix },
      pageSize: 100,
      pageToken,
    }),
  )) {
    found.push(user);
    if (found.length >= limit) {
      break;
    }
  }
  return found;
}
```

Breaking out of the loop stops further requests.

## Batch requests

Resources with many lookups have a `getBatch` function that takes an array of request elements and returns a `data` map keyed by ID. Each documents its maximum batch size in JSDoc; `Users.getBatch` accepts up to 500:

```ts title="src/usernames.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { Users } from "@osdk/foundry.admin";

export async function usernames(client: Client, userIds: string[]) {
  const { data } = await Users.getBatch(
    client,
    userIds.map((userId) => ({ userId })),
  );
  return userIds.map((id) => data[id]?.username ?? "Unknown user");
}
```

## Handle errors

A failed call rejects with a `PalantirApiError`, exported from `@osdk/client`. This includes network failures and error responses that are not JSON; those have no `errorName`, and the underlying error is on `cause`. If the token provider itself throws, the call rejects with a plain `Error`.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | `string` | The server's message, or `Failed to fetch <status> <statusText>`. |
| `errorName` | `string \| undefined` | Stable identifier, such as `UserNotFound` or `ApiFeaturePreviewUsageOnly`. Switch on this. |
| `errorCode` | `string \| undefined` | Category, such as `NOT_FOUND`, `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, or `CONFLICT`. |
| `errorDescription` | `string \| undefined` | Human-readable description. |
| `statusCode` | `number \| undefined` | HTTP status. |
| `errorInstanceId` | `string \| undefined` | Server-side ID for this occurrence. Include it in support requests. |
| `parameters` | `object \| undefined` | Context for the error, such as `{ userId }`. |

```ts title="src/findUser.ts"
import { PalantirApiError, type Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { Users, type User } from "@osdk/foundry.admin";

export async function findUser(client: Client, userId: string): Promise<User | undefined> {
  try {
    return await Users.get(client, userId);
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof PalantirApiError && error.errorName === "UserNotFound") {
      return undefined;
    }
    throw error;
  }
}
```

Each package exports a type for every error it can return, with the exact `errorName`, `errorCode`, and `parameters`. Import them to see what to expect:

```ts
import type { UserNotFound } from "@osdk/foundry.admin";
// { errorCode: "NOT_FOUND"; errorName: "UserNotFound"; parameters: { userId: unknown }; ... }
```

Shared errors, such as `ApiFeaturePreviewUsageOnly`, `InvalidPageToken`, and `ApiUsageDenied`, are exported from `@osdk/foundry.core`.

The client retries `429` and `503` responses up to three times before rejecting. Other errors reject immediately.

## Preview endpoints

Functions tagged `@beta` or `@alpha` in JSDoc call preview endpoints. They take a `preview` query parameter, and the server rejects the call with `ApiFeaturePreviewUsageOnly` unless you set it to `true`:

```ts title="src/classificationBanner.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { CbacBanners } from "@osdk/foundry.admin";

export async function classificationBanner(client: Client, markingIds: string[]) {
  const banner = await CbacBanners.get(client, { markingIds, preview: true });
  return banner.classificationString;
}
```

`preview` always goes in the query-parameter object, after any body:

```ts title="src/parseClassification.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { Markings } from "@osdk/foundry.admin";

export async function parseClassification(client: Client, classification: string) {
  return Markings.parseClassifications(
    client,
    { classificationStrings: [classification] },
    { preview: true },
  );
}
```

Preview endpoints can change shape between package versions. Pin the package version, and check the changelog when you upgrade.

# Datasets

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/datasets

> Read dataset files and tables, upload files in transactions, and manage branches with @osdk/foundry.datasets.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Datasets](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/data-integration/datasets)
- [Dataset API](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/api/v2/datasets-v2-resources/datasets/dataset-basics)

`@osdk/foundry.datasets` reads and writes Foundry datasets. Use it to download a file, export a table as CSV or Arrow, upload files, and group several uploads into one transaction.

```npm
npm install @osdk/client @osdk/oauth @osdk/foundry.datasets
```

Every sample takes a `client` from `createClient` or `createPlatformClient`; see [Set up](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/setup.md). Reads need the `api:datasets-read` scope and writes need `api:datasets-write`. A dataset is identified by its RID, such as `ri.foundry.main.dataset.<id>`.

> [!NOTE]
> This page describes version 2.78 of `@osdk/foundry.datasets`. In older versions, such as 2.5, `Files.content` and `Datasets.readTable` resolve to a `Blob` instead of a `Response`.

## Get a dataset

`Datasets.get` returns the dataset's `rid`, `name`, and `parentFolderRid`. `Datasets.getSchema` returns its column schema:

```ts title="src/describeDataset.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { Datasets } from "@osdk/foundry.datasets";

export async function describeDataset(client: Client, datasetRid: string) {
  const [dataset, { schema }] = await Promise.all([
    Datasets.get(client, datasetRid),
    Datasets.getSchema(client, datasetRid),
  ]);
  return {
    name: dataset.name,
    columns: schema.fieldSchemaList.map((field) => `${field.name}: ${field.type}`),
  };
}
```

`Datasets.getSchema` reads the latest committed version of the default branch. Pass `{ branchName }` or `{ endTransactionRid }` to read another.

## Read a table

`Datasets.readTable` exports a tabular dataset as CSV or Apache Arrow and resolves to a `Response`:

```ts title="src/readCsv.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { Datasets } from "@osdk/foundry.datasets";

export async function readCsv(client: Client, datasetRid: string): Promise<string> {
  const response = await Datasets.readTable(client, datasetRid, {
    format: "CSV",
    columns: ["employeeId", "fullName", "department"],
    rowLimit: 1000,
  });
  return response.text();
}
```

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `format` | `"CSV" \| "ARROW"` | Required. The export format. |
| `columns` | `string[]` | Required. The columns to include. Pass `[]` for all columns. |
| `rowLimit` | `number` | The maximum number of rows. Row order is not deterministic. |
| `branchName` | `string` | The branch to read. Defaults to the dataset's default branch. |
| `startTransactionRid`, `endTransactionRid` | `string` | Read the view at, or between, specific transactions. |

For `"ARROW"`, read the body with `response.arrayBuffer()` and decode it with an Arrow library such as `apache-arrow`. `readTable` does not support views.

## List and download files

`Files.list` lists the files in the latest view of the default branch, one page at a time. `Files.content` downloads one file:

```ts title="src/downloadFiles.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { Files } from "@osdk/foundry.datasets";

export async function listCsvFiles(client: Client, datasetRid: string): Promise<string[]> {
  const { data } = await Files.list(client, datasetRid, { pageSize: 100 });
  return data.filter((file) => file.path.endsWith(".csv")).map((file) => file.path);
}

export async function downloadFile(
  client: Client,
  datasetRid: string,
  filePath: string,
): Promise<Blob> {
  const response = await Files.content(client, datasetRid, filePath);
  return response.blob();
}
```

Each `File` has `path`, `transactionRid`, `sizeBytes` (a string, when known), and `updatedTime`. `Files.get` returns the same metadata for one path.

`Files.list`, `Files.get`, and `Files.content` take the same view options:

| Option | Reads |
| --- | --- |
| None | The latest view of the default branch. |
| `branchName` | The latest view of that branch. |
| `endTransactionRid` | The view as of that transaction. |
| `startTransactionRid` and `endTransactionRid` | Files changed between the two transactions. Set both to the same RID to see only that transaction's files. |

To read every page of `Files.list`, use the `paginate` helper from [Call platform APIs](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/calling-apis.md#paginate).

## Upload a single file

`Files.upload` takes the dataset RID, the file path, and the content as a `Blob`. Without options, it uploads in a new transaction on the default branch and commits it:

```ts title="src/uploadFile.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { Files } from "@osdk/foundry.datasets";

export async function uploadCsv(client: Client, datasetRid: string, csv: string) {
  return Files.upload(
    client,
    datasetRid,
    "exports/employees.csv",
    new Blob([csv], { type: "text/csv" }),
  );
}
```

It resolves to the new `File`. If a file already exists at that path, only the newest version is visible afterwards.

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `branchName` | `string` | Upload to this branch in a new transaction, which is committed. |
| `transactionType` | `"APPEND" \| "UPDATE" \| "SNAPSHOT" \| "DELETE"` | With `branchName`, the type of the new transaction. Defaults to `"UPDATE"`. |
| `transactionRid` | `string` | Upload into an open transaction that you commit yourself. |

In a browser, a `File` from `<input type="file">` is a `Blob`, so you can pass it as the content.

## Upload in a transaction

To upload several files atomically, open a transaction, upload into it, then commit. If anything fails, abort it so no partial upload becomes visible:

Create a transaction with `Transactions.create`. Pass the branch as a query parameter, or omit it for the default branch.
Upload each file with `Files.upload`, passing `transactionRid`.
Call `Transactions.commit`, or `Transactions.abort` on failure.

```ts title="src/uploadBatch.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { Files, Transactions } from "@osdk/foundry.datasets";

export async function replaceDatasetContents(
  client: Client,
  datasetRid: string,
  files: Array<{ path: string; content: Blob }>,
) {
  const transaction = await Transactions.create(
    client,
    datasetRid,
    { transactionType: "SNAPSHOT" },
    { branchName: "master" },
  );

  try {
    for (const file of files) {
      await Files.upload(client, datasetRid, file.path, file.content, {
        transactionRid: transaction.rid,
      });
    }
    return await Transactions.commit(client, datasetRid, transaction.rid);
  } catch (error) {
    await Transactions.abort(client, datasetRid, transaction.rid);
    throw error;
  }
}
```

The transaction type decides what the committed view contains:

| Type | Effect on the view |
| --- | --- |
| `SNAPSHOT` | Replaces every file. The view contains only files from this transaction. |
| `UPDATE` | Adds files and overwrites files at the same paths. |
| `APPEND` | Adds new files. It cannot overwrite existing files. |
| `DELETE` | Removes files. Use it with `Files.deleteFile` and `transactionRid`. |

A `Transaction` has `rid`, `transactionType`, `status` (`"OPEN"`, `"COMMITTED"`, or `"ABORTED"`), `createdTime`, and `closedTime`. Check a transaction later with `Transactions.get`.

## Delete a file

`Files.deleteFile` removes a file in a new `DELETE` transaction on the default branch, which it commits. The file stays visible in historical views. Pass `branchName` for another branch, or `transactionRid` to delete several files in one open `DELETE` transaction:

```ts title="src/deleteFile.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { Files } from "@osdk/foundry.datasets";

export async function deleteExport(client: Client, datasetRid: string) {
  await Files.deleteFile(client, datasetRid, "exports/employees.csv");
}
```

## Work with branches

`Branches` creates, reads, lists, and deletes dataset branches. A new branch can point at a committed transaction:

```ts title="src/branches.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { Branches, Files } from "@osdk/foundry.datasets";

export async function uploadToFeatureBranch(
  client: Client,
  datasetRid: string,
  content: Blob,
) {
  const main = await Branches.get(client, datasetRid, "master");
  await Branches.create(client, datasetRid, {
    name: "feature-update",
    transactionRid: main.transactionRid,
  });
  await Files.upload(client, datasetRid, "data/latest.csv", content, {
    branchName: "feature-update",
  });

  const { data } = await Branches.list(client, datasetRid);
  return data.map((branch) => branch.name);
}
```

Each `Branch` has a `name` and the `transactionRid` it points to, if any. Delete one with `Branches.deleteBranch(client, datasetRid, branchName)`. The default branch is `master` on most stacks.

## Create a dataset

`Datasets.create` creates an empty dataset in a folder, with a default branch:

```ts title="src/createDataset.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { Datasets } from "@osdk/foundry.datasets";

export async function createDataset(client: Client, folderRid: string) {
  const dataset = await Datasets.create(client, {
    name: "employee-exports",
    parentFolderRid: folderRid,
  });
  return dataset.rid;
}
```

## Reference

| Function | Endpoint | Scope | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Datasets.get(client, datasetRid)` | `GET /v2/datasets/{datasetRid}` | `api:datasets-read` | `Dataset` |
| `Datasets.create(client, body)` | `POST /v2/datasets` | `api:datasets-write` | `Dataset` |
| `Datasets.getSchema(client, datasetRid, query?)` | `GET /v2/datasets/{datasetRid}/getSchema` | `api:datasets-read` | `GetDatasetSchemaResponse` |
| `Datasets.readTable(client, datasetRid, query)` | `GET /v2/datasets/{datasetRid}/readTable` | `api:datasets-read` | `Response` |
| `Files.list(client, datasetRid, query?)` | `GET /v2/datasets/{datasetRid}/files` | `api:datasets-read` | `ListFilesResponse` |
| `Files.get(client, datasetRid, filePath, query?)` | `GET /v2/datasets/{datasetRid}/files/{filePath}` | `api:datasets-read` | `File` |
| `Files.content(client, datasetRid, filePath, query?)` | `GET /v2/datasets/{datasetRid}/files/{filePath}/content` | `api:datasets-read` | `Response` |
| `Files.upload(client, datasetRid, filePath, blob, query?)` | `POST /v2/datasets/{datasetRid}/files/{filePath}/upload` | `api:datasets-write` | `File` |
| `Files.deleteFile(client, datasetRid, filePath, query?)` | `DELETE /v2/datasets/{datasetRid}/files/{filePath}` | `api:datasets-write` | `void` |
| `Transactions.create(client, datasetRid, body, query?)` | `POST /v2/datasets/{datasetRid}/transactions` | `api:datasets-write` | `Transaction` |
| `Transactions.get(client, datasetRid, transactionRid)` | `GET /v2/datasets/{datasetRid}/transactions/{transactionRid}` | `api:datasets-read` | `Transaction` |
| `Transactions.commit(client, datasetRid, transactionRid)` | `POST .../transactions/{transactionRid}/commit` | `api:datasets-write` | `Transaction` |
| `Transactions.abort(client, datasetRid, transactionRid)` | `POST .../transactions/{transactionRid}/abort` | `api:datasets-write` | `Transaction` |
| `Branches.list(client, datasetRid, query?)` | `GET /v2/datasets/{datasetRid}/branches` | `api:datasets-read` | `ListBranchesResponse` |
| `Branches.get(client, datasetRid, branchName)` | `GET /v2/datasets/{datasetRid}/branches/{branchName}` | `api:datasets-read` | `Branch` |
| `Branches.create(client, datasetRid, body)` | `POST /v2/datasets/{datasetRid}/branches` | `api:datasets-write` | `Branch` |
| `Branches.deleteBranch(client, datasetRid, branchName)` | `DELETE /v2/datasets/{datasetRid}/branches/{branchName}` | `api:datasets-write` | `void` |

All of these are stable. The package also covers views (`Views`) and a dataset's schedules (`Datasets.getSchedules`), and has preview endpoints for transaction history, jobs, and health checks that need `preview: true`, as described in [Call platform APIs](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/calling-apis.md#preview-endpoints).

# Platform SDK overview

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform

> The @osdk/foundry packages wrap Foundry platform REST APIs for users, datasets, media sets, builds, and more, alongside the Ontology SDK.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Foundry REST APIs](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/api/v2/general/overview/introduction)

{/* cspell:ignore aipagents datahealth geojson languagemodels mediasets publicapis sqlqueries thirdpartyapplications CBAC */}

The Platform SDK is a set of `@osdk/foundry.*` packages, one per area of the Foundry API. Use it to call the parts of Foundry that are not Ontology data: users and groups, datasets, media sets, builds, folders, and Ontology metadata.

## OSDK and Platform SDK

The Ontology SDK (OSDK) and the Platform SDK can share one client and one token provider. They cover different parts of Foundry.

| | Ontology SDK | Platform SDK |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Use it for | Reading and editing your Ontology: objects, links, actions, functions. | Foundry platform resources: users, groups, markings, datasets, media sets, builds, files, Ontology metadata. |
| Packages | `@osdk/client` plus an SDK generated for your Ontology, such as `@my-app/sdk`. | Fixed packages published by Palantir, such as `@osdk/foundry.admin`. The same package works on every Foundry stack. |
| Types | Generated from your object types, so `Employee` has `fullName` and `startDate`. | Generic request and response types from the public API, such as `User` and `Dataset`. |
| Call style | `client(Employee).fetchPage()` | `Users.getCurrent(client)` |
| Client | `createClient(baseUrl, ontologyRid, auth)` | The same client, or `createPlatformClient(baseUrl, auth)` when there is no Ontology. |

```ts title="src/whoami.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { Users } from "@osdk/foundry.admin";

export async function loadDashboard(client: Client) {
  const [me, employees] = await Promise.all([
    Users.getCurrent(client),
    client(Employee).fetchPage({ $pageSize: 10 }),
  ]);
  return { username: me.username, employees: employees.data };
}
```

Use the Platform SDK when the OSDK has no equivalent. To read objects, apply actions, or upload media to an object property, use the OSDK.

## Packages

Each package exports one namespace per resource. Install only the packages you call.

| Package | Namespaces | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@osdk/foundry.admin` | `Users`, `Groups`, `GroupMembers`, `GroupMemberships`, `Markings`, `MarkingCategories`, `MarkingMembers`, `Organizations`, `Roles`, `CbacBanners`, and more | Users, groups, memberships, markings, organizations, and classification banners. |
| `@osdk/foundry.aipagents` | `Agents`, `AgentVersions`, `Sessions`, `Contents`, `SessionTraces` | Start and read conversations with AIP Agents. |
| `@osdk/foundry.agents` | `AgentDefinitionVersions`, `AgentSessions` | Agent definitions and sessions. Published from version 2.83.0. |
| `@osdk/foundry.audit` | `LogFiles` | List and download audit log files. |
| `@osdk/foundry.checkpoints` | `Records` | Read checkpoint records. |
| `@osdk/foundry.connectivity` | `Connections`, `FileImports`, `TableImports`, `VirtualTables` | Data Connection sources, imports, and virtual tables. |
| `@osdk/foundry.core` | Types only | Shared types, such as `PageSize`, `PageToken`, `UserId`, and `PreviewMode`, used by every other package. |
| `@osdk/foundry.datahealth` | `Checks`, `CheckReports` | Data health checks and their reports. |
| `@osdk/foundry.datasets` | `Datasets`, `Branches`, `Files`, `Transactions`, `Views` | Create datasets, read and upload files, read tables, and manage branches and transactions. |
| `@osdk/foundry.filesystem` | `Folders`, `Projects`, `Resources`, `ResourceRoles`, `Spaces`, and more | Folders, projects, and resource permissions in the Foundry filesystem. |
| `@osdk/foundry.functions` | `Queries`, `Executions`, `ValueTypes`, `VersionIds` | Function metadata, execution, and value types. |
| `@osdk/foundry.geo` | Types only | Types for geographic data. |
| `@osdk/foundry.geojson` | Types only | GeoJSON types. |
| `@osdk/foundry.languagemodels` | `Anthropic`, `OpenAi` | Call language models hosted in Foundry. |
| `@osdk/foundry.mediasets` | `MediaSets` | Upload media items, read their content and metadata, and run transformations. |
| `@osdk/foundry.models` | `Models`, `ModelVersions`, `LiveDeployments`, `Experiments`, and more | Models, versions, deployments, and experiments. |
| `@osdk/foundry.notepad` | `Templates`, `GenerationJobs`, `ExportJobs`, `Files` | Generate and export Notepad documents. |
| `@osdk/foundry.ontologies` | `OntologiesV2`, `ObjectTypesV2`, `ActionTypesV2`, `QueryTypes`, `OntologyInterfaces`, and more | Ontology metadata and the raw object, action, and query endpoints that the OSDK is built on. |
| `@osdk/foundry.operations` | `AsyncOperations` | Poll long-running operations. |
| `@osdk/foundry.orchestration` | `Builds`, `Jobs`, `Schedules`, `ScheduleVersions` | Start and monitor builds, and manage schedules. |
| `@osdk/foundry.pack` | `Documents`, `DocumentTypes` | PACK documents and document types. |
| `@osdk/foundry.publicapis` | `ApiDefinitions`, `OpenApiDefinitions` | Fetch API specifications. |
| `@osdk/foundry.sqlqueries` | `SqlQueries` | Run SQL queries and read their results. |
| `@osdk/foundry.streams` | `Datasets`, `Streams`, `Subscribers` | Streaming datasets, streams, and subscribers. |
| `@osdk/foundry.thirdpartyapplications` | `ThirdPartyApplications`, `Versions`, `Websites` | Developer Console applications and hosted website versions. |
| `@osdk/foundry.widgets` | `WidgetSets`, `Releases`, `Repositories`, `WidgetsDevModeSettings`, `WidgetsDevModeSettingsV2` | Custom widget sets, releases, and dev mode. |

`@osdk/foundry` re-exports every package as a namespace, such as `Admin` and `Datasets`. Prefer the individual packages: they version independently and keep your bundle small.

```ts
import { Admin } from "@osdk/foundry";

const me = await Admin.Users.getCurrent(client);
```

## Stable and preview endpoints

Every function's JSDoc carries a release tag:

| Tag | Meaning | How to call it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@public` | Stable. | Call it normally. |
| `@beta` | Preview. The shape can change between versions. | Pass `preview: true` in the query parameters. |
| `@alpha` | Early preview. Expect changes, and the endpoint may not be enabled on every stack. | Pass `preview: true` in the query parameters. |

Preview endpoints take an optional `preview` query parameter of type `PreviewMode` (a `boolean`). Without it, the server rejects the request with an `ApiFeaturePreviewUsageOnly` error:

```ts
import { Groups } from "@osdk/foundry.admin";

const { data: myGroups } = await Groups.listCurrent(client, { preview: true });
```

The [calling convention](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/calling-apis.md#preview-endpoints) page covers where `preview` goes when an endpoint has a body.
