- [Call platform APIs](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/calling-apis.md): Argument order, pagination, errors, and binary responses.
- [Users and groups](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/users-and-groups.md): Look up users, list groups and members, and read markings.
- [Datasets](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/datasets.md): Read files and tables, and upload in transactions.
- [Media sets](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/media-sets.md): Upload media items and read their content and metadata.
- [Ontology metadata](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/ontology-metadata.md): List object types and action types at runtime.

For React hooks that call the admin APIs, see [Users and markings in React](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/platform-apis.md).

# Media sets

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/media-sets

> Upload media items, read their content and metadata, and run transformations with @osdk/foundry.mediasets.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Media set API](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/api/v2/media-sets-v2-resources/media-sets/media-set-basics)

{/* cspell:ignore mediasets webp dicom */}

`@osdk/foundry.mediasets` works with media sets: Foundry collections of images, documents, audio, video, and other files. Use it to upload items to a media set, download them, read their metadata, and convert them with transformations.

```npm
npm install @osdk/client @osdk/oauth @osdk/foundry.mediasets
```

Every sample takes a `client` from `createClient` or `createPlatformClient`; see [Set up](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/setup.md). Reads need the `api:mediasets-read` scope, uploads need `api:mediasets-write`, and transformations need `api:mediasets-transform`. All functions are on the `MediaSets` namespace.

> [!NOTE]
> To read media from an object property or upload a file as an action parameter, use the OSDK instead. It handles the media reference and read token for you. See [Media](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/media.md).

## Identify a media item

A media set has a RID such as `ri.mio.main.media-set.<id>`, and each item in it has a media item RID. Functions take both as path parameters, in that order.

When you only have the item's path in the set, look up its RID with `getRidByPath`. It is a preview endpoint:

```ts title="src/findItem.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { MediaSets } from "@osdk/foundry.mediasets";

export async function findItem(client: Client, mediaSetRid: string, path: string) {
  const { mediaItemRid } = await MediaSets.getRidByPath(client, mediaSetRid, {
    mediaItemPath: path,
    preview: true,
  });
  return mediaItemRid;
}
```

`mediaItemRid` is `undefined` when no item has that path.

## Download an item

`MediaSets.read` resolves to a `Response` with the item's content:

```ts title="src/downloadItem.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { MediaSets } from "@osdk/foundry.mediasets";

export async function itemObjectUrl(
  client: Client,
  mediaSetRid: string,
  mediaItemRid: string,
): Promise<string> {
  const response = await MediaSets.read(client, mediaSetRid, mediaItemRid);
  return URL.createObjectURL(await response.blob());
}
```

If the set converted the file on upload, `read` returns the converted content. `MediaSets.readOriginal` returns the file as it was uploaded.

## Read metadata

`MediaSets.info` returns basic information, and `MediaSets.metadata` returns details that depend on the media type:

```ts title="src/describeItem.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { MediaSets } from "@osdk/foundry.mediasets";

export async function describeItem(client: Client, mediaSetRid: string, mediaItemRid: string) {
  const [info, metadata] = await Promise.all([
    MediaSets.info(client, mediaSetRid, mediaItemRid),
    MediaSets.metadata(client, mediaSetRid, mediaItemRid),
  ]);

  const details =
    metadata.type === "imagery" && metadata.dimensions != null
      ? `${metadata.dimensions.width}×${metadata.dimensions.height}`
      : metadata.type === "document"
        ? `${metadata.pages ?? "?"} pages`
        : metadata.type;

  return `${info.path ?? mediaItemRid} (${info.mimeType ?? "unknown type"}, ${info.sizeBytes ?? 0} bytes): ${details}`;
}
```

| `info` field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `path` | The item's path in the media set, if it has one. |
| `mimeType` | The item's media type. |
| `originallyUploadedFileMimeType` | The media type of the file as uploaded, when it was converted. |
| `sizeBytes` | Size in bytes. |
| `viewRid` | The media set view the item belongs to. |
| `logicalTimestamp` | When the item was added. |

`metadata.type` is one of `"imagery"`, `"document"`, `"spreadsheet"`, `"audio"`, `"video"`, `"cad"`, `"model3d"`, `"dicom"`, `"email"`, or `"untyped"`. Narrow on it to read type-specific fields, such as `dimensions` for images or `pages` for documents. Every variant has `sizeBytes`.

## Pass a read token

A media reference from an Ontology object carries a read token that grants access to that one item. Pass it as the `ReadToken` header parameter, after any query parameters:

```ts title="src/readWithToken.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { MediaSets } from "@osdk/foundry.mediasets";

export async function readWithToken(
  client: Client,
  mediaSetRid: string,
  mediaItemRid: string,
  readToken: string,
): Promise<Response> {
  return MediaSets.read(client, mediaSetRid, mediaItemRid, { ReadToken: readToken });
}
```

`read`, `readOriginal`, `info`, and `metadata` take the header object as their fourth argument. Preview functions such as `reference` take query parameters first: `MediaSets.reference(client, mediaSetRid, mediaItemRid, { preview: true }, { ReadToken })`.

## Upload an item

`MediaSets.upload` adds a file to a media set. It is a preview endpoint, so pass `preview: true`:

```ts title="src/uploadItem.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { MediaSets } from "@osdk/foundry.mediasets";

export async function uploadPhoto(client: Client, mediaSetRid: string, file: File) {
  const { mediaItemRid } = await MediaSets.upload(client, mediaSetRid, file, {
    mediaItemPath: `photos/${file.name}`,
    preview: true,
  });
  return mediaItemRid;
}
```

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mediaItemPath` | `string` | The item's path in the set. Some media sets require one. |
| `branchName`, `branchRid`, `viewRid` | `string` | Where to upload. Set at most one; without any, the item goes to the default branch. |
| `transactionId` | `string` | An open transaction to upload into. |
| `preview` | `boolean` | Must be `true`. |

The content is a `Blob`; a `File` from `<input type="file">` works directly. The response has the new `mediaItemRid` and the `mediaSetViewRid`.

### Upload into a transaction

Some media sets require uploads in a transaction. `MediaSets.get` returns the set's `transactionPolicy`; when its `type` is `"batchTransactions"`, open a transaction, upload, then commit:

```ts title="src/uploadBatch.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { MediaSets } from "@osdk/foundry.mediasets";

export async function uploadBatch(client: Client, mediaSetRid: string, files: File[]) {
  const mediaSet = await MediaSets.get(client, mediaSetRid, { preview: true });
  if (mediaSet.transactionPolicy.type !== "batchTransactions") {
    for (const file of files) {
      await MediaSets.upload(client, mediaSetRid, file, {
        mediaItemPath: file.name,
        preview: true,
      });
    }
    return;
  }

  const transactionId = await MediaSets.create(client, mediaSetRid, { preview: true });
  try {
    for (const file of files) {
      await MediaSets.upload(client, mediaSetRid, file, {
        mediaItemPath: file.name,
        transactionId,
        preview: true,
      });
    }
    await MediaSets.commit(client, mediaSetRid, transactionId, { preview: true });
  } catch (error) {
    await MediaSets.abort(client, mediaSetRid, transactionId, { preview: true });
    throw error;
  }
}
```

`MediaSets.create` resolves to the transaction ID as a string. Items uploaded in a transaction appear when it is committed; aborting deletes them.

### Upload temporary media

`MediaSets.uploadMedia` uploads a file that is not yet in any media set, and returns a `MediaReference`. Pass the reference to an action parameter or media property to keep the file; otherwise it is deleted after one hour. It needs `api:ontologies-read` and `api:ontologies-write` instead of the media set scopes:

```ts title="src/uploadTemporary.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { MediaSets } from "@osdk/foundry.mediasets";

export async function uploadTemporary(client: Client, file: File) {
  const reference = await MediaSets.uploadMedia(client, file, { filename: file.name });
  return reference;
}
```

The reference has `mimeType` and `reference.mediaSetViewItem`, with `mediaSetRid`, `mediaSetViewRid`, `mediaItemRid`, and a read `token`. The OSDK uses this endpoint when you pass a file to an action; prefer that path when you are applying an action.

## Transform an item

Transformations convert a media item, for example resizing an image or extracting text from a document. Start a job with `MediaSets.transform`, poll `getStatus` until it is `"SUCCESSFUL"` or `"FAILED"`, then download the output with `getResult`. All three are preview endpoints and need `api:mediasets-transform`:

```ts title="src/thumbnail.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { MediaSets } from "@osdk/foundry.mediasets";

export async function webpThumbnail(
  client: Client,
  mediaSetRid: string,
  mediaItemRid: string,
): Promise<Blob> {
  let job = await MediaSets.transform(
    client,
    mediaSetRid,
    mediaItemRid,
    {
      transformation: {
        type: "image",
        encoding: { type: "webp" },
        operations: [{ type: "resizeToFitBoundingBox", width: 256, height: 256 }],
      },
    },
    { preview: true },
  );

  while (job.status === "PENDING") {
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 2000));
    job = await MediaSets.getStatus(client, mediaSetRid, mediaItemRid, job.jobId, {
      preview: true,
    });
  }
  if (job.status === "FAILED") {
    throw new Error(`Transformation ${job.jobId} failed`);
  }

  const result = await MediaSets.getResult(client, mediaSetRid, mediaItemRid, job.jobId, {
    preview: true,
  });
  return result.blob();
}
```

`transformation.type` selects the conversion, such as `"image"`, `"documentToImage"`, `"documentToText"`, `"audioToText"`, or `"videoToImage"`. Each type has its own options; your editor lists them from the `Transformation` type. To transform an item you can only read through a read token, pass it as the `Token` header parameter.

## Reference

| Function | Scope | Status | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `read(client, mediaSetRid, mediaItemRid, headers?)` | `api:mediasets-read` | Stable | `Response` |
| `readOriginal(client, mediaSetRid, mediaItemRid, headers?)` | `api:mediasets-read` | Stable | `Response` |
| `info(client, mediaSetRid, mediaItemRid, headers?)` | `api:mediasets-read` | Stable | `GetMediaItemInfoResponse` |
| `metadata(client, mediaSetRid, mediaItemRid, headers?)` | `api:mediasets-read` | Stable | `MediaItemMetadata` |
| `uploadMedia(client, blob, { filename }, headers?)` | `api:ontologies-read`, `api:ontologies-write` | Stable | `MediaReference` |
| `get(client, mediaSetRid, query?)` | `api:mediasets-read` | Beta | `GetMediaSetResponse` |
| `getRidByPath(client, mediaSetRid, query)` | `api:mediasets-read` | Beta | `GetMediaItemRidByPathResponse` |
| `reference(client, mediaSetRid, mediaItemRid, query?, headers?)` | `api:mediasets-read` | Beta | `MediaReference` |
| `upload(client, mediaSetRid, blob, query?)` | `api:mediasets-write` | Beta | `PutMediaItemResponse` |
| `create(client, mediaSetRid, query?)` | `api:mediasets-write` | Beta | Transaction ID |
| `commit(client, mediaSetRid, transactionId, query?)` | `api:mediasets-write` | Beta | `void` |
| `abort(client, mediaSetRid, transactionId, query?)` | `api:mediasets-write` | Beta | `void` |
| `clear(client, mediaSetRid, query)` | `api:mediasets-write` | Beta | `void` |
| `transform(client, mediaSetRid, mediaItemRid, body, query?, headers?)` | `api:mediasets-transform` | Beta | `TransformMediaItemResponse` |
| `getStatus(client, mediaSetRid, mediaItemRid, jobId, query?, headers?)` | `api:mediasets-transform` | Beta | `GetTransformationJobStatusResponse` |
| `getResult(client, mediaSetRid, mediaItemRid, jobId, query?, headers?)` | `api:mediasets-transform` | Beta | `Response` |

Beta functions need `preview: true`. See [Preview endpoints](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/calling-apis.md#preview-endpoints).

# Ontology metadata

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/ontology-metadata

> List ontologies, object types, link types, action types, and query types at runtime with @osdk/foundry.ontologies, and know when the OSDK is the better fit.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Ontology API](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/api/v2/ontologies-v2-resources/ontologies/ontology-basics)

`@osdk/foundry.ontologies` reads the schema of any Ontology at runtime: its object types, properties, link types, action types, and query types. Use it for tools that work across object types you do not know at build time, such as schema browsers, admin pages, and code generators.

```npm
npm install @osdk/client @osdk/oauth @osdk/foundry.ontologies
```

Every sample takes a `client` from `createClient` or `createPlatformClient`; see [Set up](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/setup.md). Metadata reads need the `api:ontologies-read` scope.

## When to use the OSDK instead

Your generated SDK already contains the schema of every type it includes, checked at compile time. For those types, `client.fetchMetadata` returns runtime metadata without the Platform SDK:

```ts title="src/employeeMetadata.ts"
import { Employee, modifyEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";

export async function describeEmployee(client: Client) {
  const objectMetadata = await client.fetchMetadata(Employee);
  const actionMetadata = await client.fetchMetadata(modifyEmployee);
  return {
    title: objectMetadata.pluralDisplayName,
    properties: Object.keys(objectMetadata.properties),
    links: Object.keys(objectMetadata.links),
    actionParameters: Object.keys(actionMetadata.parameters),
  };
}
```

| Need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Display names, descriptions, and properties of types in your SDK | `client.fetchMetadata` from `@osdk/client` |
| Load, filter, or aggregate objects | The OSDK. See [Objects](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/objects.md). |
| Discover object types, actions, or queries that are not in your SDK | `@osdk/foundry.ontologies` |
| List the ontologies a user can see | `OntologiesV2.list` |
| Datasources, release status, and other fields `fetchMetadata` does not return | `@osdk/foundry.ontologies` |

`@osdk/foundry.ontologies` also contains the raw object, link, action, and query endpoints that the OSDK calls. Prefer the OSDK for those: it adds types, pagination helpers, caching in React, and result conversion.

## Identify the Ontology

Every function after `OntologiesV2.list` takes the Ontology as its first path parameter: its API name or its RID. With a generated SDK, pass `$ontologyRid`:

```ts title="src/ontologies.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { OntologiesV2 } from "@osdk/foundry.ontologies";

export async function listOntologies(client: Client) {
  const { data } = await OntologiesV2.list(client);
  return data.map((ontology) => ({
    apiName: ontology.apiName,
    displayName: ontology.displayName,
    rid: ontology.rid,
  }));
}
```

`OntologiesV2.get(client, ontology)` returns one Ontology's `apiName`, `displayName`, `description`, and `rid`.

## List object types

`ObjectTypesV2.list` returns one page of object types:

```ts title="src/objectTypes.ts"
import { $ontologyRid } from "@my-app/sdk";
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { ObjectTypesV2, type ObjectTypeV2 } from "@osdk/foundry.ontologies";

export async function listObjectTypes(client: Client): Promise<ObjectTypeV2[]> {
  const objectTypes: ObjectTypeV2[] = [];
  let pageToken: string | undefined;
  do {
    const page = await ObjectTypesV2.list(client, $ontologyRid, { pageSize: 500, pageToken });
    objectTypes.push(...page.data);
    pageToken = page.nextPageToken;
  } while (pageToken != null);
  return objectTypes;
}
```

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pageSize`, `pageToken` | | Pagination. See [Paginate](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/calling-apis.md#paginate). |
| `includeDatasources` | `boolean` | Include each type's backing `datasources`. |
| `branch` | `string` | Read the schema on a Foundry branch. |

The list endpoint leaves `aliases` empty. Call `ObjectTypesV2.get` to read them.

## Get an object type

`ObjectTypesV2.get` takes the object type's API name:

```ts title="src/employeeSchema.ts"
import { $ontologyRid } from "@my-app/sdk";
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { ObjectTypesV2 } from "@osdk/foundry.ontologies";

export async function propertyTypes(client: Client, objectTypeApiName: string) {
  const objectType = await ObjectTypesV2.get(client, $ontologyRid, objectTypeApiName);
  return {
    primaryKey: objectType.primaryKey,
    titleProperty: objectType.titleProperty,
    properties: Object.entries(objectType.properties).map(([apiName, property]) => ({
      apiName,
      displayName: property.displayName ?? apiName,
      type: property.dataType.type,
    })),
  };
}
```

| `ObjectTypeV2` field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `apiName`, `displayName`, `pluralDisplayName`, `description` | Names and description. |
| `rid` | The object type RID. |
| `primaryKey` | API name of the primary key property. |
| `titleProperty` | API name of the property used as the object's title. |
| `properties` | Map from property API name to `PropertyV2`: `dataType` (discriminated by `type`, such as `"string"`, `"integer"`, `"date"`, `"array"`), `displayName`, `description`, `rid`, and `typeClasses`. |
| `status` | `"ACTIVE"`, `"ENDORSED"`, `"EXPERIMENTAL"`, or `"DEPRECATED"`. |
| `icon`, `visibility` | Display hints. |
| `aliases` | Alternative names. |
| `datasources` | Backing datasources, when requested with `includeDatasources`. |

## List link types

`ObjectTypesV2.listOutgoingLinkTypes` returns the links from an object type to other types:

```ts title="src/links.ts"
import { $ontologyRid } from "@my-app/sdk";
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { ObjectTypesV2 } from "@osdk/foundry.ontologies";

export async function describeLinks(client: Client) {
  const { data } = await ObjectTypesV2.listOutgoingLinkTypes(client, $ontologyRid, "Employee");
  return data.map(
    (link) => `${link.apiName} → ${link.objectTypeApiName} (${link.cardinality === "ONE" ? "one" : "many"})`,
  );
}
```

For the example `Employee`, this lists `lead`, `reports`, and `office`. Each `LinkTypeSideV2` has `apiName`, `displayName`, `objectTypeApiName` (the target type), `cardinality` (`"ONE"` or `"MANY"`), `foreignKeyPropertyApiName` when the link is backed by a foreign key, `status`, and `linkTypeRid`. `ObjectTypesV2.getOutgoingLinkType` returns one link by API name.

## List action types

`ActionTypesV2.list` returns one page of action types, and `ActionTypesV2.get` returns one by API name:

```ts title="src/actionParameters.ts"
import { $ontologyRid } from "@my-app/sdk";
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { ActionTypesV2 } from "@osdk/foundry.ontologies";

export async function requiredParameters(client: Client, actionApiName: string) {
  const actionType = await ActionTypesV2.get(client, $ontologyRid, actionApiName);
  return Object.entries(actionType.parameters)
    .filter(([, parameter]) => parameter.required)
    .map(([id, parameter]) => ({ id, displayName: parameter.displayName, type: parameter.dataType.type }));
}
```

An `ActionTypeV2` has `apiName`, `displayName`, `description`, `status`, `rid`, `parameters` (a map from parameter ID to `{ displayName, description, dataType, required, typeClasses }`), and `operations`, which describe the objects and links the action creates, modifies, or deletes. `ActionTypesV2.getByRid` looks one up by RID.

## List query types

`QueryTypes.list` and `QueryTypes.get` return functions registered in the Ontology. Each `QueryTypeV2` has `apiName`, `displayName`, `description`, `parameters`, `output`, `rid`, and `version`. `list` returns each query at its latest version; pass `{ version }` to `get` for a specific one:

```ts title="src/queries.ts"
import { $ontologyRid } from "@my-app/sdk";
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { QueryTypes } from "@osdk/foundry.ontologies";

export async function listQueries(client: Client) {
  const { data } = await QueryTypes.list(client, $ontologyRid, { pageSize: 100 });
  return data.map((query) => `${query.apiName}@${query.version}`);
}
```

## Interfaces and full metadata

Interface types and full-Ontology metadata are preview endpoints, so pass `preview: true`:

```ts title="src/interfaces.ts"
import { $ontologyRid } from "@my-app/sdk";
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { OntologiesV2, OntologyInterfaces } from "@osdk/foundry.ontologies";

export async function describeOntology(client: Client) {
  const worker = await OntologyInterfaces.get(client, $ontologyRid, "Worker", { preview: true });
  const full = await OntologiesV2.getFullMetadata(client, $ontologyRid, { preview: true });
  return {
    workerImplementedBy: worker.implementedByObjectTypes,
    objectTypeCount: Object.keys(full.objectTypes).length,
  };
}
```

`OntologiesV2.getFullMetadata` returns objects, links, actions, queries, and interfaces in one response. It may omit entities rather than fail, so do not treat a missing type as proof that it does not exist.

| `OntologiesV2.getFullMetadata(client, ontology, query?)` | `GET /v2/ontologies/{ontology}/fullMetadata` | Beta |

| `QueryTypes.list(client, ontology, query?)` | `GET /v2/ontologies/{ontology}/queryTypes` | Stable |
| `QueryTypes.get(client, ontology, queryApiName, query?)` | `GET /v2/ontologies/{ontology}/queryTypes/{queryApiName}` | Stable |
| `OntologyInterfaces.list(client, ontology, query?)` | `GET /v2/ontologies/{ontology}/interfaceTypes` | Beta |
| `OntologyInterfaces.get(client, ontology, interfaceType, query?)` | `GET /v2/ontologies/{ontology}/interfaceTypes/{interfaceType}` | Beta |

All of these need `api:ontologies-read`.

# Set up the Platform SDK

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/setup

> Install @osdk/foundry packages, create a client with createPlatformClient or reuse an OSDK client, and request the OAuth scopes each API needs.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [API authentication](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/api/v2/general/overview/authentication)

{/* cspell:ignore mediasets datahealth thirdpartyapplications */}

Install the `@osdk/foundry.*` packages you need, create a client, and make sure your token carries the scopes those APIs require.

## Install

Install `@osdk/client` for the client, `@osdk/oauth` for tokens, and one package per API area:

```npm
npm install @osdk/client @osdk/oauth @osdk/foundry.admin
```

Add more packages as you need them, for example `@osdk/foundry.datasets` or `@osdk/foundry.mediasets`. See the [package list](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform.md#packages) for every package. Shared types such as `PageToken` live in `@osdk/foundry.core`, which each package depends on; install it directly if you import its types.

## Create a platform client

If your app does not use the Ontology SDK, create a client with `createPlatformClient`:

```ts
createPlatformClient(baseUrl, tokenProvider, options?, fetchFn?)
```

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `baseUrl` | `string` | The base URL of your Foundry stack, such as `https://example.palantirfoundry.com`. Requests go to `<baseUrl>/api/v2/...`. An empty string throws `baseUrl cannot be empty`. |
| `tokenProvider` | `() => Promise<string>` | Returns a bearer token for each request. Usually an OAuth client from `@osdk/oauth`. |
| `options` | `undefined` | Reserved. Pass `undefined` if you need to set `fetchFn`. |
| `fetchFn` | `typeof fetch` | The `fetch` used for every request. Defaults to the global `fetch`. |

```ts title="src/platformClient.ts"
import { createPlatformClient } from "@osdk/client";
import { createPublicOauthClient } from "@osdk/oauth";

const foundryUrl = "https://example.palantirfoundry.com";

export const auth = createPublicOauthClient(
  "<your-client-id>",
  foundryUrl,
  "http://localhost:8080/auth/callback",
  { scopes: ["api:admin-read"] },
);

export const platformClient = createPlatformClient(foundryUrl, auth);
```

The returned `PlatformClient` works only with `@osdk/foundry.*` functions. It has no Ontology, so it cannot load objects or apply actions.

## Reuse an OSDK client

A client from `createClient` also works with every platform function. `Client` extends the same `SharedClient` interface that the platform functions accept, so you do not need a second client:

```ts title="src/currentUser.ts"
import { $ontologyRid } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { createClient } from "@osdk/client";
import { Users } from "@osdk/foundry.admin";
import { createPublicOauthClient } from "@osdk/oauth";

const foundryUrl = "https://example.palantirfoundry.com";

const auth = createPublicOauthClient(
  "<your-client-id>",
  foundryUrl,
  "http://localhost:8080/auth/callback",
  {
    scopes: [
      "api:read-data",
      "api:write-data",
      "api:use-ontologies-read",
      "api:use-ontologies-write",
      "api:admin-read",
    ],
  },
);

export const client = createClient(foundryUrl, $ontologyRid, auth);

export async function currentUsername(): Promise<string> {
  const user = await Users.getCurrent(client);
  return user.username;
}
```

In React, `OsdkProvider` holds this client and the hooks in `@osdk/react/platform-apis` call the admin APIs with it. See [Users and markings in React](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/platform-apis.md).

Both kinds of client add the `Authorization` header to each request and retry a request up to three times, with backoff, when Foundry responds with `429` or `503`.

## Request scopes

Each function's JSDoc lists the OAuth scopes it needs under **Required Scopes**. Foundry rejects calls from a token that lacks them. The scopes used by the packages on these pages:

| Package | Read | Write |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@osdk/foundry.admin` | `api:admin-read` | `api:admin-write` |
| `@osdk/foundry.datasets` | `api:datasets-read` | `api:datasets-write` |
| `@osdk/foundry.mediasets` | `api:mediasets-read` | `api:mediasets-write`, plus `api:mediasets-transform` for transformations |
| `@osdk/foundry.ontologies` | `api:ontologies-read` | `api:ontologies-write` |
| `@osdk/foundry.filesystem` | `api:filesystem-read` | `api:filesystem-write` |
| `@osdk/foundry.orchestration` | `api:orchestration-read` | `api:orchestration-write` |

Some endpoints differ from their package's pattern. For example, `MarkingMembers.list` needs `api:admin-write`, `MediaSets.uploadMedia` needs `api:ontologies-read` and `api:ontologies-write`, and `Groups.listCurrent` needs no scope. Check the JSDoc of each function you call; your editor shows it on hover.

Pass the scopes to your OAuth client, and allow each one for your application on **OAuth & scopes** in Developer Console. `@osdk/oauth` only requests the four Ontology scopes by default, so add platform scopes explicitly. A stored refresh token is reused only for the same set of scopes, so changing `scopes` signs users in again. See [Authentication](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/authentication.md#scopes).

For a server or scheduled job, pass the scopes as the fourth argument of `createConfidentialOauthClient`:

```ts title="src/serverClient.ts"
import { createPlatformClient } from "@osdk/client";
import { createConfidentialOauthClient } from "@osdk/oauth";

const foundryUrl = "https://example.palantirfoundry.com";

const auth = createConfidentialOauthClient(
  "<your-client-id>",
  "<your-client-secret>",
  foundryUrl,
  ["api:datasets-read", "api:datasets-write"],
);

export const platformClient = createPlatformClient(foundryUrl, auth);
```

## Next steps

Read [Call platform APIs](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/calling-apis.md) for argument order, pagination, and error handling.

# Users and groups

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/users-and-groups

> Look up users, search and list them, read group memberships, manage group members, and read markings with @osdk/foundry.admin.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [User API](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/api/v2/admin-v2-resources/users/user-basics)
- [Group API](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/api/v2/admin-v2-resources/groups/group-basics)

{/* cspell:ignore CBAC Uncategorized */}

`@osdk/foundry.admin` reads and manages Foundry users, groups, and markings. Use it to show who is signed in, resolve user IDs to names, check group membership, and list the markings a user can view.

```npm
npm install @osdk/client @osdk/oauth @osdk/foundry.admin
```

Every sample takes a `client` from `createClient` or `createPlatformClient`; see [Set up](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/setup.md). Reads need the `api:admin-read` scope and writes need `api:admin-write`. In React, the hooks in `@osdk/react/platform-apis` wrap several of these calls; see [Users and markings in React](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/platform-apis.md).

## Get the signed-in user

`Users.getCurrent` returns the user the token belongs to:

```ts title="src/currentUser.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { Users } from "@osdk/foundry.admin";

export async function displayName(client: Client): Promise<string> {
  const user = await Users.getCurrent(client);
  const fullName = [user.givenName, user.familyName].filter(Boolean).join(" ");
  return fullName || user.username;
}
```

A `User` has these fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | The user ID. Other endpoints take this as `userId` or `principalId`. |
| `username` | `string` | The username. |
| `givenName` | `string \| undefined` | First name. |
| `familyName` | `string \| undefined` | Last name. |
| `email` | `string \| undefined` | Email address. |
| `realm` | `string` | The authentication realm the user belongs to. |
| `organization` | `string \| undefined` | RID of the user's primary organization. |
| `status` | `"ACTIVE" \| "DELETED"` | Whether the user is active. |
| `attributes` | `Record<string, string[]>` | Attributes from the identity provider. |

## Look up users by ID

`Users.get` takes a user ID. Pass `status: "DELETED"` to resolve a user who has been removed, for example the author of an old record:

```ts title="src/lookupUser.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { Users } from "@osdk/foundry.admin";

export async function lookupUser(client: Client, userId: string) {
  const active = await Users.get(client, userId);
  const deleted = await Users.get(client, userId, { status: "DELETED" });
  return { active, deleted };
}
```

To resolve many IDs at once, use `Users.getBatch`. It takes up to 500 elements and returns a map keyed by user ID. IDs that do not resolve are missing from the map:

```ts title="src/resolveUsers.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { Users, type User } from "@osdk/foundry.admin";

export async function resolveUsers(
  client: Client,
  userIds: string[],
): Promise<Map<string, User>> {
  const { data } = await Users.getBatch(
    client,
    userIds.map((userId) => ({ userId })),
  );
  return new Map(Object.entries(data));
}
```

## Search and list users

`Users.search` runs a case-insensitive prefix search on username, given name, and family name. It only returns active users:

```ts title="src/searchUsers.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { Users } from "@osdk/foundry.admin";

export async function searchUsers(client: Client, prefix: string) {
  const { data, nextPageToken } = await Users.search(client, {
    where: { type: "queryString", value: prefix },
    pageSize: 20,
  });
  return { users: data, nextPageToken };
}
```

`Users.list` lists every user, one page at a time. Its query parameters:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `include` | `"ACTIVE" \| "DELETED"` | Active users | Which users to list. Pass `"DELETED"` to list removed users. |
| `pageSize` | `number` | | Preferred page size. The server can return more or fewer. |
| `pageToken` | `string` | | `nextPageToken` from the previous page. |

To read every page, use the `paginate` helper from [Call platform APIs](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/calling-apis.md#paginate).

## Show a profile picture

`Users.profilePicture` returns the image as a `Response`:

```ts title="src/profilePicture.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { Users } from "@osdk/foundry.admin";

export async function profilePictureUrl(client: Client, userId: string): Promise<string> {
  const response = await Users.profilePicture(client, userId);
  return URL.createObjectURL(await response.blob());
}
```

A user without a picture rejects with a `ProfilePictureNotFound` error.

## Read group memberships

`Groups.listCurrent` returns every group the signed-in user belongs to, directly or through another group. It needs no scope, so any signed-in user can call it, but it is a preview endpoint:

```ts title="src/myGroups.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { Groups } from "@osdk/foundry.admin";

export async function isInGroup(client: Client, groupName: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const { data } = await Groups.listCurrent(client, { preview: true });
  return data.some((group) => group.name === groupName);
}
```

For any other user, `GroupMemberships.list` returns the IDs of their groups. Set `transitive: true` to include groups they belong to through other groups, then resolve the IDs with `Groups.getBatch`:

```ts title="src/userGroups.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { GroupMemberships, Groups } from "@osdk/foundry.admin";

export async function userGroupNames(client: Client, userId: string): Promise<string[]> {
  const memberships = await GroupMemberships.list(client, userId, { transitive: true });
  const { data } = await Groups.getBatch(
    client,
    memberships.data.map(({ groupId }) => ({ groupId })),
  );
  return Object.values(data).map((group) => group.name);
}
```

This reads one page. Paginate with `pageToken` for users in many groups.

A `Group` has `id`, `name`, `description`, `realm`, `organizations` (organization RIDs), and `attributes`.

## Find groups and their members

`Groups.search` runs a prefix search on group name. `GroupMembers.list` returns a group's members, which can be users or groups:

```ts title="src/groupMembers.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { GroupMembers, Groups, Users } from "@osdk/foundry.admin";

export async function memberUsernames(client: Client, groupName: string): Promise<string[]> {
  const { data: groups } = await Groups.search(client, {
    where: { type: "queryString", value: groupName },
  });
  const group = groups.find((g) => g.name === groupName);
  if (group == null) {
    return [];
  }

  const members = await GroupMembers.list(client, group.id, { transitive: true });
  const userIds = members.data
    .filter((member) => member.principalType === "USER")
    .map((member) => ({ userId: member.principalId }));
  const { data: users } = await Users.getBatch(client, userIds);
  return Object.values(users).map((user) => user.username);
}
```

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `transitive` | `boolean` | Include members of nested groups. |
| `includeExpirations` | `boolean` | Include each member's `expiration`, when one is set. |
| `pageSize`, `pageToken` | | Pagination. See [Paginate](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/calling-apis.md#paginate). |

Each member is `{ principalType: "USER" | "GROUP", principalId, expiration? }`.

## Add and remove group members

Adding and removing members needs `api:admin-write` and permission to manage the group. Both take the group ID and a list of principal IDs, which can be user or group IDs, and resolve to `undefined`:

```ts title="src/manageMembers.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { GroupMembers } from "@osdk/foundry.admin";

export async function addTemporaryMember(client: Client, groupId: string, userId: string) {
  await GroupMembers.add(client, groupId, {
    principalIds: [userId],
    expiration: "2026-12-31T23:59:59Z",
  });
}

export async function removeMember(client: Client, groupId: string, userId: string) {
  await GroupMembers.remove(client, groupId, { principalIds: [userId] });
}
```

`expiration` is optional. Without it, the membership does not expire.

## Read markings

Markings restrict who can view a resource. `Users.getMarkings` returns the IDs of the markings a user is a member of, and `Markings.list` and `MarkingCategories.list` return the markings and categories the token can see. Join them on `categoryId`:

```ts title="src/userMarkings.ts"
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";
import { MarkingCategories, Markings, Users } from "@osdk/foundry.admin";

export async function describeUserMarkings(client: Client, userId: string): Promise<string[]> {
  const [{ view }, markings, categories] = await Promise.all([
    Users.getMarkings(client, userId),
    Markings.list(client, { includeDeleted: false, pageSize: 100 }),
    MarkingCategories.list(client, { includeDeleted: false, pageSize: 100 }),
  ]);

  const categoryName = new Map(categories.data.map((c) => [c.id, c.name] as const));
  const viewable = new Set(view);
  return markings.data
    .filter((marking) => viewable.has(marking.id))
    .map((marking) => `${categoryName.get(marking.categoryId) ?? "Uncategorized"}: ${marking.name}`);
}
```

`Markings.list` and `MarkingCategories.list` accept at most 100 per page and include deleted entries unless you pass `includeDeleted: false`. Paginate to read them all. To look up specific markings, use `Markings.get` or `Markings.getBatch`.

| Marking field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | The marking ID. |
| `categoryId` | The category it belongs to. |
| `name`, `description` | Display text. |
| `organization` | The organization RID, for organization markings. |
| `deleted` | Whether the marking has been deleted. |
| `createdTime`, `createdBy` | When and by whom it was created. |

Listing who can view a marking, with `MarkingMembers.list`, needs `api:admin-write` because only marking administrators can see its members.

For classification-based access control (CBAC), `CbacBanners.get` returns the banner text and colors for a set of marking IDs. It is a preview endpoint; see the example in [Call platform APIs](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/platform/calling-apis.md#preview-endpoints).

## Reference

| Function | Endpoint | Scope | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Users.getCurrent(client)` | `GET /v2/admin/users/getCurrent` | `api:admin-read` | Stable |
| `Users.get(client, userId, { status? })` | `GET /v2/admin/users/{userId}` | `api:admin-read` | Stable |
| `Users.getBatch(client, elements)` | `POST /v2/admin/users/getBatch` | `api:admin-read` | Stable |
| `Users.list(client, { include?, pageSize?, pageToken? })` | `GET /v2/admin/users` | `api:admin-read` | Stable |
| `Users.search(client, body)` | `POST /v2/admin/users/search` | `api:admin-read` | Stable |
| `Users.profilePicture(client, userId)` | `GET /v2/admin/users/{userId}/profilePicture` | `api:admin-read` | Stable |
| `Users.getMarkings(client, userId)` | `GET /v2/admin/users/{userId}/getMarkings` | `api:admin-read` | Stable |
| `Groups.listCurrent(client, { preview })` | `GET /v2/admin/groups/listCurrent` | None | Beta |
| `Groups.get(client, groupId)` | `GET /v2/admin/groups/{groupId}` | `api:admin-read` | Stable |
| `Groups.getBatch(client, elements)` | `POST /v2/admin/groups/getBatch` | `api:admin-read` | Stable |
| `Groups.search(client, body)` | `POST /v2/admin/groups/search` | `api:admin-read` | Stable |

| `GroupMembers.list(client, groupId, query?)` | `GET /v2/admin/groups/{groupId}/groupMembers` | `api:admin-read` | Stable |
| `GroupMembers.add(client, groupId, body)` | `POST /v2/admin/groups/{groupId}/groupMembers/add` | `api:admin-write` | Stable |
| `GroupMembers.remove(client, groupId, body)` | `POST /v2/admin/groups/{groupId}/groupMembers/remove` | `api:admin-write` | Stable |
| `Markings.list(client, query?)` | `GET /v2/admin/markings` | `api:admin-read` | Stable |
| `MarkingCategories.list(client, query?)` | `GET /v2/admin/markingCategories` | `api:admin-read` | Stable |
| `MarkingMembers.list(client, markingId, query?)` | `GET /v2/admin/markings/{markingId}/markingMembers` | `api:admin-write` | Stable |
| `CbacBanners.get(client, { markingIds, preview })` | `GET /v2/admin/cbacBanner` | `api:admin-read` | Beta |

The package also covers creating and deleting users and groups, organizations, roles, enrollments, and authentication providers. Browse the exports of `@osdk/foundry.admin` in your editor for the full list.

# Apply actions

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/actions

> Apply and validate ontology actions from React with useOsdkAction, including error handling, debounced validation, and batch application.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Action types](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/action-types/overview)

{/* cspell:ignore debounced refetches */}

Use `useOsdkAction` to apply an action, validate its parameters before submitting, and track pending and error state. When an action succeeds, the cache refetches every object it edited, so components that show those objects update without extra code.

## Apply an action

Pass the action from your generated SDK, then call `applyAction` with its parameters:

```tsx title="src/PromoteButton.tsx"
import { Employee, modifyEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkAction } from "@osdk/react";

export function PromoteButton({
  employee,
  jobTitle,
}: {
  employee: Employee.OsdkInstance;
  jobTitle: string;
}) {
  const { applyAction, isPending, error } = useOsdkAction(modifyEmployee);

  async function handleClick() {
    try {
      await applyAction({ employee, jobTitle });
    } catch (e) {
      console.error("modifyEmployee failed", e);
    }
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <button disabled={isPending} onClick={() => void handleClick()}>
        {isPending ? "Saving…" : `Make ${jobTitle}`}
      </button>
      {error && <p role="alert">Could not update {employee.fullName}.</p>}
    </div>
  );
}
```

> [!WARNING]
> `applyAction` rethrows every failure after it records it in `error`. Always `await` it inside `try`/`catch`, or attach `.catch`, or the failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection.

Parameters are typed from the action's definition. Object parameters accept an object instance or its primary key.

### Return value

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `applyAction` | `(args \| args[]) => Promise<ActionEditResponse \| undefined>` | Applies the action. Pass one parameter object, or an array to apply it in a batch. Each parameter object can include `$optimisticUpdate`. Rejects on failure. |
| `isPending` | `boolean` | `true` while `applyAction` is running. |
| `data` | `ActionEditResponse \| undefined` | The edits from the last successful application. |
| `error` | `{ actionValidation?: ActionValidationError; unknown?: unknown } \| undefined` | The last failure from `applyAction` or `validateAction`. Cleared when either is called again. |
| `validateAction` | `(args) => Promise<ActionValidationResponse \| undefined>` | Checks parameters on the server without applying the action. Rejects on request failure. |
| `isValidating` | `boolean` | `true` while `validateAction` is running. |
| `validationResult` | `ActionValidationResponse \| undefined` | The result of the last completed validation. |

The hook takes no options. `$optimisticUpdate` is covered in [Optimistic updates](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/optimistic-updates.md).

## Read the result

`data` is an `ActionEditResponse`: a summary of what the action changed, not a value returned by the action's logic.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `"edits" \| "largeScaleEdits"` | `"largeScaleEdits"` when the action edited too many objects to list. Only `editedObjectTypes` is set in that case. |
| `addedObjects` | `Array<{ objectType, primaryKey }>` | Objects the action created. |
| `modifiedObjects` | `Array<{ objectType, primaryKey }>` | Objects the action changed. |
| `deletedObjects` | `Array<{ objectType, primaryKey }>` | Objects the action deleted. |
| `addedLinks` / `deletedLinks` | `Array<LinkReference>` | Links created or removed, with both sides and the link type API names. |
| `deletedObjectsCount` / `deletedLinksCount` | `number` | Counts of deletions. |
| `editedObjectTypes` | `Array<string>` | API names of every object type the action touched. |

`applyAction` resolves to the same value, which is the simplest way to act on a new object's primary key:

```ts
const result = await applyAction({ employee, jobTitle: "Staff Engineer" });
const created = result?.type === "edits" ? result.addedObjects : [];
```

## Handle errors

`error` separates validation failures from everything else:

- `error.actionValidation` is an `ActionValidationError`. The server rejected the parameters, for example because a submission criterion failed or a value is out of range.
- `error.unknown` holds any other failure: network errors, permission errors, or a `PalantirApiError` from Foundry.

Do not show `error.actionValidation.message` to users. It is `"Validation Error: "` followed by the raw validation response as JSON. Read the structured response from `error.actionValidation.validation` instead. This helper turns either a validation error or a `validationResult` into messages:

```ts title="src/validationMessages.ts"
interface ValidationLike {
  result: "VALID" | "INVALID";
  submissionCriteria: Array<{
    result: "VALID" | "INVALID";
    configuredFailureMessage?: string;
  }>;
  parameters: Record<string, { result: "VALID" | "INVALID" }>;
}

export function validationMessages(validation: ValidationLike | undefined): string[] {
  if (validation == null || validation.result === "VALID") {
    return [];
  }
  const messages = validation.submissionCriteria
    .filter((criterion) => criterion.result === "INVALID")
    .map(
      (criterion) =>
        criterion.configuredFailureMessage ?? "The action's conditions are not met.",
    );
  for (const [name, parameter] of Object.entries(validation.parameters)) {
    if (parameter.result === "INVALID") {
      messages.push(`${name} has an invalid value.`);
    }
  }
  return messages;
}
```

Use it with the hook's `error`:

```tsx title="src/ActionError.tsx"
import type { ActionValidationError } from "@osdk/client";
import { validationMessages } from "./validationMessages";

export function ActionError({
  error,
}: {
  error: { actionValidation?: ActionValidationError; unknown?: unknown } | undefined;
}) {
  if (error?.actionValidation) {
    return (
      <ul role="alert">
        {validationMessages(error.actionValidation.validation).map((message) => (
          <li key={message}>{message}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    );
  }
  if (error?.unknown != null) {
    return <p role="alert">Something went wrong. Try again.</p>;
  }
  return null;
}
```

`submissionCriteria[].configuredFailureMessage` is the message the action's author configured in Foundry, so prefer it when it is present.

## Validate before submitting

`validateAction` asks the server whether a set of parameters would pass, without applying the action. An `INVALID` result is not an error: it resolves normally and sets `validationResult`. `validateAction` rejects only when the request itself fails, so it needs a `catch` like `applyAction`.

Validating on every keystroke sends a request per keystroke. Wrap the call in `useDebouncedCallback`, exported from `@osdk/react`, so it runs once the user pauses:

```tsx title="src/JobTitleForm.tsx"
import { Employee, modifyEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useDebouncedCallback, useOsdkAction } from "@osdk/react";
import { type FormEvent, useState } from "react";
import { ActionError } from "./ActionError";
import { validationMessages } from "./validationMessages";

export function JobTitleForm({ employee }: { employee: Employee.OsdkInstance }) {
  const [jobTitle, setJobTitle] = useState(employee.jobTitle ?? "");
  const {
    applyAction,
    validateAction,
    validationResult,
    isValidating,
    isPending,
    error,
  } = useOsdkAction(modifyEmployee);

  const validate = useDebouncedCallback(async (value: string) => {
    try {
      await validateAction({ employee, jobTitle: value });
    } catch (e) {
      console.error("Validation request failed", e);
    }
  }, 400);

  async function handleSubmit(event: FormEvent) {
    event.preventDefault();
    validate.cancel();
    try {
      await applyAction({ employee, jobTitle });
    } catch (e) {
      console.error("modifyEmployee failed", e);
    }
  }

  const messages = validationMessages(validationResult);
  const canSubmit =
    jobTitle !== "" &&
    validationResult?.result === "VALID" &&
    !isValidating &&
    !isPending;

  return (
    <form onSubmit={(event) => void handleSubmit(event)}>
      <input
        value={jobTitle}
        placeholder="Job title"
        onChange={(event) => {
          setJobTitle(event.target.value);
          validate(event.target.value);
        }}
      />
      {isValidating && <span>Checking…</span>}
      {messages.map((message) => (
        <p key={message}>{message}</p>
      ))}
      <button type="submit" disabled={!canSubmit}>
        Save
      </button>
      <ActionError error={error} />
    </form>
  );
}
```

How validation and application interact:

- A new `validateAction` call supersedes one still in flight. The earlier result is discarded and resolves to `undefined`.
- `validateAction` does nothing and resolves to `undefined` while `applyAction` is running.
- `applyAction` discards any validation in flight.
- `validationResult` keeps the last completed result until the next validation finishes, so it can describe older input. Gate submission on `isValidating` as well, as the example does.

The debounced function also has `cancel()`, which drops a pending call, and `flush()`, which runs it immediately. A pending call is dropped when the component unmounts.

## Apply an action in a batch

Pass an array to apply the same action to several parameter sets in one request:

```tsx title="src/MoveTeam.tsx"
import { Employee, modifyEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkAction } from "@osdk/react";

export function MoveTeam({
  employees,
  department,
}: {
  employees: Employee.OsdkInstance[];
  department: string;
}) {
  const { applyAction, isPending } = useOsdkAction(modifyEmployee);

  async function moveAll() {
    try {
      await applyAction(
        employees.map((employee) => ({ employee, department })),
      );
    } catch (e) {
      console.error("Batch modifyEmployee failed", e);
    }
  }

  return (
    <button disabled={isPending} onClick={() => void moveAll()}>
      Move {employees.length} employees to {department}
    </button>
  );
}
```

A batch is applied with the batch apply endpoint, so it differs from a single call:

- A batch that the server rejects reports the failure in `error.unknown`. `error.actionValidation` is set only for single applications.
- `validateAction` takes one parameter object, not an array.
- Each item can carry its own `$optimisticUpdate`. They are combined into one optimistic layer.

## Apply an action with the client

You can also apply an action with the `Client` from `useOsdkClient`. This bypasses the cache: components do not update until you invalidate the affected data yourself (see [Invalidate the cache](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/cache-invalidation.md)). Prefer `useOsdkAction` in components.

```ts title="src/updateJobTitle.ts"
import { Employee, modifyEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import type { Client } from "@osdk/client";

export async function updateJobTitle(
  client: Client,
  employee: Employee.OsdkInstance,
  jobTitle: string,
) {
  const validation = await client(modifyEmployee).applyAction(
    { employee, jobTitle },
    { $validateOnly: true },
  );
  if (validation.result === "INVALID") {
    return undefined;
  }

  return client(modifyEmployee).applyAction(
    { employee, jobTitle },
    { $returnEdits: true },
  );
}
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$returnEdits` | `boolean` | `false` | Resolve to an `ActionEditResponse`. Without it, `applyAction` resolves to `undefined`. |
| `$validateOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Validate without applying, and resolve to the `ActionValidationResponse`. Cannot be combined with `$returnEdits`. |

A single `applyAction` call on the client throws an `ActionValidationError` when validation fails. For several parameter sets, call `client(modifyEmployee).batchApplyAction([...], { $returnEdits: true })`. It accepts `$returnEdits` but not `$validateOnly`.

For a generated form with fields for every parameter, see the [ActionForm component](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/components/action-form.md).

# Aggregate objects

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/aggregations

> Count, sum, average, and group objects on the server with useOsdkAggregation, without loading the objects into the browser.

{/* cspell:ignore refetches */}

`useOsdkAggregation` asks the server for counts, sums, averages, and other metrics over a set of objects, optionally grouped by property values. Only the results come back, so a total over a million objects costs one small response.

## Count and summarize

Pass an object type and an `aggregate` with a `$select`. Each key in `$select` is a metric to compute:

```tsx title="src/PayrollSummary.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkAggregation } from "@osdk/react";

export function PayrollSummary() {
  const { data, isLoading, error, refetch } = useOsdkAggregation(Employee, {
    aggregate: {
      $select: {
        $count: "unordered",
        "salary:avg": "unordered",
        "salary:max": "unordered",
        "startDate:min": "unordered",
      },
    },
  });

  return (
    <dl>
      {error && (
        <p role="alert">
          {error.message} <button onClick={() => void refetch()}>Retry</button>
        </p>
      )}
      {isLoading && !data && <p>Calculating…</p>}
      {data && (
        <>
          <dt>Employees</dt>
          <dd>{data.$count}</dd>
          <dt>Average salary</dt>
          <dd>{data.salary.avg?.toFixed(0) ?? "n/a"}</dd>
          <dt>Highest salary</dt>
          <dd>{data.salary.max ?? "n/a"}</dd>
          <dt>Earliest start date</dt>
          <dd>{data.startDate.min ?? "n/a"}</dd>
        </>
      )}
    </dl>
  );
}
```

`$count` is read as `data.$count`. A `"property:metric"` key is read as `data.property.metric`, so `"salary:avg"` becomes `data.salary.avg`. The result is fully typed from the keys you pass.

### Metrics

| Key | Property types | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$count` | | `number` |
| `"property:sum"`, `"property:avg"` | Numeric | `number`, or `undefined` when no object has a value |
| `"property:min"`, `"property:max"` | Numeric, date, timestamp | Same type as the property, or `undefined` |
| `"property:exactDistinct"` | All | `number` of distinct values |
| `"property:approximateDistinct"` | All | Estimated `number` of distinct values. Faster on large object types. |

TypeScript rejects a metric that does not fit the property, such as `avg` on a string.

## Filter before aggregating

`where` takes the same clause as [`useOsdkObjects`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/objects.md#filter-with-where). `intersectWith` adds clauses that every object must also match.

```tsx
const { data } = useOsdkAggregation(Employee, {
  where: { department: "Engineering" },
  intersectWith: [{ where: { startDate: { $gte: "2024-01-01" } } }],
  aggregate: {
    $select: { $count: "unordered", "salary:sum": "unordered" },
  },
});
```

`withProperties` defines [derived properties](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/object-sets.md#add-derived-properties) that `where` can filter on.

## Group results

Add `$groupBy` to get one row per group. `data` is then an array; each row has a `$group` object with the group's values, plus the metrics from `$select`.

```tsx title="src/HeadcountByDepartment.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkAggregation } from "@osdk/react";

export function HeadcountByDepartment() {
  const { data, isLoading } = useOsdkAggregation(Employee, {
    where: { department: { $isNull: false } },
    aggregate: {
      $groupBy: { department: "exact" },
      $select: { $count: "desc", "salary:avg": "unordered" },
    },
  });

  return (
    <table>
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th>Department</th>
          <th>Headcount</th>
          <th>Average salary</th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        {isLoading && !data && (
          <tr>
            <td colSpan={3}>Loading…</td>
          </tr>
        )}
        {data?.map((row) => (
          <tr key={row.$group.department}>
            <td>{row.$group.department}</td>
            <td>{row.$count}</td>
            <td>{row.salary.avg?.toFixed(0)}</td>
          </tr>
        ))}
      </tbody>
    </table>
  );
}
```

The value of each `$select` key sets the order of the rows: `"asc"` or `"desc"` sorts by that metric, and `"unordered"` leaves it to the server. Above, departments come back largest first.

### Grouping strategies

| Strategy | Property types | Groups by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"exact"` | All | Each distinct value. |
| `{ $exactWithLimit: n }` | All | Each distinct value, at most `n` groups. |
| `{ $exact: { $limit?, $includeNullValue: true } }` | All | Each distinct value, plus a group for missing values. `$group` values are then nullable. |
| `{ $exact: { $limit?, $defaultValue: "…" } }` | All | Each distinct value, with missing values grouped under the default. |
| `{ $fixedWidth: n }` | Numeric | Buckets of width `n`. |
| `{ $ranges: [[start, end], …] }` | Numeric, date, timestamp | The ranges you list. `$group` holds `{ startValue, endValue }`. |
| `{ $duration: [n, unit] }` | Date, timestamp | Time buckets, such as `[1, "years"]` or `[1, "month"]`. Dates accept day units and up; timestamps also accept seconds, minutes, and hours. |

Group by several properties to get one row per combination:

```tsx
const { data } = useOsdkAggregation(Employee, {
  aggregate: {
    $groupBy: { department: "exact", salary: { $fixedWidth: 25000 } },
    $select: { $count: "unordered" },
  },
});
```

> [!NOTE]
> **Typing $ranges and $duration**
>
> The hook infers `aggregate` as a constant, which makes the tuples in `$ranges` and `$duration` read-only. TypeScript then loses the result type and `row.$group` has no properties. Assert the tuple type to keep it: `{ $ranges: [[0, 50000], [50000, 100000]] as [number, number][] }` or `{ $duration: [1, "years"] as [1, "years"] }`.

```tsx title="src/SalaryBands.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkAggregation } from "@osdk/react";

export function SalaryBands() {
  const { data } = useOsdkAggregation(Employee, {
    aggregate: {
      $groupBy: {
        salary: {
          $ranges: [
            [0, 75000],
            [75000, 150000],
            [150000, 1000000],
          ] as [number, number][],
        },
      },
      $select: { $count: "unordered" },
    },
  });

  return (
    <ul>
      {data?.map((row) => (
        <li key={row.$group.salary.startValue}>
          {row.$group.salary.startValue} to {row.$group.salary.endValue}: {row.$count}
        </li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

## Aggregate an object set

To aggregate a set that a type and a `where` cannot express, such as a pivot or a union, pass it as `objectSet`. The first argument must be the type of that set. `where`, `intersectWith`, and `withProperties` still apply on top of it.

```tsx title="src/SalesOfficesByCity.tsx"
import { Employee, Office } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkAggregation, useOsdkClient } from "@osdk/react";
import { useMemo } from "react";

export function SalesOfficesByCity() {
  const client = useOsdkClient();
  const salesOffices = useMemo(
    () => client(Employee).where({ department: "Sales" }).pivotTo("office"),
    [client],
  );

  const { data } = useOsdkAggregation(Office, {
    objectSet: salesOffices,
    aggregate: {
      $groupBy: { city: "exact" },
      $select: { $count: "desc" },
    },
  });

  return (
    <ul>
      {data?.map((row) => (
        <li key={row.$group.city}>
          {row.$group.city}: {row.$count} offices
        </li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

`objectSet` must be an `ObjectSet`, not `undefined`, and works with object types only. The `objectSet` field returned by [`useOsdkObjects`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/objects.md) and [`useObjectSet`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/object-sets.md) is `undefined` until their first page loads, so build the set with the client as above when you need it on the first render. See [Work with object sets](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/object-sets.md) for union, intersect, and subtract.

## Refresh and disable

Aggregations recompute when an action changes the object type, like other queries. `refetch` invalidates the object type, which refetches every cached query for that type.

With `enabled: false`, the hook does not fetch and returns `data: undefined`, `isLoading: false`, and `error: undefined`. `refetch` does nothing while disabled.

## Reference

### `useOsdkAggregation(type, options)`

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aggregate` | `{ $select, $groupBy? }` | Required | The metrics to compute and the optional grouping. |
| `aggregate.$select` | `{ [metric]: "unordered" \| "asc" \| "desc" }` | Required | Metric keys, such as `$count` or `"salary:avg"`, and how to order groups by them. |
| `aggregate.$groupBy` | `{ [property]: strategy }` | | Group by these properties. See [Grouping strategies](#grouping-strategies). |
| `where` | `WhereClause<T>` | | Filter the objects first. |
| `intersectWith` | `Array<{ where: WhereClause<T> }>` | | Additional filters that every object must also match. |
| `withProperties` | `DerivedProperty.Clause` | | Derived properties that `where` can reference. |
| `objectSet` | `ObjectSet<T>` | | Aggregate this set instead of every object of `type`. Object types only. |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | When `false`, no request is made. |
| `dedupeIntervalMs` | `number` | `2000` | Identical aggregations within this window share one request. |

| Return | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | Result object, array of rows, or `undefined` | An object of metrics without `$groupBy`; an array of rows with `$group` and metrics with it. |
| `isLoading` | `boolean` | `true` while a request is in flight. |
| `error` | `Error \| undefined` | The last error, if the aggregation failed. |
| `refetch` | `() => Promise<void>` | Invalidate the object type and recompute. No-op while disabled. |

# Invalidate the cache

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/cache-invalidation

> Refetch cached objects, lists, and function results with useObservableClient when data changes outside OSDK actions.

{/* cspell:ignore refetch refetches refetched refetching canonicalization */}

Invalidating cached data makes every component that shows it refetch. Most apps rarely need it: the cache updates itself after actions. This page covers the cases it cannot see and the methods that handle them. For how the cache stores and shares data, see [Caching](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/concepts/caching.md).

## When the cache updates itself

You do not need to invalidate after:

- **Actions applied with `useOsdkAction`.** The server reports which objects the action added, modified, and deleted. The cache refetches those objects, and every list, link, aggregation, and function that depends on their types re-evaluates.
- **Optimistic updates.** They are removed when the action finishes. See [Optimistic updates](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/optimistic-updates.md).
- **Lists with `streamUpdates: true`.** The server pushes changes over a WebSocket.
- **Functions with `dependsOn` or `dependsOnObjects`.** They rerun after actions edit what they declare. See [Call functions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/functions.md#refetch-when-objects-change).

## When to invalidate

The cache only learns about changes that pass through it. Invalidate when data changes some other way:

- A pipeline, schedule, or external system writes to the ontology.
- Your code applies an action with the `Client` directly, as in `client(modifyEmployee).applyAction(...)`, instead of through `useOsdkAction`.
- Another service tells your app, for example over its own WebSocket, that records changed.
- A function reads data the cache cannot track, and you did not declare `dependsOn`.

## Get the observable client

`useObservableClient` returns the `ObservableClient` that `OsdkProvider` created. Call it in a component or hook below the provider, and call the invalidation methods from an event handler or effect:

```tsx title="src/RefreshEmployee.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useObservableClient } from "@osdk/react";
import { useState } from "react";

export function RefreshEmployee({ employee }: { employee: Employee.OsdkInstance }) {
  const observableClient = useObservableClient();
  const [isRefreshing, setRefreshing] = useState(false);

  async function refresh() {
    setRefreshing(true);
    try {
      await observableClient.invalidateObjects(employee);
    } finally {
      setRefreshing(false);
    }
  }

  return (
    <button disabled={isRefreshing} onClick={() => void refresh()}>
      {isRefreshing ? "Refreshing…" : "Refresh"}
    </button>
  );
}
```

## Invalidation methods

| Method | Refetches | Use it when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invalidateObjects(objects)` | The given object or array of objects, in every variant cached for them. Also reruns functions that list one of them in `dependsOnObjects`, and refreshes links from or to their type. An object that is not cached yet is fetched. | You know exactly which objects changed. |
| `invalidateObjectType(type)` | Every cached query that reads the type: its objects, lists and object sets over it, aggregations over it, links from or to it, and functions that declare it in `dependsOn`. Takes the type from your SDK or its API name. | Many objects of one type changed, or you do not know which. |
| `invalidateFunction(fn, params?)` | With `params`, the one cached call with exactly those parameters. Without, every cached call of that function. Takes the function from your SDK or its API name. | A function's inputs changed outside the cache. |
| `invalidateFunctionsByObject(apiName, primaryKey)` | Functions that list that object in `dependsOnObjects`. | One object changed and you only want its functions to rerun. |
| `invalidateAll()` | Everything in the cache. | Last resort, when you cannot tell what changed. |

All methods return a promise that resolves when the refetches have settled. The promise does not reject: a failed refetch shows up as `error` on the hooks that read the data. While a refetch runs, those hooks keep their current data and report `isLoading: true`.

## Examples

### After an external write

A component that starts a server-side job, then refreshes the type the job writes to once it finishes:

```tsx title="src/ImportEmployeesButton.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useObservableClient } from "@osdk/react";
import { useState } from "react";
import { runEmployeeImport } from "./api";

export function ImportEmployeesButton() {
  const observableClient = useObservableClient();
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<"idle" | "running" | "failed">("idle");

  async function handleImport() {
    setStatus("running");
    try {
      await runEmployeeImport();
      await observableClient.invalidateObjectType(Employee);
      setStatus("idle");
    } catch (e) {
      console.error("Import failed", e);
      setStatus("failed");
    }
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <button disabled={status === "running"} onClick={() => void handleImport()}>
        Import employees
      </button>
      {status === "failed" && <p role="alert">The import failed.</p>}
    </div>
  );
}
```

### After a direct client call

When you apply an action with the `Client`, invalidate what it edited. Ask for the edits with `$returnEdits` and invalidate by type:

```tsx title="src/useUpdateJobTitle.ts"
import { Employee, modifyEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useObservableClient, useOsdkClient } from "@osdk/react";
import { useCallback } from "react";

export function useUpdateJobTitle() {
  const client = useOsdkClient();
  const observableClient = useObservableClient();

  return useCallback(
    async (employee: Employee.OsdkInstance, jobTitle: string) => {
      const edits = await client(modifyEmployee).applyAction(
        { employee, jobTitle },
        { $returnEdits: true },
      );
      await Promise.all(
        edits.editedObjectTypes.map((type) =>
          observableClient.invalidateObjectType(String(type)),
        ),
      );
    },
    [client, observableClient],
  );
}
```

`useOsdkAction` does this for you, and more precisely, so prefer it. See [Apply actions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/actions.md).

### Refresh a function

```tsx title="src/RefreshMetrics.tsx"
import { getEmployeeMetrics } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useObservableClient } from "@osdk/react";

export function RefreshMetrics({ department }: { department: string }) {
  const observableClient = useObservableClient();

  return (
    <div>
      <button
        onClick={() =>
          void observableClient.invalidateFunction(getEmployeeMetrics, { department })
        }
      >
        Refresh this department
      </button>
      <button onClick={() => void observableClient.invalidateFunction(getEmployeeMetrics)}>
        Refresh all departments
      </button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

For a single call site, `refetch` from `useOsdkFunction` does the same as `invalidateFunction` with that call's parameters.

### Refresh when another service notifies you

Subscribe in an effect and invalidate when a message arrives. `invalidateObjects` needs an object instance, so with only a primary key, invalidate the type, and rerun the functions bound to that one object with `invalidateFunctionsByObject`:

```tsx title="src/useEmployeeChangeFeed.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useObservableClient } from "@osdk/react";
import { useEffect } from "react";

export function useEmployeeChangeFeed(url: string) {
  const observableClient = useObservableClient();

  useEffect(() => {
    const socket = new WebSocket(url);
    socket.addEventListener("message", (event) => {
      const { employeeId } = JSON.parse(String(event.data)) as { employeeId: number };
      void observableClient.invalidateFunctionsByObject(Employee.apiName, employeeId);
      void observableClient.invalidateObjectType(Employee);
    });
    return () => socket.close();
  }, [observableClient, url]);
}
```

## Best practices

1. **Let actions drive updates.** If a change comes from `useOsdkAction`, do not invalidate afterward. It refetches data that is already fresh.
2. **Invalidate the narrowest thing you can.** `invalidateObjects` is cheaper than `invalidateObjectType`, which is cheaper than `invalidateAll`.
3. **Declare function dependencies.** `dependsOn` and `dependsOnObjects` let the cache rerun functions after actions, so you do not invalidate them by hand.
4. **Do not invalidate on mount.** Calling `invalidateAll` or `invalidateObjectType` in a mount effect refetches on every navigation and defeats the cache.
5. **Keep OSDK data in the cache.** Copying it into component state, Redux, or another query library creates a second copy that invalidation and optimistic updates do not reach.

## Debug the cache

The `devMode` prop on `OsdkProvider` turns on logging in development builds. It has no effect in production builds.

```tsx title="src/main.tsx"
import { OsdkProvider } from "@osdk/react";
import { client } from "./client";
import { App } from "./App";

export function Root() {
  return (
    <OsdkProvider
      client={client}
      devMode={{ logLevel: "debug", debug: { refCounts: true, cacheKeys: true } }}
    >
      <App />
    </OsdkProvider>
  );
}
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `logLevel` | `"trace" \| "debug" \| "info" \| "warn" \| "error" \| "fatal"` | `"error"` | Log level for the observable client. Set `"debug"` to see its tracing. |
| `debug.refCounts` | `boolean` | `false` | Logs when cache entries are created, referenced, and cleaned up, and shortens how long unused entries are kept so cleanup happens sooner. |
| `debug.cacheKeys` | `boolean` | `false` | Logs cache-key lookups and whether each key already existed. |
| `actionDelayMs` | `number` | `1000` | Delay before optimistic updates are removed. See [Optimistic updates](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/optimistic-updates.md#simulate-latency-in-development). |

To browse cache entries in the running app instead, use [OSDK Devtools](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/devtools.md).

# Cache

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/devtools/cache

> Use the Cache tab in OSDK Devtools to inspect and invalidate observable cache entries and review recent cache hits and misses.

The Cache tab shows the entries in the `@osdk/react` observable cache and a timeline of recent cache hits and misses. Use it to confirm that a repeated read came from the cache, or to see when a read went to the network. For how the cache works, see [Caching](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/concepts/caching.md).

![Cache tab](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/img/react-devtools/cache.png)

## Cache inspector

The summary shows the number of entries and their estimated total size. **Search cache** matches cache keys, object types, and entry types.

Each entry header shows its status (`init`, `loading`, `loaded`, or `error`), age, and estimated size. Expand an entry to see its cache key, current value, and query details.

| Control | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| **Refresh** | Reloads the inspector snapshot. It does not refetch data. |
| Refresh icon on an object entry | Invalidates that object. |
| Refresh icon on a list, link, or object set entry | Invalidates every entry for that object type. |
| **Clear cache** | After you confirm, invalidates the whole cache. Active queries refetch. |

## Cache history

Cache history lists recent cache hits and misses in time order. Each row shows the query or object signature, the time, and the response time when one was recorded.

## Related metrics

Requests saved, Cache hit rate, and Avg response time on [Overview](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/devtools/overview.md) summarize the same operations. Select **View in Cache** under Cache hit rate to move from the metric to the entries behind it.

# Components

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/devtools/components

> Use the Components tab in OSDK Devtools to find which React components call OSDK hooks and what objects, actions, and properties they use.

The Components tab maps `@osdk/react` hooks to the React components that mounted them. Use it to find the component that owns a query, compare components that read the same object type, or trace an overfetching recommendation back to its source.

![Components tab](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/img/react-devtools/components.png)

## What appears

Only components that call an `@osdk/react` hook, such as `useOsdkObject` or `useOsdkObjects`, appear. A component that only renders an OSDK-aware child like `ObjectTable`, or receives objects through props, does not appear; look for the child that owns the hook instead. Data loaded with raw network calls or another state library is not tracked.

Component attribution relies on the Fiber hook that the Vite plugin installs before React loads. If the panel shows a notice that component inspection is unavailable, see [Troubleshooting](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/devtools.md#troubleshooting).

## Find a component

- **Search ontology** matches component names and the object types and actions they use.
- The summary line counts mounted components, object types, and action types.
- The filter chips narrow the list to one object type or action. Select **All** to clear the filter.

## Component cards

Each card groups what the monitor observed for one component:

| Section | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| Related objects | Object types the component loads, with primary keys. |
| Related actions | Actions the component applies through `@osdk/react`. |
| Related properties | Fields that the component's descendants read. |
| React props | Props captured from the mounted component. |

## Health badge

A card shows **Healthy** unless the monitor detects a problem. After a component has rendered more than five times, the monitor flags:

- Wasted renders: renders in which the component read no tracked property.
- Properties the component accessed in fewer than 10% of its renders.

An unhealthy card replaces the badge with a summary of what it found.

# Console

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/devtools/console

> Use the Console tab in OSDK Devtools to search and filter browser console output captured while your OSDK React app runs.

The Console tab captures browser console output while the panel is active and keeps it as you navigate within the app. Use it to match an Errors & warnings count on [Overview](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/devtools/overview.md) to the original message, or to keep a brief warning visible after the page changes.

![Console tab](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/img/react-devtools/console.png)

## Search and filter

- **Filter logs** searches the serialized arguments of each entry.
- The level menu shows all entries, or only `log`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, or `debug`.
- **Clear logs**, in the same menu, empties the feed. It does not reset the other devtools metrics.

The toolbar shows counts for errors, warnings, and other entries. When a search or level filter hides entries, it also shows how many are hidden.

## Log entries

Each entry shows its level, timestamp, arguments, and source location when the browser provides one. Objects and errors are serialized with depth and size limits, so a large payload cannot take over the panel.

## Limits

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Entries stored | 1,000 most recent |
| Entries rendered | 200 most recent that match the current search and level |

Narrow the search or level filter to bring an older matching entry back into the rendered list.

# OSDK Devtools

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/devtools
