> Add an in-app panel that shows Ontology usage, hook owners, console output, and the observable cache of a running OSDK React app.

`@osdk/react-devtools` adds a panel to your `@osdk/react` app during development. Use it to see which components own OSDK hooks, how often reads hit the cache, and what your app logs to the console.

> [!WARNING]
> `@osdk/react-devtools` is experimental. Its panels and metrics can change between minor versions.

## Set up the panel

### Install the package

Add `@osdk/react-devtools` as a dev dependency:

```npm
npm install -D @osdk/react-devtools
```

The package has peer dependencies on `@osdk/api`, `@osdk/client`, `@osdk/react`, `react`, `react-dom`, `@types/react`, and `vite` 5, 6, or 7. An OSDK React app created with `@osdk/create-app` already has them.
### Add the Vite plugin

Import `osdkDevTools` from `@osdk/react-devtools/vite` and add it to `plugins`:

```ts title="vite.config.ts"
import { osdkDevTools } from "@osdk/react-devtools/vite";
import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react";
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), osdkDevTools()],
});
```

`osdkDevTools` is also the default export of `@osdk/react-devtools/vite`.
### Keep your existing provider

You do not add any JSX. During `vite dev`, the plugin injects two scripts into `index.html`: one that installs a React Fiber hook, and one that imports the panel:

```html
<script type="module">import '@osdk/react-devtools';</script>
```

The import registers the devtools with `@osdk/react`. Your existing `OsdkProvider` then wraps its client with the monitor and renders the panel:

```tsx title="src/main.tsx"
import { OsdkProvider } from "@osdk/react";
import ReactDOM from "react-dom/client";
import App from "./App.js";
import { client } from "./client.js";

ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById("root")!).render(
  <OsdkProvider client={client}>
    <App />
  </OsdkProvider>,
);
```
### Start the dev server

Run your dev script, for example `npm run dev`. The panel opens in the top right corner of the page on the Overview tab.

## Plugin options

All options are optional.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `true` unless `NODE_ENV` is `"production"` | Set to `false` to keep the plugin in your config without injecting the panel. |
| `verbose` | `boolean` | `false` | Logs plugin diagnostics, including whether the scripts were injected into `index.html`. |

```ts title="vite.config.ts"
osdkDevTools({ enabled: true, verbose: true });
```

## Open and arrange the panel

Select **Minimize** in the panel header to collapse it to a `</>` launcher in the bottom right corner. Select the launcher to reopen the panel.

![Collapsed OSDK Devtools launcher](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/img/react-devtools/launcher.png)

The header controls apply to every tab:

| Control | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Theme | Cycles through dark (the default), light, and auto, which follows your system setting. |
| Dock mode | Cycles through floating, docked to the bottom, and docked to the right. |
| Reset metrics | Clears the metrics collected in this session. It does not change app data or the cache. |
| Minimize | Collapses the panel to the `</>` launcher. |

Drag the header to move a floating panel, and drag an edge or corner to resize it. The panel saves its position, size, theme, dock mode, and collapsed state in `localStorage`, so they survive reloads.

## Tabs

| Tab | Use it to |
| --- | --- |
| [Overview](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/devtools/overview.md) | See Ontology usage, requests saved, cache hit rate, optimistic coverage, errors, overfetching, and recommendations. |
| [Components](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/devtools/components.md) | Find which React components call OSDK hooks and which object types, actions, and properties they use. |
| [Console](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/devtools/console.md) | Search and filter captured console output by level. |
| [Cache](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/devtools/cache.md) | Inspect cache entries, invalidate them, and review recent cache hits and misses. |

## How collection works

The panel observes the app you already run. It does not send its own requests.

- **Requests and cache.** The devtools wrap the observable client that `OsdkProvider` creates and record the cache reads, network requests, and actions that pass through it. Data you load with raw `fetch`, `axios`, or another state library does not appear.
- **Components.** The injected Fiber hook attributes each `@osdk/react` hook to the component that mounted it. The hook must install before React loads. If React loads first, the panel still works but shows a notice that component inspection is unavailable.
- **Console.** The monitor captures `console` calls made while the page is open.

Open the panel before you exercise the flow you want to inspect, and use **Reset metrics** to start from zero.

## Production builds

The plugin applies only to `vite dev` and `vite serve`. It does nothing during `vite build`, in `production` mode, or under Vitest, so the panel does not ship to users. To turn it off during development, do one of the following:

- Pass `osdkDevTools({ enabled: false })`.
- Remove `osdkDevTools()` from `plugins`.
- Uninstall `@osdk/react-devtools`.

## Compatibility

Use compatible versions of `@osdk/react-devtools` and your other `@osdk/*` packages. Mismatched versions can behave unexpectedly. See [Installation](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/installation.md) for how to keep OSDK packages in sync.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| The panel does not appear. | Confirm `osdkDevTools()` is in `plugins`, `enabled` is not `false`, and you run `vite dev`. Set `verbose: true` and look for `Injected devtools into HTML` in the terminal. Your `index.html` needs a `</head>` or `</body>` tag. |
| The panel appears but shows no data. | Confirm the app renders `OsdkProvider` and the screen reads data through `@osdk/react` hooks. |
| Component inspection is unavailable. | Something loaded React before the injected script. Remove manual imports or scripts in `index.html` that load React ahead of it. |
| The panel appears in a deployed build. | Look for code that imports `@osdk/react-devtools` directly, or a stale development bundle on the server. |

# Overview

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/devtools/overview

> Read the Overview tab in OSDK Devtools to check Ontology usage, cache hit rate, optimistic coverage, errors, overfetching, and recommendations.

{/* cspell:ignore revalidations */}

The Overview tab is the first tab the panel shows. It summarizes how the mounted components use the Ontology and how the client has performed since the page loaded or since you last selected **Reset metrics**.

![Overview tab](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/img/react-devtools/overview.png)

## Ontology

Counts the distinct object types, action types, and links that mounted components use. If no component uses the Ontology yet, the section says so and links to these docs.

## Metrics

| Metric | What it measures | Highlighted when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Requests saved | Reads served from the cache, revalidations, and deduplicated requests that did not reach the network. | Never |
| Optimistic coverage | Share of actions that updated the UI before the server responded. See [Optimistic updates](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/optimistic-updates.md). | Never |
| Cache hit rate | Share of object reads served from the cache instead of the network. Blank until the session has 20 reads. | Green above 70%, amber from 40% to 70%, red below 40% |
| Avg response time | Average response time across cache and network reads. Cache reads typically take under 1 ms, so network reads dominate. | Never |
| Errors & warnings | `console.error` and `console.warn` entries captured this session. | Red when above 0 |
| Overfetching | Components whose queries fetch fields their descendants never read. A query counts when descendants read less than 70% of the fetched fields. | Red when above 0 |

Select the help icon on a metric for its definition and thresholds. Three metrics link to the tab with the detail behind them:

| Metric | Link | Opens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cache hit rate | **View in Cache** | [Cache](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/devtools/cache.md) |
| Errors & warnings | **View in Console** | [Console](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/devtools/console.md) |
| Overfetching | **View in Components** | [Components](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/devtools/components.md) |

## Recommendations

Recommendations turn the metrics and component observations into specific fixes, such as a query that fetches unused fields. Some include a copyable prompt you can paste into a coding assistant. With nothing to suggest, the section reads `No recommendations right now.`

## Measure one flow

1. Select **Reset metrics** in the panel header. This clears the collected metrics without touching app data or the cache.
2. Run the flow you want to measure in your app.
3. Read the metrics and recommendations for that flow alone.

# Call functions

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/functions

> Run Foundry functions from React with useOsdkFunction and useOsdkFunctions, with caching, dependency-based refetching, and error handling.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Functions](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/functions/overview)

{/* cspell:ignore refetched refetches refetching */}

Use `useOsdkFunction` to call a Foundry function (an ontology query) and render its result. The result is cached and shared across components, and you can tell the cache which objects the function reads so it reruns after actions change them.

## Call a function

Pass the function from your generated SDK and its parameters:

```tsx title="src/EmployeeMetrics.tsx"
import { getEmployeeMetrics } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkFunction } from "@osdk/react";

export function EmployeeMetrics({ department }: { department: string }) {
  const { data, isLoading, error } = useOsdkFunction(getEmployeeMetrics, {
    params: { department },
  });

  return (
    <section>
      {isLoading && <span>Updating…</span>}
      {error && <p role="alert">Could not load metrics: {error.message}</p>}
      {data && <p>Headcount: {data.headcount}</p>}
    </section>
  );
}
```

`params` is typed from the function's signature. Required parameters must be present, and optional ones can be left out. A function with no parameters takes no options:

```tsx title="src/EmployeeCount.tsx"
import { countEmployees } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkFunction } from "@osdk/react";

export function EmployeeCount() {
  const { data } = useOsdkFunction(countEmployees);

  return <span>{data ?? "…"} employees</span>;
}
```

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `params` | Function parameters | `undefined` | Arguments for the function. Omit for functions without parameters. |
| `dependsOn` | `Array<ObjectTypeDefinition \| string>` | `undefined` | Object types the function reads. A change to any object of these types refetches it. Pass the type from your SDK or its API name. |
| `dependsOnObjects` | `Array<Osdk.Instance \| ObjectSet>` | `undefined` | Specific objects, or object sets, the function reads. See [Refetch when specific objects change](#refetch-when-specific-objects-change). |
| `dedupeIntervalMs` | `number` | `2000` | Within this many milliseconds of the last fetch, a new subscriber reuses the cached result instead of calling the function again. |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | When `false`, the function is not called and `data` stays `undefined`. |

### Return value

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | Function return type `\| undefined` | The result. `undefined` before the first result arrives and after an error. |
| `isLoading` | `boolean` | `true` while a call is in flight, including refetches. The previous `data` stays available while it refetches. |
| `error` | `Error \| undefined` | Set when the last call failed. |
| `lastUpdated` | `number` | Time of the last successful call, in milliseconds since the epoch. `0` before the first result. |
| `refetch` | `() => Promise<void>` | Calls the function again with the same parameters, ignoring `dedupeIntervalMs`. |

## How results are cached

Each result is cached under the function's API name, its version, and its parameters. Parameters are compared by value, so two components that call `getEmployeeMetrics` with `{ department: "Sales" }` share one cache entry and one network request. A different `department` is a separate entry.

A cached result does not expire on a timer. It is refetched when:

- you call `refetch`, or invalidate it through the observable client (see [Invalidate the cache](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/cache-invalidation.md)),
- an action edits an object the function depends on (`dependsOn` or `dependsOnObjects`), or
- a component subscribes after `dedupeIntervalMs` has passed since the last call.

Without `dependsOn` or `dependsOnObjects`, actions never refetch the function, because the cache cannot know what it reads. For the full cache model, see [Caching](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/concepts/caching.md).

## Refetch when objects change

Declare the object types your function reads with `dependsOn`. After an action adds, modifies, or deletes an object of one of those types, the function runs again:

```tsx title="src/DepartmentHeadcount.tsx"
import { Employee, getEmployeeMetrics } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkFunction } from "@osdk/react";

export function DepartmentHeadcount({ department }: { department: string }) {
  const { data, isLoading, refetch } = useOsdkFunction(getEmployeeMetrics, {
    params: { department },
    dependsOn: [Employee],
  });

  return (
    <div>
      {data && <span>Headcount: {data.headcount}</span>}
      {isLoading && <span> (updating)</span>}
      <button onClick={() => void refetch()}>Refresh</button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`dependsOn` also accepts API name strings, such as `dependsOn: ["Employee"]`, which is useful when you do not import the type.

### Refetch when specific objects change

`dependsOnObjects` narrows the trigger. Pass object instances, and the function reruns only when one of those exact objects (matched by type and primary key) is edited:

```tsx title="src/EmployeeReport.tsx"
import { Employee, getEmployeeReport } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkFunction } from "@osdk/react";

export function EmployeeReport({ employee }: { employee: Employee.OsdkInstance }) {
  const { data } = useOsdkFunction(getEmployeeReport, {
    params: { employeeId: employee.$primaryKey },
    dependsOnObjects: [employee],
  });

  return <pre>{data ? JSON.stringify(data, null, 2) : "Loading report…"}</pre>;
}
```

`dependsOnObjects` also accepts object sets. The cache looks up the set's object type in the background and then treats it like `dependsOn` for that type: a change to any object of that type refetches the function, not only changes to objects in the set. Because the result is the same, pass the type to `dependsOn` instead. It takes effect immediately and avoids a type error, since a typed object set such as `Employee.ObjectSet` is not assignable to the option's `ObjectSet<ObjectTypeDefinition>` type.

> [!WARNING]
> The first component to subscribe to a function and parameter combination sets its dependencies. A later component that passes different `dependsOn` or `dependsOnObjects` for the same parameters shares the existing entry and its dependencies. Pass the same dependency options everywhere you call a function with the same parameters.

## Wait for inputs

Hooks cannot be called conditionally. To hold a call until its inputs exist, set `enabled`:

```tsx title="src/ReportForEmployee.tsx"
import { Employee, getEmployeeReport } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkFunction, useOsdkObject } from "@osdk/react";

export function ReportForEmployee({ employeeId }: { employeeId: number }) {
  const { object: employee } = useOsdkObject(Employee, employeeId);

  const { data, isLoading } = useOsdkFunction(getEmployeeReport, {
    params: { employeeId },
    dependsOnObjects: employee ? [employee] : [],
    enabled: employee != null,
  });

  return (
    <div>
      <h2>{employee?.fullName ?? "Loading employee…"}</h2>
      {isLoading && <span>Loading report…</span>}
      {data && <pre>{JSON.stringify(data, null, 2)}</pre>}
    </div>
  );
}
```

While `enabled` is `false`, `isLoading` is `false` and `data` is `undefined`.

## Handle errors

When a call fails, `error` holds the `Error` and `data` becomes `undefined`. The error stays until a later call succeeds, so render it next to the rest of the component rather than in place of it. `refetch` doubles as a retry:

```tsx title="src/MetricsWithRetry.tsx"
import { getEmployeeMetrics } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkFunction } from "@osdk/react";

export function MetricsWithRetry({ department }: { department: string }) {
  const { data, error, isLoading, refetch } = useOsdkFunction(
    getEmployeeMetrics,
    { params: { department } },
  );

  return (
    <section>
      {data && <p>Headcount: {data.headcount}</p>}
      {error && (
        <p role="alert">
          {error.message}{" "}
          <button disabled={isLoading} onClick={() => void refetch()}>
            Retry
          </button>
        </p>
      )}
    </section>
  );
}
```

Errors from Foundry are `PalantirApiError` instances, exported from `@osdk/client`, which carry `errorName`, `errorCode`, and `errorInstanceId`. See [Loading and errors](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/concepts/loading-and-errors.md) for patterns that apply to every hook.

## Call several functions

`useOsdkFunctions` runs a list of function calls and returns one result per call, in the same order. Each result has the same shape as the `useOsdkFunction` return value.

```ts title="src/functionCall.ts"
import type { QueryDefinition } from "@osdk/client";
import type { UseOsdkFunctionOptions, UseOsdkFunctionsProps } from "@osdk/react";

type FunctionCall = UseOsdkFunctionsProps["queries"][number];

export function functionCall<Q extends QueryDefinition<unknown>>(
  queryDefinition: Q,
  options?: UseOsdkFunctionOptions<Q>,
): FunctionCall {
  return { queryDefinition, options } as unknown as FunctionCall;
}
```

```tsx title="src/DepartmentCards.tsx"
import { getEmployeeMetrics } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkFunctions } from "@osdk/react";
import { functionCall } from "./functionCall";

export function DepartmentCards({ departments }: { departments: string[] }) {
  const results = useOsdkFunctions({
    queries: departments.map((department) =>
      functionCall(getEmployeeMetrics, { params: { department } }),
    ),
    maxConcurrent: 4,
  });

  return (
    <ul>
      {results.map((result, index) => (
        <li key={departments[index]}>
          {departments[index]}:{" "}
          {result.error
            ? result.error.message
            : result.isLoading
              ? "…"
              : JSON.stringify(result.data)}
        </li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

Each call is cached exactly as if it came from `useOsdkFunction`, so a call that another component already made is served from the cache. Because the list can mix functions, `queries` is typed for any function and does not accept a specific function's `params` as written. The `functionCall` helper above checks `params` against each function, then widens the entry. Narrow or cast each result's `data` before use.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `queries` | `Array<{ queryDefinition, options? }>` | Required | The calls to make. `options` takes the same fields as the `useOsdkFunction` options: `params`, `dependsOn`, `dependsOnObjects`, `dedupeIntervalMs`, and `enabled`. |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | When `false`, no call runs. A call whose own `options.enabled` is `false` is skipped either way. |
| `maxConcurrent` | `number` | `undefined` | Limit on calls in flight at once. The next call starts when a running one finishes, successfully or not. Use it for functions that are slow or return large payloads. Without it, all calls start together. |

# React SDK

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react

> Build reactive Foundry apps with @osdk/react hooks backed by one shared, normalized cache.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [OSDK React applications](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/ontology-sdk-react-applications/overview)

`@osdk/react` wraps the OSDK client in hooks. Every hook reads from one normalized cache, so a list, a detail view, and a link panel that show the same object stay in sync, and an action updates them all without manual refetching.

```tsx title="src/EmployeeList.tsx"
import { useOsdkObjects } from "@osdk/react";
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";

export function EmployeeList() {
  const { data, isLoading, error } = useOsdkObjects(Employee, {
    where: { department: "Engineering" },
    orderBy: { fullName: "asc" },
  });

  return (
    <section aria-busy={isLoading}>
      {error != null && <p role="alert">Could not load employees.</p>}
      <ul>
        {data?.map((employee) => (
          <li key={employee.$primaryKey}>{employee.fullName}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </section>
  );
}
```

New to OSDK? Start with the [Quickstart](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/quickstart.md), then [create a client and add OsdkProvider](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/client.md).

## Hooks

| Hook | Use it to | Guide |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `useOsdkObjects` | Load a list of objects with filters, sorting, and paging | [Query objects](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/objects.md) |
| `useOsdkObject` | Load one object by primary key | [Query objects](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/objects.md#load-one-object) |
| `useLinks` | Load the objects linked to an object | [Follow links](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/links.md) |
| `useObjectSet` | Combine, intersect, subtract, or pivot object sets | [Work with object sets](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/object-sets.md) |
| `useStableObjectSet` | Keep an object set referentially stable across renders | [Work with object sets](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/object-sets.md) |
| `useOsdkAggregation` | Count, sum, average, and group on the server | [Aggregate data](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/aggregations.md) |
| `useOsdkAction` | Apply and validate actions | [Apply actions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/actions.md) |
| `useDebouncedCallback` | Debounce validation while a user types | [Apply actions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/actions.md) |
| `useOsdkFunction`, `useOsdkFunctions` | Call Ontology functions with caching | [Call functions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/functions.md) |
| `useObservableClient` | Invalidate cached data by hand | [Invalidate the cache](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/cache-invalidation.md) |
| `useOsdkClient` | Get the client for one-off, imperative calls | [Create a client](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/client.md) |
| `useOsdkMetadata` | Read object and action type metadata | [Reference](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/reference.md) |

User, group, and marking hooks live in `@osdk/react/platform-apis`; see [Users and markings](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/platform-apis.md). Test utilities live in `@osdk/react/testing`; see [Test your app](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/testing.md).

## How data flows

- [Caching and reactivity](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/concepts/caching.md): How hooks share one cache and stay current.
- [Loading and errors](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/concepts/loading-and-errors.md): Render without flashing while data refreshes.
- [Optimistic updates](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/optimistic-updates.md): Show the result of an action before the server confirms it.
- [Devtools](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/devtools.md): Inspect the cache, queries, and actions in your running app.

# Follow links

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/links

> Load the objects linked to one or more source objects with useLinks, or pivot a whole query to a linked type with pivotTo.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Link types](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/object-link-types/link-types-overview)

Links connect objects of one type to objects of another, such as an employee to their office or a manager to their reports. Use `useLinks` to load the linked objects of objects you already have, and `pivotTo` to turn a query for one type into a query for the linked type.

The samples on this page use these links from the example SDK:

| Link | From | To | Cardinality |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lead` | `Employee` | `Employee` | One |
| `reports` | `Employee` | `Employee` | Many |
| `office` | `Employee` | `Office` | One |
| `occupants` | `Office` | `Employee` | Many |

## Load linked objects

Pass a source object and a link name. `links` holds the linked objects:

```tsx title="src/DirectReports.tsx"
import type { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useLinks } from "@osdk/react";

export function DirectReports({ manager }: { manager: Employee.OsdkInstance }) {
  const { links, isLoading, error } = useLinks(manager, "reports");

  return (
    <div>
      <h3>Reports{links && ` (${links.length})`}</h3>
      {isLoading && !links && <p>Loading…</p>}
      {error && <p role="alert">{error.message}</p>}
      <ul>
        {links?.map((report) => (
          <li key={report.$primaryKey}>{report.fullName}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </div>
  );
}
```

TypeScript checks the link name against the source type and types `links` as the linked object type.

### Links to one object

A link to a single object uses the same hook. `links` is an array with at most one element:

```tsx title="src/OfficeLabel.tsx"
import type { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useLinks } from "@osdk/react";

export function OfficeLabel({ employee }: { employee: Employee.OsdkInstance }) {
  const { links } = useLinks(employee, "office");
  const office = links?.[0];

  return <span>{office ? `${office.name}, ${office.city}` : "No office"}</span>;
}
```

## Filter, sort, and paginate links

`useLinks` accepts `where`, `orderBy`, `$select`, and `pageSize` for the linked type. They work as they do in [`useOsdkObjects`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/objects.md#filter-with-where). `fetchMore` loads the next page and is `undefined` when there are no more.

```tsx title="src/SeniorReports.tsx"
import type { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useLinks } from "@osdk/react";

export function SeniorReports({ manager }: { manager: Employee.OsdkInstance }) {
  const { links, isLoading, fetchMore } = useLinks(manager, "reports", {
    where: { jobTitle: { $startsWith: "Senior" } },
    orderBy: { fullName: "asc" },
    $select: ["fullName", "jobTitle"],
    pageSize: 25,
  });

  return (
    <div>
      <ul>
        {links?.map((report) => (
          <li key={report.$primaryKey}>
            {report.fullName}, {report.jobTitle}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      {fetchMore && (
        <button onClick={() => void fetchMore()} disabled={isLoading}>
          Load more
        </button>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Wait for the source object

The source can be `undefined`, which lets you chain `useLinks` after a hook that is still loading. Set `enabled` so it does not query until the source arrives:

```tsx title="src/ManagerReports.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useLinks, useOsdkObject } from "@osdk/react";

export function ManagerReports({ employeeId }: { employeeId: number }) {
  const { object: manager } = useOsdkObject(Employee, employeeId);
  const { links: reports, isLoading } = useLinks(manager, "reports", {
    enabled: manager != null,
  });

  return (
    <section>
      <h2>{manager?.fullName ?? "Loading…"}</h2>
      {isLoading && !reports && <p>Loading reports…</p>}
      <ul>
        {reports?.map((report) => (
          <li key={report.$primaryKey}>{report.fullName}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </section>
  );
}
```

## Load links from many objects

Pass an array of source objects to load their links in one hook. `links` is the combined list. `linkedObjectsBySourcePrimaryKey` maps each source's primary key to its own linked objects, so you can group them:

```tsx title="src/TeamOffices.tsx"
import type { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useLinks } from "@osdk/react";

export function TeamOffices({ team }: { team: Employee.OsdkInstance[] }) {
  const { linkedObjectsBySourcePrimaryKey } = useLinks(team, "office");

  return (
    <ul>
      {team.map((employee) => {
        const office = linkedObjectsBySourcePrimaryKey.get(employee.$primaryKey)?.[0];
        return (
          <li key={employee.$primaryKey}>
            {employee.fullName}: {office?.name ?? "No office"}
          </li>
        );
      })}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

## Control refetching

Two `useLinks` calls with the same source and options share one request if the second starts within `dedupeIntervalMs` (2 seconds by default). Raise it to refetch less often on remount, or set it to `Infinity` to refetch only when the cache is invalidated, for example by an action:

```tsx
const { links } = useLinks(employee, "reports", { dedupeIntervalMs: Infinity });
```

`mode` overrides the cache policy for one call:

| `mode` | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `undefined` (default) | Fetch unless a recent result is cached. |
| `"force"` | Always fetch. |
| `"offline"` | Read the cache only; never make a request. |

## Pivot with `pivotTo`

`useLinks` starts from objects you already hold. When you want the linked objects of every object that matches a filter, pivot the query instead. `useOsdkObjects` takes a `pivotTo` option: `where` filters the source objects, and `data` contains the linked objects.

```tsx title="src/SalesOffices.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkObjects } from "@osdk/react";

export function SalesOffices() {
  const { data: offices } = useOsdkObjects(Employee, {
    where: { department: "Sales" },
    pivotTo: "office",
  });

  return (
    <ul>
      {offices?.map((office) => (
        <li key={office.$primaryKey}>
          {office.name}, {office.city}
        </li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

The pivot runs on the server, so the result is one deduplicated list of offices, however many employees share one.

With `useObjectSet`, call `pivotTo` on the object set you pass in. The result is then typed as the linked type, which the hook's own `pivotTo` option does not do:

```tsx title="src/EngineeringReports.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useObjectSet, useOsdkClient } from "@osdk/react";
import { useMemo } from "react";

export function EngineeringReports() {
  const client = useOsdkClient();
  const reports = useMemo(
    () => client(Employee).where({ department: "Engineering" }).pivotTo("reports"),
    [client],
  );
  const { data } = useObjectSet(reports, { orderBy: { fullName: "asc" } });

  return (
    <ul>
      {data?.map((report) => (
        <li key={report.$primaryKey}>{report.fullName}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

Pivoted queries do not receive real-time updates. See [Stream real-time updates](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/objects.md#stream-real-time-updates).

## Choose an approach

| You have | You want | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One object, or a few | Its linked objects | `useLinks(objects, link)` |
| Several objects | Linked objects grouped by source | `useLinks(objects, link)` and `linkedObjectsBySourcePrimaryKey` |
| A filter on the source type | All linked objects, deduplicated | `useOsdkObjects(type, { where, pivotTo })` |
| An object set from set operations | All linked objects | `useObjectSet(objectSet.pivotTo(link))` |
| A list of objects | One value from a linked object on each row, such as the lead's name | A [derived property](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/object-sets.md#add-derived-properties) with `selectProperty` |
| A list of objects | A count or sum over each row's links | A [derived property](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/object-sets.md#add-derived-properties) with `aggregate` |

Derived properties avoid one `useLinks` call per row: the server computes the value and returns it on each object.

## Reference

### `useLinks(objects, linkName, options?)`

`objects` is one `Osdk.Instance`, an array of them, or `undefined`.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `where` | `WhereClause<L>` | | Filter the linked objects. |
| `orderBy` | `{ [property]?: "asc" \| "desc" }` | | Sort the linked objects. |
| `$select` | `PropertyKeys<L>[]` | Server default set | Properties to load for each linked object. |
| `pageSize` | `number` | Server default | Linked objects per request. |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | When `false`, no request is made and `links` is `undefined`. |
| `mode` | `"force" \| "offline"` | | Cache policy override. See [Control refetching](#control-refetching). |
| `dedupeIntervalMs` | `number` | `2000` | Identical calls within this window share one request. |
| `$includeAllBaseObjectProperties` | `boolean` | `false` | When the link targets an interface, also load the implementing type's properties. |
| `resolveToObjectType` | `boolean` | `false` | When the link targets an interface, return implementing object type instances. |

| Return | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `links` | `Osdk.Instance<L>[] \| undefined` | Linked objects from all sources. |
| `linkedObjectsBySourcePrimaryKey` | `ReadonlyMap<string \| number, readonly Osdk.Instance<L>[]>` | Linked objects keyed by source primary key. Empty until loaded. |
| `isLoading` | `boolean` | `true` while a request is in flight. |
| `error` | `Error \| undefined` | The last error, if the load failed. |
| `isOptimistic` | `boolean` | Whether the links include unconfirmed optimistic changes. |
| `fetchMore` | `(() => Promise<unknown>) \| undefined` | Load the next page. `undefined` when there are no more pages. |
| `hasMore` | `boolean` | Whether more pages exist. |

# Work with object sets

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/object-sets

> Observe composed object sets with useObjectSet, combine them with union, intersect, and subtract, and compute derived properties on the server.

An object set describes a group of objects as a query: a type, filters, set operations, and link traversals. `useObjectSet` observes any object set you build with the client, and `withProperties` adds values that the server computes for each object.

## When to use `useObjectSet`

Start with [`useOsdkObjects`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/objects.md). It covers filtering, sorting, pagination, pivots, derived properties, and streaming from an object type. Reach for `useObjectSet` when you already have an `ObjectSet`:

- You combined sets with `union`, `intersect`, or `subtract`.
- You pivoted across several links.
- Another hook or component handed you one, such as `objectSet` from a `useOsdkObjects` result.

## Build an object set

Get the client with `useOsdkClient` inside the component, and call it with an object type. The result is an `ObjectSet` that you can refine with `where`, `pivotTo`, and the set operations. Building it does not send a request; the hook does.

```tsx title="src/OpenRoles.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useObjectSet, useOsdkClient } from "@osdk/react";
import { useMemo } from "react";

export function OpenRoles() {
  const client = useOsdkClient();
  const engineers = useMemo(() => client(Employee).where({ department: "Engineering" }), [client]);

  const { data, isLoading, error, fetchMore } = useObjectSet(engineers, {
    where: { jobTitle: { $isNull: false } },
    orderBy: { startDate: "desc" },
    $select: ["fullName", "jobTitle", "startDate"],
    pageSize: 25,
  });

  return (
    <div>
      {error && <p role="alert">{error.message}</p>}
      {isLoading && !data && <p>Loading…</p>}
      <ul>
        {data?.map((employee) => (
          <li key={employee.$primaryKey}>
            {employee.fullName}, {employee.jobTitle}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      {fetchMore && <button onClick={() => void fetchMore()}>Load more</button>}
    </div>
  );
}
```

Use the client from `useOsdkClient` rather than importing one from a module, so the object set runs against the same client and cache as `OsdkProvider`. `where`, `orderBy`, `pageSize`, `$select`, `autoFetchMore`, `enabled`, and `streamUpdates` behave as they do in [`useOsdkObjects`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/objects.md). `useObjectSet` also accepts `undefined`, which disables the query until you have a set.

When the options change, `useObjectSet` keeps returning the previous `data` while the new query loads, with `isLoading` set to `true`. Changing to an object set of a different type clears it.

## Combine object sets

`union`, `intersect`, and `subtract` are methods on every object set. Each takes one or more sets of the same type and returns a new set:

| Method | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `a.union(b, c)` | Objects in any of the sets. |
| `a.intersect(b, c)` | Objects in every set. |
| `a.subtract(b, c)` | Objects in `a` that are in none of the others. |

```tsx title="src/RetentionWatchList.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useObjectSet, useOsdkClient } from "@osdk/react";
import { useMemo } from "react";

export function RetentionWatchList() {
  const client = useOsdkClient();
  const watchList = useMemo(() => {
    const highEarners = client(Employee).where({ salary: { $gte: 150000 } });
    const recentHires = client(Employee).where({ startDate: { $gte: "2025-01-01" } });
    const leadership = client(Employee).where({ jobTitle: { $containsAnyTerm: "director vp" } });
    return highEarners.union(recentHires).subtract(leadership);
  }, [client]);

  const { data } = useObjectSet(watchList, { orderBy: { fullName: "asc" } });

  return (
    <ul>
      {data?.map((employee) => (
        <li key={employee.$primaryKey}>{employee.fullName}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

The same operations are available as `useObjectSet` options, each an array of object sets. `useObjectSet(highEarners, { union: [recentHires], subtract: [leadership] })` is equivalent to the set above.

`useOsdkObjects` and `useOsdkAggregation` take an `intersectWith` option instead: an array of `{ where }` clauses on the same type. Use it when every set you would intersect is a filter on that type, and `useObjectSet` when the sets come from elsewhere, such as a pivot.

## Keep object sets stable

`useObjectSet` and `useOsdkAggregation` compare object sets by their definition, not by reference. An object set rebuilt on every render with the same filters does not trigger a new request.

Your own code may still compare by reference: a `useMemo` or `useEffect` dependency array, or a memoized child component that takes the set as a prop, such as [`ObjectTable`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/components/object-table.md). `useStableObjectSet` returns the same `ObjectSet` instance until its definition changes, including any `where`, set operation, or pivot composed onto it:

```tsx title="src/DepartmentPicker.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useObjectSet, useOsdkClient, useStableObjectSet } from "@osdk/react";
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

export function DepartmentPicker({ department }: { department: string }) {
  const client = useOsdkClient();
  const employees = useStableObjectSet(client(Employee).where({ department }));
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<ReadonlySet<number>>(new Set());

  useEffect(() => {
    setSelected(new Set());
  }, [employees]);

  const { data } = useObjectSet(employees, { $select: ["fullName"] });

  return (
    <ul>
      {data?.map((employee) => (
        <li key={employee.$primaryKey}>
          <label>
            <input
              type="checkbox"
              checked={selected.has(employee.$primaryKey)}
              onChange={() =>
                setSelected((prev) => {
                  const next = new Set(prev);
                  if (!next.delete(employee.$primaryKey)) next.add(employee.$primaryKey);
                  return next;
                })
              }
            />
            {employee.fullName}
          </label>
        </li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

The effect clears the selection only when `department` changes. Without `useStableObjectSet`, `employees` would be a new instance on every render, and the effect would run on every render. It also saves you from listing every input to the set in a `useMemo` dependency array.

## Add derived properties

`withProperties` defines properties that the server computes for each object and returns alongside its regular properties. Pass it to `useOsdkObjects` or `useObjectSet`. Each entry is a function that receives a builder for the object and returns a definition:

```tsx title="src/ManagerTable.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkObjects } from "@osdk/react";

export function ManagerTable() {
  const { data } = useOsdkObjects(Employee, {
    where: { department: "Engineering" },
    withProperties: {
      leadName: (employee) => employee.pivotTo("lead").selectProperty("fullName"),
      officeCity: (employee) => employee.pivotTo("office").selectProperty("city"),
      reportCount: (employee) => employee.pivotTo("reports").aggregate("$count"),
      avgReportSalary: (employee) => employee.pivotTo("reports").aggregate("salary:avg"),
    },
  });

  return (
    <table>
      <tbody>
        {data?.map((employee) => (
          <tr key={employee.$primaryKey}>
            <td>{employee.fullName}</td>
            <td>{employee.leadName ?? "None"}</td>
            <td>{employee.officeCity}</td>
            <td>{employee.reportCount}</td>
            <td>{employee.avgReportSalary?.toFixed(0) ?? "No reports"}</td>
          </tr>
        ))}
      </tbody>
    </table>
  );
}
```

Each derived property is typed on the returned objects. Define them in the hook's `withProperties` option: if you call `.withProperties()` on the object set you pass to `useObjectSet` instead, the server still computes them but the returned objects are not typed with them.

### The builder

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pivotTo(link)` | A builder for the linked type | Follow a link. After a link to many objects, you can only `aggregate`. |
| `where(clause)` | The same builder, filtered | Narrow the objects before you select or aggregate. |
| `selectProperty(property)` | A definition | The value of one property. Available on the starting object and after links to one object. |
| `aggregate(specifier, opts?)` | A definition | A value computed over the objects. |

`aggregate` takes `"$count"` or a `"property:metric"` string:

| Metric | Property types | Value | `opts` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$count` | | `number` | |
| `sum`, `avg` | Numeric | `number \| undefined` | |
| `min`, `max` | Numeric, date, timestamp | Same as the property, or `undefined` | |
| `approximateDistinct`, `exactDistinct` | All | `number` | |
| `approximatePercentile` | Numeric | `number \| undefined` | `{ percentile: number }` |
| `collectList`, `collectSet` | Strings, numbers, dates, timestamps, booleans, geo, attachments | Array of the property's type, or `undefined` | `{ limit: number }` |

`sum`, `avg`, `min`, and `max` over no objects have no value, so render a fallback for them. `$count` is `0`.

Numeric definitions chain `add`, `subtract`, `multiply`, `divide`, `min`, `max`, `abs`, and `negate`, which take a number or another numeric definition. Date and timestamp definitions chain `min`, `max`, and `extractPart("DAYS" | "MONTHS" | "QUARTERS" | "YEARS")`.

```tsx
const { data } = useOsdkObjects(Employee, {
  withProperties: {
    seniorReports: (employee) =>
      employee
        .pivotTo("reports")
        .where({ jobTitle: { $startsWith: "Senior" } })
        .aggregate("$count"),
    reportPayroll: (employee) => employee.pivotTo("reports").aggregate("salary:sum"),
    salaryAfterRaise: (employee) => employee.selectProperty("salary").multiply(1.05),
    startYear: (employee) => employee.selectProperty("startDate").extractPart("YEARS"),
    topReportTitles: (employee) =>
      employee.pivotTo("reports").aggregate("jobTitle:collectSet", { limit: 5 }),
  },
});
```

### Filter on a derived property

`where` can reference derived properties defined in the same options. For TypeScript to infer them, annotate the builder parameter with `DerivedProperty.Builder` from `@osdk/client`:

```tsx title="src/ManagerList.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import type { DerivedProperty } from "@osdk/client";
import { useOsdkObjects } from "@osdk/react";

export function ManagerList() {
  const { data } = useOsdkObjects(Employee, {
    withProperties: {
      reportCount: (employee: DerivedProperty.Builder<Employee, false>) =>
        employee.pivotTo("reports").aggregate("$count"),
    },
    where: { reportCount: { $gt: 0 } },
  });

  return (
    <ul>
      {data?.map((manager) => (
        <li key={manager.$primaryKey}>
          {manager.fullName} ({manager.reportCount} reports)
        </li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

The `false` type argument says that the builder has not yet followed a link to many objects. `orderBy` accepts only the type's own properties, so you cannot sort by a derived property.

Queries with derived properties do not receive real-time updates. See [Stream real-time updates](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/objects.md#stream-real-time-updates).

## Reference

### `useObjectSet(objectSet, options?)`

`objectSet` is an `ObjectSet` or `undefined`. When it is `undefined`, the hook does not query.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `where` | `WhereClause<T>` | | Filter the set. Can reference properties defined in `withProperties`. |
| `withProperties` | `DerivedProperty.Clause` | | Properties computed on the server, typed on the results. |
| `union` | `ObjectSet<T>[]` | | Add the objects in these sets. |
| `intersect` | `ObjectSet<T>[]` | | Keep only objects that are also in these sets. |
| `subtract` | `ObjectSet<T>[]` | | Remove the objects in these sets. |
| `pivotTo` | Link name | | Follow a link. Prefer calling `pivotTo` on the object set, which types the results as the linked type. |
| `orderBy` | `{ [property]?: "asc" \| "desc" }` | | Sort order, in key order. |
| `pageSize` | `number` | Server default | Objects per request. |
| `autoFetchMore` | `boolean \| number` | | Load pages automatically: `true` for all, a number for at least that many. |
| `$select` | `PropertyKeys<T>[]` | Server default set | Properties to load. Does not narrow the returned type. |
| `streamUpdates` | `boolean` | `false` | Subscribe to live changes. Not with `pivotTo` or `withProperties`. |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | When `false`, no request is made and `data` is `undefined`. |
| `dedupeIntervalMs` | `number` | `2000` | Identical queries within this window share one request. |

| Return | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `Osdk.Instance<T>[] \| undefined` | Loaded objects, with derived properties. Keeps the previous result while a changed query loads. |
| `isLoading` | `boolean` | `true` until the current query has loaded or failed. |
| `error` | `Error \| undefined` | The last error, if the query failed. |
| `isOptimistic` | `boolean` | Whether the list includes unconfirmed optimistic changes. |
| `fetchMore` | `(() => Promise<void>) \| undefined` | Load the next page. `undefined` when there are no more pages. |
| `hasMore` | `boolean` | Whether more pages exist. |
| `totalCount` | `string \| undefined` | Total matching objects, when the server reports it. |
| `objectSet` | `ObjectSet<T> \| undefined` | The final object set after all options are applied. |
| `refetch` | `() => Promise<void>` | Invalidate the object type and refetch. |

### `useStableObjectSet(objectSet)`

Returns `objectSet`, or the instance returned on an earlier render if the definition is unchanged. Accepts and returns `ObjectSet | undefined`.

# Query objects

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/objects

> Load, filter, sort, paginate, and stream lists of objects with useOsdkObjects, and load a single object with useOsdkObject.

{/* cspell:ignore refetches geopoints geoshapes */}

`useOsdkObjects` loads a list of objects of one type, and `useOsdkObject` loads a single object. Both read from the shared cache that `OsdkProvider` sets up, so every component that shows the same object re-renders when it changes.

## List objects

Pass an object type from your generated SDK. The hook fetches the first page and returns it as `data`.

```tsx title="src/EmployeeList.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkObjects } from "@osdk/react";

export function EmployeeList() {
  const { data, isLoading, error, refetch } = useOsdkObjects(Employee);

  return (
    <div>
      {error && (
        <p role="alert">
          Could not load employees: {error.message}{" "}
          <button onClick={() => void refetch()}>Retry</button>
        </p>
      )}
      {isLoading && !data && <p>Loading employees…</p>}
      <ul>
        {data?.map((employee) => (
          <li key={employee.$primaryKey}>
            {employee.fullName}, {employee.jobTitle}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`data` is `undefined` until the first page arrives. After that, `isLoading` can be `true` while `data` still holds the previous result, for example while the hook revalidates after an action. Keep rendering `data` during those refreshes instead of replacing the list with a spinner. [Loading and errors](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/concepts/loading-and-errors.md) covers the pattern in depth.

`isOptimistic` is `true` when the order or membership of the list reflects an optimistic update that the server has not confirmed yet. It only describes the list of primary keys. To check whether one object's contents are optimistic, pass that object to [`useOsdkObject`](#load-one-object).

## Filter with `where`

`where` takes the same clause as `ObjectSet.where` in `@osdk/client`. A bare value on a property means equality:

```tsx
const { data } = useOsdkObjects(Employee, {
  where: { department: "Engineering" },
});
```

For anything else, give the property an object with one operator:

```tsx
const { data } = useOsdkObjects(Employee, {
  where: {
    department: { $in: ["Engineering", "Design"] },
    salary: { $gte: 100000 },
    jobTitle: { $isNull: false },
  },
});
```

Several properties in the same clause must all match. The operators each property accepts depend on its type:

| Operator | Property types | Matches |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$eq`, `$ne` | Strings, numbers, booleans, dates, timestamps | Equal to, or not equal to, the value. `{ department: "Sales" }` is shorthand for `$eq`. |
| `$in` | Strings, numbers, booleans, dates, timestamps | Any of the listed values. |
| `$isNull` | All | `true` for missing values, `false` for present ones. |
| `$gt`, `$gte`, `$lt`, `$lte` | Numbers, dates, timestamps, strings | Greater or less than the value. Dates and timestamps take ISO 8601 strings. |
| `$startsWith`, `$containsAnyTerm`, `$containsAllTerms`, `$containsAllTermsInOrder` | Strings | Text search. See [Search text](#search-text). |
| `$matchesRegex` | Strings | A regular expression. Beta. |
| `$contains` | Arrays | Arrays that contain the value. |
| `$within`, `$intersects` | Geopoints, geoshapes | A distance, bounding box, or polygon. |

You can also filter on `$primaryKey`, for example `{ $primaryKey: { $in: [101, 102] } }`, without knowing the name of the primary key property.

> [!WARNING]
> `$in` with an empty array matches every object. If the list comes from user input, set `enabled: false` (see [Fetch conditionally](#fetch-conditionally)) or leave the filter out when the list is empty.

### Combine conditions

Each property takes exactly one operator, so a range on one property needs `$and`:

```tsx
const { data } = useOsdkObjects(Employee, {
  where: {
    $and: [{ salary: { $gte: 80000 } }, { salary: { $lt: 120000 } }],
  },
});
```

`$or` matches any of its clauses, and `$not` negates one clause. They nest:

```tsx
const { data } = useOsdkObjects(Employee, {
  where: {
    $or: [
      { department: "Sales" },
      { $and: [{ department: "Engineering" }, { $not: { jobTitle: { $startsWith: "Intern" } } }] },
    ],
  },
});
```

To intersect several independent filters, you can also pass `intersectWith`, an array of `{ where }` clauses. The result contains only objects that match `where` and every entry.

```tsx
const { data } = useOsdkObjects(Employee, {
  where: { department: "Engineering" },
  intersectWith: [{ where: { salary: { $gte: 100000 } } }, { where: { startDate: { $lt: "2020-01-01" } } }],
});
```

### Search text

String properties support four search operators. `$containsAnyTerm` and `$containsAllTerms` also accept `{ term, fuzzySearch: true }` to tolerate small typos. All four accept `{ term, phoneticSearch: true }`, which matches similarly pronounced terms, such as `Jon` and `John`, on properties with phonetic search enabled. A filter cannot set both `fuzzySearch` and `phoneticSearch`; combine the two with `$or`.

| Operator | Matches | Fuzzy | Phonetic | Example value | Matches `"Senior Software Engineer"` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$startsWith` | Values that begin with the prefix | No | Yes | `"Senior"` | Yes |
| `$containsAnyTerm` | Values that contain any of the space-separated terms | Yes | Yes | `"designer engineer"` | Yes |
| `$containsAllTerms` | Values that contain every term, in any order | Yes | Yes | `"engineer senior"` | Yes |
| `$containsAllTermsInOrder` | Values that contain every term, in this order | No | Yes | `"engineer senior"` | No |

A search box that waits for two characters before it queries:

```tsx title="src/EmployeeSearch.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkObjects } from "@osdk/react";
import { useState } from "react";

export function EmployeeSearch() {
  const [query, setQuery] = useState("");

  const { data, isLoading } = useOsdkObjects(Employee, {
    where: { fullName: { $containsAnyTerm: { term: query, fuzzySearch: true } } },
    $select: ["fullName", "jobTitle"],
    pageSize: 20,
    enabled: query.length >= 2,
  });

  return (
    <div>
      <input
        type="search"
        placeholder="Search employees"
        value={query}
        onChange={(e) => setQuery(e.target.value)}
      />
      {isLoading && <p>Searching…</p>}
      <ul>
        {data?.map((employee) => (
          <li key={employee.$primaryKey}>{employee.fullName}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </div>
  );
}
```

To send fewer requests while the user types, debounce the state update with `useDebouncedCallback` from `@osdk/react`.

### Load specific objects by RID

`rids` starts from a fixed set of objects instead of every object of the type. `where` and `orderBy` then filter and sort that set. Objects loaded this way have `$rid` set.

```tsx
const { data } = useOsdkObjects(Employee, {
  rids: ["ri.phonograph2-objects.main.object.1", "ri.phonograph2-objects.main.object.2"],
  where: { department: "Engineering" },
});
```

## Sort with `orderBy`

`orderBy` maps property names to `"asc"` or `"desc"`. List several properties to break ties, in priority order:

```tsx
const { data } = useOsdkObjects(Employee, {
  orderBy: { department: "asc", salary: "desc" },
});
```

`orderBy` accepts the object type's own properties. To sort by a value computed from linked objects, see [derived properties](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/object-sets.md#add-derived-properties).

## Select properties

Without `$select`, the server returns its default property set for each object. Pass `$select` with only the properties the component reads; the primary key is always included.

```tsx
const { data } = useOsdkObjects(Employee, {
  $select: ["fullName", "jobTitle"],
});
```

Loading unused properties costs bandwidth and slows down the query, and filtering them out after the fact does not get that cost back. Unlike `fetchPage` in `@osdk/client`, `useOsdkObjects` does not narrow the returned type to the selected properties. Reading a property you did not select still type-checks but is `undefined` at runtime, so keep `$select` in sync with what you render.

### Query an interface

When you pass an interface instead of an object type, each object only exposes the interface's properties. Two options change that:

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `$includeAllBaseObjectProperties: true` | The server also returns every property of the implementing object type. |
| `resolveToObjectType: true` | The hook returns instances of the implementing object type instead of interface views, so properties such as `$title` and properties that are not on the interface are available. Only allowed for interfaces. |

```tsx
import { Worker } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkObjects } from "@osdk/react";

export function WorkerList() {
  const { data } = useOsdkObjects(Worker, {
    $includeAllBaseObjectProperties: true,
    resolveToObjectType: true,
  });

  return (
    <ul>
      {data?.map((worker) => (
        <li key={worker.$primaryKey}>
          {worker.name} ({worker.$objectType})
        </li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

## Paginate

`pageSize` sets how many objects each request loads. It is not a limit on the total. Call `fetchMore` to load the next page; it is `undefined` once there are no more pages, and `hasMore` is `false`.

```tsx title="src/EmployeeDirectory.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkObjects } from "@osdk/react";

export function EmployeeDirectory() {
  const { data, isLoading, fetchMore, totalCount } = useOsdkObjects(Employee, {
    orderBy: { fullName: "asc" },
    pageSize: 50,
  });

  return (
    <div>
      {totalCount != null && <p>{Number(totalCount).toLocaleString()} employees</p>}
      <ul>
        {data?.map((employee) => (
          <li key={employee.$primaryKey}>{employee.fullName}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      {fetchMore && (
        <button onClick={() => void fetchMore()} disabled={isLoading}>
          {isLoading ? "Loading…" : "Load more"}
        </button>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

`totalCount` is a string because the count can exceed `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`. It is `undefined` when the server does not report it.

To load more pages without a button, set `autoFetchMore`:

| Value | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `undefined` (default) | Load the first page only. |
| A number, such as `200` | Keep loading pages until the list has at least that many objects or runs out. |
| `true` | Load every page. |

```tsx
const { data } = useOsdkObjects(Employee, {
  pageSize: 50,
  autoFetchMore: 200,
});
```

> [!WARNING]
> `autoFetchMore: true` on a large object type can take a long time and hold every object in memory. Prefer a number, or `fetchMore` on demand. For counts, sums, and group-bys, use [`useOsdkAggregation`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/aggregations.md) instead of loading objects.

> [!NOTE]
> **Paging consistency**
>
> Pages load without a snapshot. If objects are added, removed, or edited between page requests, later pages can repeat or skip objects. When you need every object from one consistent view, call `asyncIter()` on the client from [`useOsdkClient`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/client.md) in an event handler or effect.

## Stream real-time updates

Set `streamUpdates: true` to subscribe to changes over a WebSocket. The list then updates when matching objects are created, edited so that they start or stop matching `where`, or deleted, without waiting for a refetch.

```tsx title="src/LiveHiresList.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkObjects } from "@osdk/react";

export function LiveHiresList() {
  const { data } = useOsdkObjects(Employee, {
    where: { startDate: { $gte: "2026-01-01" } },
    orderBy: { startDate: "desc" },
    streamUpdates: true,
  });

  return (
    <ul>
      {data?.map((employee) => (
        <li key={employee.$primaryKey}>
          {employee.fullName} started {employee.startDate}
        </li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

> [!WARNING]
> **Streaming does not work with pivotTo or withProperties**
>
> The server has no WebSocket subscriptions for link traversals or derived properties. TypeScript rejects `streamUpdates` together with `pivotTo`. With `withProperties`, the code compiles, but the hook ignores `streamUpdates` and logs a warning in development. Both kinds of query still load data normally; they refresh when the cache is invalidated instead of in real time. The same applies to `useObjectSet`.

## Fetch conditionally

Hooks cannot be called inside a condition, so use `enabled` instead. While `enabled` is `false`, the hook makes no request and returns `data: undefined` and `isLoading: false`. Setting it back to `true` starts the query.

```tsx title="src/DepartmentRoster.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkObjects } from "@osdk/react";

export function DepartmentRoster({ department }: { department: string | undefined }) {
  const { data, isLoading } = useOsdkObjects(Employee, {
    where: { department: department ?? "" },
    enabled: department != null,
  });

  if (department == null) {
    return <p>Pick a department.</p>;
  }

  return (
    <ul>
      {isLoading && !data && <li>Loading…</li>}
      {data?.map((employee) => (
        <li key={employee.$primaryKey}>{employee.fullName}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

## Load one object

`useOsdkObject` takes an object type and a primary key, and returns `object`:

```tsx title="src/EmployeeCard.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkObject } from "@osdk/react";

export function EmployeeCard({ employeeId }: { employeeId: number }) {
  const { object: employee, isLoading, error } = useOsdkObject(Employee, employeeId);

  return (
    <section>
      {isLoading && !employee && <p>Loading…</p>}
      {error && <p role="alert">{error.message}</p>}
      {employee && (
        <>
          <h2>{employee.fullName}</h2>
          <p>
            {employee.jobTitle}, {employee.department}
          </p>
        </>
      )}
    </section>
  );
}
```

The third argument is either a boolean that enables or disables the query, or an options object:

```tsx
const disabled = useOsdkObject(Employee, employeeId, false);

const withOptions = useOsdkObject(Employee, employeeId, {
  $select: ["fullName", "jobTitle"],
  $loadPropertySecurityMetadata: true,
  enabled: employeeId > 0,
});
```

### Track an instance you already have

When a component receives an object from a list, pass the instance itself. The hook does not fetch; it subscribes to the cached copy, so the component re-renders when an action or optimistic update changes that object, and `isOptimistic` tells you whether the change is confirmed.

```tsx title="src/EmployeeRow.tsx"
import type { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkObject } from "@osdk/react";

export function EmployeeRow({ employee }: { employee: Employee.OsdkInstance }) {
  const { object, isOptimistic } = useOsdkObject(employee);
  const current = object ?? employee;

  return (
    <li style={{ opacity: isOptimistic ? 0.6 : 1 }}>
      {current.fullName}, {current.jobTitle}
    </li>
  );
}
```

The instance form takes an optional boolean as its second argument to disable it.

## Refresh data

`refetch` on the `useOsdkObjects` result invalidates the whole object type: every cached object, list, and link query of that type refetches, not only this list. Actions already invalidate the types they modify, so you only need `refetch` for changes made outside the app.

To refresh one object, invalidate it with the observable client:

```tsx
import type { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useObservableClient } from "@osdk/react";

export function RefreshButton({ employee }: { employee: Employee.OsdkInstance }) {
  const observableClient = useObservableClient();

  return <button onClick={() => void observableClient.invalidateObjects(employee)}>Refresh</button>;
}
```

`useOsdkObject` also returns a `forceUpdate` function, but it is not implemented and throws when called. [Cache invalidation](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/cache-invalidation.md) covers the other invalidation methods.

## Reference

### `useOsdkObjects(type, options?)`

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `where` | `WhereClause<T>` | | Filter clause. Can reference properties defined in `withProperties`. |
| `orderBy` | `{ [property]?: "asc" \| "desc" }` | | Sort order, in key order. |
| `pageSize` | `number` | Server default | Objects per request. |
| `autoFetchMore` | `boolean \| number` | | Load pages automatically: `true` for all, a number for at least that many. |
| `$select` | `PropertyKeys<T>[]` | Server default set | Properties to load. Does not narrow the returned type. |
| `rids` | `readonly string[]` | | Start from these objects instead of the whole type. Adds `$rid` to results. |
| `intersectWith` | `Array<{ where: WhereClause<T> }>` | | Additional filters that every result must also match. |
| `pivotTo` | Link name | | Return the objects linked from the matching objects instead. See [Follow links](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/links.md#pivot-with-pivotto). |
| `withProperties` | `DerivedProperty.Clause` | | Properties computed on the server. See [derived properties](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/object-sets.md#add-derived-properties). |
| `streamUpdates` | `boolean` | `false` | Subscribe to live changes. Not with `pivotTo` or `withProperties`. |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | When `false`, no request is made and `data` is `undefined`. |
| `dedupeIntervalMs` | `number` | `2000` | Two identical queries within this window share one request. |
| `$loadPropertySecurityMetadata` | `boolean` | `false` | Populate `$propertySecurities` on each object with per-property marking requirements. |
| `$includeAllBaseObjectProperties` | `boolean` | `false` | Interfaces only: also load the implementing type's properties. |
| `resolveToObjectType` | `boolean` | `false` | Interfaces only: return implementing object type instances. |

| Return | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `Osdk.Instance<T>[] \| undefined` | Loaded objects. `undefined` before the first page and while disabled. |
| `isLoading` | `boolean` | `true` while a request is in flight, including revalidation with `data` present. |
| `error` | `Error \| undefined` | The last error, if the query failed. |
| `isOptimistic` | `boolean` | Whether the list order or membership includes unconfirmed optimistic changes. |
| `fetchMore` | `(() => Promise<void>) \| undefined` | Load the next page. `undefined` when there are no more pages. |
| `hasMore` | `boolean` | Whether more pages exist. |
| `totalCount` | `string \| undefined` | Total matching objects, when the server reports it. |
| `objectSet` | `ObjectSet<T> \| undefined` | The object set the hook queried, after `where`, `intersectWith`, and `pivotTo`. Pass it to [`useOsdkAggregation`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/aggregations.md#aggregate-an-object-set) or [`useObjectSet`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/object-sets.md). |
| `refetch` | `() => Promise<void>` | Invalidate the object type and refetch. |

### `useOsdkObject`

| Signature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `useOsdkObject(type, primaryKey, enabled?)` | Load by primary key. |
| `useOsdkObject(type, primaryKey, options?)` | Load by primary key with options. |
| `useOsdkObject(instance, enabled?)` | Subscribe to an instance you already have. Reads the cache without fetching. |

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | When `false`, no request is made. |
| `$select` | `PropertyKeys<T>[]` | Server default set | Properties to load. |
| `$loadPropertySecurityMetadata` | `boolean` | `false` | Populate `$propertySecurities` with per-property marking requirements. |
| `$includeAllBaseObjectProperties` | `boolean` | `false` | Interfaces only: also load the implementing type's properties. |

| Return | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `object` | `Osdk.Instance<T> \| undefined` | The object. `undefined` while loading, while disabled, or if it was not found. |
| `isLoading` | `boolean` | `true` while a request is in flight. `false` once there is an error. |
| `error` | `Error \| undefined` | The last error, if the load failed. |
| `isOptimistic` | `boolean` | Whether the object includes unconfirmed optimistic changes. |
| `forceUpdate` | `() => void` | Not implemented; throws. Use `invalidateObjects` instead. |

# Optimistic updates

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/optimistic-updates

> Show an action's result before the server responds by layering optimistic edits on the cache, with automatic rollback when the action fails.

{/* cspell:ignore refetched refetches */}

An optimistic update shows the expected result of an action as soon as the user triggers it. You describe the edits, the cache shows them on top of the real data, and they are removed when the action finishes, whether it succeeds or fails.

## Add an optimistic update

Add `$optimisticUpdate` to the parameters you pass to `applyAction` from `useOsdkAction`. The callback receives a builder for the edits you expect:

```tsx title="src/DepartmentPicker.tsx"
import { Employee, modifyEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkAction, useOsdkObject } from "@osdk/react";

export function DepartmentPicker({ employee }: { employee: Employee.OsdkInstance }) {
  const { object, isOptimistic } = useOsdkObject(employee);
  const { applyAction, error } = useOsdkAction(modifyEmployee);
  const current = object ?? employee;

  async function moveTo(department: string) {
    try {
      await applyAction({
        employee,
        department,
        $optimisticUpdate: (update) => {
          update.updateObject(employee.$clone({ department }));
        },
      });
    } catch (e) {
      console.error("modifyEmployee failed", e);
    }
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <p>
        {current.fullName} works in {current.department}
        {isOptimistic && " (saving)"}
      </p>
      <button onClick={() => void moveTo("Platform")}>Move to Platform</button>
      {error && <p role="alert">The move failed and was undone.</p>}
    </div>
  );
}
```

`$optimisticUpdate` runs synchronously when you call `applyAction`, before the request is sent. The `$` prefix keeps it apart from the action's own parameters, and it is not sent to the server.

## Builder methods

Each method returns the builder, so you can chain calls.

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `updateObject(instance)` | Replaces a cached object with `instance`. Build it with `$clone`. |
| `createObject(type, primaryKey, properties)` | Adds a new object of `type` to the cache. `properties` lists every property of the type; pass `undefined` for values you do not know yet. |
| `deleteObject(instance)` | Removes the object from the cache and from every list that contains it. |

OSDK objects are immutable. `$clone` returns a copy with the properties you pass changed:

```ts
const moved = employee.$clone({ department: "Platform" });
```

### Create an object

The server assigns the real primary key, so give the optimistic object a temporary one that cannot collide with a real object. This example uses `applyAction` from `useOsdkAction(createOffice)`, for an `Office` type whose properties are `officeId`, `name`, and `city`:

```ts
await applyAction({
  name,
  city,
  $optimisticUpdate: (update) => {
    const temporaryId = `tmp-${crypto.randomUUID()}`;
    update.createObject(Office, temporaryId, {
      officeId: temporaryId,
      name,
      city,
    });
  },
});
```

Lists of that type add the new object if it matches their `where` clause. When the action finishes, the temporary object goes away and the real one loads in its place.

### Edit several objects

One callback can describe every edit the action makes. For an action that moves a lead and their reports to a new department:

```ts
$optimisticUpdate: (update) => {
  update
    .updateObject(lead.$clone({ department }))
    .updateObject(report.$clone({ department }));
},
```

## What happens when the action runs

### The optimistic layer is applied

Your edits go into a separate layer on top of the cached server data. Every component that reads an edited object, or a list that contains one, re-renders with the edits.
### The action is sent

The request goes to Foundry while the layer is shown. `isPending` from `useOsdkAction` is `true`.
### The layer is removed

If the action succeeds, the cache first refetches every object the server reports as edited, then removes the layer, so the UI moves from your edits to the server's values without showing the old ones in between.

If the action fails, the layer is removed straight away and the UI returns to the previous server values. `applyAction` rejects and `error` is set. You do not undo anything yourself.

An optimistic edit can add an object to a list or remove a deleted one, but it does not remove an object that stops matching a list's `where` clause. That list catches up when the server responds.

Because the layer is always removed, write the update you expect the server to make. If the server's result differs, for example a property computed on the server, the server's value replaces yours when the layer goes.

## Show that a change is pending

Hooks that read from the cache report whether what they show includes optimistic edits:

| Hook | Field | `true` when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `useOsdkObject` | `isOptimistic` | The object comes from an optimistic layer. |
| `useOsdkObjects`, `useObjectSet`, `useLinks` | `isOptimistic` | The membership or order of the list comes from an optimistic layer. An edit that only changes properties of an object already in the list does not set it; check those objects with `useOsdkObject`. |

Use `isOptimistic` for a subtle "saving" cue, and `isPending` from `useOsdkAction` to disable controls.

## Simulate latency in development

Against a fast backend, the optimistic state can disappear before you see it. In development builds, the cache waits 1000 ms after the server responds before removing the layer, so you can check that the optimistic state renders correctly. The first time it waits, it logs a message to the console.

The delay applies only to single `applyAction` calls that pass `$optimisticUpdate`. Batches and actions without an optimistic update are not delayed, and production builds never delay. Change it with the `devMode` prop on `OsdkProvider`:

```tsx title="src/main.tsx"
import { OsdkProvider } from "@osdk/react";
import { client } from "./client";
import { App } from "./App";

export function Root() {
  return (
    <OsdkProvider client={client} devMode={{ actionDelayMs: 200 }}>
      <App />
    </OsdkProvider>
  );
}
```

Set `actionDelayMs: 0` to turn the delay off. `devMode` also accepts `logLevel` and `debug` for logging cache internals; see [Invalidate the cache](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/cache-invalidation.md#debug-the-cache).

# Users and markings

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/platform-apis

> Load Foundry users, markings, and CBAC classification banners in React with the hooks in @osdk/react/platform-apis.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Foundry REST APIs](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/api/v2/general/overview/introduction)

{/* cspell:ignore CBAC cbac refetch refetches */}

The hooks in `@osdk/react/platform-apis` call Foundry platform APIs for users and markings with the client from `OsdkProvider`. Use them to show who is signed in, look up other users, list markings, and render classification banners.

## Install the platform packages

The hooks depend on two optional peer packages. Install them before importing from `@osdk/react/platform-apis`:

```npm
npm install @osdk/foundry.admin @osdk/foundry.core
```

Without them, the bundler fails with `Rollup failed to resolve import "@osdk/foundry.admin"` or a similar error. The rest of `@osdk/react` works without these packages.

Every hook needs an `OsdkProvider` above it. The signed-in user's token must allow the platform API you call; a missing permission comes back as an `error`.

## Show the signed-in user

`useCurrentFoundryUser` loads the user the client's token belongs to:

```tsx title="src/CurrentUserBadge.tsx"
import { useCurrentFoundryUser } from "@osdk/react/platform-apis";

export function CurrentUserBadge() {
  const { currentUser, isLoading, error } = useCurrentFoundryUser();

  return (
    <span>
      {currentUser && `Signed in as ${currentUser.givenName ?? currentUser.username}`}
      {isLoading && !error && "Loading…"}
      {error && "Could not load your profile"}
    </span>
  );
}
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | When `false`, no request is made. |

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `currentUser` | `User \| undefined` | The user, with `id`, `username`, `givenName`, `familyName`, `email`, `realm`, `organization`, `status`, and `attributes`. |
| `isLoading` | `boolean` | `true` while the request runs. |
| `error` | `Error \| undefined` | Set when the request failed. |
| `refetch` | `() => void` | Requests the user again. |

## Look up a user

`useFoundryUser` takes the user ID as its first argument and options second:

```tsx title="src/UserName.tsx"
import { useFoundryUser } from "@osdk/react/platform-apis";

export function UserName({ userId }: { userId: string }) {
  const { user, error } = useFoundryUser(userId);
  const fullName = [user?.givenName, user?.familyName].filter(Boolean).join(" ");

  return (
    <span title={error?.message}>
      {error ? "Unknown user" : user ? fullName || user.username : "…"}
    </span>
  );
}
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | When `false`, no request is made. |
| `status` | `"ACTIVE" \| "DELETED"` | `"ACTIVE"` | Status of the user to look up. Pass `"DELETED"` to resolve users who have been removed. |

The result has `user`, `isLoading`, `error`, and `refetch`. A new `userId` triggers a new request.

## List users

`useFoundryUsersList` returns one page of users. Pass the previous page's `nextPageToken` as `pageToken` to load the next one:

```tsx title="src/UserDirectory.tsx"
import { useFoundryUsersList } from "@osdk/react/platform-apis";
import { useState } from "react";

export function UserDirectory() {
  const [pageToken, setPageToken] = useState<string | undefined>();
  const { users, nextPageToken, isLoading, error } = useFoundryUsersList({
    pageSize: 50,
    pageToken,
  });

  return (
    <div>
      {error && <p role="alert">Could not load users.</p>}
      {isLoading && !error && <p>Loading…</p>}
      <ul>
        {users?.map((user) => (
          <li key={user.id}>{user.username}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      <button
        disabled={nextPageToken == null || isLoading}
        onClick={() => setPageToken(nextPageToken)}
      >
        Next page
      </button>
    </div>
  );
}
```
