# useObservableClient

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/reference/react/use-observable-client

> Return the ObservableClient that backs the shared cache of the nearest OsdkProvider.

```ts
import { useObservableClient } from "@osdk/react";

function useObservableClient(): ObservableClient;
```

Returns the `ObservableClient` that `OsdkProvider` builds from its `client`. Use it to invalidate cached data after changes that do not go through an action, such as an update from an external system or a background job.

## Returns

`ObservableClient` from `@osdk/client/observable`. The methods you are most likely to need:

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `invalidateObjects(objects)` | Reloads one object instance or an array of them. Interface instances refetch their backing object. |
| `invalidateObjectType(type)` | Reloads every cached query for an object type, by definition or API name. |
| `invalidateFunction(queryDef, params?)` | Reloads a function's cached result for `params`, or every cached call when `params` is omitted. |
| `invalidateAll()` | Reloads everything in the cache. |

## Example

```tsx title="src/RefreshButton.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useObservableClient } from "@osdk/react";

export function RefreshButton({ employee }: { employee: Employee.OsdkInstance }) {
  const observableClient = useObservableClient();

  return (
    <button onClick={() => void observableClient.invalidateObjects(employee)}>
      Refresh
    </button>
  );
}
```

## See also

- [Cache invalidation](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/cache-invalidation.md)

# useOsdkAction

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/reference/react/use-osdk-action

> Apply or validate an action from a component, with pending state, errors, and optional optimistic updates.

```ts
import { useOsdkAction } from "@osdk/react";

function useOsdkAction<Q extends ActionDefinition<any>>(
  actionDef: Q,
): UseOsdkActionResult<Q>;
```

Returns functions that apply or validate `actionDef` through the shared cache. After an action succeeds, cached objects and lists that it changed are refreshed.

## Returns

The result type has little JSDoc, so this table is written by hand.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `applyAction` | `(args: ApplyActionParams<Q> \| ApplyActionParams<Q>[]) => Promise<ActionEditResponse \| undefined>` | Applies the action. Pass an array to apply a batch. Rethrows on failure after setting `error`. |
| `validateAction` | `(args) => Promise<ActionValidationResponse \| undefined>` | Validates the parameters without applying the action. A new call cancels the previous one, and the cancelled call resolves to `undefined`. Resolves to `undefined` without validating while `applyAction` is pending. |
| `data` | `ActionEditResponse \| undefined` | The response from the last successful `applyAction`. |
| `error` | `{ actionValidation?: ActionValidationError; unknown?: unknown } \| undefined` | The last failure. `actionValidation` is set when the server rejected the parameters; `unknown` holds any other error. Cleared when the next call starts. |
| `isPending` | `boolean` | `true` while `applyAction` is running. |
| `isValidating` | `boolean` | `true` while `validateAction` is running. |
| `validationResult` | `ActionValidationResponse \| undefined` | The response from the last completed `validateAction`. |

### `applyAction` arguments

`ApplyActionParams<Q>` is the action's parameters plus:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$optimisticUpdate` | `(ctx: OptimisticBuilder) => void` | Writes temporary changes to the cache that are rolled back when the action settles. In a batch, every entry's update runs. |

## Example

```tsx title="src/PromoteButton.tsx"
import { Employee, modifyEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkAction } from "@osdk/react";

export function PromoteButton({ employee }: { employee: Employee.OsdkInstance }) {
  const { applyAction, isPending, error } = useOsdkAction(modifyEmployee);

  async function promote() {
    try {
      await applyAction({
        employee,
        jobTitle: "Senior Engineer",
        $optimisticUpdate: (ctx) => {
          ctx.updateObject(employee.$clone({ jobTitle: "Senior Engineer" }));
        },
      });
    } catch {
      // The hook result exposes the failure as error.
    }
  }

  return (
    <>
      <button disabled={isPending} onClick={() => void promote()}>
        Promote
      </button>
      {error?.actionValidation && <p role="alert">Invalid parameters.</p>}
    </>
  );
}
```

## See also

- [Actions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/actions.md)
- [Optimistic updates](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/optimistic-updates.md)
- [Errors](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/reference/client/errors.md)

# useOsdkAggregation

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/reference/react/use-osdk-aggregation

> Run a server-side aggregation, such as counts or averages grouped by a property, and keep the result cached.

```ts
import { useOsdkAggregation } from "@osdk/react";

function useOsdkAggregation<
  Q extends ObjectOrInterfaceDefinition,
  const A extends AggregateOpts<Q>,
  RDPs extends Record<string, SimplePropertyDef> = {},
>(
  type: Q,
  options: UseOsdkAggregationOptions<Q, A, RDPs>,
): UseOsdkAggregationResult<Q, A>;

function useOsdkAggregation<
  Q extends ObjectTypeDefinition,
  const A extends AggregateOpts<Q>,
  RDPs extends Record<string, SimplePropertyDef> = {},
>(
  type: Q,
  options: UseOsdkAggregationOptionsWithObjectSet<Q, A, RDPs>,
): UseOsdkAggregationResult<Q, A>;
```

Aggregates every object of `type` that matches `where`, or the objects in `objectSet` when you pass one. `aggregate` takes the same `$select` and `$groupBy` clauses as `ObjectSet.aggregate`.

## Options

### UseOsdkAggregationOptions

| Prop                | Type                                                          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `where?`            | `WhereClause<T, RDPs>`                                        | Standard OSDK Where clause to filter objects before aggregation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `withProperties?`   | `{ [K in keyof RDPs]: DerivedProperty.Creator<T, RDPs[K]>; }` | Define derived properties (RDPs) to be computed server-side. The derived properties can be used in the where clause and aggregation groupBy/select.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `intersectWith?`    | `{ where: WhereClause<T, RDPs>; }[]`                          | Intersect the main query with additional filtered object sets. Each entry creates a separate object set with its own where clause, and the final result is the intersection of all sets.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `aggregate`         | `A`                                                           | Aggregation options including `$groupBy` and `$select`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `dedupeIntervalMs?` | `number`                                                      | The number of milliseconds to wait after the last observed aggregation change. Two uses of `useOsdkAggregation` with the same parameters will only trigger one network request if the second is within `dedupeIntervalMs`.                                                                                                                                               |
| `enabled?`          | `boolean`                                                     | Enable or disable the aggregation. When `false`, the hook does not subscribe or fetch from the server and reports `data: undefined`, `isLoading: false`, and `error: undefined`. `refetch()` is also a no-op while disabled, so it will not invalidate the object type or trigger network requests. Setting it back to `true` re-subscribes and fetches. Default: `true` |

The second overload (`UseOsdkAggregationOptionsWithObjectSet`) adds a required `objectSet: ObjectSet<Q>` to aggregate a pivoted, filtered, or composed set. It accepts object types only, not interfaces.

## Returns

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `AggregationsResults<Q, A> \| undefined` | The aggregation result. An array of groups when `$groupBy` is set, otherwise one object of metrics. |
| `isLoading` | `boolean` | `true` while enabled and the result has not loaded. |
| `error` | `Error \| undefined` | The error from the last run, if any. |
| `refetch` | `() => Promise<void>` | Invalidates cached data for `type` and reruns the aggregation. No-op while disabled. |

## Example

```tsx title="src/HeadcountByDepartment.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkAggregation } from "@osdk/react";

export function HeadcountByDepartment() {
  const { data, isLoading, error } = useOsdkAggregation(Employee, {
    aggregate: {
      $select: { $count: "unordered", "salary:avg": "unordered" },
      $groupBy: { department: "exact" },
    },
  });

  return (
    <table aria-busy={isLoading}>
      <tbody>
        {error && (
          <tr>
            <td role="alert">{error.message}</td>
          </tr>
        )}
        {data?.map((group) => (
          <tr key={group.$group.department}>
            <td>{group.$group.department}</td>
            <td>{group.$count}</td>
            <td>{group.salary.avg}</td>
          </tr>
        ))}
      </tbody>
    </table>
  );
}
```

## See also

- [Aggregations](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/aggregations.md)
- [Aggregations in `@osdk/client`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/aggregations.md)

# useOsdkClient

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/reference/react/use-osdk-client

> Return the OSDK Client passed to the nearest OsdkProvider.

```ts
import { useOsdkClient } from "@osdk/react";

function useOsdkClient(): Client;
```

Returns the `client` prop of the surrounding `OsdkProvider`. Use it to build object sets for `useObjectSet` or to call the client directly, for example in an event handler. Calls made directly on the client bypass the shared cache.

## Returns

`Client`: the client from `createClient` in `@osdk/client`.

## Example

```tsx title="src/ExportButton.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkClient } from "@osdk/react";

export function ExportButton() {
  const client = useOsdkClient();

  async function exportNames() {
    const names: string[] = [];
    for await (const employee of client(Employee).asyncIter({ $select: ["fullName"] })) {
      names.push(employee.fullName ?? "");
    }
    console.log(names.join("\n"));
  }

  return <button onClick={() => void exportNames().catch(console.error)}>Export</button>;
}
```

## See also

- [Create a client](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/client.md)
- [createClient](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/reference/client/create-client.md)

# useOsdkFunction

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/reference/react/use-osdk-function

> Execute a Foundry function and cache its result, refetching when the objects it depends on change.

```ts
import { useOsdkFunction } from "@osdk/react";

function useOsdkFunction<Q extends QueryDefinition<unknown>>(
  queryDef: Q,
  options?: UseOsdkFunctionOptions<Q>,
): UseOsdkFunctionResult<Q>;
```

Runs the function when the component mounts and again when `params` change. Calls with the same function and `params` share one cached result. Use `dependsOn` or `dependsOnObjects` to refetch after actions change related objects.

## Options

### UseOsdkFunctionOptions

| Prop                | Type                                                                                                                                          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `params?`           | `(CompileTimeMetadata<Q>["parameters"] extends Record<string, never> ? undefined : QueryParameterType<CompileTimeMetadata<Q>["parameters"]>)` | Parameters to pass to the function. Must include all required parameters; optional parameters can be omitted.                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `dependsOn?`        | `(string \| ObjectTypeDefinition)[]`                                                                                                          | Object types this function depends on. When actions modify objects of these types, the function will automatically refetch.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `dependsOnObjects?` | `(ObjectSet<ObjectTypeDefinition, never> \| Osdk.Instance<ObjectTypeDefinition, never, any, {}>)[]`                                           | Specific object instances or ObjectSets this function depends on. When any of these specific objects change, the function will refetch. More fine-grained than dependsOn for precise invalidation control. For ObjectSets, the object type is extracted asynchronously and changes to any object of that type will trigger a refetch. |
| `dedupeIntervalMs?` | `number`                                                                                                                                      | The number of milliseconds to dedupe identical function calls. Two calls with the same function and params will share results if the second call is within this interval of the first. Default: `2000`                                                                                                                                |
| `enabled?`          | `boolean`                                                                                                                                     | Whether to enable the query. When false, the query will not execute. Useful for: - Dependent queries that need to wait for other data - Conditional queries based on component state Default: `true`                                                                                                                                  |

## Returns

### UseOsdkFunctionResult

| Prop          | Type                                                                                                            | Description                                                                    |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `data`        | `(CompileTimeMetadata<Q>["signature"] extends (...args: never[]) => infer R ? Awaited<R> : never) \| undefined` | The function result, or undefined if not yet loaded or on error.               |
| `isLoading`   | `boolean`                                                                                                       | True while the function is executing.                                          |
| `error`       | `Error \| undefined`                                                                                            | Error if the function execution failed.                                        |
| `lastUpdated` | `number`                                                                                                        | Timestamp (ms since epoch) of when the result was last fetched.                |
| `refetch`     | `() => Promise<void>`                                                                                           | Manually refetch the function. Useful for "pull to refresh" or retry patterns. |

`isLoading` is `true` only while a request is in flight. On the first render, before the hook subscribes, and while it is disabled, `isLoading` is `false` and `data` is `undefined`, so check both.

## Example

```tsx title="src/EmployeeReport.tsx"
import { Employee, getEmployeeReport } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkFunction } from "@osdk/react";

export function EmployeeReport({ employee }: { employee: Employee.OsdkInstance }) {
  const { data, isLoading, error, refetch } = useOsdkFunction(getEmployeeReport, {
    params: { employeeId: employee.$primaryKey },
    dependsOnObjects: [employee],
  });

  return (
    <section aria-busy={isLoading}>
      {error && <p role="alert">{error.message}</p>}
      <p>{data}</p>
      <button onClick={() => void refetch()}>Refresh</button>
    </section>
  );
}
```

## See also

- [Functions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/functions.md)
- [useOsdkFunctions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/reference/react/use-osdk-functions.md)

# useOsdkFunctions

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/reference/react/use-osdk-functions

> Execute several Foundry functions from one hook and get their results in input order.

```ts
import { useOsdkFunctions } from "@osdk/react";

function useOsdkFunctions(props: UseOsdkFunctionsProps): UseOsdkFunctionsResult;

type UseOsdkFunctionsResult = Array<UseOsdkFunctionResult<QueryDefinition<unknown>>>;
```

Use it when the number of function calls varies at runtime, which rules out calling `useOsdkFunction` in a loop. Each query shares the cache with `useOsdkFunction`, so identical calls elsewhere do not hit the network twice.

## Props

### UseOsdkFunctionsProps

| Prop             | Type                                              | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `queries`        | `FunctionQueryParams<QueryDefinition<unknown>>[]` | Array of query configurations to execute                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `enabled?`       | `boolean`                                         | Whether to enable all queries. When false, no queries will execute. Individual query enabled states are also respected. Default: `true`                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `maxConcurrent?` | `number`                                          | Maximum number of queries to execute concurrently. When set, queries are subscribed in batches — the next query starts only after a running one completes (status "loaded" or "error"). Useful for large payloads that may exceed server time limits. Default: `undefined (all queries run in parallel)` |

### `FunctionQueryParams`

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `queryDefinition` | `Q` | The function from your generated SDK. |
| `options` | `UseOsdkFunctionOptions<Q>` | The same options as [`useOsdkFunction`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/reference/react/use-osdk-function.md): `params`, `dependsOn`, `dependsOnObjects`, `dedupeIntervalMs`, and `enabled`. |

## Returns

An array with one [`UseOsdkFunctionResult`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/reference/react/use-osdk-function.md#returns) per query, in the order of `queries`.

`queries` is typed with `QueryDefinition<unknown>`, so an entry with typed `params` does not type-check as written, and each result's `data` loses the function's return type. Cast each entry to `UseOsdkFunctionsProps["queries"][number]`, as the example does, and narrow `data` where you read it.

## Example

```tsx title="src/DepartmentHeadcounts.tsx"
import { getEmployeeMetrics } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkFunctions, type UseOsdkFunctionsProps } from "@osdk/react";

type FunctionCall = UseOsdkFunctionsProps["queries"][number];

export function DepartmentHeadcounts({ departments }: { departments: string[] }) {
  const results = useOsdkFunctions({
    queries: departments.map(
      (department) =>
        ({
          queryDefinition: getEmployeeMetrics,
          options: { params: { department } },
        }) as unknown as FunctionCall,
    ),
    maxConcurrent: 4,
  });

  return (
    <ul>
      {departments.map((department, i) => (
        <li key={department}>
          {department}: {results[i].isLoading ? "…" : JSON.stringify(results[i].data)}
        </li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

## See also

- [Functions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/functions.md)

# useOsdkMetadata

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/reference/react/use-osdk-metadata

> Fetch the runtime metadata of an object type, interface, or action, such as display names and property descriptions.

```ts
import { useOsdkMetadata } from "@osdk/react";

function useOsdkMetadata<T extends ObjectOrInterfaceDefinition | ActionDefinition<any>>(
  type: T,
): UseOsdkMetadataResult<T>;
```

Calls `client.fetchMetadata(type)` and returns the result. The metadata type follows the definition you pass: `ObjectMetadata` for an object type, `InterfaceMetadata` for an interface, and `ActionMetadata` for an action. The result is held in component state, not in the shared cache, so each component that calls the hook fetches once.

## Returns

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `true` until the request settles. |
| `metadata` | `ObjectMetadata \| InterfaceMetadata \| ActionMetadata \| undefined` | The metadata, once loaded. |
| `error` | `string \| undefined` | The error message if the request failed. |

## Example

```tsx title="src/EmployeeHeading.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkMetadata } from "@osdk/react";

export function EmployeeHeading() {
  const { metadata, loading, error } = useOsdkMetadata(Employee);

  return (
    <header aria-busy={loading}>
      {error && <p role="alert">{error}</p>}
      <h1>{metadata?.pluralDisplayName ?? "Employees"}</h1>
      <p>{metadata?.description}</p>
    </header>
  );
}
```

## See also

- [Load objects](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/objects.md)

# useOsdkObject

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/reference/react/use-osdk-object

> Load one object by primary key, or observe an object instance you already have, from the shared cache.

```ts
import { useOsdkObject } from "@osdk/react";

function useOsdkObject<Q extends ObjectOrInterfaceDefinition>(
  type: Q,
  primaryKey: PrimaryKeyType<Q>,
  options?: UseOsdkObjectOptions<Q>,
): UseOsdkObjectResult<Q>;

function useOsdkObject<Q extends ObjectOrInterfaceDefinition>(
  type: Q,
  primaryKey: PrimaryKeyType<Q>,
  enabled?: boolean,
): UseOsdkObjectResult<Q>;

function useOsdkObject<Q extends ObjectOrInterfaceDefinition>(
  obj: Osdk.Instance<Q>,
  enabled?: boolean,
): UseOsdkObjectResult<Q>;
```

Pass a type and primary key to fetch the object, or pass an `Osdk.Instance` to observe it in the cache without a network request. The component re-renders when the cached object changes, for example after an action or an optimistic update.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `Q` | | The object type or interface from your generated SDK. |
| `primaryKey` | `PrimaryKeyType<Q>` | | The primary key of the object to load. |
| `obj` | `Osdk.Instance<Q>` | | An object you already loaded. The hook reads it from the cache only and does not fetch. |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | When `false`, the hook does not subscribe or fetch, and `object` is `undefined`. |
| `options` | `UseOsdkObjectOptions<Q>` | | See below. |

## Options

The options type has little JSDoc, so this table is written by hand.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$select` | `readonly PropertyKeys<Q>[]` | All properties | Properties to load. |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | When `false`, the hook does not subscribe or fetch, and `object` is `undefined`. |
| `$loadPropertySecurityMetadata` | `boolean` | `false` | Loads per-property marking requirements into `$propertySecurities`. |
| `$includeAllBaseObjectProperties` | `boolean` | `false` | For an interface, loads every property of the underlying object type. No effect for object types. |

## Returns

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `object` | `Osdk.Instance<Q> \| undefined` | The object, or `undefined` before it loads, on error, or while disabled. |
| `isLoading` | `boolean` | `true` while enabled and the object has not loaded. `false` once `error` is set. |
| `error` | `Error \| undefined` | The error from the last load, if any. |
| `isOptimistic` | `boolean` | `true` while the cached object reflects an optimistic update that the server has not confirmed. |
| `forceUpdate` | `() => void` | Not implemented. Calling it throws. |

## Example

```tsx title="src/EmployeeCard.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkObject } from "@osdk/react";

export function EmployeeCard({ employeeId }: { employeeId: number }) {
  const { object: employee, isLoading, error } = useOsdkObject(
    Employee,
    employeeId,
    { $select: ["fullName", "jobTitle"] },
  );

  return (
    <article aria-busy={isLoading}>
      {error && <p role="alert">{error.message}</p>}
      <h2>{employee?.fullName}</h2>
      <p>{employee?.jobTitle}</p>
    </article>
  );
}
```

## See also

- [Load objects](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/objects.md)
- [Osdk.Instance](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/reference/client/osdk-instance.md)

# useOsdkObjects

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/reference/react/use-osdk-objects

> Load a live, cached list of objects of one type or interface.

```ts
import { useOsdkObjects } from "@osdk/react";

function useOsdkObjects<T extends ObjectOrInterfaceDefinition>(
  type: T,
  options?: UseOsdkObjectsOptions<T>,
): UseOsdkListResult<T>;
```

Subscribes the component to a list in the shared cache and re-renders when the list or any object in it changes. With `pivotTo`, the list holds the linked type instead of `T`; with `rids`, each object also carries `$rid`.

## Options

### UseOsdkObjectsOptions

| Prop                               | Type                                                          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rids?`                            | `readonly string[]`                                           | Fetch objects by their RIDs (Resource Identifiers). When provided, starts with a static objectset containing these RIDs. Can be combined with `where` to filter the RID set, and with `orderBy` to sort results.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `where?`                           | `WhereClause<T, RDPs>`                                        | Standard OSDK Where clause with RDP support. When used with `rids`, filters the RID set. When used alone, filters all objects of the type.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `orderBy?`                         | `{ [K in PropertyKeys<T>]?: "asc" \| "desc" \| undefined; }`  | Sort results by one or more properties.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `pageSize?`                        | `number`                                                      | The preferred page size for the list.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `withProperties?`                  | `{ [K in keyof RDPs]: DerivedProperty.Creator<T, RDPs[K]>; }` | Define derived properties (RDPs) to be computed server-side and attached to each object. These properties will be available on the returned objects alongside their regular properties.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `dedupeIntervalMs?`                | `number`                                                      | The number of milliseconds to wait after the last observed list change. Two uses of `useOsdkObjects` with the same parameters will only trigger one network request if the second is within `dedupeIntervalMs`.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `enabled?`                         | `boolean`                                                     | Enable or disable the query. When `false`, the query does not run and the hook returns no data, even if the cache already holds a result. Default: `true`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `intersectWith?`                   | `{ where: WhereClause<T, RDPs>; }[]`                          | Intersect the results with additional object sets. Each element defines a where clause for an object set to intersect with. The final result will only include objects that match ALL conditions.                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `pivotTo?`                         | `LinkNames<T>`                                                | Pivot to related objects through a link. This changes the return type from T to the linked object type. Cannot be combined with `streamUpdates`. The server does not support websocket subscriptions for link-traversal queries.                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `autoFetchMore?`                   | `number \| boolean`                                           | Causes the list to automatically fetch more as soon as the previous page has been loaded. If a number is provided, it will continue to automatically fetch more until the list is at least that long. - `true`: Fetch all available pages automatically - `number`: Fetch pages until at least this many items are loaded - `undefined` (default): Only fetch the first page, user must call fetchMore() |
| `streamUpdates?`                   | `boolean`                                                     | Enable streaming updates via websocket subscription. Cannot be combined with `pivotTo`. The server does not support websocket subscriptions for link-traversal queries.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `$select?`                         | `readonly PropertyKeys<T>[]`                                  | Restrict which properties are returned for each object. When provided, only the specified properties will be fetched, reducing payload sizes for list views.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `$loadPropertySecurityMetadata?`   | `boolean`                                                     | When true, loads per-property security metadata (marking requirements) alongside each object. The returned objects will have `$propertySecurities` populated with conjunctive/disjunctive marking requirements per property.                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `$includeAllBaseObjectProperties?` | `boolean`                                                     | When true, includes all properties of the underlying concrete object type for interface queries. Has no effect for non-interface queries.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `resolveToObjectType?`             | `boolean`                                                     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

## Returns

### UseOsdkListResult

| Prop           | Type                                                                                            | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `fetchMore`    | `(() => Promise<void>) \| undefined`                                                            | Function to fetch more pages (undefined if no more pages)                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `data`         | `Osdk.Instance<T, "$allBaseProperties" \| EXTRA_OPTIONS, PropertyKeys<T>, RDPs>[] \| undefined` | The fetched data with derived properties                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `isLoading`    | `boolean`                                                                                       | Whether data is currently being loaded                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `error`        | `Error \| undefined`                                                                            | Any error that occurred during fetching                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `isOptimistic` | `boolean`                                                                                       | Refers to whether the ordered list of objects (only considering the $primaryKey) is optimistic or not. If you need to know if the contents of the list are optimistic you can do that on a per object basis with useOsdkObject |
| `totalCount?`  | `string`                                                                                        | The total count of objects matching the query (if available from the API)                                                                                                                                                      |
| `hasMore`      | `boolean`                                                                                       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `objectSet`    | `ObjectSet<T, RDPs> \| undefined`                                                               |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `refetch`      | `() => Promise<void>`                                                                           |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

## Example

```tsx title="src/EngineeringList.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useOsdkObjects } from "@osdk/react";

export function EngineeringList() {
  const { data, isLoading, error, fetchMore } = useOsdkObjects(Employee, {
    where: { department: "Engineering" },
    orderBy: { fullName: "asc" },
    pageSize: 50,
  });

  return (
    <section>
      {error && <p role="alert">{error.message}</p>}
      <ul>
        {data?.map((employee) => (
          <li key={employee.$primaryKey}>{employee.fullName}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      {isLoading && <p>Loading…</p>}
      {fetchMore && <button onClick={() => void fetchMore()}>Load more</button>}
    </section>
  );
}
```

## See also

- [Load objects](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/objects.md)
- [Filtering](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/filtering.md)

# useStableObjectSet

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/reference/react/use-stable-object-set

> Return a referentially stable ObjectSet that changes only when its definition changes.

```ts
import { useStableObjectSet } from "@osdk/react";

function useStableObjectSet<
  Q extends ObjectOrInterfaceDefinition,
  RDPs extends Record<string, SimplePropertyDef> = Record<string, never>,
>(objectSet: ObjectSet<Q, RDPs> | undefined): ObjectSet<Q, RDPs> | undefined;
```

Returns the same `ObjectSet` instance across renders until the serialized definition, including `where`, `union`, `intersect`, `subtract`, and pivots, changes. Use it instead of `useMemo` when you build an object set inline and pass it to a hook, an effect, or a memoized child.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `objectSet` | `ObjectSet<Q, RDPs> \| undefined` | The object set to stabilize. `undefined` passes through. |

## Returns

`ObjectSet<Q, RDPs> | undefined`: the object set from the first render with the current definition.

## Example

```tsx title="src/TeamTable.tsx"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useObjectSet, useOsdkClient, useStableObjectSet } from "@osdk/react";

export function TeamTable({ department }: { department: string }) {
  const client = useOsdkClient();
  const team = useStableObjectSet(client(Employee).where({ department }));
  const { data } = useObjectSet(team);

  return (
    <ul>
      {data?.map((employee) => (
        <li key={employee.$primaryKey}>{employee.fullName}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

- [Object sets](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/object-sets.md)

# Actions

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/actions

> Apply Ontology actions with applyAction and batchApplyAction, validate parameters first, read returned edits, and handle ActionValidationError.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Action types](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/action-types/overview)

Actions are the way to change Ontology data: they create, modify, and delete objects and links according to rules defined in Foundry. `client(modifyEmployee)` returns an invoker with two methods, `applyAction` for one request and `batchApplyAction` for several.

```ts title="src/promote.ts"
import { Employee, modifyEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { ActionValidationError } from "@osdk/client";
import { client } from "./client";

const employee = await client(Employee).fetchOne(12345);

try {
  await client(modifyEmployee).applyAction({
    employee,
    jobTitle: "Senior Engineer",
  });
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof ActionValidationError) {
    console.error("Rejected by validation", e.validation);
  } else {
    throw e;
  }
}
```

`applyAction` rejects when the action fails, so always await it inside `try`/`catch` or attach `.catch`. The parameter names and types come from your generated SDK. In the example SDK, `modifyEmployee` takes `employee` (required), `jobTitle`, and `department`.

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$returnEdits` | `boolean` | `false` | Resolve to the edits the action made. See [Read the edits](#read-the-edits). |
| `$validateOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Check the parameters without applying the action. See [Validate first](#validate-first). `applyAction` only. |

You cannot set both on one call; the types reject it.

| Options | `applyAction` resolves to |
| --- | --- |
| None | `undefined` |
| `{ $returnEdits: true }` | `ActionEditResponse` |
| `{ $validateOnly: true }` | `ActionValidationResponse` |

When `applyAction` resolves, the action has run. Edits to objects in Object Storage V2 are visible to the next read. Edits in Object Storage V1 are eventually consistent and can take a moment to appear.

## Parameter values

| Parameter type | Pass |
| --- | --- |
| Object | A loaded object, its primary key, or `{ $apiName, $primaryKey }`. |
| Interface | A plain `{ $objectType, $primaryKey }` object, where `$objectType` is the concrete object type. Do not pass a loaded object: the client would send only its primary key. |
| Object set | An object set, such as `client(Employee).where({ ... })`. |
| Primitive | A value of the parameter's TypeScript type: `string`, `number`, `boolean`. Dates and timestamps are ISO 8601 strings. `long` and `decimal` accept a `number` or a `string`. |
| List | An array of values of the element type. |
| Struct | An object whose keys are the struct's fields. |
| Attachment | An attachment RID, a `File`, or the result of `createAttachmentUpload`. See [Attachments and media](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/media.md#upload-through-an-action). |
| Media reference | A `MediaUpload`, a `Media` from an object, or a `MediaReference`. See [Attachments and media](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/media.md#upload-through-an-action). |

Omit an optional parameter to leave it out of the request. Pass `null` to send an empty value, which clears the property in a modify action:

```ts title="src/clearTitle.ts"
import { modifyEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

await client(modifyEmployee).applyAction({ employee: 12345, jobTitle: null });
```

Parameter default values configured on the action type are not applied when you call the action from the client. Pass every value you need.

## Validate first

`$validateOnly: true` runs the action's submission criteria and parameter constraints without applying it. It resolves to the validation result, valid or not, and does not throw on an invalid result:

```ts title="src/validate.ts"
import { modifyEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const validation = await client(modifyEmployee).applyAction(
  { employee: 12345, department: "Research" },
  { $validateOnly: true },
);

if (validation.result === "INVALID") {
  for (const [name, parameter] of Object.entries(validation.parameters)) {
    if (parameter.result === "INVALID") {
      console.warn(`${name} is invalid`, parameter.evaluatedConstraints);
    }
  }
}
```

The validation result has this shape:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `result` | `"VALID" \| "INVALID"` | The overall result. |
| `submissionCriteria` | `{ result, configuredFailureMessage? }[]` | One entry per submission criterion, with the failure message configured on the action type. |
| `parameters` | `Record<string, { result, required, evaluatedConstraints }>` | One entry per parameter. `evaluatedConstraints` lists the checks that ran, such as `range`, `stringLength`, `oneOf`, or `stringRegexMatch`. |

## Handle validation errors

When you apply an action whose validation fails, `applyAction` throws an `ActionValidationError` from `@osdk/client`. Its `validation` field holds the same validation result:

```ts title="src/validationMessage.ts"
import { modifyEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { ActionValidationError } from "@osdk/client";
import { client } from "./client";

function describeValidation(error: ActionValidationError): string {
  const criteria = error.validation.submissionCriteria
    .filter((criterion) => criterion.result === "INVALID")
    .flatMap((criterion) => criterion.configuredFailureMessage ?? []);
  const parameters = Object.entries(error.validation.parameters)
    .filter(([, parameter]) => parameter.result === "INVALID")
    .map(([name]) => `${name} is invalid`);
  return [...criteria, ...parameters].join("\n") || "The action was rejected.";
}

try {
  await client(modifyEmployee).applyAction({ employee: 12345, department: "Research" });
} catch (e) {
  console.error(e instanceof ActionValidationError ? describeValidation(e) : e);
}
```

Every other failure, such as a missing permission or an invalid parameter type, rejects with a `PalantirApiError`. See [Errors](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/errors.md).

## Read the edits

`$returnEdits: true` resolves to the edits the action made:

```ts title="src/edits.ts"
import { modifyEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const result = await client(modifyEmployee).applyAction(
  { employee: 12345, jobTitle: "Staff Engineer" },
  { $returnEdits: true },
);

if (result.type === "edits") {
  for (const edited of result.modifiedObjects) {
    console.log(`Modified ${edited.objectType} ${edited.primaryKey}`);
  }
}
console.log("Edited types:", result.editedObjectTypes);
```

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `"edits" \| "largeScaleEdits"` | `"largeScaleEdits"` when the action made too many edits to list. Only `editedObjectTypes` is set then. |
| `addedObjects`, `modifiedObjects`, `deletedObjects` | `{ objectType, primaryKey }[]` | The objects the action created, changed, and deleted. |
| `addedLinks`, `deletedLinks` | `{ linkTypeApiNameAtoB, linkTypeApiNameBtoA, aSideObject, bSideObject }[]` | The links the action created and removed. |
| `deletedObjectsCount`, `deletedLinksCount` | `number` | The number of deletions. |
| `editedObjectTypes` | `string[]` | The API names of every object type the action touched. |

The edits name objects by type and primary key. To read the new values, load the objects again.

## Apply in a batch

`batchApplyAction` takes an array of parameter objects for the same action and applies them in one request:

```ts title="src/bulkRetitle.ts"
import { modifyEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const ids = [101, 102, 103];

const result = await client(modifyEmployee).batchApplyAction(
  ids.map((employee) => ({ employee, jobTitle: "Engineer II" })),
  { $returnEdits: true },
);
```

Differences from `applyAction`:

- It accepts `$returnEdits` but not `$validateOnly`.
- It does not throw `ActionValidationError`. If a request in the batch fails, the call rejects with a `PalantirApiError`.
- A batch holds up to 20 requests. Actions that only modify objects in Object Storage V2 and call no functions may have a higher limit. For more, split the array and send several batches.
- Action notifications are not sent for batched requests.

## In React

`useOsdkAction` from `@osdk/react` wraps `applyAction`, tracks pending and validation state, and refreshes cached objects after the action. See [Actions in React](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/actions.md).

# Aggregations

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/aggregations

> Count, sum, average, and find the min, max, or distinct values of object sets on the server, grouped by exact values, ranges, fixed widths, or durations.

`aggregate` computes counts and metrics over an object set on the server and returns only the numbers. It loads no objects, so it is the right tool for totals, averages, and breakdowns, however large the set.

```ts title="src/headcount.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const stats = await client(Employee)
  .where({ department: "Engineering" })
  .aggregate({
    $select: { $count: "unordered", "salary:avg": "unordered", "salary:max": "unordered" },
  });

console.log(stats.$count, stats.salary.avg, stats.salary.max);
```

`aggregate` takes `$select`, the metrics to compute, and an optional `$groupBy`. Filter first with [`where`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/filtering.md); every object set method that returns an object set, such as `pivotTo` or `intersect`, can come before it.

## Metrics

Each `$select` key is `$count` or `"<property>:<metric>"`. The value is a sort direction, described in [Sort groups](#sort-groups); use `"unordered"` when you do not need one.

| Metric | Property types | Result type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$count` | Not applicable | `number` |
| `sum`, `avg` | Numeric | `number \| undefined` |
| `min`, `max` | Numeric, date, timestamp | The property's type, or `undefined` |
| `approximateDistinct` | All | `number` |
| `exactDistinct` | All | `number` |

A metric that does not apply to the property's type, such as `"fullName:sum"`, does not typecheck. `approximateDistinct` is faster on large sets and can be off by a small amount; `exactDistinct` is exact.

## Read the result

Without `$groupBy`, the result is one object. `$count` is a number, and each property is an object keyed by metric name:

```ts title="src/salaryRange.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const result = await client(Employee).aggregate({
  $select: {
    $count: "unordered",
    "salary:min": "unordered",
    "salary:max": "unordered",
    "startDate:min": "unordered",
    "department:exactDistinct": "unordered",
  },
});

const { $count, salary, startDate, department } = result;
console.log(`${$count} employees in ${department.exactDistinct} departments`);
console.log(`Salaries ${salary.min} to ${salary.max}, earliest start ${startDate.min}`);
```

With `$groupBy`, the result is an array with one entry per group. Each entry has the group's values under `$group`, plus the same metric fields:

```ts title="src/byDepartment.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const groups = await client(Employee).aggregate({
  $select: { $count: "desc", "salary:avg": "unordered" },
  $groupBy: { department: "exact" },
});

for (const group of groups) {
  console.log(group.$group.department, group.$count, group.salary.avg);
}
```

## Group by

`$groupBy` maps each property to a grouping. Several properties group by every combination of their values.

| Grouping | Property types | `$group` value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `"exact"` | All | The property's value | One group per distinct value. |
| `{ $exactWithLimit: n }` | All | The property's value | At most `n` groups. |
| `{ $exact: { $limit?, $includeNullValue: true } }` | All | The value, or `null` | Adds a group for objects with no value. |
| `{ $fixedWidth: n }` | Numeric | The bucket's lower bound | Buckets of width `n`. |
| `{ $ranges: [[start, end], ...] }` | Numeric, date, timestamp | `{ startValue, endValue }` | One group per range. `start` is inclusive and `end` exclusive. |
| `{ $duration: [n, unit] }` | Date, timestamp | The bucket's start | Buckets of `n` time units. |

`$duration` units:

| Property type | Units |
| --- | --- |
| Date | `"days"`, `"weeks"`, `"months"`, `"quarters"`, `"years"`, and singular or short forms such as `"day"`, `"wk"`, `"mos"`, `"yr"` |
| Timestamp | The date units, plus `"seconds"`, `"minutes"`, and `"hours"` and their short forms such as `"sec"`, `"min"`, `"hr"` |

For weeks, months, quarters, and years, `n` must be `1`.

```ts title="src/breakdowns.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const bySalaryBand = await client(Employee).aggregate({
  $select: { $count: "unordered" },
  $groupBy: {
    salary: { $ranges: [[0, 100_000], [100_000, 200_000], [200_000, 1_000_000]] },
  },
});
for (const band of bySalaryBand) {
  console.log(`${band.$group.salary.startValue} to ${band.$group.salary.endValue}: ${band.$count}`);
}

const hiresPerYear = await client(Employee).aggregate({
  $select: { $count: "unordered" },
  $groupBy: { startDate: { $duration: [1, "years"] } },
});

const byDepartmentAndTitle = await client(Employee).aggregate({
  $select: { $count: "unordered", "salary:avg": "unordered" },
  $groupBy: { department: "exact", jobTitle: { $exactWithLimit: 20 } },
});

const withUnassigned = await client(Employee).aggregate({
  $select: { $count: "unordered" },
  $groupBy: { department: { $exact: { $includeNullValue: true } } },
});
for (const group of withUnassigned) {
  console.log(group.$group.department ?? "No department", group.$count);
}
```

## Sort groups

Set a metric's value in `$select` to `"asc"` or `"desc"` to order the groups by that metric. `$count: "desc"` lists the largest groups first.

Sorting has two limits, both enforced by the types:

- With more than one `$groupBy` property, every `$select` value must be `"unordered"`.
- With `$exact: { $includeNullValue: true }`, every `$select` value must be `"unordered"`.

## Aggregate over links and set operations

Because `aggregate` runs on any object set, you can aggregate over linked objects or combined sets without loading them:

```ts title="src/officeStats.ts"
import { Employee, Office } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const newYorkSalaries = await client(Office)
  .where({ city: "New York" })
  .pivotTo("occupants")
  .aggregate({ $select: { "salary:sum": "unordered", $count: "unordered" } });

const lead = await client(Employee).fetchOne(12345);
const teamByTitle = await lead.$link.reports.aggregate({
  $select: { $count: "desc" },
  $groupBy: { jobTitle: "exact" },
});
```

To attach a per-object aggregate, such as each employee's report count, as a property you can filter and sort on, use [derived properties](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/derived-properties.md).

## In React

`useOsdkAggregation` from `@osdk/react` runs the same request, caches the result, and loads it again when objects of the type change. See [Aggregations in React](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/aggregations.md).

# Derived properties

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/derived-properties

> Add computed properties to an object set with withProperties, from linked objects, link aggregations, and expressions, then filter and sort on them.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Derived properties](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/object-link-types/derived-properties)

`withProperties` adds properties that the server computes at query time, such as an employee's number of reports or their lead's name. You can select, filter, sort, and aggregate on them like stored properties, and nothing is written to the Ontology.

```ts title="src/teamSizes.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const page = await client(Employee)
  .withProperties({
    reportCount: (base) => base.pivotTo("reports").aggregate("$count"),
    leadName: (base) => base.pivotTo("lead").selectProperty("fullName"),
  })
  .where({ reportCount: { $gt: 5 } })
  .fetchPage({
    $select: ["fullName", "reportCount", "leadName"],
    $orderBy: { reportCount: "desc" },
  });

for (const employee of page.data) {
  console.log(employee.fullName, employee.reportCount, employee.leadName);
}
```

`withProperties` takes an object that maps each new property name to a function. The function receives a builder for the object it computes on, and returns a definition. The result is a new object set with the new properties typed: `reportCount` is a `number` and `leadName` is `string | undefined`.

## Builder methods

Start from the builder and chain:

| Method | Available on | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pivotTo(link)` | Every builder | A builder over the linked objects. After a many link, such as `reports`, the builder can only aggregate. |
| `where(clause)` | Every builder | The builder, filtered. See [Filter objects](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/filtering.md). |
| `selectProperty(property)` | The base object, and builders reached through single links only | The property's value. |
| `aggregate(metric, options?)` | Builders reached through a many link | One value computed over the linked objects. |

`selectProperty` after a many link does not typecheck: an employee has many reports, so there is no single report name to select. Aggregate instead, for example with `collectList`.

## Link aggregations

`aggregate` takes `$count` or `"<property>:<metric>"`:

| Metric | Property types | Options | Result type |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$count` | Not applicable | None | `number` |
| `sum`, `avg` | Numeric | None | `number \| undefined` |
| `min`, `max` | Numeric, date, timestamp | None | The property's type, or `undefined` |
| `approximateDistinct`, `exactDistinct` | All | None | `number` |
| `approximatePercentile` | Numeric | `{ percentile }` | `number \| undefined` |
| `collectList` | All | `{ limit }`, up to 100. Default 100. | An array of the property's type |
| `collectSet` | All | `{ limit }`, up to 100. Default 100. | An array of distinct values |

```ts title="src/teamStats.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const page = await client(Employee)
  .withProperties({
    avgReportSalary: (base) => base.pivotTo("reports").aggregate("salary:avg"),
    reportNames: (base) =>
      base.pivotTo("reports").aggregate("fullName:collectList", { limit: 20 }),
    engineeringReports: (base) =>
      base.pivotTo("reports").where({ department: "Engineering" }).aggregate("$count"),
    skipLevelCount: (base) => base.pivotTo("reports").pivotTo("reports").aggregate("$count"),
  })
  .fetchPage({ $pageSize: 20 });
```

## Values from single links

On a single link, `selectProperty` reads one property of the linked object. Chain single links to go further:

```ts title="src/leadInfo.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const page = await client(Employee)
  .withProperties({
    officeCity: (base) => base.pivotTo("office").selectProperty("city"),
    leadsLeadName: (base) => base.pivotTo("lead").pivotTo("lead").selectProperty("fullName"),
  })
  .where({ officeCity: "London" })
  .fetchPage({ $select: ["fullName", "officeCity", "leadsLeadName"] });
```

## Expressions

A numeric definition, from `selectProperty` on a numeric property or a numeric aggregation, has expression methods. Each binary method takes a number or another numeric definition:

| Method | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `add(x)`, `subtract(x)`, `multiply(x)`, `divide(x)` | Arithmetic. |
| `min(x)`, `max(x)` | The smaller or larger value. |
| `abs()`, `negate()` | The absolute value, or the value times -1. |

A date or timestamp definition has:

| Method | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `min(other)`, `max(other)` | The earlier or later of two date or timestamp definitions. |
| `extractPart(part)` | The `"DAYS"`, `"MONTHS"`, `"QUARTERS"`, or `"YEARS"` part, as a string. |

```ts title="src/expressions.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const page = await client(Employee)
  .withProperties({
    salaryPerReport: (base) =>
      base.selectProperty("salary").divide(base.pivotTo("reports").aggregate("$count")),
    proposedSalary: (base) => base.selectProperty("salary").multiply(1.05),
    startYear: (base) => base.selectProperty("startDate").extractPart("YEARS"),
    earlierStart: (base) =>
      base.selectProperty("startDate").min(base.pivotTo("lead").selectProperty("startDate")),
  })
  .fetchPage({ $pageSize: 20 });
```

Arithmetic on two integers returns an integer. When either side is a `double`, a `float`, or a number literal, the result is a `double`.

## Use derived properties

Once added, a derived property works everywhere a stored property does on that object set:

| Use | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Filter | `.where({ reportCount: { $gte: 3 } })` |
| Sort | `.fetchPage({ $orderBy: { reportCount: "desc" } })` |
| Select | `.fetchPage({ $select: ["fullName", "reportCount"] })` |
| Aggregate | `.aggregate({ $select: { "reportCount:avg": "unordered" } })` |
| Load by key | `.fetchOne(12345, { $select: ["reportCount"] })` |

Derived properties are returned when you omit `$select`. If you pass `$select`, list them in it, along with every stored property you need.

```ts title="src/avgTeamSize.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const byDepartment = await client(Employee)
  .withProperties({
    reportCount: (base) => base.pivotTo("reports").aggregate("$count"),
  })
  .where({ reportCount: { $gt: 0 } })
  .aggregate({
    $select: { "reportCount:avg": "unordered", $count: "unordered" },
    $groupBy: { department: "exact" },
  });
```

Each call to `withProperties` returns a new object set, and the properties exist only on it and on the sets derived from it. To reuse a set of definitions, store the object set in a variable.

# Errors

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/errors

> The errors @osdk/client throws, the fields of PalantirApiError and ActionValidationError, Result-returning methods, retries, and patterns for handling them.

Every `@osdk/client` method that sends a request rejects on failure. This page lists what it rejects with, which fields to branch on, and the methods that return a result instead of throwing.

## Error types

| Error | Import | Thrown when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PalantirApiError` | `@osdk/client` | Foundry returned an error response. Also the base class for the next row. |
| `UnknownError` | Not exported. Check `error.name === "UnknownError"`. | The request never got a response, such as a DNS, TLS, CORS, or connection failure, or the response was not JSON. A subclass of `PalantirApiError`. |
| `ActionValidationError` | `@osdk/client` | `applyAction` ran the action's validation and it failed. |
| `Error` | Built in | The client rejected your input before sending anything. See [Errors before a request](#errors-before-a-request). |

Errors thrown by your token provider pass through unchanged.

## `PalantirApiError`

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | `string` | The server's message, or `Failed to fetch <status> <statusText>`. |
| `errorCode` | `string \| undefined` | The category, such as `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `NOT_FOUND`, `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `CONFLICT`, or `TIMEOUT`. |
| `errorName` | `string \| undefined` | The specific error, such as `ObjectTypeNotFound` or `ActionNotFound`. |
| `errorDescription` | `string \| undefined` | A longer description. |
| `statusCode` | `number \| undefined` | The HTTP status. `undefined` when no response arrived. |
| `errorInstanceId` | `string \| undefined` | An ID for this occurrence. Log it, and include it when you report a problem to your Foundry administrator. |
| `parameters` | `unknown` | Error-specific details, such as the API name that was not found. |

On an `UnknownError`, `originalError` holds the underlying error when there is one, such as the `TypeError` from a failed `fetch`.

When no object matches, `fetchOne` and `$link.<link>.fetchOne` reject with a `PalantirApiError` that carries only a message, `Expected a single result but got 0 instead`, and no `statusCode`, `errorCode`, or `errorName`.

Branch on `statusCode` and `errorCode`, which are stable. Use `errorName` for a specific case. Do not parse `message`.

```ts title="src/describeError.ts"
import { PalantirApiError } from "@osdk/client";

export function describeError(error: unknown): string {
  if (!(error instanceof PalantirApiError)) {
    return error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
  }
  if (error.name === "UnknownError") {
    return "Could not reach Foundry. Check the network and the Foundry URL.";
  }
  if (error.statusCode === 401) {
    return "The token is missing or expired.";
  }
  if (error.errorCode === "PERMISSION_DENIED" || error.statusCode === 403) {
    return "You do not have access to this data.";
  }
  if (error.errorCode === "NOT_FOUND") {
    return `Not found: ${error.errorName ?? error.message}`;
  }
  return `${error.message} (error instance ${error.errorInstanceId ?? "unknown"})`;
}
```

A `NOT_FOUND` error can also mean that the user cannot see a resource that exists.

## `ActionValidationError`

`applyAction` throws `ActionValidationError` when the server ran the action's submission criteria and parameter constraints and they failed. It is not a `PalantirApiError`. Its `validation` field has `result`, `submissionCriteria`, and `parameters`. See [Actions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/actions.md#handle-validation-errors) for the shape and a message helper.

`batchApplyAction` does not throw it. A batch that fails validation rejects with a `PalantirApiError`.

## Methods that return a result

Three methods resolve to a `Result` instead of rejecting:

| Method | On |
| --- | --- |
| `fetchOneWithErrors(primaryKey, options?)` | Object type sets |
| `fetchPageWithErrors(options?)` | Every object set |
| `$link.<link>.fetchOneWithErrors(options?)` | Single links |

A `Result` is `{ value }` on success or `{ error }` on failure, where `error` is an `Error`. Narrow it with `isOk` from `@osdk/client`:

```ts title="src/optionalLead.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { isOk } from "@osdk/client";
import { client } from "./client";

const result = await client(Employee).fetchOneWithErrors(12345, { $select: ["fullName"] });

if (isOk(result)) {
  console.log(result.value.fullName);
} else {
  console.warn("Employee not available:", result.error.message);
}
```

`error` is the same error the throwing variant would have thrown, so the narrowing above still applies.

## Retries

The client retries a request that fails with `429 Too Many Requests` or `503 Service Unavailable`, up to three times, unless the response sets the header `QoS-Retry-Hint: do-not-retry`. The delays grow exponentially from about one second, with random jitter. Other errors, including network failures, are not retried. Your code sees the error only after the last attempt.

## Errors before a request

These throw a plain `Error` before any request is sent:

| Error | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `Invalid ontology RID` | `createClient` got an Ontology RID string that does not start with `ri.`. If you pass a `Promise`, the check runs when it resolves and surfaces as an unhandled rejection instead. |
| `baseUrl cannot be empty` | `createClient` got an empty base URL. A malformed URL throws a `TypeError` from `new URL`. |
| `Cannot filter on property "<name>" with an undefined or null value` | A `where` clause had a `null` or `undefined` value. See [Filter objects](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/filtering.md#how-a-clause-combines). |
| `A WhereClause Filter with multiple clauses/fields is not allowed` | One property in a `where` clause had more than one operator. |
| `Object does not implement interface '<name>'` | `$as` was called with an interface the object type does not implement. See [Interfaces](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/interfaces.md#convert-one-object-with-as). |
| `Union return types are not yet supported` | A function returned a union type. See [Functions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/functions.md#return-values). |

## Patterns

- Await every call inside `try`/`catch`, or attach `.catch`. A rejected promise that nothing handles crashes a Node.js process and logs an unhandled rejection in the browser.
- Catch `ActionValidationError` before `PalantirApiError`, and show the validation messages to the user. Other action errors usually need a retry or an administrator.
- For loads where a missing object is expected, use the `WithErrors` variants instead of catching.
- In long jobs, log `errorInstanceId` and `errorName` with each failure, and keep going instead of stopping at the first error.

For errors in `@osdk/react` hooks, see [Loading and errors](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/concepts/loading-and-errors.md).

# Filter objects

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/filtering

> Reference for where clauses in @osdk/client, covering comparison, set, null, text, array, date, geospatial, and logical operators, with examples.

{/* cspell:ignore geospatial enginer */}

`where` narrows an object set on the server. It takes a clause object and returns a new object set, so you can chain it with other `where` calls, [links](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/links.md), [aggregations](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/aggregations.md), and any load method.

```ts title="src/seniorEngineers.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const page = await client(Employee)
  .where({
    department: "Engineering",
    salary: { $gte: 150_000 },
    jobTitle: { $containsAnyTerm: "senior staff" },
  })
  .fetchPage({ $select: ["fullName", "jobTitle", "salary"] });
```

`where` sends no request by itself. The filter runs when you call `fetchPage`, `asyncIter`, `aggregate`, or another method that loads data.

## How a clause combines

- Each key of the clause is a property name, `$title`, `$primaryKey`, or one of `$and`, `$or`, `$not`.
- Several keys in one clause must all match. `{ department: "Engineering", salary: { $gte: 150_000 } }` is an AND.
- A bare value means equality. `{ department: "Engineering" }` is the same as `{ department: { $eq: "Engineering" } }`.
- Each property takes one operator. `{ salary: { $gte: 100_000, $lt: 200_000 } }` does not typecheck, and throws at runtime. Use `$and` for a range.
- Chained `where` calls also combine with AND.
- The value must not be `null` or `undefined`. The client throws `Cannot filter on property "<name>" with an undefined or null value`. To match missing values, use `$isNull: true`.

## Operator reference

| Operator | Property types | Value | Matches |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$eq` | Non-array, non-geo | A value of the property's type | Equal values. Also written as the bare value. |
| `$ne` | Non-array, non-geo | A value of the property's type | Values that are not equal. |
| `$in` | Non-array, non-geo | An array of values | Any value in the array. An empty array matches every object. |
| `$isNull` | All | `boolean` | `true`: the property has no value. `false`: it has one. |
| `$gt`, `$gte`, `$lt`, `$lte` | Numbers, strings, dates, timestamps | A value of the property's type | Greater than, greater or equal, less than, less or equal. Strings compare lexicographically. |
| `$startsWith` | `string` | `string`, or `{ term, phoneticSearch? }` | Values that contain the terms adjacent and in order, with the last term matched as a prefix. The match can start anywhere in the value. |
| `$containsAnyTerm` | `string` | `string`, `{ term, fuzzySearch? }`, or `{ term, phoneticSearch? }` | Values that contain any of the whitespace-separated terms. |
| `$containsAllTerms` | `string` | `string`, `{ term, fuzzySearch? }`, or `{ term, phoneticSearch? }` | Values that contain all the terms, in any order. |
| `$containsAllTermsInOrder` | `string` | `string`, or `{ term, phoneticSearch? }` | Values that contain all the terms, adjacent and in order. |
| `$interval` | `string` | An interval rule | Term proximity, ordering, prefix, and fuzzy matches. See [Interval rules](#interval-rules). |
| `$matchesRegex` | `string` | `string` | Beta. Values that match the regular expression, in the Foundry search syntax. |
| `$contains` | Array properties | An element value, or a filter on elements | Arrays with at least one element that matches. |
| `$within` | `geopoint`, `geoshape` | Distance, bounding box, or polygon | Shapes inside the area. See [Geospatial filters](#geospatial-filters). |
| `$intersects` | `geopoint`, `geoshape` | Bounding box or polygon | Shapes that overlap the area. |
| `$and` | Clause | An array of clauses | Objects that match every clause. |
| `$or` | Clause | An array of clauses | Objects that match at least one clause. |
| `$not` | Clause | One clause | Objects that do not match the clause. |

Boolean properties accept `$eq`, `$ne`, `$in`, and `$isNull`. Array properties accept only `$contains` and `$isNull`.

> [!WARNING]
> `$in: []` matches every object, not none. When the array comes from user input, check for an empty array before you add the filter.

## Comparison and sets

```ts title="src/comparisons.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const notSales = client(Employee).where({ department: { $ne: "Sales" } });

const team = client(Employee).where({ employeeId: { $in: [101, 102, 103] } });

const noTitle = client(Employee).where({ jobTitle: { $isNull: true } });

const midBand = client(Employee).where({
  $and: [{ salary: { $gte: 100_000 } }, { salary: { $lt: 200_000 } }],
});
```

## Text

The text operators match whole terms, the whitespace-separated words of the value, rather than raw substrings. `$startsWith` is a term match too: `{ fullName: { $startsWith: "ada lov" } }` matches `Ada Lovelace`, and also `Countess Ada Lovelace`.

```ts title="src/text.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const typeahead = client(Employee).where({ fullName: { $startsWith: "ada lov" } });

const anyTerm = client(Employee).where({ jobTitle: { $containsAnyTerm: "designer researcher" } });

const allTerms = client(Employee).where({ jobTitle: { $containsAllTerms: "senior engineer" } });

const phrase = client(Employee).where({ jobTitle: { $containsAllTermsInOrder: "staff engineer" } });
```

### Fuzzy matching

`$containsAnyTerm` and `$containsAllTerms` also take `{ term, fuzzySearch: true }`, which matches terms within a small edit distance, such as a typo:

```ts title="src/fuzzy.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const engineers = client(Employee).where({
  jobTitle: { $containsAnyTerm: { term: "enginer", fuzzySearch: true } },
});
```

### Phonetic matching

Every text operator also takes `{ term, phoneticSearch: true }`, which matches similarly pronounced terms, such as `Jon` and `John`. The property must support phonetic search, set with `supportsPhonetic` in [Ontology as code](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/ontology-as-code/object-types.md). `fuzzySearch` and `phoneticSearch` cannot both be `true`; use `$or` to combine them.

```ts title="src/phonetic.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const soundsLikeJon = client(Employee).where({
  fullName: { $containsAnyTerm: { term: "Jon", phoneticSearch: true } },
});
```

### Interval rules

`$interval` takes one rule. Rules nest through `$and` and `$or`:

| Rule | Fields | Matches |
| --- | --- | --- |
