| Match | `$match: string`, `$ordered: boolean`, `$maxGaps?: number` | The terms of `$match`. `$ordered: true` requires them in order. `$maxGaps` limits the number of words between them. |
| Prefix | `$match: string`, `$prefixOnLastTerm: true` | The terms in order, with the last term matched as a prefix. |
| Fuzzy | `$fuzzy: string`, `$fuzziness?: number` | A term within `$fuzziness` edits (0, 1, or 2; default 2). |
| All | `$and: IntervalRule[]`, `$ordered: boolean`, `$maxGaps?: number` | Every sub-rule. |
| Any | `$or: IntervalRule[]` | At least one sub-rule. |

```ts title="src/interval.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const typeahead = client(Employee).where({
  jobTitle: { $interval: { $match: "staff eng", $prefixOnLastTerm: true } },
});

const nearby = client(Employee).where({
  jobTitle: { $interval: { $match: "principal engineer", $ordered: true, $maxGaps: 1 } },
});
```

## Arrays

On an array property, `$contains` matches objects where at least one element matches. Pass an element value, or a filter that each element is tested against. `$isNull` is the only other operator:

```ts title="src/skills.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const typescript = client(Employee).where({ skills: { $contains: "TypeScript" } });

const anyType = client(Employee).where({ skills: { $contains: { $startsWith: "Type" } } });

const noSkills = client(Employee).where({ skills: { $isNull: true } });
```

To require several elements, combine `$contains` filters with `$and`.

## Dates and timestamps

Date and timestamp properties take ISO 8601 strings: `"2024-01-31"` for dates and `"2024-01-31T09:00:00Z"` for timestamps. They accept `$eq`, `$ne`, `$in`, `$isNull`, and the range operators:

```ts title="src/recentHires.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const hired2024 = client(Employee).where({
  $and: [{ startDate: { $gte: "2024-01-01" } }, { startDate: { $lt: "2025-01-01" } }],
});
```

## Geospatial filters

Coordinates are `[longitude, latitude]`, as in GeoJSON. The samples assume `Office` has a `geopoint` property named `location`.

| Filter | Value | Matches |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$within: { $distance, $of }` | `$distance: [number, unit]`, `$of: [lon, lat]` or a GeoJSON `Point` | Points within the distance of the center. |
| `$within: { $bbox }` or `$within: bbox` | `[west, south, east, north]` | Shapes inside the bounding box. |
| `$within: { $polygon }` | Polygon coordinates: an array of rings, each closed | Shapes inside the polygon. |
| `$within: polygon` | A GeoJSON `Polygon` | Shapes inside the polygon. |
| `$intersects: { $bbox }` or `$intersects: bbox` | `[west, south, east, north]` | Shapes that overlap the bounding box. |
| `$intersects: { $polygon }` or `$intersects: polygon` | Polygon coordinates, or a GeoJSON `Polygon` | Shapes that overlap the polygon. |

Distance units are `"m"`, `"meter"`, `"meters"`, `"km"`, `"kilometer"`, `"kilometers"`, `"cm"`, `"centimeter"`, `"centimeters"`, `"mile"`, `"miles"`, `"foot"`, `"feet"`, `"inch"`, `"inches"`, `"yard"`, `"yards"`, `"nautical_mile"`, `"nauticalMile"`, and `"nautical miles"`.

```ts title="src/nearbyOffices.ts"
import { Office } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const nearNewYork = client(Office).where({
  location: { $within: { $distance: [25, "km"], $of: [-74.006, 40.7128] } },
});

const inManhattan = client(Office).where({
  location: { $within: { $bbox: [-74.02, 40.7, -73.93, 40.88] } },
});

const inArea = client(Office).where({
  location: {
    $intersects: {
      type: "Polygon",
      coordinates: [[[-74.02, 40.7], [-73.93, 40.7], [-73.93, 40.88], [-74.02, 40.7]]],
    },
  },
});
```

## Combine clauses

`$and`, `$or`, and `$not` take clauses and nest to any depth:

```ts title="src/combined.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const result = client(Employee).where({
  $or: [
    { department: "Engineering", salary: { $gte: 200_000 } },
    { $not: { jobTitle: { $isNull: true } }, startDate: { $gte: "2025-01-01" } },
  ],
});
```

## Title and primary key

`$title` filters on the object type's title property and `$primaryKey` on its primary key, without naming them. Both are useful in code that works across object types:

```ts title="src/special.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const byTitle = client(Employee).where({ $title: { $startsWith: "Ada" } });

const byKey = client(Employee).where({ $primaryKey: { $in: [101, 102] } });
```

## Struct properties

A struct property filters on one field at a time: `{ address: { city: "Denver" } }` applies the field's own operators to `address.city`. To filter on two fields, combine two clauses with `$and`. On an array of structs, wrap the field filter in `$contains`: `{ addresses: { $contains: { city: "Denver" } } }`.

## Vector search

`nearestNeighbors(query, numNeighbors, property)` returns an object set of the objects whose vector property is closest to the query. `query` is text, which the server embeds with the property's model, or a vector with the property's dimension. `numNeighbors` is between 1 and 500. To get the closest first, and a `$score` on each object, load the result with `$orderBy: "relevance"`.

## Type a clause

Build a clause outside the call with the `WhereClause` type from `@osdk/client`:

```ts title="src/highEarners.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import type { WhereClause } from "@osdk/client";
import { client } from "./client";

function highEarnersIn(department: string, minSalary: number): WhereClause<Employee> {
  return { department, salary: { $gte: minSalary } };
}

const page = await client(Employee)
  .where(highEarnersIn("Engineering", 150_000))
  .fetchPage({ $select: ["fullName", "department"] });
```

# Functions

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/functions

> Execute Foundry functions (queries) with executeFunction, pass objects and object sets as parameters, and read struct, object, and object set results.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Functions](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/functions/overview)

Functions published to the Ontology, called queries in the API, appear in your generated SDK next to object types and actions. `client(myFunction).executeFunction(params)` runs one on the server and resolves to its typed return value.

The samples use these functions, which stand in for functions in your own SDK:

| Function | Parameters | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `countEmployees` | None | `integer` |
| `getEmployeeMetrics` | `department: string` | Struct `{ headcount: integer }` |
| `summarizeTeam` | `team: ObjectSet<Employee>` | `string` |
| `getTopEarners` | `department: string`, `limit?: integer` | `ObjectSet<Employee>` |
| `getManager` | `employee: Employee` | `Employee` |

## Execute a function

```ts title="src/metrics.ts"
import { countEmployees, getEmployeeMetrics } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const total = await client(countEmployees).executeFunction();

const metrics = await client(getEmployeeMetrics).executeFunction({ department: "Engineering" });
console.log(`${metrics.headcount} of ${total} employees are engineers`);
```

`executeFunction` takes one object with a key per parameter, or no argument when the function has no parameters. Nullable parameters are optional. It rejects with a `PalantirApiError` when the function fails or times out on the server; see [Errors](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/errors.md).

If your SDK was generated with a pinned function version, the client calls that version. Otherwise it calls the latest published version.

## Parameter values

| Parameter type | Pass |
| --- | --- |
| Primitive | A value of the parameter's TypeScript type. Dates and timestamps are ISO 8601 strings. `long` and `decimal` accept a `number` or a `string`. |
| Object | A loaded object, its primary key, or `{ $apiName, $primaryKey }`. |
| Interface | An object loaded through the interface, or `{ $objectType, $primaryKey }`, where `$objectType` is the concrete object type. |
| Object set | An object set, such as `client(Employee).where({ ... })`. The server receives its definition, not its objects. |
| List, set | An array, or a `Set` for set parameters. |
| Struct | An object whose keys are the struct's fields. |
| Map | An object keyed by the map's keys. For object keys, use each object's `$objectSpecifier`. |
| Attachment | An attachment RID, a `File`, or the result of `createAttachmentUpload`. The client uploads it first. |
| Media reference | A `MediaUpload`, a `Media` from an object, or a `MediaReference`. |

Pass an object set to let the function work on a filtered set without loading it in the client:

```ts title="src/summarize.ts"
import { Employee, summarizeTeam } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const summary = await client(summarizeTeam).executeFunction({
  team: client(Employee).where({ department: "Sales", startDate: { $gte: "2025-01-01" } }),
});
```

## Return values

| Return type | You get |
| --- | --- |
| Primitive | The value. `long` and `decimal` are strings; dates and timestamps are ISO 8601 strings. |
| List, set | An array. |
| Struct | A plain object. |
| Map | A plain object keyed by the map's keys. Object keys become object specifier strings. |
| Object | An object reference with `$apiName`, `$objectType`, and `$primaryKey`. It has no properties. |
| Object set | An object set. Load it with `fetchPage`, `asyncIter`, or `aggregate`. |
| Attachment | An `Attachment`. See [Attachments and media](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/media.md). |
| Media reference | A `Media`. See [Attachments and media](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/media.md). |
| Two-dimensional aggregation | `{ key, value }[]` |
| Three-dimensional aggregation | `{ key, groups: { key, value }[] }[]` |
| Nullable, when the function returns nothing | `undefined` |

Union return types are not supported: the client throws `Union return types are not yet supported`.

### Object results

A returned object is a reference, not a loaded object. Load it by primary key to read its properties:

```ts title="src/manager.ts"
import { Employee, getManager } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const employee = await client(Employee).fetchOne(12345);
const managerRef = await client(getManager).executeFunction({ employee });

const manager = await client(Employee).fetchOne(managerRef.$primaryKey, {
  $select: ["fullName", "jobTitle"],
});
```

### Object set results

A returned object set is like any other. Filter, sort, page, and aggregate it before loading:

```ts title="src/topEarners.ts"
import { getTopEarners } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const topEarners = await client(getTopEarners).executeFunction({ department: "Sales", limit: 10 });

const page = await topEarners.fetchPage({
  $select: ["fullName", "salary"],
  $orderBy: { salary: "desc" },
});
```

## In React

`useOsdkFunction` from `@osdk/react` executes a function, caches the result by its parameters, and can refetch when objects it depends on change. See [Functions in React](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/functions.md).

# TypeScript SDK overview

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk

> Query objects, apply actions, and run functions from any TypeScript runtime with @osdk/client, in Node.js scripts, servers, Vue, or any framework.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [TypeScript OSDK](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/ontology-sdk/typescript-osdk)

`@osdk/client` reads and edits your Ontology from any JavaScript runtime with `fetch`: Node.js scripts and servers, serverless functions, and browser apps in any framework. It has no UI dependency. Your generated SDK supplies typed definitions for your object types, interfaces, actions, and functions, and the client runs them.

## Install

Your generated SDK comes from your Foundry npm registry. Set up `.npmrc` as described in [Installation](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/installation.md), then:

```npm
npm install @osdk/client @osdk/api @osdk/oauth @my-app/sdk@latest
```

Create one client for your app with `createClient`, as described in [Create a client](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/client.md). [Authentication](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/authentication.md) covers the token provider. The samples in this section import that client from `./client`.

## Example

```ts title="src/index.ts"
import { Employee, modifyEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const page = await client(Employee)
  .where({ department: "Engineering", jobTitle: { $isNull: true } })
  .fetchPage({ $select: ["fullName"], $pageSize: 20 });

for (const employee of page.data) {
  await client(modifyEmployee).applyAction({ employee, jobTitle: "Engineer" });
  console.log(`Set title for ${employee.fullName}`);
}
```

The query runs on the server and returns typed objects. Each `applyAction` call validates and applies one edit. In real code, wrap it in `try`/`catch`, as shown in [Actions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/actions.md).

## One entry point: `client(definition)`

Call `client` with a definition from your SDK. What it returns depends on the definition:

| You pass | You get | Main methods |
| --- | --- | --- |
| An object type, such as `Employee` | An object set of every object of that type | `fetchOne`, `fetchPage`, `asyncIter`, `where`, `aggregate`, `pivotTo`, `withProperties`, `subscribe` |
| An interface, such as `Worker` | An object set over every type that implements it | The same, except `fetchOne` |
| An action, such as `modifyEmployee` | An action invoker | `applyAction`, `batchApplyAction` |
| A function (query) | A function invoker | `executeFunction` |

Object sets are lazy descriptions. `where`, `pivotTo`, `union`, and `withProperties` return new object sets without sending a request. A request goes out when you call a method that loads data: `fetchOne`, `fetchPage`, `asyncIter`, `aggregate`, or `subscribe`.

`client.fetchMetadata(definition)` loads the definition from Foundry at runtime, such as an object type's `displayName`, `description`, and `icon`, or an interface's `implementedBy`.

## Relation to `@osdk/react`

`@osdk/react` is built on this client. Its hooks accept the same `where` clauses, derived property definitions, and action parameters, and add a shared cache that keeps components current after actions and live updates. In a React app, use the hooks for data you render and call the client directly for one-off work, such as exports. See [Objects in React](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/objects.md).

Outside React, framework guides show how to wire the client in [Node.js](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/frameworks/node.md) and [Vue](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/frameworks/vue.md).

## In this section

- [Load objects](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/objects.md): fetchOne, fetchPage, asyncIter, $select, sorting, and the object shape.
- [Filter objects](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/filtering.md): Every where operator, with examples.
- [Links and object sets](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/links.md): Follow links, pivot sets, and combine them.
- [Interfaces](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/interfaces.md): Query across object types and convert between views.
- [Aggregations](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/aggregations.md): Counts, metrics, and group-bys on the server.
- [Derived properties](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/derived-properties.md): Compute properties at query time with withProperties.
- [Actions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/actions.md): Apply, validate, and batch edits.
- [Functions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/functions.md): Run Foundry functions and read their results.
- [Attachments and media](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/media.md): Download and upload files.
- [Subscriptions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/subscriptions.md): Receive live updates for an object set.
- [Errors](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/errors.md): Error types, retries, and handling patterns.

# Interfaces

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/interfaces

> Query objects of every type that implements an interface, convert between interface and object views with $as, and narrow object sets with narrowToType.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Interfaces](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/interfaces/interface-overview)

An interface describes properties that several object types share. Querying an interface returns objects of every type that implements it, viewed through the interface's properties. You can then convert each object to its concrete type.

In the example SDK, the interface `Worker` has one property, `name`. `Employee` implements it, with `fullName` as `name`.

## Query an interface

`client(Worker)` is an object set over every object that implements `Worker`. Filter, sort, and select by the interface's property names:

```ts title="src/workers.ts"
import { Worker } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const page = await client(Worker)
  .where({ name: { $startsWith: "ada" } })
  .fetchPage({ $select: ["name"], $orderBy: { name: "asc" }, $pageSize: 50 });

for (const worker of page.data) {
  console.log(worker.$objectType, worker.$primaryKey, worker.name);
}
```

On an interface object, `$apiName` is the interface (`"Worker"`) and `$objectType` is the object's concrete type (`"Employee"`). `$primaryKey` is the concrete object's primary key.

## What an interface object set supports

| Method | Supported | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `where` | Yes | On interface property names. |
| `fetchPage`, `fetchPageWithErrors`, `asyncIter` | Yes | Accept `$includeAllBaseObjectProperties`. |
| `aggregate` | Yes | On interface property names. |
| `subscribe` | Yes | See [Subscriptions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/subscriptions.md). |
| `narrowToType` | Yes | Converts to an object type set. See below. |
| `pivotTo` | Yes | For links defined on the interface. |
| `union`, `intersect`, `subtract` | With other sets of the same interface | Not with object type sets. Narrow first. |
| `fetchOne`, `fetchOneWithErrors` | No | Typed `never`. A primary key is unique only within one object type, so load by key from the object type: `client(Employee).fetchOne(id)`. |

## Convert one object with `$as`

`$as(Employee)` returns the concrete view of an interface object, with the object type's property names. `$as(Worker)` goes the other way:

```ts title="src/workerDetails.ts"
import { Employee, Worker } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const page = await client(Worker).fetchPage({ $pageSize: 20 });

for (const worker of page.data) {
  if (worker.$objectType === "Employee") {
    const employee = worker.$as(Employee);
    console.log(employee.fullName);
  }
}

const employee = await client(Employee).fetchOne(12345);
const asWorker = employee.$as(Worker);
console.log(asWorker.name);
```

`$as` makes no request. It only exposes the properties that were loaded:

- From an interface fetch, the concrete view has only the properties that the interface maps to, such as `fullName`. Reading `salary` is a type error.
- To get every property of the object type, pass `$includeAllBaseObjectProperties: true` to `fetchPage` or `asyncIter`. Then `$as(Employee)` has all `Employee` properties.

```ts title="src/fullEmployees.ts"
import { Employee, Worker } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const page = await client(Worker).fetchPage({ $includeAllBaseObjectProperties: true });

for (const worker of page.data) {
  if (worker.$objectType === "Employee") {
    const employee = worker.$as(Employee);
    console.log(employee.fullName, employee.salary, employee.department);
  }
}
```

`$includeAllBaseObjectProperties` cannot be combined with `$select`.

`$as` throws when:

- The target is an object type other than the object's own. Check `$objectType` first, as above.
- The target interface is not implemented by the object type.
- Converting an interface object to its object type, when one of the interface's properties is implemented by something other than a plain property of the object type. The message tells you to load the object type directly.

## Convert an object set with `narrowToType`

`narrowToType` converts a whole object set on the server, and keeps only objects of the given type:

```ts title="src/narrow.ts"
import { Employee, Worker } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const engineers = await client(Worker)
  .where({ name: { $startsWith: "a" } })
  .narrowToType(Employee)
  .where({ department: "Engineering" })
  .fetchPage({ $select: ["fullName", "jobTitle"] });

const workersInSales = client(Employee).where({ department: "Sales" }).narrowToType(Worker);
```

From an interface, pass a type that implements it. From an object type, pass an interface it implements. Other types do not typecheck.

## Read interface metadata

`client.fetchMetadata(Worker)` loads the interface definition from Foundry, including `implementedBy`, the API names of the object types that implement it:

```ts title="src/workerMetadata.ts"
import { Worker } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const metadata = await client.fetchMetadata(Worker);
console.log(metadata.displayName, metadata.implementedBy);
```

## Pass interface objects to actions

An action parameter of an interface type takes a plain object with the concrete type and primary key, such as `{ $objectType: worker.$objectType, $primaryKey: worker.$primaryKey }`. Pass that object, not the loaded `worker` itself. See [Actions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/actions.md#parameter-values).

# Links and object sets

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/links

> Traverse links from an object with $link, pivot whole object sets with pivotTo, and combine object sets with union, intersect, and subtract.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Link types](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/object-link-types/link-types-overview)

Links connect objects of one type to objects of another, such as an `Employee` to their `Office`. You can follow a link from one loaded object with `$link`, or from a whole object set with `pivotTo`. Object sets also combine with `union`, `intersect`, and `subtract`, all on the server.

In the example SDK, `Employee` has three links: `lead` (one `Employee`), `reports` (many `Employee`), and `office` (one `Office`). `Office` has `occupants` (many `Employee`).

## Follow a link from an object

Every object has a `$link` field with one entry per link type. What the entry is depends on the link's cardinality:

| Link | `$link` entry | Methods |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One, such as `office` | A single-link accessor | `fetchOne(options?)`, `fetchOneWithErrors(options?)` |
| Many, such as `reports` | An object set of the linked type | Everything an object set has: `where`, `fetchPage`, `asyncIter`, `aggregate`, `pivotTo`, and more |

### One-to-one and many-to-one links

```ts title="src/employeeOffice.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const employee = await client(Employee).fetchOne(12345);

const office = await employee.$link.office.fetchOne({ $select: ["name", "city"] });
console.log(`${employee.fullName} works in ${office.name}, ${office.city}`);
```

`fetchOne` takes `$select` and `$includeRid`. It rejects when the object has no linked object, with a `PalantirApiError` whose message is `Expected a single result but got 0 instead`. If the link is optional, use `fetchOneWithErrors` and check the result:

```ts title="src/employeeLead.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { isOk } from "@osdk/client";
import { client } from "./client";

const employee = await client(Employee).fetchOne(12345);
const lead = await employee.$link.lead.fetchOneWithErrors({ $select: ["fullName"] });

console.log(isOk(lead) ? `Reports to ${lead.value.fullName}` : "No lead");
```

### One-to-many and many-to-many links

A many link is an object set, so you can filter, sort, page, and aggregate it before loading anything:

```ts title="src/directReports.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const lead = await client(Employee).fetchOne(12345);

const engineers = await lead.$link.reports
  .where({ department: "Engineering" })
  .fetchPage({ $select: ["fullName", "jobTitle"], $orderBy: { fullName: "asc" } });

const { $count } = await lead.$link.reports.aggregate({ $select: { $count: "unordered" } });
console.log(`${engineers.data.length} engineers of ${$count} reports`);
```

`$link` sends no request until you call a load method. You do not need to `$select` anything for `$link` to work: the link resolves from the object's primary key.

## Pivot an object set

`pivotTo(link)` returns the set of objects linked to any object in the source set. Use it to traverse links for many objects in one request instead of one request per object:

```ts title="src/engineeringOffices.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const offices = await client(Employee)
  .where({ department: "Engineering" })
  .pivotTo("office")
  .fetchPage({ $select: ["name", "city"] });
```

The result has no duplicates: an office with ten engineers appears once. Pivots chain, and the result is a full object set:

```ts title="src/skipLevel.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const skipLevelReports = client(Employee)
  .where({ employeeId: 12345 })
  .pivotTo("reports")
  .pivotTo("reports");

const result = await skipLevelReports
  .where({ jobTitle: { $containsAnyTerm: "manager" } })
  .aggregate({ $select: { $count: "unordered" } });
```

The link name must exist on the source type. `pivotTo("occupants")` on an `Employee` set does not typecheck.

## Combine object sets

`union`, `intersect`, and `subtract` take one or more object sets of the same type and return a new object set. Nothing loads until you call a load method:

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `a.union(b, c)` | Objects in any of the sets. |
| `a.intersect(b, c)` | Objects in every set. |
| `a.subtract(b, c)` | Objects in `a` that are in none of the other sets. |

```ts title="src/promotionCandidates.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const longTenure = client(Employee).where({ startDate: { $lt: "2020-01-01" } });
const highRated = client(Employee).where({ jobTitle: { $containsAnyTerm: "senior" } });
const leads = client(Employee).where({ employeeId: { $in: [101, 102] } }).pivotTo("lead");

const candidates = longTenure.intersect(highRated).subtract(leads);

const page = await candidates.fetchPage({ $select: ["fullName", "jobTitle"] });
```

The sets must be of the same object type. An `Employee` set and a `Worker` interface set do not combine; see [Interfaces](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/interfaces.md) to convert between them with `narrowToType`.

## Load links in bulk

`experimental_asyncIterLinks(links)` iterates over the links of every object in a set and yields `{ source, target, linkType }`, where `source` and `target` carry `$apiName` and `$primaryKey`. It is experimental and may change. Use it to build an in-memory graph:

```ts title="src/orgChart.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const managerOf = new Map<number, number>();

for await (const { source, target } of client(Employee).experimental_asyncIterLinks(["lead"])) {
  managerOf.set(source.$primaryKey, target.$primaryKey);
}
```

Limits:

- Links can be stale: a returned primary key may no longer exist.
- The server loads source objects in pages. If one page has more than 100,000 links, the result for that page is cut off at 100,000.
- Object Storage V1 links are not supported and throw.
- Interface links are not supported.

## In React

`@osdk/react` wraps these calls in hooks that cache and update: `useLinks` for `$link`, and `useObjectSet` for pivots and set operations. See [Links in React](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/links.md) and [Object sets in React](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/object-sets.md).

# Attachments and media

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/media

> Read attachment and media reference properties with fetchContents and fetchMetadata, and upload files by passing them to action parameters.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Media set API](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/api/v2/media-sets-v2-resources/media-sets/media-set-basics)

Objects store files in two property types. Attachment properties hold files uploaded through actions. Media reference properties point to items in a Foundry media set, such as images, documents, audio, and video. Both load lazily: the object holds a handle, and you download the content when you need it.

The samples assume `Employee` has an attachment property `resume` and a media reference property `photo`, and that an action `updateEmployeeFiles` takes `employee`, `resume` (attachment), and `photo` (media reference).

## Read an attachment

An attachment property is an `Attachment`:

| Member | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rid` | `string` | The attachment RID. |
| `fetchMetadata()` | `Promise<AttachmentMetadata>` | Loads `rid`, `filename`, `sizeBytes`, and `mediaType`. |
| `fetchContents()` | `Promise<Response>` | Downloads the file. Read it with `blob()`, `arrayBuffer()`, or `text()`. |

```ts title="src/downloadResume.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const employee = await client(Employee).fetchOne(12345, { $select: ["resume"] });

if (employee.resume != null) {
  const metadata = await employee.resume.fetchMetadata();
  console.log(metadata.filename, metadata.mediaType, metadata.sizeBytes);

  const response = await employee.resume.fetchContents();
  if (response.ok) {
    const blob = await response.blob();
    console.log(`Downloaded ${blob.size} bytes`);
  }
}
```

## Read a media reference

A media reference property is a `Media`:

| Member | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fetchMetadata()` | `Promise<MediaMetadata>` | Loads `mediaType`, `sizeBytes`, and `path` when the item has one. |
| `fetchFullMetadata?()` | `Promise<MediaFullMetadata>` | Loads type-specific metadata, such as page count for documents and dimensions for images. Optional in the type, but every `Media` the client returns has it. |
| `fetchContents()` | `Promise<Response>` | Downloads the item. |
| `getMediaReference()` | `MediaReference` | The reference itself: the MIME type and the media set item it points to. Pass it to an action or function. |

```ts title="src/employeePhoto.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const employee = await client(Employee).fetchOne(12345, { $select: ["photo"] });

const metadata = await employee.photo?.fetchMetadata();
console.log(metadata?.mediaType, metadata?.sizeBytes);

const full = await employee.photo?.fetchFullMetadata?.();
if (full?.itemMetadata.type === "imagery") {
  console.log(full.itemMetadata.dimensions);
}

const response = await employee.photo?.fetchContents();
if (response?.ok) {
  const image = await response.blob();
}
```

`itemMetadata.type` is one of `"document"`, `"imagery"`, `"audio"`, `"video"`, `"dicom"`, `"email"`, `"model3d"`, `"spreadsheet"`, or `"untyped"`. When the server returns a type this client version does not know, `type` is `"unknown"` and the payload is on `raw`.

`fetchContents` resolves to a standard `Response`. A non-2xx status does not reject, so check `response.ok`.

## Upload through an action

The client does not write files to objects directly. Pass the file as an action parameter, and the client uploads it before it applies the action:

| Parameter type | Pass |
| --- | --- |
| Attachment | `createAttachmentUpload(blob, fileName)`, a `File`, or the RID of an existing attachment. |
| Media reference | A `MediaUpload` (`{ data: blob, fileName }`), a `Media` from another object, or a `MediaReference`. |

**Node.js**

```ts title="src/uploadFiles.ts"
import { updateEmployeeFiles } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { createAttachmentUpload, type MediaUpload } from "@osdk/client";
import { openAsBlob } from "node:fs";
import { client } from "./client";

const resume = await openAsBlob("./resume.pdf", { type: "application/pdf" });
const photo: MediaUpload = {
  data: await openAsBlob("./photo.png", { type: "image/png" }),
  fileName: "photo.png",
};

await client(updateEmployeeFiles).applyAction({
  employee: 12345,
  resume: createAttachmentUpload(resume, "resume.pdf"),
  photo,
});
```

`openAsBlob` needs Node.js 19.8 or later.
**Browser**

```ts title="src/uploadFiles.ts"
import { updateEmployeeFiles } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

export async function uploadResume(employeeId: number, input: HTMLInputElement) {
  const file = input.files?.[0];
  if (file == null) {
    return;
  }
  await client(updateEmployeeFiles).applyAction({ employee: employeeId, resume: file });
}
```

A `File` from an `<input type="file">` already has a name, so you can pass it as is.

To reuse a file that is already in Foundry, pass its handle instead of uploading again:

```ts title="src/copyPhoto.ts"
import { Employee, updateEmployeeFiles } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const source = await client(Employee).fetchOne(12345, { $select: ["resume", "photo"] });

await client(updateEmployeeFiles).applyAction({
  employee: 67890,
  resume: source.resume?.rid,
  photo: source.photo,
});
```

Uploads are temporary until an action links them to an object. If the action fails, or you never apply one, Foundry deletes the uploaded file after one hour.

Functions accept the same values for attachment and media reference parameters. See [Functions](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/functions.md#parameter-values).

# Load objects

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/objects

> Load one object by primary key, page through object sets, iterate over every object, select properties, sort, and read the Osdk.Instance shape.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Object types](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/object-link-types/object-types-overview)

An object set from `client(Employee)` loads objects in three ways: one object by primary key, one page at a time, or every object with an async iterator. This page covers each method, its options, and the shape of the objects it returns.

The samples import a client from `./client`. See [Create a client](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/client.md) to set one up.

## Load one object

`fetchOne` takes a primary key and resolves to the object:

```ts title="src/getEmployee.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const employee = await client(Employee).fetchOne(12345, {
  $select: ["fullName", "jobTitle", "department"],
});

console.log(employee.$primaryKey, employee.fullName, employee.jobTitle);
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$select` | `PropertyKeys[]` | The API's default property set | Properties to load. The primary key is always returned. |
| `$includeRid` | `boolean` | `false` | Adds `$rid` to the returned object. |

`fetchOne` rejects when no object has that primary key, or when you cannot see it. The error is a `PalantirApiError` with the message `Expected a single result but got 0 instead` and no `statusCode` or `errorName`.

`fetchOne` exists only on object types. Interface object sets do not have it; see [Interfaces](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/interfaces.md).

### Without exceptions

`fetchOneWithErrors` takes the same arguments and resolves to a `Result` instead of rejecting. Narrow it with `isOk`:

```ts title="src/getEmployee.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { isOk } from "@osdk/client";
import { client } from "./client";

const result = await client(Employee).fetchOneWithErrors(12345, {
  $select: ["fullName"],
});

if (isOk(result)) {
  console.log(result.value.fullName);
} else {
  console.error("Could not load employee", result.error.message);
}
```

A `Result` is either `{ value }` or `{ error }`, where `error` is an `Error`. See [Errors](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/errors.md) for the error types.

## Load a page

`fetchPage` resolves to one page of objects:

```ts title="src/listEngineers.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const page = await client(Employee)
  .where({ department: "Engineering" })
  .fetchPage({
    $select: ["fullName", "jobTitle", "startDate"],
    $orderBy: { startDate: "desc" },
    $pageSize: 50,
  });

for (const employee of page.data) {
  console.log(employee.fullName, employee.jobTitle);
}
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$select` | `PropertyKeys[]` | The API's default property set | Properties to load. See [Select properties](#select-properties). |
| `$orderBy` | `{ [property]: "asc" \| "desc" } \| "relevance"` | Unordered | Sort order. See [Sort](#sort). |
| `$pageSize` | `number` | Server default | Objects in this page. It does not limit the total; continue with `nextPageToken`. |
| `$nextPageToken` | `string` | | The `nextPageToken` from the previous page. |
| `$snapshot` | `boolean` | `false` | Pages through one consistent view of the data. See [Paging and consistency](#paging-and-consistency). |
| `$includeRid` | `boolean` | `false` | Adds `$rid` to each object. |
| `$includeAllBaseObjectProperties` | `boolean` | `false` | Interface object sets only. Loads every property of the underlying object type. See [Interfaces](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/interfaces.md). |

The page has three fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `Osdk.Instance[]` | The objects in this page. |
| `nextPageToken` | `string \| undefined` | Pass as `$nextPageToken` to load the next page. `undefined` on the last page. |
| `totalCount` | `string` | The number of objects in the set, as a string. |

`fetchPageWithErrors` takes the same options and resolves to a `Result` of the page instead of rejecting.

### Page through results

Pass each page's `nextPageToken` into the next request until it is `undefined`:

```ts title="src/allEngineers.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const engineers = client(Employee).where({ department: "Engineering" });

let nextPageToken: string | undefined;
do {
  const page = await engineers.fetchPage({
    $select: ["fullName"],
    $pageSize: 100,
    $nextPageToken: nextPageToken,
    $snapshot: true,
  });
  for (const employee of page.data) {
    console.log(employee.fullName);
  }
  nextPageToken = page.nextPageToken;
} while (nextPageToken != null);
```

Keep the other options the same on every page. Only `$nextPageToken` changes.

## Load every object

`asyncIter` loads page after page until it has every object in the set, and yields them one at a time:

```ts title="src/countSkills.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const skillCounts = new Map<string, number>();

for await (const employee of client(Employee).asyncIter({ $select: ["skills"] })) {
  for (const skill of employee.skills ?? []) {
    skillCounts.set(skill, (skillCounts.get(skill) ?? 0) + 1);
  }
}
```

`asyncIter` accepts `$select`, `$orderBy`, `$includeRid`, and `$includeAllBaseObjectProperties`. It requests pages of 10,000 objects and always requests a snapshot.

Before you iterate over a large object type:

- Pass `$select` with only the properties you read. Loading unused properties costs bandwidth and server time, and reading fewer properties afterwards does not undo it.
- Handle each object as it arrives. Collecting every object into an array makes memory grow with the size of the set.
- For counts, sums, and group-bys, use [`aggregate`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/aggregations.md). It runs on the server and loads no objects.
- For a sample or the first N objects, use `fetchPage` with `$pageSize`.

## Paging and consistency

| Method | Loads | Snapshot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fetchPage({ $pageSize })` | One page. Continue with `nextPageToken`. | Only with `$snapshot: true`, passed on every page. |
| `asyncIter()` | Every matching object, page after page. | Always. |
| `aggregate({ ... })` | Counts, sums, and groups only. | Not applicable. |

Without a snapshot, later pages can repeat or skip objects if objects are added, removed, or edited between requests. A snapshot configured for a function run still applies, whatever you pass.

With a snapshot, every page of a non-stream-backed object type reflects the same point in time, so a completed traversal returns each object exactly once. Paging fails if the snapshot expires or the server detects a paging inconsistency (`PagingInconsistencyDetected`). Stream-backed object types do not keep a snapshot across pages: changes during a traversal can make it fail, and exactly-once traversal is not guaranteed.

If an `asyncIter` traversal of a frequently updated object type fails:

1. Aggregate instead, if you only need a summary.
2. Select fewer properties and filter the set so the traversal finishes sooner.
3. Loop over `fetchPage` without a snapshot and de-duplicate by `$primaryKey`. De-duplication removes repeated objects but cannot recover skipped ones.

## Select properties

Without `$select`, the server returns its default property set for the object type. Vector properties, for example, are not in it. With `$select`, the result type narrows to the properties you asked for, so reading anything else is a type error:

```ts title="src/names.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import type { Osdk } from "@osdk/client";
import { client } from "./client";

const page = await client(Employee).fetchPage({ $select: ["fullName", "department"] });

const first: Osdk.Instance<Employee, never, "fullName" | "department"> = page.data[0];
console.log(first.fullName, first.department);
```

Rules for `$select`:

- The primary key is always returned, as a property and as `$primaryKey`.
- Ontology-defined derived properties are not returned by default. Name them in `$select`.
- Derived properties you add with [`withProperties`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/derived-properties.md) are returned when `$select` is omitted. If you pass `$select`, name them in it too.

## Sort

`$orderBy` maps property names to `"asc"` or `"desc"`. With several keys, the first key sorts first and later keys break ties:

```ts title="src/directory.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const page = await client(Employee).fetchPage({
  $select: ["department", "fullName"],
  $orderBy: { department: "asc", fullName: "asc" },
  $pageSize: 100,
});
```

When you pass `$select`, every `$orderBy` key must also be in `$select`. Otherwise the call does not typecheck.

`$orderBy: "relevance"` sorts by how well each object matches the text filters in your `where` clause, and adds a numeric `$score` to each object:

```ts title="src/search.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const page = await client(Employee)
  .where({ jobTitle: { $containsAnyTerm: "staff engineer" } })
  .fetchPage({ $orderBy: "relevance", $pageSize: 10 });

for (const employee of page.data) {
  console.log(employee.$score, employee.jobTitle);
}
```

## The object shape

Each object is an `Osdk.Instance`: its properties plus a few `$` fields. Objects are frozen, so assigning to a property throws in strict mode.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$primaryKey` | The primary key type | The object's primary key, such as `12345`. |
| `$apiName` | `string` | The API name of the type you queried: the object type, or the interface for interface queries. |
| `$objectType` | `string` | The API name of the object's concrete object type. Differs from `$apiName` on interface objects. |
| `$title` | `string \| undefined` | The value of the object type's title property. |
| `$rid` | `string` | The object's RID. Present only when you pass `$includeRid: true`. |
| `$objectSpecifier` | `string` | A string that identifies the object across types. |
| `$link` | `object` | Accessors for linked objects. See [Links](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/links.md). |
| `$as` | `(type) => Osdk.Instance` | Views the object as an interface it implements, or an interface object as its object type. See [Interfaces](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/interfaces.md). |
| `$clone` | `(changes?) => Osdk.Instance` | Returns a copy, optionally with some property values replaced. |

Nullable properties are typed `T | undefined`. Property values use these TypeScript types:

| Property type | TypeScript type |
| --- | --- |
| `string` | `string` |
| `integer`, `short`, `byte`, `float`, `double` | `number` |
| `long`, `decimal` | `string` |
| `boolean` | `boolean` |
| `date`, `timestamp` | `string`, in ISO 8601 format |
| Array properties | `T[]` |
| `geopoint` | GeoJSON `Point` |
| `geoshape` | GeoJSON geometry |
| `attachment` | `Attachment`. See [Attachments and media](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/media.md). |
| `mediaReference` | `Media`. See [Attachments and media](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/media.md). |

### Copy with changes

`$clone` builds a new local object. It does not write to Foundry; use an [action](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/actions.md) for that. It throws if the changes include a different primary key:

```ts title="src/preview.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const employee = await client(Employee).fetchOne(12345);
const preview = employee.$clone({ jobTitle: "Senior Engineer" });

console.log(employee.jobTitle, "->", preview.jobTitle);
```

### Type objects in your code

Use `Osdk.Instance<Employee>` from `@osdk/client`, or the generated alias `Employee.OsdkInstance`. Narrow the properties with the third type argument, and add `"$rid"` as the second to include the RID:

```ts title="src/types.ts"
import type { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import type { Osdk } from "@osdk/client";

type FullEmployee = Osdk.Instance<Employee>;
type EmployeeName = Osdk.Instance<Employee, never, "fullName">;
type EmployeeWithRid = Osdk.Instance<Employee, "$rid", "fullName" | "jobTitle">;

function label(employee: EmployeeName): string {
  return employee.fullName ?? String(employee.$primaryKey);
}
```

A function that takes `Osdk.Instance<Employee, never, "fullName">` accepts any `Employee` loaded with at least `fullName`.

# Subscriptions

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/subscriptions

> Receive live updates when objects in an object set are added, changed, or removed, with subscribe, its four callbacks, and unsubscribe.

Related Palantir Foundry documentation:
- [Subscribe to Ontology changes](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/ontology-sdk/typescript-subscriptions)

`subscribe` opens a live connection to an object set. The server pushes each change to an object in the set, so you can keep a local copy current without polling.

```ts title="src/watchEngineers.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { client } from "./client";

const subscription = client(Employee)
  .where({ department: "Engineering" })
  .subscribe(
    {
      onChange(update) {
        console.log(update.state, update.object.$primaryKey, update.object.fullName);
      },
      onSuccessfulSubscription() {
        console.log("Subscribed");
      },
      onOutOfDate() {
        console.log("Missed changes; reload the set");
      },
      onError({ subscriptionClosed, error }) {
        console.error("Subscription error", { subscriptionClosed, error });
      },
    },
    { properties: ["fullName", "jobTitle"] },
  );

subscription.unsubscribe();
```

`subscribe` works on any object set, including filtered sets, pivots, and [interfaces](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/sdk/interfaces.md). It returns immediately with `{ unsubscribe }`; the connection opens in the background.

## Callbacks

All callbacks are optional.

| Callback | Called when |
| --- | --- |
| `onSuccessfulSubscription()` | The server accepted the subscription. Changes from here on reach `onChange`. |
| `onChange(update)` | An object in the set changed. See [Updates](#updates). |
| `onOutOfDate()` | The client cannot account for every change, for example after the connection dropped and reconnected. Reload the whole set. |
| `onError({ subscriptionClosed, error })` | Something failed. When `subscriptionClosed` is `true`, no more updates arrive. When it is `false`, the subscription continues. |

An exception thrown inside `onChange` or another callback does not stop the subscription. The client reports it to `onError` with `subscriptionClosed: false`. If `onError` itself throws, the client closes the subscription.

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `properties` | `PropertyKeys[]` | Every property of the type | The properties to receive. `update.object` is typed to these. |
| `includeRid` | `boolean` | `false` | Adds `$rid` to each updated object. Not available when `properties` includes a geotime series reference property. |

Request only the properties you display. Without `properties`, each update can carry every property of the type.

## Updates

`onChange` receives `{ object, state }`:

| `state` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `"ADDED_OR_UPDATED"` | The object was created, was edited, or now matches the set's filter. `object` has the latest values of the subscribed properties. |
| `"REMOVED"` | The object was deleted, or no longer matches the filter. Drop it by `$primaryKey`. |

Updates to a geotime series reference property arrive as separate updates that carry only the primary key and that property. Merge each update into your copy of the object rather than replacing it, so a property missing from an update keeps its last value.

## Keep a local copy current

Load the set once the subscription is live, apply each change, and reload on `onOutOfDate`:

```ts title="src/liveRoster.ts"
import { Employee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import type { Osdk } from "@osdk/client";
import { client } from "./client";

type Row = Osdk.Instance<Employee, never, "fullName" | "jobTitle">;

const engineers = client(Employee).where({ department: "Engineering" });
const roster = new Map<number, Row>();

async function reload() {
  roster.clear();
  for await (const employee of engineers.asyncIter({ $select: ["fullName", "jobTitle"] })) {
    roster.set(employee.$primaryKey, employee);
  }
}

const subscription = engineers.subscribe(
  {
    onSuccessfulSubscription() {
      void reload();
    },
    onOutOfDate() {
      void reload();
    },
    onChange({ object, state }) {
      if (state === "REMOVED") {
        roster.delete(object.$primaryKey);
        return;
      }
      const existing = roster.get(object.$primaryKey);
      roster.set(object.$primaryKey, existing == null ? object : existing.$clone(object));
    },
    onError({ subscriptionClosed, error }) {
      if (subscriptionClosed) {
        console.error("Roster is no longer live", error);
      }
    },
  },
  { properties: ["fullName", "jobTitle"] },
);
```

Loading after `onSuccessfulSubscription`, not before, means a change made while the first load runs still reaches `onChange`.

## Connection

All subscriptions from one client share a single WebSocket. When the connection drops, the client reconnects with exponential backoff, resubscribes, and calls `onOutOfDate` on each subscription it restored. In Node.js, the client uses the `ws` package, so no polyfill is needed.

Call `unsubscribe` when you no longer need updates, such as when a component unmounts or a request handler finishes. An open subscription keeps the connection open.

## In React

`useOsdkObjects` and `useObjectSet` accept `streamUpdates: true`, which subscribes for you and writes each change into the shared cache. See [Objects in React](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/react/objects.md).

# ActionForm

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/components/action-form

> ActionForm renders form fields from an OSDK action definition, validates input in the browser, and applies the action on submit.

## Import

```typescript
import { ActionForm } from "@osdk/react-components/action-form";
import type {
  ActionFormContentItem,
  FormFieldDefinition,
} from "@osdk/react-components/action-form";
```

## Basic Usage

> [!NOTE]
> `@my-app/sdk` is a placeholder for your generated SDK package. `./client` (used in scoped object-select examples below) is the file in your app where you exported the OSDK client returned by `createClient(...)`. Replace both with the actual paths in your project.

```tsx
import { updateEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { ActionForm } from "@osdk/react-components/action-form";

function UpdateEmployeeForm() {
  return <ActionForm actionDefinition={updateEmployee} />;
}
```

`ActionForm` fetches action metadata, renders fields for the action parameters, runs client-side validation, and calls the OSDK action when the user submits. The form title is hidden by default. Pass `showFormTitle={true}` to show it; the title uses `formTitle` when provided, otherwise the action display name, otherwise the action API name.

## Props Reference

`ActionForm` is a discriminated union: provide both `formState` and `onFormStateChange` for controlled mode, or omit both for uncontrolled mode.

<!-- AUTOGEN:props START src=src/action-form/ActionFormApi.ts interface=ActionFormProps — generated by scripts/gen-props.mjs; run `pnpm --filter @osdk/react-components gen-props` -->

Type parameters: `Q extends ActionDefinition<unknown>`

| Name                     | Type                                                                                                                                        | Description                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `formTitle`              | `string`                                                                                                                                    | Title shown in the form header. Omit to hide the header.                                                                                                             |
| `isSubmitDisabled`       | `boolean`                                                                                                                                   | Whether the submit button is disabled. Default `false`.                                                                                                              |
| `actionDefinition`       | `Q`                                                                                                                                         | **Required.** The OSDK action definition. Its parameters drive the rendered fields and the submission.                                                               |
| `showFormTitle`          | `boolean`                                                                                                                                   | Whether to show the form title. Defaults to `false`.                                                                                                                 |
| `onSubmit`               | `(formState: FormState<Q>, applyAction: (formState: FormState<Q>) => Promise<ActionEditResponse \| undefined>) => Promise<unknown> \| void` | If supplied, this will override the default submit action. By default, the action's applyAction will be called.                                                      |
| `onValidationResponse`   | `(results: ActionValidationResponse) => void`                                                                                               | Called when the validation response is returned from a validateOnly submission                                                                                       |
| `onSuccess`              | `(results: ActionEditResponse \| undefined) => void`                                                                                        | Called when the action is successfully executed from a non-validateOnly submission                                                                                   |
| `onError`                | `(error: FormError) => void`                                                                                                                | Called when action metadata fails to load or form submission fails.                                                                                                  |
| `formFieldDefinitions`   | `ReadonlyArray<FormFieldDefinition<Q>>`                                                                                                     | Custom flat list of field definitions.                                                                                                                               |
| `formContentDefinitions` | `ReadonlyArray<ActionFormContentItem<Q>>`                                                                                                   | Ordered list of fields and sections that define the form layout.                                                                                                     |
| `formState`              | `FormState<Q>`                                                                                                                              | The current form values. If provided, the form state is controlled.                                                                                                  |
| `onFormStateChange`      | `(updater: (prevState: FormState<Q>) => FormState<Q>) => void`                                                                              | Called when a field value changes, with a state updater. Required when the form state is controlled; also fires in uncontrolled mode so callers can observe changes. |

<!-- AUTOGEN:props END -->

## Choosing ActionForm vs BaseForm

| Use case                                                                 | Use this API                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| Render a form directly from an OSDK action and submit with `applyAction` | `ActionForm`                             |
| Override generated fields for an OSDK action                             | `ActionForm` with `formFieldDefinitions` |
| Build a form from manually-authored field definitions                    | `BaseForm`                               |
| Group an OSDK action's fields into sections, or order standalone fields | `ActionForm` with `formContentDefinitions` |
| Build a custom form layout without an OSDK action                        | `BaseForm`                               |

## Default Field Rendering

When `formFieldDefinitions` is omitted, `ActionForm` derives one field per action parameter from action metadata.

| Action parameter type                          | Default field component | Default behavior                               |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `string`                                       | `TEXT_INPUT`            | Single-line text input                         |
| `boolean`                                      | `RADIO_BUTTONS`         | True/False radio options                       |
| `integer`, `double`, `long`                    | `NUMBER_INPUT`          | Numeric input                                  |
| `datetime`, `timestamp`                        | `DATETIME_PICKER`       | Date picker                                    |
| `attachment`, `mediaReference`                 | `FILE_PICKER`           | File picker                                    |
| `{ type: "object" }`                           | `OBJECT_SELECT`         | Object selector for the referenced object type |
| `{ type: "objectSet" }`                        | `OBJECT_SET`            | Read-only object set summary                   |
| `marking`, `geohash`, `geoshape`, `objectType` | `UNSUPPORTED`           | Disabled field recommending a custom field     |
| `{ type: "interface" }`, `{ type: "struct" }`  | `UNSUPPORTED`           | Disabled field recommending a custom field     |

Required validation is inferred from the action parameter's nullability. Additional client-side validation comes from field-specific props such as `min`, `max`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, and `maxSize`.

## Unsupported Features

`ActionForm` is a lightweight OSDK component and does not yet match the full ActionForm in Foundry. The table below lists the main gaps to account for when adopting it.

| Feature                                     | Current behavior                                                                                                                                                                                              | Workaround                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Backend action validation                   | The form does not call backend validation before submit and does not process validation-derived displays, allowed values, defaults, or section results.                                                       | Use `formFieldDefinitions` validation props, field-level `validate`, `onSubmit`, and `onError` for app-owned checks and submission error handling.      |
| Unsupported generated parameter types       | `marking`, `geohash`, `geoshape`, `objectType`, `interface`, and `struct` render as disabled unsupported fields by default.                                                                                   | Override those parameters with `fieldComponent: "CUSTOM"` or another compatible component in `formFieldDefinitions`.                                    |
| Action-authored layout metadata             | Action-defined sections, form content ordering, section validation, and layout toggles are not read from metadata. Fields render in metadata parameter order unless fully replaced by `formFieldDefinitions`. | Group fields with `formContentDefinitions` sections, or control field order with `formFieldDefinitions`.                                                |
| Conditional logic and dynamic display state | Backend-driven hidden, disabled, required, and allowed-value rules are not evaluated as the user edits the form.                                                                                              | Encode static display state in field definitions, or manage dynamic state in your app and pass updated `formFieldDefinitions` / controlled `formState`. |
| Defaults and prefills                       | Backend prefills, type-class defaults, current timestamp defaults, and validation-derived default values are not applied automatically.                                                                       | Provide `defaultValue` in field definitions, seed controlled `formState`, or compute defaults in app code before rendering.                             |

## Custom Field Definitions

Use `formFieldDefinitions` when the default rendering for a parameter is not the UI you want. The list is a complete replacement: include every parameter that should appear in the form.

```tsx
const fields = [
  {
    fieldKey: "fullName",
    label: "Full name",
    fieldComponent: "TEXT_INPUT",
    fieldComponentProps: {
      placeholder: "Jane Doe",
      minLength: 2,
    },
  },
  {
    fieldKey: "yearsExperience",
    label: "Years of experience",
    fieldComponent: "NUMBER_INPUT",
    fieldComponentProps: {
      min: 0,
      max: 80,
    },
  },
  {
    fieldKey: "isRemote",
    label: "Remote employee",
    fieldComponent: "SWITCH",
    fieldComponentProps: {},
  },
] satisfies Array<FormFieldDefinition<typeof updateEmployee>>;

<ActionForm actionDefinition={updateEmployee} formFieldDefinitions={fields} />;
```

## Sections

Use `formContentDefinitions` instead of `formFieldDefinitions` to group fields into sections. Each item is either `{ type: "field", definition }` or `{ type: "section", key, definition }`, and items render in array order. Like `formFieldDefinitions`, the list replaces the generated fields.

```tsx
const content = [
  { type: "field", definition: fields[0] },
  {
    type: "section",
    key: "details",
    definition: {
      title: "Details",
      description: "Optional employment details",
      columnCount: 2,
      collapsedByDefault: true,
      fields: [fields[1], fields[2]],
    },
  },
] satisfies Array<ActionFormContentItem<typeof updateEmployee>>;

<ActionForm actionDefinition={updateEmployee} formContentDefinitions={content} />;
```

| Section option       | Default | Description                                                    |
| -------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `title`              |         | Section heading.                                               |
| `description`        |         | Text under the heading.                                        |
| `fields`             |         | The fields in the section.                                     |
| `collapsedByDefault` | `false` | Starts collapsed.                                              |
| `showTitleBar`       | `true`  | Shows the title bar.                                           |
| `columnCount`        | `1`     | `1` or `2` columns.                                            |
| `style`              | `"box"` | `"box"` renders a bordered card, `"minimal"` only the heading. |

### Rich dropdown labels

Use `itemToStringLabel` for the dropdown's text behavior: search matching, accessibility labels, fallback item keys, and default visual text. Add `renderItemLabel` when the visible label needs richer React content while preserving the same string behavior.

```tsx
const fields = [
  {
    fieldKey: "assigneeUserId",
    label: "Assignee",
    fieldComponent: "DROPDOWN",
    fieldComponentProps: {
      items: userIds,
      itemToStringLabel: (userId) => userNames[userId] ?? userId,
      renderItemLabel: (userId) => (
        <span>
          <strong>{userNames[userId] ?? userId}</strong>
          <span>{userTeams[userId]}</span>
        </span>
      ),
    },
  },
] satisfies Array<FormFieldDefinition<typeof updateEmployee>>;
```

### Scoped object select fields

`OBJECT_SELECT` can load options from either an object type or a pre-scoped object set. Pass `objectType` for an unfiltered selector, or pass `objectSet` to limit selectable options. The two are mutually exclusive. Search text is applied within the object set, and the current value is not automatically cleared when it is outside that set.

```tsx
import { Employee, updateEmployee } from "@my-app/sdk";
import { useMemo } from "react";
import client from "./client";

function UpdateEmployeeForm() {
  const marketingEmployees = useMemo(
    () => client(Employee).where({ department: "Marketing" }),
    [],
  );

  const fields = [
    {
      fieldKey: "manager",
      label: "Marketing manager",
      fieldComponent: "OBJECT_SELECT",
      fieldComponentProps: {
        objectSet: marketingEmployees,
        placeholder: "Search Marketing employees…",
      },
    },
  ] satisfies Array<FormFieldDefinition<typeof updateEmployee>>;

  return (
    <ActionForm
      actionDefinition={updateEmployee}
      formFieldDefinitions={fields}
    />
  );
}
```

For a completely custom field, use `fieldComponent: "CUSTOM"` and provide `customRenderer`:

```tsx
const fields = [
  {
    fieldKey: "approvalReason",
    label: "Approval reason",
    fieldComponent: "CUSTOM",
    fieldComponentProps: {
      customRenderer: ({ value, onChange }) => (
        <textarea
          value={value != null ? String(value) : ""}
          onChange={(event) => onChange?.(event.target.value)}
        />
      ),
    },
  },
] satisfies Array<FormFieldDefinition<typeof approveEmployee>>;

<ActionForm actionDefinition={approveEmployee} formFieldDefinitions={fields} />;
```

## Behavior Notes

- `formFieldDefinitions` replaces generated fields. Passing one custom field means only that field renders.
- Pass `formFieldDefinitions` or `formContentDefinitions`, not both.
- `fieldKey` must match the action parameter key; submitted form state uses the same keys.
- `fieldComponentProps` should not include `value`, `onChange`, or `id`; form state wiring provides those.
- Controlled mode requires both `formState` and `onFormStateChange`.
- Use `onSubmit` for custom submission behavior. If `onSubmit` is omitted, `ActionForm` calls `applyAction` and then `onSuccess`.

## Examples

### Controlled form state

```tsx
const [formState, setFormState] = useState({
  fullName: "Ada Lovelace",
  isRemote: true,
});

<ActionForm
  actionDefinition={updateEmployee}
  formState={formState}
  onFormStateChange={setFormState}
/>;
```

### Custom submit handling

```tsx
<ActionForm
  actionDefinition={updateEmployee}
  onSubmit={async (formState, applyAction) => {
    await applyAction(formState);
    showToast("Employee updated");
  }}
/>
```

## Styling

`ActionForm` is built on `BaseForm`, so the form layout and field styling use the same CSS variables documented in [CSSVariables.md](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/components/css-variables.md).

`ActionForm` does not add outer padding by default. Apply internal spacing by setting the form padding variables on the form or a wrapper element:

```css
.employeeForm {
  --osdk-form-content-padding-inline: calc(var(--osdk-surface-spacing) * 4);
  --osdk-form-content-padding-block: calc(var(--osdk-surface-spacing) * 4);
}
```

```tsx
<div className="employeeForm">
  <ActionForm actionDefinition={updateEmployee} />
</div>
```

Use `--osdk-form-content-padding-inline` to apply shared horizontal padding to the header, fields, and footer. Use `--osdk-form-content-padding-block` to control vertical padding for the form fields section. For card-style outer spacing, apply margin, border, background, and border radius to the wrapper rather than the form itself.

# AipAgentChat

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/components/aip-agent-chat

> AipAgentChat renders an AI chat interface backed by a Foundry language model through useChat from @osdk/react/experimental/aip.

Importing the component is sufficient. You do not need to import `useChat` or
`foundryModel` yourself.

## Import

```tsx
import {
  AipAgentChat,
  BaseAipAgentChat,
} from "@osdk/react-components/experimental/aip-agent-chat";
```

- **`AipAgentChat`** — Primary component for OSDK usage. Accepts a
  Foundry `PlatformClient` and an LMS model API name; constructs the
  language-model handle, drives `useChat`, and renders the chat UI.
- **`BaseAipAgentChat`** — Lower-level OSDK-agnostic component that
  accepts `messages`, `status`, and `onSendMessage` directly. Use this
  when you already manage chat state yourself (a custom hook, a
  non-OSDK backend, etc.).

## Basic Usage

### Minimal Example

The simplest way to use `AipAgentChat` is with just a platform client;
`model` and `defaultModel` are both optional and fall back to `"gpt-4o"`:

```tsx
import { AipAgentChat } from "@osdk/react-components/experimental/aip-agent-chat";
import { platformClient } from "./foundryClient.js";

<AipAgentChat client={platformClient} />;
```

### Pinned model

```tsx
<AipAgentChat
  client={platformClient}
  model="gpt-4o"
  system="You are a concise assistant. Keep answers short."
/>
```

### With model picker (controlled)

```tsx
function MyChat() {
  const [model, setModel] = useState("gpt-4o");
  return (
    <AipAgentChat
      client={platformClient}
      model={model}
      availableModels={["gpt-4o", "AnthropicClaude_4_6_Sonnet"]}
      onModelChange={setModel}
    />
  );
}
```

### With model picker (uncontrolled)

```tsx
<AipAgentChat
  client={platformClient}
  defaultModel="gpt-4o"
  availableModels={["gpt-4o", "AnthropicClaude_4_6_Sonnet"]}
  onModelChange={(modelName) => analytics.track({ modelName })}
/>
```

The component manages model state internally; `onModelChange` is a
non-controlling listener (analytics, persistence, etc.).

### Custom render

```tsx
import {
  AipAgentChat,
  getUIMessageText,
  type UIMessage,
} from "@osdk/react-components/experimental/aip-agent-chat";

<AipAgentChat
  client={platformClient}
  model="gpt-4o"
  renderMessage={(message: UIMessage) => (
    <div>
      <strong>{message.role}:</strong> {getUIMessageText(message)}
    </div>
  )}
  renderEmptyState={() => <p>Ready when you are.</p>}
/>;
```

### Drop down to BaseAipAgentChat

`BaseAipAgentChat` is OSDK-agnostic — the consumer drives the chat by
passing the current `messages`, `status`, `error`, and an `onSendMessage`
callback that resolves once the user's message has been forwarded.
Use it for non-OSDK backends, custom transports, or unit tests.

```tsx
import {
  BaseAipAgentChat,
  type ChatStatus,
  type UIMessage,
} from "@osdk/react-components/experimental/aip-agent-chat";

function MyChat() {
  const [messages, setMessages] = useState<ReadonlyArray<UIMessage>>([]);
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<ChatStatus>("ready");
  const [error, setError] = useState<Error | undefined>();

  return (
    <BaseAipAgentChat
      messages={messages}
      status={status}
      error={error}
      onSendMessage={async (text) => {
        setStatus("submitted");
        try {
          const reply = await callMyBackend(text, { history: messages });
          setMessages((prev) => [
            ...prev,
            {
              id: crypto.randomUUID(),
              role: "user",
              parts: [{ type: "text", text }],
            },
            {
              id: crypto.randomUUID(),
              role: "assistant",
              parts: [{ type: "text", text: reply }],
            },
          ]);
          setStatus("ready");
        } catch (err) {
          setError(err as Error);
          setStatus("error");
        }
      }}
      onStop={() => setStatus("ready")}
      onClearError={() => setError(undefined)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Drop further: useChat directly

For full control over the chat hook (regenerate, custom transports), call
`useChat` from `@osdk/react/experimental/aip` yourself and feed the result
into your own UI. `useChat` is text-only: it does not run tools or multi-step
agent loops.

```tsx
import { foundryModel } from "@osdk/aip-core";
import { useChat } from "@osdk/react/experimental/aip";

function MyChat() {
  const lmsModel = useMemo(
    () => foundryModel({ client: platformClient, model: "gpt-4o" }),
    [],
  );
  const { messages, status, error, sendMessage, stop, clearError } = useChat({
    model: lmsModel,
  });

  return (
    <YourCustomChatLayout
      messages={messages}
      status={status}
      error={error}
      onSend={(text) => void sendMessage({ text })}
      onStop={stop}
      onClearError={clearError}
    />
  );
}
```

## Props Reference

See [`AipAgentChatApi.ts`](https://github.com/palantir/osdk-ts/blob/main/packages/react-components/src/aip-agent-chat/AipAgentChatApi.ts) for
the full prop list with JSDoc. `client` is the only required prop.
`model` (controlled) and `defaultModel` (uncontrolled) are both
optional; if neither is supplied the chat falls back to the first
entry of `availableModels` (when provided), or to `"gpt-4o"`. Notable
optional props:

- `availableModels` + `onModelChange` — render a model picker in the
  composer footer.
- `system` — system prompt prepended to every request.
- `initialMessages` — seed conversation snapshot.
- `enableAutoScroll` (default `true`) — auto-pin to the bottom of the
  message list as new tokens arrive.
- `renderEmptyState` / `renderMessage` — render overrides.
- `onError`, `onFinish` — listeners forwarded to `useChat`.

## Theming

CSS variables are documented in
[`docs/CSSVariables.md`](https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/components/css-variables.md#aip-agent-chat) under **AIP
Agent Chat**. The `--osdk-aip-agent-chat-*` namespace covers the
container, spacing, message bubbles, composer, empty state, and the
3-dot streaming loader. Defaults live in
[`src/tokens/component-tokens/aip-agent-chat.css`](https://github.com/palantir/osdk-ts/blob/main/packages/react-components/src/tokens/component-tokens/aip-agent-chat.css);
color, spacing, and radius tokens derive from `--osdk-*` semantic
tokens, so brand overrides applied at the `--osdk-*` layer flow through
automatically.

# CSS Variables API Reference

Source: https://older.zaini.me/osdk-ts/components/css-variables

> Reference for the CSS custom properties in @osdk/react-components, from Blueprint token mappings to per-component tokens.

## Overview

This package provides CSS custom properties for theming OSDK React components. All tokens can be overridden using CSS custom properties to create custom themes.

The token system has two main categories:

1. **Blueprint Token Mappings**: OSDK-namespaced aliases to Blueprint's design tokens
2. **OSDK Component Tokens**: Component-specific semantic tokens

## Token Architecture

```
Blueprint Core (@blueprintjs/core)
    ↓ (imported via @import)
Blueprint Tokens (--bp-*)
    ↓ (mapped to)
OSDK Tokens (--osdk-*)
    ↓ (applied to)
React Components
```

## Blueprint Token Mappings

These tokens provide OSDK-namespaced aliases to Blueprint's design system tokens. They reference Blueprint's `--bp-*` tokens which are imported from `@blueprintjs/core`.

### Surface Tokens

Control layout, spacing, shadows, and z-index layering.

| Variable                                         | Maps to Blueprint Token                        | Description                                |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `--osdk-surface-z-index-1`                       | `--bp-surface-z-index-1`                       | Z-index layer 1                            |
| `--osdk-surface-z-index-2`                       | `--bp-surface-z-index-2`                       | Z-index layer 2                            |
| `--osdk-surface-z-index-3`                       | `--bp-surface-z-index-3`                       | Z-index layer 3                            |
| `--osdk-surface-z-index-4`                       | `--bp-surface-z-index-4`                       | Z-index layer 4                            |
